title: Open chat tool-result cards by default for image results
description:
## What

When the `send` tool's result contains an image (e.g., a plot), the R and Python client adapters now return a tool-result object carrying `display = list(open = TRUE)` / `{"display": {"open": True}}` in its `extra` metadata, following shinychat's tool-result display convention. shinychat-compatible chat UIs open the drill-down card by default, so plots are immediately visible instead of sitting behind two clicks (activity row → card).

Text-only results keep their existing return shapes, and errored results never set the flag.

- **R** (`console_tool()`): a successful result containing an image returns an `ellmer::ContentToolResult` whose value holds the ordered text and image content and whose `extra` carries the display hint.
- **Python** (`mcp_console.chatlas.tool()`): same semantics via `chatlas.ContentToolResult(value=..., extra={"display": {"open": True}})`, for both sync and async consoles.
- **No new dependencies**: shinychat accepts the plain-list/dict display form and validates its fields, so the metadata is inert for clients that do not read it.
- **Known limitation**: `mcp_console.chatlas.register()` uses chatlas's native MCP support, which owns that connection's result objects, so the hint cannot be attached there. This is documented in the docstring.

## An alternative worth mentioning

A shinychat-side default (auto-open any settled tool result containing an image) would benefit all image-producing tools without per-tool opt-ins. This per-tool metadata is the less presumptuous first step and works with shinychat as it exists today — happy to defer to you on which layer should own the behavior.

## Validation

- `scripts/preflight` — environment ok
- `scripts/test client_server/integrations/test_python::chatlas_tool_opens_image_results_by_default client_server/integrations/test_python::chatlas_registers_on_existing_chat client_server/integrations/test_python::chatlas_callable_registers_concrete_schema` — pass (DIRECT and SANDBOXED, sync and async parity; snapshot replayed without `--update`)
- `scripts/test` (smoke profile) — pass
- R package tests (as CI runs them, `MCP_CONSOLE_TEST_BINARY=target/release/mcp-console`): full `r/tests/testthat` suite — pass. Note: locally this requires a clean R profile (`R_PROFILE_USER=/dev/null`); the host's startup profile otherwise attaches devtools/usethis and pollutes worker text output, failing two exact-text assertions including one pre-existing test. CI is unaffected.
- `scripts/format` — no changes to PR files; `yamark` reports failures confined to untouched files, identical on the base commit in this environment (pre-existing).
- `scripts/check-core` phases: runtime-sources, architecture, rust-format, clippy — pass.
- Coverage note: the full `rust-tests` phase was not completed locally (the suite exceeds a one-hour command limit on this machine; the patch touches no Rust code). One test, `native_python_inspection_rejects_old_version_and_other_runtime`, fails identically on the base commit in this environment (host native-Python inspection), pre-existing and unrelated.

title: Add the migration notice and documentation redirects
description:
MCP Console development and documentation now live at [posit-dev/mcp-console](https://github.com/posit-dev/mcp-console). Add a README notice directing new issues, pull requests, and development there while retaining this repository's earlier discussions and history.

The documentation workflow renders and checks the existing site, then converts its HTML pages into browser redirects to `https://posit-dev.github.io/mcp-console/`. Redirects preserve page paths, query strings, and anchors. Each page also provides a direct link for browsers without JavaScript, and downloadable assets remain available at their existing URLs. A custom 404 page forwards requested paths to the new site, including pages added there later.

The conversion runs only when explicitly invoked; local documentation renders and previews retain the historical content. This adds redirect checks and documents the deployment step without changing Console runtime behavior or publishing configuration.

Merging this PR deploys the redirects through the existing Pages workflow. Archiving the repository and handling its remaining open PRs are separate steps.

title: Maintain portable session bundles
description:
Keep portable source and result documents available for each recorded worker session, so an agent can inspect the report, copy the bundle, or point a user at it while work proceeds.

- Maintain `sessions/session-NNN/session.qmd`, `session.md`, and portable `images/` links. Announce the bundle's Console-host paths in the first assembled response after it becomes available. Paths are JSON strings so embedded line breaks and other escaped characters remain unambiguous. Restarts and automatic replacement produce separate bundles. Execution previews keep their existing 8 KiB budget; the path notice is separate location metadata.
- Preserve recorded client-facing previews, errors, prompts, omission notices, and images. Later polls stay with their actual cells and observed intervals. The source QMD retains accepted dependencies and failed or rejected submissions without captured outputs.
- Update reports from the recorder's existing events and assembled results, with one anonymous temporary spool and no code, SQL, plot, or Quarto replay. Append report changes and rewrite only an affected suffix when late results belong to an earlier interval; keep source QMD replacement atomic. Use pinned directory capabilities for managed bundle writes and permission updates. Keep one report handle open; rebuild evicted reports from the existing spool when late results arrive. Publish image copies from emitted bytes before their report links. Keep capture usable if a document projection fails. Warmup excludes location metadata from runtime diagnostics and separates progress from later check output.

Copy bundles with ordinary filesystem tools under their existing permissions. Discovery paths grant no sandbox access, and live bundles can change during copying. Completed managed documents become read-only after recording settlement; a working copy may need its write permissions restored.

Storage selection, recording identifiers, raw retention limits, lazy first-send publication, and retirement/delivery barriers remain unchanged. Existing recordings are not migrated. Update public acceptance coverage and the recording, runtime, and architecture documentation for the bundle layout and discovery behavior.

title: Preserve DuckDB cache in native R startup tests
description:
Fix the native R startup fixtures losing the caller's DuckDB extension cache when they isolate `HOME`. The resulting fresh downloads caused [macOS main CI](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/39861115929/job/120111752541) to fail when the extension server returned HTTP 502 for ICU, even though the startup containment check succeeded.

Retain the caller's extension cache alongside its R package cache, preserving explicit cache-directory overrides. Add regression checks that initial startup and restart leave the temporary home's extension directory unused. Existing containment, preparation-isolation, and transcript assertions remain intact. This changes test fixtures only; public runtime behavior is unchanged.

title: Fix managed Python restart transcript polling
description:
Fix the managed Python restart transcript that failed in [macOS main CI](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/39844693016/job/120054768688). A bundled restart, cell, and stdin can return a running or input-request response before the replacement consumes its queued input. The test now collects the accepted evaluation to completion before checking that output, without resubmitting the cell or input.

Use a zero observation timeout to exercise the early return deterministically. Keep the full transcript comparison and the check that the retired worker never consumes the replacement input. This changes acceptance coverage only; public runtime behavior is unchanged.

The previous assertion fails with the zero-timeout regression. The repaired case passes in direct and sandbox modes, along with the related live-package and failed-preparation cases. Local macOS validation also passes `scripts/format`, `git diff --check`, and `scripts/check`.

title: Advance sandbox runner and fix main CI failures
description:
Advance the bundled `rust-v0.163.0` sandbox runner to `74218bd69ceb35e855027a7e3123656200bb3c89` and fix causes of recent `main` CI failures.

The runner update makes `.claude` read-only in its native `:workspace` preset and Console's `sandbox.profile: workspace`, which extends that preset. Console retains its temporary-storage policy and launch-root checks. Update the permissions reference, configuration starter, examples, and developer documentation to match. Public acceptance checks exercise the workspace profile's inherited protection without an explicit `.claude` rule, including child processes and worker replacement.

On Windows, expand short (8.3) interpreter paths during bootstrap so virtualenv imports use the selected environment and retain the correct base interpreter. Preserve the selected executable spelling in public Python state and process arguments across restart.

The remaining CI changes are internal:

- Make transcript-measurement uploads optional so an artifact-service timeout does not skip subsequent installation checks.
- Measure decoder allocations on the output-ingestion thread, excluding concurrent journal and projection work. Retain the allocation ceiling, exact previews, and complete raw-output checks.
- Observe finalized worker output and subsequent relay diagnostics before starting launcher shutdown, so fixture gates do not consume the launcher's retirement deadline. Close worker streams before the terminal worker outcome and assert that the fixture sends no later relay events.

Local `scripts/check`, formatting, and focused sandbox, configuration-starter, import-isolation, prelaunch-retirement, allocation, recording-boundary, and shutdown cases passed. The recording regression rejects the previous invalid event order. The configuration-starter regression rejects the previous metadata guidance and checks that its uncommented examples load. Snapshots were regenerated through `scripts/test --update` and verified without updates. Temporarily reintroducing an extra decoder copy failed the allocation assertion at approximately 8.9 MiB versus a 0.5 MiB baseline; that temporary change was removed.

Five focused Windows import and interpreter-selection cases passed, including a new short-path regression on startup and restart that failed before the fix. Two native Windows MXC acceptance cases passed in interactive Session 1 with native coverage required and no skips. Running under SSH Session 0 reproduces `0xC0000142` with both the previous and updated runners, including Python and `cmd.exe` workloads. That local startup failure is separate from hosted CI; hosted Windows skips native MXC cases when the capability is unavailable.

title: Record per-worker source documents and readable transcripts
description:
New recordings write source to `sessions/session-NNN.qmd`, one document per actual worker lifetime, and keep a recording-wide `transcript.md` focused on calls, source, results, polls, input, controls, and session boundaries. The transcript links to source files and retained output while preserving previews and omission notices.

Session QMDs preserve failed and rejected source, including source submitted with controls, and project accepted dependency state. They contain source and environment metadata, with error-permitting chunks and an `ir render` hint. The original working directory is descriptive metadata; the recording guide explains copying a QMD and its inputs for editing and rendering.

Internally, source admission, association, and settlement use the existing bounded recorder queue. Pending source survives early responses, settled call state is released, replacement requirements stay out of retiring documents, and QMD permissions finalize with recording settlement. Projection failures remain fail-open for computation. The runtime API, raw capture layout, recorder ownership, and previous recordings are unchanged.

CI preserves Cargo’s target-directory marker and compiled dependencies but discards Console’s own restored artifacts before rebuilding, preventing cached timestamps from hiding source changes. Finished release outputs use a fresh cache namespace. The import-isolation acceptance case waits for completion and includes the imported module path when its value assertion fails.

title: Discover user-installed uv with a limited PATH
description:
Desktop launches can supply a PATH that omits `~/.local/bin`, causing Console to report that uv is missing even when it is installed. Console now discovers uv in its default user executable directory after checking PATH, allowing managed Python and SQL sessions to start with the default Console cache policy.

The user directory follows uv's selection order: absolute `XDG_BIN_HOME`, absolute `XDG_DATA_HOME/../bin`, or `~/.local/bin` (`uv.exe` on Windows). Console captures this directory from the server's launch environment and passes it through the private preparation handshake, independently of preparation cache redirects. R-backed preparation also uses the discovered uv. Existing PATH precedence, explicit R-backed uv selection, and reticulate bootstrap remain in place. Discovery does not modify PATH or launch a shell, and a selected executable that fails still reports its failure.

Internally, Console captures the server's launch environment before runtime discovery and includes it in the private `session_started` journal event, including failed startup. The values are unredacted and appear only in `internal/events.jsonl`; Markdown and QMD projections omit them. The resolver, environment, and recording documentation describe these contracts.

Public regressions cover default and XDG executable directories under the default cache policies, PATH precedence, R-backed preparation, and launch-environment recording. `scripts/check` and focused discovery, cache, bootstrap, trust-boundary, and preparation-protocol cases passed on macOS. Native Linux and Windows validation remains to CI.

title: Cache R manuals as Markdown with navigation and search
description:
R's installed manuals can exceed Console's text response size, and native `RShowDoc()` sends HTML to a browser. This change caches each installed HTML manual as one complete Markdown file and makes it discoverable, readable, and searchable through Console-only R clients and ordinary filesystem tools.

`RShowDoc("R-exts")` prints a compact TOC and cache location. Original-anchor requests, including qualified `utils::RShowDoc()` calls, select bounded previews from the same document. Larger sections provide exact continuation commands that stay within the requested section; previews prefer paragraph and block boundaries, and partial code examples retain their fences. `.console$manual()` exposes document paths and line/column ranges. `.console$manual_search()` returns heading paths, excerpts, and read commands, with heading matches first and phrases matched across line wraps and inline formatting. Reading and search are capturable without the R client package or a Python dependency.

The collection contains `R-*.md`, a compact index, and a manifest recording installation identity, R version, source SHA-256 fingerprints, conversion-format version, heading hierarchy, section ranges, and original-anchor locations. Same-manual and cross-manual links resolve within those complete files. Manual bodies occur once; no separate complete export is needed.

Materialization happens on first use under Console's platform cache policy, independently of `MCP_CONSOLE_HOME`. Workers validate the complete cache inventory against installed sources using bounded reads and verified handles. Publication uses exclusive file creation and descriptor writes. A host-created advisory lock outside the worker-writable subtree serializes repair and atomic publication, reporting contention without blocking the interpreter. Repair restores directory access and removes invalid entries through no-follow directory handles, including Windows junctions, and reclaims abandoned staging. Restart repairs missing or invalid cache roots and publication locks while preserving valid lock inodes and leaving conversion lazy.

The implementation reuses the HTML parser and caption handling from merged PR #615. It uses installed UTF-8 HTML without document rebuilding, Pandoc, JavaScript execution, or downloads. R versions before 4.6 use a compatibility adapter through the same browser-option hook. Native invisible returns, plain-text pager behavior, and later browser overrides remain available. UTF-8 document URLs retain their encoding under native C locales. PDF extraction is outside this change.

Two YAML recordings show installed-R client workflows: investigate supported C entry points, follow a chapter continuation, and read an allocation contract using the cached API index; then investigate argument evaluation using function help and manual search. Runtime guidance distinguishes function references and package-help discovery from the broader explanations in manuals.

title: Expose R documentation to clients
description:
## Problem

Installed R documentation is available through ordinary execution, but clients need a discoverable route for qualified lookups, ambiguous topics, installed-version provenance and long pages that exceed Console’s response budget. The optional French acceptance capability also launched selected R executables during test discovery, before a case owned them.

## Fix

Add an installed-R-help guide, runtime cross-reference and sidebar entry. Start with a one-line qualified lookup, then offer scoped text capture, bounded excerpts, candidate search, package indexes and continuation over retained full text. Recipes restore pager and format settings, preserve UTF-8 bytes, report installed provenance and fail on missing documentation without package preparation or example execution.

Five public acceptance cases execute the literal recipes, including hostile viewer settings, complete errors, installed-R references, French indexes and Unicode titles in a non-UTF-8 locale. French coverage requires explicit R_HOME and MCP_CONSOLE_TEST_R_FRENCH_MESSAGES=1, with actual gettext verification inside Console. Public discovery regressions verify that scoped/full listing launches no R executable and preserves broken-selection eligibility. Production code and tool schemas are unchanged relative to main.

## Validation

At clean head bb3a7629, `scripts/check` and `uv run --script tests/transcript_runner.py TranscriptDiscoveryTests` pass, including all 12 discovery tests.

`env -u MCP_CONSOLE_TEST_R_FRENCH_MESSAGES scripts/test client_server/r/test_help_recipes client_server/r/test_documentation client_server/server/test_r_selection::rejects_invalid_local_r_home` passes with explicit capability skips.

`R_HOME=/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.6/Resources MCP_CONSOLE_TEST_R_FRENCH_MESSAGES=1 LANGUAGE=fr LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 scripts/test client_server/r/test_help_recipes` passes all five cases. Inherited-French and C-locale runs without the declaration pass four cases and skip French coverage clearly. A false C-locale declaration fails the real gettext assertion as expected.

Unchanged `scripts/format`, whitespace checks, scoped Quarto rendering and standalone literal recipes on R 4.2.3–4.6.1 pass. Snapshots are unchanged. MCP coverage is macOS/R 4.6.1; native Windows/Linux and full website rendering remain unexecuted. Native documentation fixtures under inherited French messages fail an existing English-menu assertion; ordinary native acceptance passes and those fixtures are unchanged. Hosted review and CI were not checked.

Passed local checks: `uv run --no-project --python 3.13 python scripts/check`.

title: Cache official Python manuals for cell inspection
description:
## Problem

Clients lack a documented path from installed-object help to an offline official Python manual matching their worker. On Python 3.14, checking manifest existence also hides permission errors and incorrectly reports an unreadable cache as missing.

## Fix

Add `help(object)` guidance, long-output and provenance examples, and an explicit trusted host administration command, `prepare-python-docs`. Preparation selects the official page’s linked plain-text ZIP, supports minor-only and patch-version filenames and offline inputs, validates bounded extraction, and publishes atomically with source URLs, release labels, hashes, indexes and license material.

Expose lazy `_console.python_docs()` lookup inside ordinary Python cells, matching the worker host and active interpreter major/minor without startup downloads. Read the manifest directly and return `None` only for `FileNotFoundError`, preserving permission errors. Document file reading/searching and native write-access limits. Internal changes embed and install the helper; the MCP schema, resolver policy and native permissions remain unchanged.

## Validation

Passed on macOS for the committed content:

- `scripts/test client_server/python/test_help_recipes cli/interface/test_help::help` — 10 cases.
- With `UV_PYTHON` selecting CPython 3.14.7: `scripts/test client_server/python/test_help_recipes::manual_cache_preserves_permission_errors client_server/python/test_help_recipes::manual_cache_is_worker_local_and_version_matched` — direct and sandboxed workers. The permission regression failed before repair and also passes on Python 3.13.
- `scripts/format`, `git diff --check`, and clean-head `scripts/check` at `367c5aa3`.

Coverage includes offline reuse/missing caches, version selection/restart, reads/search, write denial, archive bounds/corruption, download failure/retry and real permission denial. Native Linux/Windows, full-profile and website checks were not run for this head; hosted CI/review remains unverified.

Passed local checks: `uv run --no-project --python 3.13 python scripts/check`.

title: Fix process retirement checks on Linux and Windows
description:
Make retirement acceptance observe the owner of each process. The prelaunch closure check pins kernel exit events so an adopted zombie broker does not count as a live process while its host reaps it. The Windows framing fixture confirms that its real R child has exited before starting the relay wrapper's one-second shutdown grace.

Add regressions for delayed host reaping and an R finalizer held at a checkpoint. The existing relay deadline, zero-exit assertions, and separate direct-child reaping checks remain. These changes are confined to acceptance tests and fixtures.

title: Prepare MCP Console 0.0.6 for PyPI
description:
Prepare MCP Console 0.0.6 for its five-platform PyPI wheel release. Synchronize the package version in Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock and regenerate the CLI/MCP version snapshots.

Make release acceptance deterministic around asynchronous evaluation, recording finalization, R activation, and bootstrap completion. Public readiness checks and FIFO checkpoints establish the states exercised by each race. Hold the real Ready frame until interpreter bootstrap completes, then replay buffered frames with poll readiness preserved. R activation and cache probes declare the R bridge requirements they exercise explicitly. Retry-input and combined SQL preparation cases collect completed responses before checking exact output or submitting another cell. Protocol-fixture pipe-closure checks remain separate from real R session-reset acceptance.

Prepare the companion's rendezvous directory inside the disposable nested namespace before making `/tmp` read-only. Keep permission denials, generation ownership, retirement checks, and existing race deadlines intact. Document the remaining Unix fixture limitation for interpreter paths containing spaces.

Validation for `014910125cf7c6bc4649eada9e4cf1c80ee8937a` passed the full local check (2,050 functional executions plus installation), 30 native Linux executions including resolver trust checks, [CI](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/39714889417), [documentation](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/39714889296), and the [build-only rehearsal](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/39714926357). All five installed-wheel jobs and both native Ubuntu 22.04 floor-runtime jobs passed; publication was skipped.

title: Exercise workspace profile across worker replacements
description:
The sandbox worker-replacement test expects workspace metadata protection but configures only a writable-root grant. Select `sandbox.profile: workspace` so the test exercises the profile that supplies those protections, while retaining its additional read-only directory.

Verify that the selected profile, private temporary-storage settings, and complete launch policy survive explicit restart, worker crash recovery, and dependency replacement. Include `.aws` in the denied-write checks and add a canonical tool-discovery snapshot for the profile. These are test changes only; runtime behavior and public APIs are unchanged.

Validation: the profile-selection assertion failed against the previous fixture. After selecting the profile, the worker-replacement case, CLI profile suite, private-temp cleanup case, and canonical initialization cases passed locally on macOS. Snapshots were regenerated through `scripts/test --update` and rerun without it. `scripts/format`, `git diff --check`, and `scripts/check` passed. Hosted Linux and Windows coverage remains pending.

title: Wait for worker readiness in R configuration tests
description:
The R configuration workflow test can receive `[running; poll with an empty send]` when dependency preparation outlasts the first call's observation budget, as in the [macOS main CI failure](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/39638363182). It then compares that pending response with `42`, failing CI even though the cell remains admitted.

Wait for worker readiness through the public requirements inspection before submitting the cell. Share the existing bounded readiness helper with the integration suite and preserve the exact output assertion. This changes test synchronization only; public APIs and runtime behavior are unchanged.

Validation: the two affected R suites passed 112 assertions. The configuration workflow also passed separately with a fresh offline uv cache. The four startup and recording regressions reported by the previous main run passed on the current base. `scripts/format`, `git diff --check`, and `scripts/check` passed locally on macOS. Hosted CI provides Linux and Windows coverage.

title: Repair writable-root permissions and startup CI failures
description:
Repair shared-cache and startup failures seen in CI. Writable-root grants now cover their complete subtrees, including metadata directories, without creating implicit read-only mount targets. Overlapping dependency resolvers can use a shared cache without one launch retiring another launch's synthetic metadata paths. Explicit read-only and deny entries, including workspace-profile rules, remain enforced. Linux writable-file grants also work without treating files as metadata directories.

Adopt the exact companion revision from https://github.com/t-kalinowski/cobox/pull/63. Public regressions cover both writable-root forms, repeated launches, overlapping host and managed caches, and nested execution with a read-only `/tmp` and a writable environment-selected temporary directory.

Warmup now reports a consistent closed-connection failure when the server exits during initialization, preserving stderr and the exit status. Internally, repair stale recording fixtures, use filesystem gates for restricted-network discovery, keep loader interposers out of paths with spaces, and bound discovery probes to four concurrent clients while retaining every assertion and the existing deadline.

Native Windows execution remains unverified. The update is published for review with that validation gap recorded; optional-mode Windows CI does not establish native sandbox coverage.

title: Fix Windows environment inheritance probe execution
description:
The shared environment-inheritance regression enabled in #702 still failed on Windows: the uv probe's `os.execv` delegation lost Python argument grouping and could return before its child finished, leaving the resolved interpreter path empty. Use a waited subprocess on Windows for both seeded Python and real uv delegation, while retaining Unix process replacement.

Configure `TMPDIR`, `TEMP`, and `TMP` for the fixture's worker and resolver environments so disabled inheritance uses its writable temporary directory instead of falling back to `C:\Windows`. Preserve all four inheritance combinations, restart assertions, and the existing shared snapshot.

These changes are confined to test fixtures; public APIs and runtime behavior are unchanged.

title: Enable shared environment inheritance tests on Windows
description:
Enable the shared environment-inheritance and restart regression on Windows by replacing its shebang-based uv probe with a native launcher. Preserve all four worker/resolver inheritance combinations and the existing cache and temporary-directory assertions, and exercise workspace paths containing spaces.

The launcher is shared with the resolver-cache tests, which now declare `rustc` as a fixture dependency. Update the Windows coverage guide and TODO entry. These are test-infrastructure and documentation changes; public APIs and runtime behavior are unchanged.

Closes #701.

title: Enable shared runtime discovery tests on Windows
description:
Ten shared runtime-discovery cases were skipped on Windows because their fixture used a shebang R probe, `fork()`, and FIFOs. Replace that fixture with a native R probe and a loopback gate so initialization, discovery failures, cancellation, early cells, phase reporting, and explicit retry run on Windows too. Pin the Windows descendant's process handle before releasing the gate so cleanup assertions verify its exit directly.

This changes internal test fixtures, capability requirements, a fixture-description snapshot, and the Windows coverage notes. Public runtime behavior and interfaces are unchanged. Pipe-backpressure, R FIFO, and native-interposition cases retain their platform requirements.

Local `scripts/check`, 25 focused macOS cases (29 executions), and all 36 website tests passed.

Closes #695.

title: Clarify language choices across R, Python, and SQL
description:
Encourage choosing whichever language makes each step easiest to express, with concrete guidance for moving from Python into R data frames and combining R expressions with Python objects and function calls through reticulate. Add a brief reminder of DuckDB's file and database access, including a JSON/JSONL file-glob example. The description adapts to the languages exposed by the tool.

Replace overlapping language-selection text and move reusable R script guidance into the R argument description to preserve the 2,048-character description budget. Synchronize the owning documentation, public presentation assertions, and generated snapshots. Runtime execution and the tool's schema structure are unchanged.

title: Refresh SQL traceback snapshots
description:
The DuckDB result cleanup change moved embedded Python SQL code by three lines, leaving acceptance snapshots stale and failing CI.

Regenerate the warmup, Python requirement, SQL selection, and SQL startup snapshots through their public acceptance cases. This updates internal test expectations only. Public behavior, complete traceback content, and error messages are unchanged apart from the source line numbers.

title: Capture output intervals and finalize recording files
description:
Record output by the interval in which Console observes it, so later polls and worker replacement preserve its original ownership.

New recordings keep `capture/events.jsonl` and raw text/images under `capture/sessions/NNN/`. Each worker session has startup, numbered cell, and post-cell intervals. Silent executed cells get empty logs; polls, input, controls, and rejected source do not create cells. Text/image ordering is retained through explicit owners and text ranges. The recording-wide `transcript.md` and `transcript.qmd` remain available with updated capture links.

Completed interval logs and images become read-only. The journal and documents finalize after worker retirement, delivery settlement, queued initial capture, and blocking result writers finish. Cancellation and delivery deadlines cannot release capture ownership early. Recording remains fail-open, and retained files receive final permissions even after capture or projection failure.

Internally, the worker reports cell entry, the output tape carries interval ownership through bounded previews and response recovery, and the recording queue tracks task completion separately from transport delivery. Live file handles remain relocatable during prelude publication; completed handles are released. Public regressions cover interval ordering, attribution, permissions, partial retention, and stalled-writer shutdown behavior.

title: Preserve CI for every main commit
description:
New merges currently cancel CI for earlier commits on main, leaving those revisions without complete validation. Group CI by commit SHA for main pushes while retaining PR-number grouping so newer PR revisions replace older runs.

Document that a release can retain its selected revision while later merges continue. This changes CI scheduling and release instructions; there are no public API or runtime changes.

The recent DuckDB failures are already fixed on main by #696, and the older Windows relocation failure by #687. The four failing SQL cases pass locally in direct and sandboxed execution. Actionlint, development tests, formatting, and the ordinary local check pass.

title: Support DuckDB 2.0 alongside 1.x
description:
Support DuckDB 2.0 alongside 1.x while keeping the default package request unpinned as `duckdb`.

DuckDB 2.0 keeps unfinished query results attached to their connection. Console now clears those results when it discards them, so selecting another SQL connection and later reusing the original connection works. Cleanup preserves the connection, completes pending writes, and leaves transaction commit or rollback to the caller.

Internally, cleanup uses DuckDB's empty `execute("")` operation, which works on both major versions. Add public coverage with DuckDB 1.5.6 and 2.0.0 in direct and sandbox modes, update fixtures and snapshots for the new driver behavior, and document native result lifetime. R provider behavior and dependency defaults are unchanged.

title: Synchronize Python SQL provider-probe interruption
description:
The Python DB-API provider-probe test can receive SIGINT between publishing readiness and entering its wait, producing different traceback lines under CI load. Hold the probe inside one native call until the public interrupt response confirms delivery, then release it and collect the exception.

The test still records the complete KeyboardInterrupt traceback and verifies that the next SQL query succeeds. This changes test synchronization and its snapshot only; runtime behavior is unchanged.

title: Synchronize poll ownership in the interrupt test
description:
The interrupt regression can fail when the competing poll reaches the server before the intended waiter has claimed the evaluation. This caused the Ubuntu CI failure on #259.

Send a stdin marker with the waiting request and wait for the scripted relay to acknowledge it through a FIFO before submitting the competing poll. Stdin is forwarded after the request claims the evaluation, so the checkpoint establishes the ordering the test requires. The exact ownership error, interrupt result, and output assertions remain in place; the generated wire snapshot includes the marker.

This changes only test synchronization. Production behavior is unchanged.

Core checks and the full interrupt suite passed. The full local check stopped on a worker-startup timeout in the unchanged `worker_reports_closed_output_pipe_without_r_sigpipe_handler` test; that case passed in the focused run.

title: Synchronize interrupt test fixtures
description:
Interrupt tests can hang or report different states depending on when the worker consumes stdin or a resolver finishes after SIGINT. Use a wakeup pipe and FIFO checkpoints to synchronize those events and keep the resolver active until the interrupt response is collected.

The tests retain exact interruption errors, terminal signal counts, console prefix replay, idle responses, and successful retries. This changes test fixtures and their snapshots; production behavior is unchanged.

The full local check stopped on a timeout in the unchanged processx descendant-retirement test. That case and all modified regressions passed in the focused run.

title: Initialize Python before arming the interruption checkpoint
description:
The Python interruption test starts its checkpoint deadline while the interpreter is still initializing, so slow setup can exhaust the deadline before the intended dispatch begins. Complete interpreter initialization in the existing R setup cell before arming the checkpoint, after setting the FIFO environment variables that Python captures on startup.

This changes only test setup and its source snapshot. The R and Python interruption scenarios, output expectations, and deadlines are unchanged.

title: Synchronize the R fatal-input recovery test
description:
Observe R's fatal-signal menu before submitting abort input. The recovery test previously assumed queued stdin would be consumed before the input-report grace elapsed, so a valid waiting response failed its error assertion under load.

Collect the exact abort and replacement output through provisional responses, preserving the complete crash report, error status, and state-loss checks. The shared collector can now expect an error on completion and use this case's existing 60-second budget; other callers retain their existing defaults. This changes test coordination only.

title: Make interruption and retirement checkpoints deterministic
description:
Two lifecycle tests depend on scheduling outside the behavior they intend to check. Python interruption can land while the readiness file is still being created, changing the recorded traceback. The sandbox retirement test treats an unreaped descendant PID as a live process, even though descendant reaping belongs to its external parent.

Hold the Python evaluation at an explicit native checkpoint until the test sends the interrupt, then record signal acceptance at a stable call site and verify that session state survives. Observe exit events for the complete relay subtree and sandbox manager under the existing retirement deadlines, while still requiring the launcher to reap its direct relay and manager.

This changes only test synchronization and its transcript. Runtime behavior and public protocols are unchanged.

title: Expose the transcript client API and bound response waits
description:
The transcript client could block indefinitely on a partial response or server shutdown, and its methods were private in name despite being used throughout the suites. Expose those methods as the supported test API and add configurable response and shutdown deadlines with a server stderr tail in failures.

Use synchronous, buffered descriptor reads to drain stdout and stderr together while preserving the tests' explicit response gates. A context manager closes input, allows staged retirement, and reaps the server after assertions fail; the final fallback targets only the server PID. The socket gate shares the same reader, and two resource-owning fixtures now use the context manager.

Under the transcript runner, response waits reserve time before the absolute case deadline for cleanup and diagnostics. Server retirement and forced reaping share a budget shorter than the supervisor's cleanup window, including when a signal interrupts the case.

This changes test infrastructure only. Call-site renames preserve embedded programs and snapshots. Public client regressions cover partial responses, stalled shutdown, cleanup after an assertion, and response and cleanup deadlines under the runner.

title: Simplify response waits and restart acknowledgment
description:
Prepared-cell and polling paths duplicated the existing wait-result mapping. Route both through `send_response_from_wait()` and give restart delivery the same capacity-one acknowledgment used by ordinary delivery. This lets transport completion or Drop publish its single settlement without waiting for the restart receiver to be scheduled. The restart owner keeps its existing receive before composing the response.

Public output and timing stay unchanged, including reclaimed/restarted response mapping, terminal notices, timeout start points, transport admission, cancellation, request identity, and write acknowledgment. No deadlock was demonstrated; the channel change removes unnecessary scheduling coupling.

- Production: 7 added / 21 removed lines in wait conversion and restart handoff.
- Tests: existing public and transport coverage; no new tests.
- Snapshots: unchanged.
- Documentation: clarify that Console owns a recoverable response until local transport settlement. It cannot prove exactly-once client observation because cancellation can race with bytes already visible to the client.

`scripts/format` and the complete `scripts/check` passed, including public output, restart/interrupt/transport transcripts and source/wheel installation checks. Capability-inapplicable cases were skipped by the runner.

An initial full-check run timed out waiting for ping in the existing 1,024-restart image-recovery fixture while other full checks were running. The subsequent serial full check passed without changing timeouts or assertions. The cause of the initial timeout remains unconfirmed.

title: Route all send operations through the session coordinator
description:
Every `send` combination now enters the session coordinator, including standalone requirement preparation. The MCP adapter decodes arguments, filters languages, and translates responses; the coordinator owns requirement validation and operation selection.

This removes the separate preparation dispatch, duplicated capability state, and the valid-or-invalid requirement wrapper. Requirement validation still runs after interruption, stdin, and prior-evaluation settlement for interrupt-plus-cell calls. Preparation results, error text, generation admission, response delivery, and the public schema remain unchanged.

title: Wait for console output and retain retirement checkpoints
description:
Existing console regressions can fail when a response arrives before the next input prompt or the completion event, or when sandbox cleanup removes a checkpoint file before the test reads it.

Collect every output fragment while polling, require the exact expected result, and retain that complete result in the transcript. The UTF-8 test now waits for its second prompt. Partial-sideband restart and shutdown tests attach the existing fixture event channel before releasing the worker, so the flushed-frame checkpoint remains observable after its directory is removed.

These changes affect test coordination only. Runtime behavior and the expected transcript output are unchanged.

title: Accept Python interruption at the provider-probe checkpoint
description:
The Python SQL provider-probe interruption test could report `KeyboardInterrupt` from context-manager cleanup instead of its paused native call. Holding the GIL delayed Python signal handling, but returning through `ctypes.PyDLL` did not process the pending signal.

Have the fixture wait for Python's signal wakeup descriptor and process the pending interrupt before returning from the native checkpoint. The public test still verifies interrupt delivery, the complete traceback, and a subsequent successful SQL query. This changes test synchronization and its expected transcript; runtime behavior is unchanged.

title: Bound transcript case execution and failure cleanup
description:
A hanging transcript case could keep the suite running indefinitely, including while another case's failure was waiting to be reported. The runner now gives each case a 600-second deadline, configurable with `scripts/test --timeout SECONDS` for slower resolver workflows.

Each case and its snapshot checks run in a fresh process with captured diagnostics. An external supervisor owns interruption and forced cleanup, so fixtures can use `fork` and `preexec_fn` without a monitoring thread, and cleanup remains possible when native code holds the case's GIL. Snapshot formatting and filesystem work share the case deadline and cannot block the coordinator's signal handling. A timeout allows 15 seconds for fixture cleanup before killing the case by PID. After a failure, Ctrl-C, SIGTERM, or SIGHUP, the runner cancels queued cases and bounds cleanup of running cases while retaining concurrent failures. An ownership pipe requests the same cleanup if the runner is killed outright. Fixtures still own their descendants.

This changes the development runner only; MCP and runtime behavior are unchanged. Public runner regressions cover deadlines, concurrent failures, signals, runner loss, fork safety, and a native GIL hold. Existing transcript snapshots remain unchanged.

title: Avoid races with exiting validation resources
description:
Two test-fixture lifetime races can fail otherwise successful CI runs. Workflow tests copy a freshly committed repository while Git's detached maintenance removes its lock file. On Linux, a process can exit after its `/proc/<pid>/stat` file is opened, making the read fail with `ESRCH`.

Disable automatic maintenance only in the test-owned repositories. Treat `ProcessLookupError` as an exited process alongside `FileNotFoundError` in the procfs helpers. Existing process-identity, lifecycle, output, and cleanup assertions remain unchanged. There are no production or user-facing changes.

This is independent of #350 and starts from main at `6cd4cfd4f61ec5df723cc0e25b8f35a90ba8377e`. The failures were observed in its macOS and Ubuntu jobs in [CI run 35273051914](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/35273051914).

Local validation passed on clean revision `5cea6fc9d4e4fcff0d35df34a8ddb25ae482370e`: `scripts/check`, the focused startup lifecycle suites, and all 22 workflow tests. All four formatters and `git diff --check` passed. Validation ran on macOS ARM; the Linux-specific procfs path awaits Ubuntu CI, and unavailable platform/provider fixtures retained their existing capability skips.

title: Amortize streaming text buffers and borrow direct chunks
description:
Tiny events from one producer repeatedly shifted the retained terminal suffix after each append. Advance a UTF-8 boundary offset instead, compact periodically, and cap tail storage at 16 KiB. Complete direct stdout/stderr chunks now use a borrowed decoding path. Remove decoder origin/event counters because every direct push flushes the other decoder first, leaving at most one incomplete scalar across polls and stream closes.

Public output stays unchanged: the complete 8 KiB text budget, latest tail, redraws, omission counts, raw logs, stream order, and recovery behavior retain their existing contracts.

- Production: 39 added / 33 removed lines in terminal collection and direct decoding.
- Tests: four public scenarios cover same-producer storage bounds, complete-chunk allocation, Unicode editing after overflow, and partial UTF-8 across polls and stream/cell boundaries. They check raw bytes, exact head/tail and omission accounting, and subsequent polls.
- Snapshots: four new transcripts; existing transcripts unchanged.
- Documentation: no document changes.

On an Apple M4 Max with recording enabled, medians of three profiled runs after warm-up for 100,000 same-producer 2-byte events measured 91,808 overlapping copies moving 752,091,136 bytes before this change and zero overlapping copies after. Total interposed copy bytes fell from approximately 756.8 MB to 4.9 MB, including periodic compaction and protocol work. Requested console-path allocation was unchanged. For 64 direct chunks of 64 KiB, allocation requests fell from 8,633,130 to 4,438,808 bytes.

Profiled CPU time varies by workload: recorded same-producer console output measured 144.32 → 143.78 ms; the same direct workload with recording disabled measured 73.07 → 56.92 ms. Alternating producers, 256-byte and 64-KiB chunks, redraws, disabled recording, and injected recording failure were also profiled. These figures establish copy/allocation reductions, with no claim of a uniform elapsed-time improvement.

The recording profile measured 100,001 raw-file writes for 200,018 bytes in the tiny-event case. Buffering remains separate work; this change preserves synchronous recording and cut behavior.

`scripts/format` and the complete `scripts/check` passed, including source/wheel installation checks. The new complete-chunk allocation assertion failed on main. Snapshots were generated through `scripts/test --update`. Capability-inapplicable cases were skipped by the runner.

An initial full-check run timed out at the existing 1,024-restart recovery fixture while other full checks were running. That fixture passed against unchanged main and this candidate in isolation, and the subsequent serial full check passed without changing timeouts or assertions. The cause of the initial timeout remains unconfirmed.

title: Synchronize interruption and retirement tests
description:
Fix CI races in interruption and retirement tests by making their checkpoints explicit.

- Receive SIGINT with `sigwait()` in the relay output fixtures, so blocking socket reads cannot leave Python's signal callback pending.
- Poll for the exact R and Python input-interruption results when their handlers outlast the control call's 100 ms grace period.
- Keep the partial-sideband worker alive until explicit retirement closes stdin. A separate natural-exit scenario checks automatic replacement and descendant cleanup.
- Hold the final stdout read until retirement joins its reader, and trigger the protocol failure only after that read has captured the complete payload. This preserves the exact byte assertion without depending on the 100 ms allowance for reading remaining pipe data.

The existing expected output and snapshots are preserved. These changes affect test synchronization and coverage only; there are no user-facing, runtime, or protocol changes.

title: Represent each relay reader with one ownership state
description:
The relay now stores each stdout, stderr, and sideband reader in a single state that owns either the unstarted stream or its running reader. This replaces paired optional fields whose cleanup had to check that exactly one was populated.

Failed reader startup retains the raw stream for the existing cleanup path. Cancellation order, the shared retirement deadline, and relay output remain unchanged. This is an internal ownership refactor with no console or protocol changes.

title: Keep R tool cleanup scoped to the server
description:
Releasing an ellmer console tool can stop the sandbox manager before it finishes cleanup. Close the server's input and allow up to 15 seconds for staged shutdown, then signal only the server if it remains alive. Interrupting that wait still runs the server-only fallback. Worker retirement stays with the sandbox launcher and manager.

Disable processx's automatic process-group and tree cleanup, use its process handle with `ps` for the server-only fallback, and declare `ps` as a direct dependency. Update the R documentation to describe tool shutdown.

title: Check companion repositories and nested guide links
description:
Follow up #691 to catch companion source links that escaped the documentation smoke check. Compare both repository and commit, retain recognition of the original companion repository after a migration, and scan nested Markdown and Quarto guides. Dated audit and benchmark records retain their revisions, and generated website output is excluded.

Add command-level regression fixtures for repository changes, stale nested links, valid links, and the exclusions. Update the development guide to describe the check. Runtime behavior and public APIs are unchanged.

title: Inventory local tools and build artifacts without provisioning
description:
`scripts/preflight` inventories the checkout, development and installed executables, artifact presence, companion pin and recorded target/revision, Python/R selections and compiler metadata, optional provider capabilities, and cache locations. Missing, failed, or timed-out required tool probes produce a nonzero status; optional provider skips remain nonfatal. Metadata-command failures remain in the report and also return a nonzero status. Human-readable and JSON output use the same inventory.

The command reuses staging metadata and existing capability probes without installing tools, provisioning providers, or building artifacts. The command requires Python 3.11 or later. Platform setup remains in RELEASE.md, and staging and Cargo retain build-readiness validation; malformed existing metadata remains an explicit error. Console runtime behavior is unchanged.

title: Bound queued relay output and preserve control progress
description:
When downstream relay output pauses, worker output now waits for queue capacity instead of accumulating indefinitely. The ordinary budget covers 8 MiB or 512 encoded frames, including the write in progress. Frames from the worker remain unlimited: one oversized frame can occupy the ordinary budget by itself.

Interrupt results, shutdown acceptance, and retirement outcomes use a small reserved allowance in the same FIFO. They preserve ordering while allowing the supervisor to keep handling commands; exhausting that allowance fails the transport and retires the worker.

Internally, each event is serialized once before admission, and the writer reports one retained transport failure. For pipe and socket output, capacity waits share the output retirement deadline; regular files retain ordinary blocking behavior. These limits cover admitted output payloads; framing buffers, individual large frames, and worker-input queues retain their existing behavior.

The large-frame regression also removes repeated scans of the growing buffer in the test capture helper; its timeout and exact-output checks stay the same.

title: Bound relay output flushing during retirement
description:
A paused downstream reader can leave the relay waiting to flush shutdown acceptance or join its output writer indefinitely. Enqueue shutdown acceptance and begin worker shutdown immediately, then give pipe or socket output one shared second to flush after direct-worker retirement, starting before local I/O joins. Startup failures use the same deadline.

The event writer owns nonblocking output, its wakeup, and the retirement deadline in one module. Senders serialize each event once before queueing its frame, keeping JSON encoding outside the output flush window and avoiding a native write for each JSON fragment. The writer applies the deadline while bytes remain pending. It preserves the ordered JSONL stream and supports large frames. If pipe or socket output remains blocked at the deadline, the relay returns a transport error and may leave a partial final frame. Regular-file redirection keeps its usual file-system behavior.

Public regressions cover shutdown, natural worker exit, and startup failure with a full downstream pipe, complete delivery after a paused reader resumes, success when the deadline passes after the final frame has been written, and regular-file delivery after that interval. The protocol guides describe the delivery boundary and unchanged sandbox ownership.

title: Prepare built-in environments on first use
description:
Built-in sessions currently install their default environments before answering MCP initialization. Defer that work until an operation needs an environment so clients can discover the tool before package installation and poll or interrupt preparation for the first cell.

Keep the existing scientific package defaults, resolver selection order, and ambient reticulate bootstrap. Startup captures configuration and checks capability without invoking installation. The first cell prepares defaults after admission; explicit requirements remain preconditions and combine their additions with those defaults. Bare runtimes and custom-worker requirements retain their existing behavior.

The session environment owns pending bootstrap state and commits the complete prepared candidate for the accepting generation. Failed preparation remains retryable. Interrupt remains effective before and between resolver processes, including when a first cell overlaps idle input; restart discards the old generation's cell and stdin. Public regressions cover handshake ordering, preserved defaults, ambient bootstrap failure, preparation ordering, interruption, restart, and input closure. The runtime guides describe the new timing and failure behavior.

title: Make shared CLI fixtures portable on Windows
description:
Four shared CLI cases exclude Windows because they use a shell fixture, a Unix executable path, or unnecessary POSIX requirements. Replace the resolver's shell fixture with a native executable that returns the test interpreter's path, and use Console's `--version` command in configuration-conflict coverage. Remove the POSIX restrictions from those cases and the oversized/invalid startup cases.

This changes test fixtures, one snapshot, and contributor documentation. Public CLI and runtime behavior are unchanged. The TODO and Windows coverage notes retain the remaining fixture exclusions and document the native fixture's `rustc` requirement.

Both affected CLI suites passed locally on macOS (18 cases), along with `scripts/format` and `scripts/check`. Native Windows execution remains unverified locally.

title: Use a privately bundled native sandbox executable
description:
Replace direct macOS sandbox construction with a privately bundled native runner so the sandbox implementation can evolve independently of the console.

Public commands and the MCP protocol stay the same; platform support remains macOS-only. Wheels install `mcp-console-sandbox` under private `libexec`, and only `mcp-console` is exposed on PATH. Debug, release, and installed binaries resolve it relative to the public executable and verify its build-time digest.

The runner is pinned to `4a061c4ec94f5ad99e148982168ea4f21367c26c`, protocol 2, with Rust 1.95.0. The launcher starts it with original stdio attached and sends one framed JSON configuration through `--bootstrap-fd <N>` after manager readiness, recovery installation, and owner validation. One nonblocking write per event-loop iteration keeps cancellation observable between writes. The setup frame replaces the separate target gate; the remaining hidden wrapper restores the target's original signal mask and execs its command.

MCP Console retains supervision, terminal ownership, signal delivery, and cleanup. Policy additions preserve host-terminal restrictions and disposable temporary-directory semantics. Each exception has its own rationale, with unresolved historical attribution documented. Group-directed signals received before target creation are not replayed to the command; this startup limitation is documented. Managed networking, configurable policies, and extending the runner contract remain outside this change.

CI and release builds stage the pinned executable for the selected Cargo target and verify packaging, installation, and sandbox launches.

Supersedes #166.

title: Compare PyTorch autograd inside and outside the sandbox
description:
Compare a live PyTorch CPU autograd calculation outside and inside the default sandbox. Each run refreshes the unpinned torch environment, then uses the same interpreter and small script for both executions. The test compares the loss, all 65,536 gradient values, and thread count against the unsandboxed result.

This is a direct sandbox CLI test. It records numerical agreement without fixing dependency versions, warning text, or numerical values in the snapshot; command failures retain stdout and stderr for diagnosis. The existing libomp allowance remains an unverified compatibility exception. There are no runtime or sandbox-policy changes.

title: Route background worker activity through explicit operations
description:
## Summary

Route background worker frames through the next explicit evaluation or live preparation instead of modeling idle activity as a separate protocol transaction. The worker is single-threaded, so the requested command can be sent immediately and its ordinary terminal can fence any preceding callback work.

## User-facing changes

Built-in between-cell execution remains unchanged in this layer. A custom worker may publish background console output, images, input requests, Python resolver requests, and version-selection requests before the next explicit result. Managed-Python activation receipts remain reserved for server-managed workers; a custom worker that sends one fails the active operation. A custom worker must queue an unrelated command while waiting for a nested resolver reply. Background input joins an evaluation's input flow, but fails noninteractive requirement preparation instead of leaving it blocked.

## Internal changes

- Let evaluation and live-preparation readers accept leading background frames after sending their command.
- Use each explicit operation's existing terminal as the only activity boundary; no readiness probe or `activity_completed` frame is added.
- Validate and queue background images received during preparation, then persist them when a response drains pending output.
- Exercise command queuing, resolver routing, preparation failure, and evaluation input through the custom-worker fixture.

title: Warm managed SQL connections during background startup
description:
Enabled SQL currently opens its managed DuckDB connection on first use. This PR moves connection creation into the default worker's background startup, so an installed provider can be ready before the first SQL cell.

- R owns the managed connection when available; otherwise Python does. The startup catalog remains available to subsequent SQL cells, and MCP initialization, tool discovery, and pings remain responsive during warmup.
- Warmup skips absent optional providers and does not resolve missing packages. Python also skips workspace modules or packages shadowing the installed DuckDB distribution.
- Optional provider failures remain visible through `send` and leave unrelated cells usable. An interrupt withholds an early waiting cell while retaining the worker. Later SQL demand can retry connection creation.
- First-query work remains deferred. Custom workers retain lazy initialization, and disabled SQL does not warm a connection.

Internally, the coordinator opens the connection after enabled interpreter startup on its owning thread, using the existing managed provider configuration and bootstrap interrupt receipt. On macOS, sideband pipes suppress SIGPIPE at the descriptor before DuckDB starts native threads, preserving orderly shutdown.

Acceptance fixtures now compare canonical R package paths, wait for input and recording completion checkpoints, and verify that failed extension preparation retains the existing managed connection.

title: Keep small task checkpoints and explicit stopping conditions
description:
The task checkpoint template keeps the task objective and scope, checkout state, runnable validation commands, evidence, next action, and requested stopping condition in ignored `.dev-workflow/task.md`. It gives resumed work the context to continue and keeps validation claims tied to the available evidence.

The resume recipe checks saved revisions and requires inspecting dirty edits. It accepts missing metadata as `not recorded`, manually captured evidence for commands without completion records, and review-only handoffs with validation `not run`. Unfinished runs retain their original terminal or task handle. Stopping conditions distinguish review completion, local validation, publication, and requested hosted CI completion, with no default watcher.

This layer changes contributor documentation only. Console runtime behavior is unchanged.

title: Plan review boundaries and measure each layer against its base
description:
The development workflow adds a brief review-boundary template covering observable behavior, owning modules, public cases, expected snapshots, and intended PR base. It is a planning aid without an additional approval step.

`scripts/review-diff BASE` measures the tracked working tree from the merge base of `BASE` and `HEAD`, including staged and unstaged changes. Parent-only changes are excluded when a stack's parent advances. The report separates production, tooling, tests, documentation, generated snapshots, and binary files, lists excluded untracked files, and supports JSON output. Core checks run its public command regressions. Console runtime behavior is unchanged.

title: Document fixture authoring and report formatter results
description:
Embedded test programs need consistent formatting and explicit lifecycle checkpoints. Add a compact boundary-authoring recipe for readable `code()` payloads, formatting directives, execution modes, and public lifecycle receipts, with links to existing examples. Keep `code(` and the opening string delimiter on one line, directly below the formatting directive; align the existing fixtures with that convention.

For contributors, `scripts/format` reports the result of Ruff, Yamark, rustfmt, and Air while attempting every formatter. The default remains best effort; optional `--strict` returns failure if any formatter fails or is missing. Core checks run the formatter command regression, covering tool order, result reporting, and exit status. Console runtime behavior and transcript snapshots are unchanged.

title: Remove managed Python checkpoints
description:
## Summary

Replace terminal managed-Python manifest checkpoints with standalone activation receipts and payload-free operation completion. Reticulate's accepted activation and explicit preparation already provide the relevant commit boundaries, so repeating the manifest on every completed cell adds protocol and lifecycle state without improving the live-worker result.

## User-facing changes

Successful live activations and explicit Python preparations remain retained for later worker generations. A lazy `py_require()` declaration made before Python initializes now remains worker-owned until Python initializes or an explicit preparation materializes it; losing the worker before either boundary loses that declaration. A Python environment accepted during mixed live preparation remains retained if a later R update fails.

## Internal changes

- Make `completed` and `python_prepared` payload-free.
- Remove cell-end Python materialization and terminal checkpoint selection.
- Retain environments through `python_activated`, or through the server-known resolver candidate after successful explicit materialization.
- Accept an activation and validate its worker generation atomically, so a receipt cannot commit after restart claims the generation.
- Discard unmatched evaluation candidates and remove the obsolete checkpoint bridge, protocol cases, and fixture behavior.

title: Enable shared warmup coverage on Windows
description:
Enable five shared warmup cases on Windows to cover missing or unusable R and interactive startup input. This reduces the fixture-only exclusions tracked by SP-3; public runtime behavior is unchanged.

Use a native R launcher fixture for invalid discovery output, retain the Windows missing-file diagnostic in a platform snapshot, and update the coverage documentation.

title: Check documented preparation defaults and companion links
description:
Keep preparation defaults and companion source links from drifting as configuration and the native pin change. Add smoke checks that compare the documented YAML example with public `config resolve` output and reject companion source links that differ from `sandbox-runner.json`, preserving dated audit and benchmark revisions.

Show the default preparation policies in the package reference and remove completed TODO item DX-2. Runtime behavior and public APIs are unchanged.

title: Fix the Linux sandbox signal test race
description:
The Linux job for #307 timed out in `cli/sandbox/test_linux::relays_signal_and_preserves_target_status`. SIGINT can reach CPython after it releases the GIL for `signal.pause()` but before the native `pause()` starts waiting. The Python handler stays pending while the target sleeps. `Popen.__exit__` then waits indefinitely after the test's 15-second timeout, until the 600-second case deadline interrupts cleanup.

Block SIGINT before announcing readiness and consume it with `sigwait()`, checking that the inherited mask originally allowed SIGINT. Kill and reap a surviving launcher in `finally` with the existing timeout. This changes only the test fixture; runtime behavior and snapshots are unchanged.

Validation:

- A native checkpoint through the public sandbox CLI reproduced the original hang and verified that the corrected target consumes an already-pending SIGINT with the exact output and exit status 23.
- The Linux signal and descendant-retirement cases passed against their existing snapshots in a namespace-capable container. The fresh-procfs case is unavailable in that container.
- With a deliberately non-exiting sandbox target, the test reported its original timeout and completed cleanup in 15.06 seconds.
- `scripts/format` and `scripts/check` passed on macOS, including the available transcript cases and source/wheel installation checks. Platform-specific and unconfigured real-provider cases retained their capability skips.
- GitHub Actions passed on `ubuntu-24.04` and `macos-latest` for the current PR head.

title: Consolidate selected-target sessions and compute probes
description:
SSH, Docker, and SBX now expose one selected-target session and one generation retirement receipt to worker orchestration. Docker and SBX share compute probing, owner-command/bootstrap construction, and controller replacement blocking.

The production refactor removes the separate SSH/compute options from client state, worker specifications, launch, output-envelope handling, and retirement checks. Each generation keeps its cleanup receipt; compute generations also retain their owned-resource name. SSH preparation keeps its separate connection and protocol, and startup cancellation still leaves SSH connected for remote cleanup confirmation.

Docker still owns endpoint/TLS capture, immutable image resolution, and exact container cleanup. The SBX adapter still owns CLI/template validation, creation acknowledgment, name/UUID checks, and VM removal; provider policy remains externally managed. Inner-launcher retirement remains distinct from outer-resource retirement. Provider output routing and timeout values are preserved. Shared diagnostics now use the correct provider label; there is no new public configuration or execution capability.

Existing code moved or reused: the compute dispatch is folded into `target_session.rs`; the owner request and workload-environment decoder are shared; SSH uses the bounded bootstrap encoder and generic transfer/payload helpers directly; queued-output draining uses the existing readiness helper. The two SBX controller-isolation fixtures are extracted into test support, and Docker peer logs reuse the JSONL reader. No cases were added and no snapshots changed.

The architecture documentation records the timing audit: Docker still allows 8 seconds for probe cancellation and 6 for generation retirement, while cleanup CLI operations have separate deadlines. SBX retains its 20-second owner allowances. No timing failure was reproduced or fixed in this PR.

Raw diff categories: production Rust +482/-540 (including the source relocations above); fixture refactoring +51/-67; documentation +83/-31; generated snapshots unchanged.

Validation on macOS 26.6.2 arm64:

- `scripts/format` completed with no formatter failures; `scripts/check` passed, including 47 Rust tests, 570 public transcript cases, and uv source/wheel installation checks.
- The same 70 focused SSH/preparation/Docker/SBX-provider cases passed on the starting main binary and on the refactor, without snapshot updates.
- Built both example images from this checkout and imported the digest-qualified SBX template. The full check used Docker Engine 29.5.2 / CLI 29.8.0 and standalone sbx v0.42.1, including all 13 real microVM runtime/lifecycle/policy cases, scoped network-rule checks, and retirement of an independently started inner container. Fake-peer coverage remains separate from this real-provider evidence.
- Local direct/native execution and real loopback SSH passed, including preparation cancellation, chunked results, transport loss, generation replacement, and recordings. Provider cases covered creation cancellation, uncertain cleanup blocking replacement, backpressured output, exact resource ownership, environment isolation, and restart.

Explicit skips: 16 Linux-specific cases, two unsupported-platform cases, both SEGV_MAPERR modes of the alternate null-fault case, and the unconfigured external SSH policy fixture (20 distinct cases; 21 case/mode entries). Linux-controller/KVM validation was not run. Colima denied nested native namespace creation; the Docker rejection path passed, while the suite did not run native permission-success assertions on that daemon.

title: Add foreground terminal handling to standalone sandboxes
description:
## Summary

Standalone `mcp-console sandbox` commands now run in a dedicated process group. The launcher relays `SIGHUP`, `SIGINT`, `SIGQUIT`, and `SIGTERM` addressed to it into that group. For a direct foreground invocation with no process-group peer, it transfers controlling-terminal ownership to the target and restores it during cleanup. If a pipeline peer shares the foreground group, terminal ownership remains with that group.

## Implementation

- Add a blocking `kqueue` root waiter for direct-root exit, launcher signals, and explicit owner-side supervision wakeups.
- Keep descendant observation and crash-manager cleanup separate. Observer and manager-monitor completion now trigger an `EVFILT_USER` wake instead of relying on timeout polling.
- Treat a gated root that exits before release as normal retirement so its signal-derived status is preserved. Other startup-gate write failures retain the existing error cleanup path.
- Update the architecture, sandbox-supervision documentation, and documentation maps for the implemented ownership boundaries.

The process-group and terminal behavior is public. The root-waiter and manager-monitor coordination is internal and does not change the MCP worker-generation lifecycle.

## Validation

- `scripts/test cli/sandbox_supervision cli/sandbox_crash`
- `scripts/check`

The public transcript coverage exercises launcher-addressed `SIGINT` with an out-of-group descendant, single terminal-generated interrupt delivery, pre-readiness terminal interrupt status preservation, terminal ownership with a foreground peer, terminal revocation, exit-status preservation, and descendant retirement. The foreground-peer, terminal-close, and pre-readiness interrupt cases use causal event or FIFO gates and identity-aware cleanup.

## Intentional limits

This remains macOS-only. Stopped and continued job state is not proxied, so `Ctrl-Z` followed by `fg` remains unsupported. General shell-pipeline job control is also outside this change, although the launcher does not take terminal ownership when a live peer already shares its foreground group. The existing post-spawn observation boundary for a descendant orphaned before either observer sees its fork is unchanged.

title: Make transcript checks reliable under concurrency
description:
## Summary

High-parallelism transcript runs could fail when tests inferred worker, relay, or response state from short wall-clock windows. Managed R resolution could also use pak's five-second subprocess startup limit, which is too short when the host is oversubscribed.

This change replaces those scheduler assumptions with causal checkpoints and gives pak's asynchronous resolver subprocess a 60-second startup allowance.

## User-facing changes

- Managed R requirements no longer fail only because pak's resolver child takes more than five seconds to report readiness under host load.
- MCP inputs, outputs, and lifecycle semantics are unchanged.

## Internal changes

- Publish fixture markers atomically and observe them with kqueue, FIFO, sideband, and process-state checkpoints.
- Gate stdin ownership, idle input, completion, replacement startup, partial frames, and relay retirement before asserting their results.
- Replace Python and R poll-count assumptions with public input boundaries or worker-private FIFOs.
- Verify that the pak startup timeout overrides an inherited value and start a fresh poll before releasing a blocked automatic resolver.

## Notes

The complete transcript suite passed with 32 jobs on a 16-core macOS host. `scripts/check` also passed.

title: Add Python integrations for chatlas and other LLM clients
description:
Add Python integrations for chatlas and other LLM clients so existing applications can use persistent MCP Console sessions. Applications retain ownership of their chats, model clients, agents, configuration, and tool loops.

`MCPConsole` and `AsyncMCPConsole` provide synchronous and asynchronous Python calls. Product submodules provide explicit SDK tool adapters, native MCP registration helpers, and a single server entry for caller-owned thread configuration. Tool adapters use the connected server's MCP schema and description directly, including configured languages and requirement availability. OpenAI Responses and native MCP paths preserve images. Examples cover synchronous and asynchronous use, registration on existing chats and agents, and receiving a response from the thread SDK. Python 3.11 or newer is required; framework dependencies are optional extras.

The implementation delegates transport cleanup to MCP 2.2 and synchronous access to AnyIO. Python types use the standard library; SDK registration does not infer schemas from the clients' Python annotations. Public acceptance tests compare the full adapter schemas with the connected server and invoke the adapters through the SDKs, using both clients in direct and sandboxed execution. Wheel checks exercise clean Python 3.11 and 3.14 consumers. Python sources ship with the executable and sandbox bundle and participate in the wheel cache key.

The dependency refresh switches the default R environment and CI prewarming to CRAN reticulate. SQL previews preserve Unicode when MCP starts R in the C locale, with a public regression covering headers, cell values, and escaping.

title: Add Docker Sandbox compute enforcement through sbx
