description:
Add `target.compute.kind: docker_sandbox` with `sandbox.provider: compute`, so users select Docker Sandboxes in project configuration and run `mcp-console serve` normally. Console constructs argument arrays for standalone `sbx v0.42.1`; both relay and worker execute inside an owned microVM. The MCP server and recording writer stay on the controller. This execution path never discovers, verifies, installs, probes, or invokes the native companion.

- Require a prepared digest-qualified template, an existing absolute VM workspace, and explicit same-path read/write or read-only shares. Each generation uses the captured template identity; restart discards VM-local changes and preserves shared files.
- Accept only `provider`, `environment`, and `inherit_environment` under compute-provider `sandbox` configuration. Reject native restrictions, `extends`, and `--writable-root`. Docker owns its existing policy and inherited host integrations; Console does not change global settings. `serve --no-sandbox` retains the microVM and Docker policy.
- Keep runtime selection inside the VM and use preinstalled packages. Disable managed resolution, omit and reject `requirements`, and preserve workload environment controls without applying them to the controller's SBX process.
- Retire the exact owned VM through forced removal and structured listing confirmation. Failed transport, controller loss, and blocked output enter the same cleanup path; uncertain creation or retirement blocks replacement.
- Record provider, template, VM identity, workspace, and share access separately from controller recording paths. Document that shares can expose metadata and recordings. Add the complete configuration reference, a Linux shell template recipe, and an explicit OCI export/import utility.

Internally, share the existing Docker ownership/process/runtime mechanics through `target_launch` and keep SBX commands and output decoding in its adapter. The target bootstrap advances to protocol 3, requiring matching Console builds at execution targets; the relay protocol is unchanged. A separate commit restores Python's saved main-thread attachment before normal worker exit, preventing a DuckDB extension shutdown crash exposed by the real VM restart test.

Validation passed on macOS 26.6.2 arm64 with sbx v0.42.1: `scripts/format`, targeted tests, and the full `scripts/check`, including 47 Rust tests, applicable public transcript tests, and source/wheel installation checks. New coverage includes 13 real VM cases, six fake CLI race/error cases, and three public CLI configuration cases. Real probes verified binary non-TTY stdin/stdout, separate stderr, EOF, exit status, cancellation, and execution-transport loss. Runtime coverage includes mixed R/Python/SQL, images, input, polling, interrupt, restart, native/resolver sentinels, shares, and cleanup barriers. Global policy and unrelated-resource listings were identical before and after testing.

All SBX cases ran. The full suite reported 21 capability skips for Linux-native/ELF/procfs cases, fault-signal prerequisites, unsupported-platform checks, and an unconfigured external SSH fixture. Existing local, SSH, ordinary Docker, native-policy, and `--no-sandbox` paths were exercised. Linux SBX controllers remain unvalidated. Daemon unavailability was injected at the CLI boundary without stopping the shared daemon; actual host/daemon/owner-helper failure recovery remains outside the tested guarantees. Registry publication and organization/credential integration experiments were not performed. Hosted CI has not been verified.

title: Sandbox Windows dependency preparation through MXC
description:
Windows dependency preparation currently runs package installers, build hooks, and executable runtime inspection with host permissions. Run preparation through the pinned MXC companion by default, including R-backed and Python-only environments, late dependencies, and DuckDB extensions. Preparation requires no administrator privileges, custom profiles, or custom firewall rules. Unavailable or failed MXC stops preparation; explicit `--no-sandbox` retains host execution.

Support applicable `resolver.sandbox` settings independently of agent permissions. Defaults preserve host reads while limiting writes to dependency caches and private temporary storage, with downloads through the managed proxy. Host extension caches use an absolute `USERPROFILE` when Windows `HOME` is absent or relative. Preserve explicit filesystem and network restrictions, and reject unsupported settings, including explicit `allow_local_binding: false` with an MXC proxy.

Reuse the existing launch, policy, proxy, and retirement owners, preserving cancellation, descendant cleanup, accepted requirements, cache ownership, and running-session state after failed late preparation. Adapt preparation Rscript read/search checks with native file operations, use renv copies, and resume uv once after its specific optional-junction failure and confirmed cleanup. Pin the companion's Windows system-DNS proxy fix, add public enforcement and lifecycle regressions, and update the owning documentation and configuration example.

Companion change: [t-kalinowski/cobox#60](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/cobox/pull/60). The pin targets that source commit without requiring a merge.

title: Add native Windows sandbox support
description:
Windows local sessions currently require `--no-sandbox`. This integrates the native Windows runner so Console can launch sandboxed R and Python sessions, enforce filesystem policy, and confirm descendant retirement before restarting a session or deleting its private storage.

This PR is stacked on #338 (`windows-no-sandbox`) and includes the latest main merge. The companion runner commit is published at [t-kalinowski/cobox@6a18b21c2e](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/cobox/commit/6a18b21c2e75a10229a842424403d71cbd1e60ef) on `mcp-console/sandbox-runner/rust-v0.154.0`.

## Changes

- Bundle and verify the pinned runner plus both Windows helpers during source and wheel builds; serialize packaging with native checkout locks.
- Add explicit `sandbox-setup` / `--status` commands. Default sandbox launches require elevated setup and fail closed when it is missing. An explicitly selected restricted-token backend supports network-enabled workloads with host reads.
- Pass native policies and private temporary storage to workers, allow restricted tokens to use the private relay pipes, and preserve the runner's confirmed Job-retirement receipt through shutdown and restart.
- Document Windows setup, policy limitations, storage ownership, and validation; add public sandbox acceptance tests.

## Validation

- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passed.
- `cargo test --all-targets --all-features`: 34 passed.
- `python scripts/validate_runtime_sources.py` passed; `python tests/architecture.py`: 4 passed.
- `uv build --wheel --out-dir target/windows-wheels` passed; installed the fresh wheel in an isolated environment.
- `python tests/windows.py -v` against that wheel: 42 passed, including all seven sandbox tests. One generated relay fixture was blocked by host Application Control (4551); the affected `WindowsConsole.test_restart_after_forced_relay_retirement` test passed on a targeted retry.
- `scripts/format` ran unchanged before each commit: Ruff and Rustfmt passed; Yamark was blocked by Application Control and Air was unavailable.

The documented native Windows validation ladder was used; Unix `scripts/preflight` / `scripts/check` are unavailable on this host. Elevated sandbox and network-isolation acceptance still need a provisioned machine; this host has not run the explicit UAC setup. Linux/macOS coverage is left to CI.

title: Add native Windows sandboxing and managed R/Python environments
description:
Adds native sandbox execution and managed R/Python dependency resolution to the existing experimental Windows x64 runtime.

- **Sandboxed local sessions and standalone commands.** `mcp-console serve` now supports the default native sandbox on Windows, and `mcp-console sandbox -- COMMAND...` can run standalone workloads. `mcp-console sandbox-setup` explicitly provisions Console-specific accounts and network rules through UAC; `--status` checks readiness without provisioning. Missing setup produces guidance instead of falling back to unsandboxed execution. `serve --no-sandbox` remains available.
- **Windows policy and lifetime enforcement.** The default elevated backend enforces filesystem and network restrictions. An explicitly selected `restricted-token` backend supports write restrictions without account provisioning, but requires enabled networking and host reads. Sandboxed workers receive private temporary storage through `TMPDIR`, `TEMP`, and `TMP`. The native runner confirms that workload descendants have exited before a replacement generation starts or private storage is removed; unconfirmed cleanup blocks replacement. Relay pipes now work under restricted tokens.
- **Managed dependencies with the shared session semantics.** Windows invokes the existing hidden `mcp-console resolve` subcommand, with `ir` and `uv` doing environment materialization on the host. Sessions support requirement declarations, automatic requests when missing imports or R package loads are reached, compatible live additions that preserve state, and requirement changes as part of a restart. Failed restart preparation preserves the current worker and accepted declaration. Explicit Python selections continue to use preinstalled packages; R can use preinstalled packages when no resolver bootstrap is available. Tool descriptions expose managed requirements while omitting Windows-inapplicable SQL guidance.
- **Owned host preparation.** Resolver children enter kill-on-close Windows Jobs before executing, and preparation completes only after confirmed descendant cleanup. Interrupt terminates the active resolver Job; otherwise it requests cooperative interruption of the worker. Dependency preparation remains a trusted host operation outside the worker sandbox. Embedded R resolver programs run from temporary script files to preserve multiline source on Windows.
- **Build and installation support.** Update the pinned native companion to `t-kalinowski/cobox` and bundle the Windows runner plus its setup and execution helpers, with digest verification before use. Windows wheel builds stage the bundle automatically; direct Cargo builds require staging first, and companion builds require CMake. Cargo keeps immutable bundles so rebuilding does not overwrite helpers used by running sessions. Staging supports long Windows paths and preserves unchanged artifact timestamps.

Windows SQL and SSH/Docker/Docker Sandbox controllers remain unsupported; startup does not prepare DuckDB extensions. Windows sandbox managed proxies and custom cleanup timeouts are also unsupported. Windows wheels can be built locally, but this PR does not add them to published release artifacts.

Acceptance coverage adds real R/Python environment materialization, resolver failure and cancellation, descendant cleanup, sandbox write policy and temporary storage, helper verification, repeated staging, and rebuilding while helpers are running. Existing bootstrap tests also assert retirement using host process identities, and R/SQL fixtures avoid initializing unused Python converters.

Validation completed on `7b67b251`:

- Native Windows: `scripts/preflight`, `scripts/stage-sandbox-runner`, and `scripts/check --full` passed, including 55 checkout acceptance tests, 55 installed-wheel tests, and two source-install tests.
- Linux (WSL2): `scripts/check` and focused SSH, bootstrap/restart, and preparation-retirement regressions passed.
- Automated sandbox execution covers restricted-token mode plus setup/status diagnostics. Elevated account provisioning and offline-network enforcement require separate interactive administrator validation; they are not covered by these runs. macOS was unavailable locally.
- `scripts/format` ran before commits; Ruff, Yamark, and rustfmt completed, but Air was unavailable. Unrelated formatter output was discarded, and `git diff --check` passed.

title: Require MXC for sandboxed Windows execution
description:
Windows sandboxed execution now requires MXC. This removes legacy provisioning and automatic backend selection while enforcing the same restriction for sessions, standalone sandbox commands, and complete native policies at the Console-facing runner boundary.

User-facing changes:

- Unsupported hosts and policies fail before user code runs. Explicit `serve --no-sandbox` remains available; there is no automatic host fallback. Complete Windows policies cannot select legacy backends or `external-sandbox`.
- `allow_local_binding` accepts `auto`, null, true, or false. Omission and null select auto after normal file and CLI layering, including when null overrides an earlier boolean. Resolved configuration exposes the concrete boolean. Unix defaults are preserved; Windows managed proxies enable binding under auto and reject explicit false. The R configuration API follows the same contract.
- `sandbox-setup`, backend selectors, persistent state-directory controls, and provisioning scripts are removed. Removed settings are rejected without compatibility aliases.
- Existing legacy installations receive a startup diagnostic directing administrators to a one-time cleanup procedure covering accounts, credentials, firewall/WFP state, and persistent ACLs. The credential-protection guard remains intact. Launch never deletes machine resources.

Internally, Windows staging and installation require only the MXC companion executable, retaining artifact identity checks and main's runner pin and working-directory fixes. Legacy helper packaging, account/ACL provisioning, and retired backend tests are removed from CI and release consumer workflows. Working-directory alias regressions remain under MXC. Concurrent resolver fixtures use their own writable state, and startup cancellation coverage waits for the recovered result before admitting another cell.

Windows acceptance probes MXC through a real public launch. Only the explicit unavailable-runtime diagnostic permits skipping native execution cases, which activate automatically on capable runners. Configuration, integrity, unavailable-MXC and legacy-account diagnostics, migration, and explicit host-execution checks still run. Native coverage retains R, Python, SQL, permissions, interruption, restart, descendant retirement, and private-storage cleanup. Proxy coverage makes allowed and denied HTTP, CONNECT, and SOCKS requests to controlled endpoints. A separate administrator fixture verifies the narrowly scoped WFP migration script. Set `MCP_CONSOLE_TEST_REQUIRE_MXC=1` to require native coverage locally.

Windows dependency preparation still runs with host permissions, including downloads, installation hooks, and cache writes. Moving preparation into MXC remains separate work.

title: Reuse installed R fixtures across execution modes
description:
Automatic R activation tests installed the same immutable local packages separately for direct and sandbox execution. Profiling the reached-package case measured 5.3–6.5 seconds of package installation per execution, while real `ir` base resolution took only 0.30–0.35 seconds.

Retain installed fixture packages for the case process, which runs both execution modes sequentially. Each execution still creates fresh library views, resolver records, checkpoints, and runtime state; packages become available only through activation. The cached `TemporaryDirectory` owns cleanup when the case process exits. There is no persistent fixture cache.

This is an internal test-fixture change with no user-facing runtime changes. Real `ir` base resolution, all existing scenarios/assertions/snapshots, the multilingual smoke selectors, command profiles, transcript concurrency, checkout ownership, and CI coverage remain unchanged. The development guide distinguishes focused activation work from real-resolver integration.

On the same 16-core macOS arm64 host, using default concurrency, both execution modes, and warm build/dependency caches, three complete command runs per variant measured:

| Selector                                                   | Before median (range) |  After median (range) |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------: | --------------------: |
| `test_r_automatic::resolves_reached_r_packages_at_runtime` | 23.47 s (22.14–23.87) | 18.50 s (18.25–20.75) |
| `test_r_automatic`                                         | 49.79 s (47.69–57.60) | 39.28 s (36.60–55.12) |

Both median reductions are about 21%. All fixture preparation is inside the command timer; each new command installs its own packages, and only the second execution mode reuses them. Other worktrees were active, so the overlapping suite ranges should not be read as a guaranteed speedup. Initial checkout staging/build work was measured separately.

The automatic-R suite and four real-`ir` acceptance cases passed all 36 direct/sandbox executions with unchanged snapshots. These retain ordered discovery and activation, cumulative requirements, redundant-resolution avoidance, persistent R/Python/SQL state, error fidelity, cancellation, and restart. Temporary instrumentation verified unchanged package-file hashes, ten fresh execution environments, and process-exit cleanup across all five fixture-backed cases.

The ordinary `scripts/check` passed, including the unchanged multilingual smoke gate. A separate incremental edit-and-check cycle added a temporary Rust source comment, ran the same gate, and restored the source: 29.90 seconds overall, including an actual 11.59-second release rebuild. First-use fixture installation and the real package-loading/activation steps remain the focused-loop costs; no build-system tuning was needed. The exhaustive local gate was not run.

title: Record workspace configuration values as YAML nodes
description:
The workspace-options transcript stores `configuration` as a YAML mapping, making native option values directly readable and structurally comparable. The test retains the mapping and serializes it only when writing the configuration file.

Document when to use each representation: YAML nodes for payload values; serialized JSON when quoting, escaping, or literal argument and stdin preservation matters. A temporary audit of 610 YAML files identified 181 strings that parse as JSON; this converts the three workspace configuration values. This changes test representation and guidance without changing public behavior.

title: Fix the R direct-stdin restart test race
description:
The direct-stdin R callback can start while the worker is idle, so its file checkpoint does not prove that the server has accepted the next cell. Restart can overtake that send, causing the test to fail with `[worker is restarting]`.

Wait for the cell's `[running]` response before requesting restart, assert the complete restart response to verify that EOF releases the callback and the submitted cell does not run, and regenerate the transcript snapshot. This changes test synchronization only; Console behavior and public interfaces are unchanged.

title: Simplify transcript test support
description:
## Summary

After the suites were organized by process boundary, their shared machinery still lived in oversized support and harness modules. This change makes that machinery easier to find and modify while preserving the transcript-oriented test system and its captured behavior.

- Splits the shared support module into explicit modules for clients, snapshots, normalization, checkpoints, capture, processes, macOS inspection, assertions, runtimes, and resolvers.
- Keeps boundary-specific launch and capture mechanics in local `_harness.py` files, with scenarios and assertions in their owning suites.
- Consolidates duplicate FIFO, JSONL capture, process cleanup, result inspection, and Darwin process helpers.
- Moves scripted relay, worker proxy, and native interposer implementations into searchable fixture files.
- Extends the runner with component-wise recursive discovery, mechanical snapshot paths, `--locate`, and orphan snapshot detection.

## User-facing changes

None. Production CLI and MCP behavior are unchanged.

## Developer-facing changes

`scripts/test --locate BOUNDARY/SUITE[::CASE]` now prints the source definition and primary snapshot path without running the case. Collection reports snapshots that no longer match a suite or case. Existing selectors, direct suite execution, update behavior, companions, skips, parallel execution, and slow-test reporting remain available.

## Internal changes

Boundary suites now import only the support responsibilities they use. Large native and Python fixture bodies no longer obscure harness mechanics, and the repository test map documents where shared helpers, boundary harnesses, scenarios, and fixtures belong.

## Validation

- `scripts/check`
- Exact ordered selector comparison with `main`: 357 selectors
- All 360 snapshot files byte-identical to `main`
- All extracted native fixture variants compiled with their original build options

title: Update rmcp and support MCP 2026-07-28 negotiation
description:
## Summary

- update `rmcp` from 2.2.0 to 3.1.4
- migrate the manual tool handler and transcript recorder to RMCP 3.x response and request-metadata types
- preserve the stable transcript schema while RMCP adds or removes `resultType` on the wire according to the negotiated protocol
- add a public stdio regression covering Codex's legacy `2025-06-18` initialize lifecycle and the optional `2026-07-28` discovery lifecycle

## Compatibility

RMCP continues to negotiate legacy initialize clients, including Codex's current default protocol, while advertising and accepting the latest MCP protocol through `server/discover`. The regression also verifies that `2025-11-25` remains advertised.

## Testing

- generated and formatted the updated lockfile and Rust sources
- added `tests/protocol_versions.rs` for both protocol lifecycles
- full repository checks run in CI

title: Require format checks before commits
description:
## Summary

- Require contributors to run `scripts/format` and review its changes before every commit.
- Make formatting verification part of the documented development workflow so unintended formatting changes are caught earlier.

## User-facing changes

- Updated contributor instructions in `AGENTS.md`.

## Internal changes

- No implementation or runtime behavior changes.

title: Consolidate runtime tests and reduce repeated setup
description:
Reduce overlapping tests and repeated runtime startup while keeping representative sandbox integration workloads.

Console runtime behavior is unchanged. Development tooling adds `scripts/test --stress` for the three allocation scale cases with their original workloads and ceilings. Linux and macOS CI run both the functional and stress profiles, preserving the allocation regressions as merge gates. Explicit case and suite selectors retain their scope.

- Consolidate seven overlapping requirements, SQL binding/connection, and Ragnar cases, and remove superseded tests and snapshots.
- Run 49 ordinary cases in one execution mode. Preserve mode-dependent coverage, distinct no-R bridge scenarios, and every sklearn/joblib workload in both modes.
- Reuse host dependency caches in isolated startup-plot fixtures, shorten the synthetic-clock fixture deadline while preserving causal gates, and exercise architecture guards without repeated source-tree copies and Python process launches.
- Include the profile module in copied MCP-client runner fixtures and refresh the macOS writable-roots transcript.

The diff removes 270 lines overall.

A single warmed macOS comparison with six workers measured 22m 02s for the baseline full transcript profile and 19m 31s for the functional profile. Running the functional and stress profiles sequentially took 21m 29s. Both full measurements included a stale snapshot failure.

Local macOS verification passed `scripts/preflight`, `scripts/format`, `scripts/check`, `actionlint`, all 21 MCP-client tests, the 71 transcript-runner tests with 13 Windows-only skips, all three allocation stress cases, and the refreshed writable-roots case. Hosted Linux and Windows verification remains pending.

title: Separate MCP admission tests from package preparation
description:
`validates_send_arguments` prepared tidyverse and started a real worker just to check MCP argument errors. Separate that integration work from the admission loop while preserving the exact errors and validation precedence through the public `send` interface.

The admission cases reuse the existing custom worker and resolver sentinel. Rejected requests retain real R, Python, and SQL source. The custom worker executes ordinary Python for the state and stdin probes and records every evaluation; the transcript records the submitted code and actual output. The main case checks rejection before startup and with a live worker, asserting no submitted code runs, dependency preparation starts, worker restart or interrupt occurs, or rejected stdin reaches a later cell. The sentinel permits version discovery and records every other resolver invocation as a failure.

`requirements/test_r::prepares_with_empty_stdin_then_restarts` retains the preparation → repeated preparation with empty stdin → preparation-plus-restart sequence together, using `praise` and `zeallot`. Direct and sandboxed executions verify real package availability, state preservation during live preparation, and state reset with retained requirements after restart. `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` gives separate admission and preparation/lifecycle commands and records this ownership.

This changes tests, their snapshots, and development guidance only. There are no public runtime changes. The canonical handshake matrix, smoke selectors, existing direct/sandbox executions, command semantics, and full CI coverage are unchanged.

Elapsed command times on the same Apple M4 Max, macOS 26.7 machine, comparing `7432aa20` with `967cbaf1`:

| Command / cache state                                                                          | Before          | After           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | --------------- |
| `scripts/test client_server/server/test_tools::validates_send_arguments`, empty `IR_CACHE_DIR` | 9.89 s          | 0.87 s          |
| Same focused command, two warm runs                                                            | 2.05 / 1.96 s   | 0.91 / 0.85 s   |
| `scripts/check`, two warm runs                                                                 | 16.77 / 18.70 s | 21.30 / 16.65 s |

Timers include fixture setup, dependency preparation, command startup, and build checks. The empty-cache baseline required a new R environment; shared package/download caches were warm, so this is not a cold-download measurement. The admission case leaves the empty cache untouched. The first baseline gate took 68.38 s with initial checkout build setup and is excluded from the warm comparison. Attempts refused by the host validation lock are excluded.

The focused warm loop uses about 56% less elapsed time. Default-gate timings varied: real-runtime transcripts took 10.5–14.6 s and core checks took 4.7–5.3 s. Both final gate runs passed on the committed revision with the same 19 smoke executions as the baseline, including actual R, Python, SQL, persistent state, mixed-language recording, and native sandbox coverage.

The nine focused admission/preparation cases passed in all 15 declared executions, including the existing causal standalone-preparation, initial/live R preparation, and custom-worker R/DuckDB restart cases. All four formatters passed. The full local gate was not run; CI retains its full checks.

title: Format embedded test programs and group related arguments
description:
Add missing Yamark language hints to embedded R and Python test programs, and indent their contents and closing delimiters consistently within the surrounding Python code. Regenerate the affected transcript snapshots, including the Linux writable-roots snapshot.

Keep related arguments together after formatting: pair SSH options with their values in separate `.args()` calls, and group each R diagnostic line in `cat()`. Add repository instructions for language hints, indentation checks, argument grouping, and platform-specific snapshot updates.

Include the output of `scripts/format`, including YAML example formatting, and clarify that quoted and unquoted profile identifiers have the same meaning. Console behavior, public interfaces, SSH arguments, and diagnostic output are unchanged.

title: Document SSH preparation and cover uv bootstrap without ir
description:
Follow up #300 by replacing the remaining preinstalled-only SSH descriptions with the implemented remote preparation contract. The docs distinguish the required remote R installation and resolver bootstrap from dependencies prepared on demand, retain bare-runtime fallback, and locate trusted resolver configuration on the execution host. They also correct the documented launch-envelope version and selected-environment field, linking to `docs/SSH.md` for details.

Add one real OpenSSH acceptance scenario for R and `uv` without `ir` on the initial remote PATH. In both direct and sandboxed modes, it records the real `uv tool run --from r-lib-ir ir` bootstrap and verifies lazy discovery, explicit `praise` and `humanize` preparation and use, remote cache paths, and untouched controller traps. The fixture isolates `UV_TOOL_DIR`, preserves other PATH tools, and disables synthetic recorder settings. Production code is unchanged.

On macOS, `scripts/format`, the new acceptance case in both execution modes, all available cases in `client_server/requirements/test_ssh`, `client_server/server/test_ssh`, and `client_server/server/test_ssh_policy`, and the core checks passed. Snapshots were generated with `scripts/test --update`.

Two `scripts/check` attempts stopped in unchanged tests: `server_crash_retires_the_worker_generation` timed out waiting for a macOS reaping event, and `restart_discards_unactivated_r_candidate` timed out waiting for its activation checkpoint. Both cases passed when rerun in the focused checks; neither test nor its production implementation changed. Source and wheel installation checks passed separately via `python3 tests/install.py`. Linux-specific and configured external-SSH coverage were unavailable locally.

title: Separate test requirements and sandbox contracts
description:
Separate sandbox contracts from ordinary runtime, protocol, and lifecycle tests while preserving the existing boundary ownership. This prepares the suite for subsequent platform work.

Cases declare capability requirements beside their definitions, with platform availability and skip reasons centralized in test support. Shared execution fixtures run ordinary cases directly and sandboxed against the same snapshots, including core detection and multiprocessing. Security and supervision retain explicit sandbox coverage.

Verify each complete initialization exchange against its mode's reference before abbreviating it, including multiple sessions in one case. Runner regressions cover selection, skip reporting, shared snapshots, handshake differences, and retention of skipped snapshots during updates.

Internal test and documentation changes only; public runtime behavior is unchanged. Linux runtime implementation, kernel compatibility, and Rust configuration changes remain outside this PR.

title: Stabilize timing- and cache-sensitive transcript cases
description:
## Summary

Several transcript acceptance tests depend on one observation timing or one IR metadata-cache state even though the console behavior is unchanged. This PR makes those cases deterministic through public console interactions and explicit transcript normalization while preserving their response assertions. It also separates lazy custom-worker startup from a bounded shutdown regression so runner load does not consume the shutdown checkpoint.

## User-facing changes

None. Runtime behavior, MCP schemas, and worker and relay protocols are unchanged.

## Internal changes

- Poll past a provisional `[stdin needed]` response before checking the final R browser result, while keeping short timeouts explicit at the managed-input and Python debugger call sites that need them.
- Keep the submitted R idle callback alive after fd 0 closes, so failed preparation exercises the expected force-stop path without discovering or signaling private worker processes from the test.
- Replace cache-dependent IR progress with a visible placeholder after verifying the complete security diagnostic, and record that replacement as structured transcript-normalization metadata.
- Start the custom worker through a completed public call before applying the detached-stdin checkpoint. The two-second shutdown bound remains unchanged and no longer includes lazy worker startup.
- Regenerate two goldens to record the submitted R fixture and the explicit IR normalization. The client-visible failure responses remain unchanged.

title: Cover the reticulate package declaration and import workflow
description:
Add a transcript for the reticulate workflow of declaring a package with `py_require()`, importing it, and using it through both R and Python. It declares `py-yaml12` before Python initializes and adds `more-itertools` after Python is running.

The change adds public workflow coverage in direct and sandboxed modes and a generated transcript snapshot. The case clears the caller's `RETICULATE_PYTHON` selection to exercise the managed environment. Its scope is limited to tests and snapshots.

Validated locally:

- `scripts/test client_server/requirements/test_python::declares_imports_and_uses_python_packages` (direct and sandboxed, including with `RETICULATE_PYTHON` set to a fresh virtual environment)
- `scripts/check` (core checks and smoke transcripts)

title: Cover scikit-learn parallel workflows in the sandbox
description:
Scikit-learn model selection with `n_jobs=-1` previously failed when joblib queried the macOS semaphore limit. #126 added the required `kern.sysv.semmns` permission, and the pinned native runner retains it. The existing regression covered a small joblib pool but did not exercise scikit-learn workflows.

Add a public MCP transcript that automatically installs scikit-learn after Python startup, then compares parallel and serial results for a preprocessing pipeline and histogram-gradient-boosting grid search, random-forest cross-validation, and permutation importance. The input exceeds joblib's default memory-mapping threshold. Run the same case directly and inside the sandbox. Require at least two effective joblib CPUs, cap the workload at two, and assert that the Console worker selects two jobs. A runner regression verifies that a one-CPU host skips both execution modes.

Document that these workflows support `n_jobs=-1` in the default sandbox. Joblib is added to the test runner dependencies for the capability check. There are no production runtime, sandbox-policy, or application-dependency changes.

title: Synchronize shutdown poll ownership before competing request
description:
## Summary

[Ubuntu CI](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/36009306668/job/107665561232) observed the competing zero-timeout poll collect the text/image/text output and running banner instead of the busy banner. The shutdown test had waited for worker output processing, then submitted two poll requests without proving which request claimed the evaluation. The pending poll now supplies a one-byte fixture token. Zod observes that token and acknowledges poll ownership before the test submits the competing request.

## User-facing changes

No runtime behavior changes. The two shutdown snapshots now record the fixture's `stdin: p` poll request. Their responses remain exact: the pending poll delivers collected output with the completed-cell result or stopped-worker notice, and the competing poll receives the busy banner.

## Internal changes

The Zod shutdown fixture consumes the poll token and emits an ownership checkpoint. The test waits for that checkpoint before sending the competing poll. The existing completion and EOF gates, bounded shutdown check, and once-only output checks remain in place.

title: Distinguish cancelled transcript cases from failures
description:
When a transcript case fails, the runner interrupts unfinished siblings but reports those expected interrupts as additional failures. Label cases observed to exit with SIGINT after cleanup was requested `cancelled`, and keep them out of failure aggregation while preserving their captured output, including errors interrupted during cleanup.

Case deadlines, interrupts observed before cleanup, and other unsuccessful exits remain failures. A concurrent independent SIGINT can receive the same cancellation label because the exit status does not identify its sender. This changes developer-facing runner diagnostics; MCP behavior and test execution are unchanged.

title: Restore sandbox workflow coverage
description:
## Summary

Follow #205 by restoring coverage for sandbox-dependent workflow compositions whose interaction is a distinct failure mode. This adds public acceptance coverage for R core detection, failed-worker replacement that retires `processx` descendants before the replacement is used, abrupt server-loss cleanup of a detached worker generation, and inherited ignored-`SIGCHLD` exit-status preservation.

Runtime behavior is unchanged.

## User-facing changes

- None. Existing `parallel::detectCores()` support and crash cleanup through `mcp-console serve` now have public regression coverage.

## Internal changes

- Restore four public or CLI transcript cases with stable snapshots.
- Exercise worker failure and server death through the built-in runtime and existing process-identity helpers, without restoring the deleted interposer fixtures.
- Map specific sandbox allowances to their motivating workflows and owning tests.
- Document that separate tests can replace a combined test only when their interaction is not itself a plausible failure mode.
- Keep the PyTorch/libomp allowance's missing workflow owner explicit for a follow-up decision.

title: Simplify CLI sandbox supervision tests
description:
## Summary

Follow #204 by simplifying the direct CLI and public MCP sandbox supervision suites around observable contracts instead of component-specific timing and failure-injection permutations. The scoped suites now contain 24 tests and snapshots, down from 59, while retaining command fidelity, job control, exit and signal behavior, security restrictions, bounded teardown, descendant retirement, startup gating, supervisor-loss diagnostics, and all three worker launch paths.

This reduces the scoped Python boundary source from 4,869 lines to 2,123 lines and removes two native interposers plus unused fixture operations. Product behavior is unchanged.

## User-facing changes

- None. Direct sandbox output, exit status, signal behavior, filesystem and network restrictions, descriptor closure, startup errors, and worker-replacement diagnostics retain snapshot coverage.

## Internal changes

- Consolidate argument and executable-name variants into one labeled snapshot matrix.
- Replace the R-specific host-write case with a language-independent read-only-host and writable-temporary-directory contract.
- Keep representative normal cleanup, forced cleanup, supervisor loss, terminal ownership, and descendant-retirement cases.
- Merge the three identical MCP descriptor snapshots into one labeled matrix that still executes the built-in worker, custom worker, and custom relay/worker paths.
- Remove manager, launcher, observer, owner-monitor, PID-reuse, and process-group fixture operations that no retained contract uses.
- Document the CLI and public MCP sandbox ownership split in the boundary README.

The scoped Python boundary source is 56.4% smaller by lines and 62.2% smaller by bytes. Test functions and snapshots both fall from 59 to 24, a 59.3% reduction. The directly coupled descriptor, startup-marker, and native-interposer fixtures fall from 1,238 to 149 lines.

title: Show complete tracebacks in Matplotlib transcripts
description:
## Summary

The Matplotlib transcript test replaced complete Python tracebacks with short placeholders before writing its golden. This made the transcript differ from the text returned to MCP clients.

This PR records the complete traceback for both the failed cell and the failed plot render.

## User-facing changes

The golden transcript now shows the exact traceback frames and error messages that an MCP client receives.

## Internal changes

The test no longer rewrites response text before snapshotting it. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

title: Skip unchanged Python distribution inventories during live activation
description:
Live Python dependency activation repeatedly walked installed wheel file inventories even when the candidate retained the same distribution versions. On native Windows, canonicalizing about 8,500 paths took 4.5–4.6 seconds per compatibility check; one ordinary managed-Python selector did this three times.

Check the candidate version before reading a distribution's file inventory. Changed or removed versions still use the original canonical file-ownership check, including namespace contributions and loaded-version rejection. Resolution, interpreter checks, activation, cancellation, and cleanup remain unchanged. The original getter-only optimization was reverted after its measured savings proved modest; #584's sandbox cache fix is preserved.

The public regression uses real uv resolution and local fixture wheels. It first verifies that a transitive upgrade of a loaded distribution is rejected without running bundled code or changing the accepted declaration, worker PID, or live object. It then uses a Python audit hook to reject reads of the unchanged distribution's RECORD during compatible preparation, and verifies that the added package works in the same interpreter. This test fails on the unoptimized baseline. The ownership condition also keeps activation traceback coordinates unchanged, preserving the full frames and messages. No existing snapshots or execution modes changed; the only new snapshot is the portable regression transcript.

Measurements on native Windows used merged main `5cbce817` for both revisions (only the production optimization was removed for the before binary), a staged companion, debug binaries selected through `MCP_CONSOLE_TEST_BINARY`, `--jobs 6`, Python runner 3.13.16, managed Python 3.12.15, R 4.6.1, uv 0.12.24, and the same already-warm dependency caches, without clearing or relocating them between revisions. Each case retained fresh sessions, workspaces, configuration, and mutable environments. Compilation and the temporary tracing runs are excluded from these measurements.

| Focus repetition | Before elapsed (s) | After elapsed (s) | Before aggregate worker (s) | After aggregate worker (s) | Executions each side |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1 | 66.237 | 50.341 | 254.884 | 166.784 | 6 passed, 0 failed/unstarted |
| 2 | 69.526 | 49.031 | 266.058 | 165.498 | 6 passed, 0 failed/unstarted |
| 3 | 65.491 | 49.228 | 248.303 | 166.108 | 6 passed, 0 failed/unstarted |
| Median | 66.237 | 49.228 | 254.884 | 166.108 | 18 passed per revision |

Median elapsed time fell 25.7%; aggregate worker time fell 34.8%. Earlier matched repetitions on main `608d77bb` measured 23.2% and 32.8%, respectively; the table repeats the comparison after merging latest main. These are distinct measures, and this is a selected-cohort result, not a claim about whole-suite speedup. Temporary tracing on the initial `608d77bb` base identified the unchanged compatibility routine. The same traced selector still executes four real uv preparations, three compatibility checks, one frontend, and three workers. Each check now canonicalizes 131–137 paths and takes 0.082–0.089 seconds. Resolver subprocesses themselves were generally only 0.2–0.5 seconds; another download cache was not the measured bottleneck. Temporary tracing was removed. The single-case traces separate the remaining work: fixture copying was about 0.036 seconds, frontend creation 1.04 seconds, initialization/discovery 0.012 seconds, first Python evaluation 2.3–2.5 seconds, ordinary SQL/state assertions 0.015–0.031 seconds, restart/crash replacement evaluations 0.64–0.76 seconds, and finish/cleanup about 0.019 seconds. Each live preparation fell from 6.24–6.46 to 1.75–1.84 seconds, with the compatibility scan accounting for the difference. The profiling hook added an evaluation and consequently shifted a traceback ordinal; those instrumented transcripts were excluded from validation and snapshot updates.

The initial complete Windows transcript baseline attempted all 300 available executions: 293 passed, seven failed, zero unstarted (1,486 unavailable mode/capability selections). Elapsed transcript phase was 729.829 seconds; aggregate worker time was 3,890.409 seconds. Python was the largest family (1,910.98 worker seconds / 117 executions), followed by requirements (854.62 / 42), SQL (484.47 / 29), R (334.27 / 40), and server (198.99 / 31). The seven failures involved plotting and the shared managed peer case; they are reported, not treated as savings. Both available joblib executions passed in direct mode; their declared execution modes and the sklearn sandbox workloads are unchanged. Windows skips the POSIX-only sklearn case and shared Seatbelt/bubblewrap modes; hosted checks supply that coverage. All selected focus cases passed in every uninstrumented repetition.

The highest case totals in that baseline were relative uv path capture (91.34 worker seconds), managed startup/restart (87.94), idle package additions (87.90), reached imports (75.11), and retaining automatic additions after import errors (73.04). The focused cohort includes the three live-addition cases from this group, plus mixed Python/SQL additions, peer replacement, and ordinary Python requirements. Startup/cold-cache behavior remains in the full suite rather than being consolidated or bypassed.

Reproduce the measured cohort from the repository root with these six selectors, repeating the same command three times per binary:

```powershell
$env:R_HOME = 'C:/Program Files/R/R-4.6.1'
$env:LC_ALL = 'C'
$env:UV_PYTHON = '3.13'
$env:MCP_CONSOLE_TEST_BINARY = (Resolve-Path target/debug/mcp-console.exe).Path
$runner = (Resolve-Path .dev-workflow/python-dev/Scripts/python.exe).Path # Python 3.13.16
$cases = @(
  'client_server/python/test_without_r::adds_python_packages_to_idle_managed_worker'
  'client_server/python/test_without_r::resolves_reached_import_in_managed_worker'
  'client_server/python/test_without_r::combines_live_python_and_duckdb_additions'
  'client_server/python/test_without_r::retains_automatic_additions_after_import_errors'
  'client_server/python/test_peer_runtime::shared_managed_bootstrap_and_replacement'
  'client_server/requirements/test_python::declares_imports_and_uses_python_packages'
)
& $runner scripts/test --jobs 6 @cases
```

Use `scripts/with-checkout.cmd cargo build` to build each debug revision, then keep the executable fixed for its transcript runs. Timing comes from the existing workflow transcript phase and per-execution timing records, not total build/test command duration. Existing Windows capability selection chooses direct mode for these cases; the new regression declares direct and sandboxed modes and uses the same capability selection.

A clean-cache check passed all five selected executions (the four no-R cases plus the regression), with zero failed/unstarted, in 43.956 seconds elapsed / 179.815 seconds aggregate worker time on final merged main. It used new directories for `UV_CACHE_DIR`, `UV_TOOL_DIR`, `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, `IR_CACHE_DIR`, `IR_LIBRARY_ROOT`, R cache/data, renv, and package caches; managed Python 3.12.15 was freshly installed. The test-runner environment was already bootstrapped. HOME and the caller's tool environment were preserved. This is a cold-start validation, not a before/after comparison.

Local validation on final head `270d7335` (merged main `5cbce817`):

- `scripts/preflight` passed the required inventory; its Windows companion probe is declared unsupported, while the native companion was staged and exercised by acceptance.
- `scripts/format` unchanged: Ruff, yamark, rustfmt, and air passed. Incidental line-ending-only output was restored. No existing snapshot changes remain.
- `scripts/check`: core checks (runtime sources, architecture, rustfmt, Clippy, all Rust tests) and all 102 native Windows acceptance tests passed.
- Full transcript phase: `uv run --python <bootstrapped Python 3.13.16> --script tests/boundaries/_run.py --full --jobs 6`, through the existing checkout owner and workflow `Run.phase`, with the fixed debug executable. All 302 available executions passed, zero failed/unstarted; 1,497 unavailable mode/capability selections were reported. Elapsed phase 627.349 seconds; aggregate worker time 3,315.005 seconds. All seven initially failing baseline selectors passed. This full run is validation, not a matched speed comparison: main changed and the initial full baseline had failures.
- Final merged focused check: six cases plus the regression, seven passed, zero failed/unstarted.
- Local review complete on the final merged head: five files, production diff seven additions/seven deletions; regression and existing coverage preserve resolver execution, lifecycle handling, and execution modes.

Hosted results are separate from local Windows validation. On previous head `0991699c`, Linux and macOS each finished with seven failed selectors and zero unstarted selectors: four were activation traceback line shifts, now corrected without snapshot edits; three were upstream long-poll handshake-description differences. Linux recorded 1,721 passed / seven failed executions; macOS recorded 1,764 passed / seven failed executions. The new regression, loaded-version/namespace protection, and sklearn/joblib workloads passed in both direct and sandboxed modes on both platforms. The source-type archive fix (#591) and SQL fixture wait fix (#589) have since been merged from main.

On final head `270d7335`, [Windows CI](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37945016214/job/113868930868) passed companion archive restoration and artifact validation, then failed the upstream `DevelopmentTests.test_windows_ci_source_archive_round_trip`: its temporary checkout lacks `scripts/restore-source-timestamps`, which the workflow now calls on a cache hit. This reproduces locally when GNU tar is available on the child PATH; the ordinary caller PATH declares the case unavailable. Neither the workflow nor that development test is changed by this PR. Hosted installation coverage is blocked by this failure, while the local ordinary Windows gate and complete transcript run passed. Documentation passed. At 11:13 EDT, current-head Linux was running transcripts and macOS had started setup; their final results remain pending and are not claimed as passing coverage. CI status checks used a ten-minute watch interval. Local review is complete and the PR is ready for review. No reviewers requested; no merge.

title: Verify the release resolver trust boundary
description:
Startup configuration capture preserves uv values, while selected wrappers, configuration files, package inputs, and explicitly writable caches can still affect later preparation. This PR adds nine public acceptance cases for OSS-79 to verify that those effects stay within the existing native resolver permissions and that target containment applies before native constructors execute.

The cases cover replacement of uv and ir wrappers, mutable uv configuration and wheel startup code, a real source-package build backend, poisoned Python startup in an explicitly writable cache, constructor write denial, executable and filesystem aliases, and rejection of the companion's external-mode selector in public configuration. Probes require actual filesystem denial and rejection of an unapproved download with fresh managed-proxy evidence, followed by successful permitted preparation. Fixtures declare their capabilities and isolate Console home while preserving `HOME` and unrelated host tool settings. Trust fixtures exclude the entire inherited `UV_*` namespace and proxy settings before adding their own uv configuration. A resolver-side sentinel and representative invalid caller settings exercise that rule without maintaining a catalog of uv variables.

Public runtime behavior, production permissions, resolver selection, and the companion pin are unchanged. Replacement launchers preserve interpreter paths containing spaces. Trust fixtures resolve selected uv/ir paths before changing directories and exercise relative caller `PATH` entries. Restricted native startup derives the compiled target's Linux loader and library directories. Internal changes add acceptance fixtures and snapshots, retain Unicode recording paths with a directory identity check, initialize SQL preview dependencies explicitly, and normalize the specific Server 2025 warning from unused ONNX startup code. Linux child observation restarts after task disappearance to include reparented children and fails explicitly after ten interrupted scans. Result, identity, and descendant-retirement assertions remain intact.

The resolver documentation links a bounded release audit with supported contracts, intentionally trusted installation effects, unsupported claims, and evidence at Console base `28b9ee4a` and companion pin `85d407d8`. No permission-boundary breach was demonstrated. Focused macOS acceptance, native Linux procfs probes, formatting, and the ordinary `scripts/check` gate pass. Release validation is pending passing CI for the final PR head and resolver checks on the final release candidate on macOS/Linux with its verified companion pin.

Tracks [OSS-79](https://linear.app/t-kalinowski/issue/OSS-79/verify-the-release-resolver-trust-boundary).

title: Use release builds for integration tests
description:
Use release builds for transcript and integration tests. In two local macOS ARM64 comparisons, this reduced the 1 GiB retention case from about 74 seconds to 5 seconds and aggregate test CPU time by 17–18%. Full-suite wall times varied, so these measurements do not establish the exact CI speedup.

`scripts/test` now builds and selects `target/release/mcp-console`. CI uses the release executable for the R package and installed-wheel checks, and prebuilds only the debug Rust test targets. The transcript step matches the wheel build’s incremental setting to reuse its release artifacts. Rust unit tests remain in debug with assertions enabled. The runner fixtures and development guidance follow the release path, with a regression that checks the public test command still builds and uses release when a stale debug executable is present.

This changes development and CI execution only; console behavior and transcript snapshots are unchanged.

title: Refine sandbox workflow coverage
description:
## Summary

Follow up on #208 by making its restored sandbox coverage observe the lifecycle and execution boundaries it claims. This removes timing-dependent checks around worker and server failure and makes the Quarto compatibility case execute through the public sandbox launcher.

## User-facing changes

None. Runtime and sandbox behavior are unchanged.

## Internal changes

- Wait for the manager to record the exact detached `processx` child before crashing the worker.
- Register process-exit and reap watches before killing the MCP server, use manager exit as the cleanup barrier, and then wait for each exact generation process to be reaped.
- Prewarm `ir` resolution on the host, then render the generated QMD through `mcp-console sandbox` and assert the sandboxed output.
- Update the workflow-ownership documentation and Quarto snapshot to state this boundary explicitly.

## Notes

This addresses the follow-up review threads on #208.

title: Simplify top-level test harnesses
description:
## Summary

Remove the duplicate top-level Rust test harnesses and incidental meta-tests so each retained contract has one primary boundary owner. Public protocol, CLI, sandbox, resolver-lifetime, and bare-runtime behavior now lives in focused Python transcript snapshots.

This removes a second MCP client and its process harness, replaces the Rust transcript-runner harness with three direct Python cases, and stops pinning release workflow layout. Product behavior is unchanged.

## User-facing changes

- None. Protocol negotiation, long multibyte transport, unsupported-platform errors, sandbox escape restrictions, bare-runtime behavior, and resolver descendant cleanup retain public snapshots.

## Internal changes

- Add the contract ownership rule to the boundary README.
- Make the transcript runner report snapshot failures from completed sibling cases while it cleans up a parallel failure.
- Keep one representative release smoke timeout at the evaluation-response boundary.
- Require `py-yaml12>=0.2.0` for the transcript runner. Regeneration removes the optional `...` document terminator from 157 existing snapshots without changing their YAML values.

title: Reorganize Python tests by boundary and behavior
description:
## Summary

Reorganizes the Python acceptance tests around process boundaries and behaviors so the suite is easier to browse and extend.

- Moves suites from `tests/transcripts` to `tests/boundaries` while preserving the four existing boundaries.
- Splits large modules into focused behavior modules, with shared code kept in boundary-local `_harness.py` files.
- Moves snapshots to `tests/snapshots` in a hierarchy parallel to the test modules.
- Updates the runner, CI cache inputs, documentation, and selectors for the new paths.

## User-facing changes

None. Runtime behavior, fixtures, test function names, collected cases, and captured coverage are unchanged. Snapshot content changes are limited to relocated `!same-as` reference paths.

## Internal changes

The suite now has 53 normal Python test modules. Every normal module is below 40 KB, and selectors reflect the nested behavior paths.

## Validation

- `scripts/check`
- 354 cases before and after
- 357 snapshots compared after normalizing the relocated canonical reference, with no missing, added, or changed snapshots

title: Respect uncaught Python cell exits
description:
Uncaught `SystemExit` from a main-thread Python cell now terminates the worker, including `sys.exit()` and exits raised by called library code. Console reports CPython's actual exit status and message, loses the old R and Python state, and starts a usable replacement worker. Explicitly caught exits preserve state; background-thread exits end only that thread.

The evaluator lets uncaught cell exits reach CPython's existing exit handler. Internal adapter, service, and plot cleanup exceptions retain their handled boundary. Runtime inspection checks the two additional CPython symbols used by this boundary. Public transcripts and runtime documentation describe the behavior.

Validation:

- Public regressions failed before the production change in sans-R and R-backed sessions. Fresh release builds passed. Final-head non-update focused validation passed 37 executions: 17 direct, 17 sandbox, and three startup cases. Coverage includes stock-Python status/message comparisons, state loss/replacement, caught and background-thread exits, handled plot cleanup, SQL dispatch/restore, automatic-import isolation, Python-version rejection, and R's existing exit lifecycle.
- Stock interactive Python and script subprocess probes agreed for omitted/None/zero, integer, string, and noninteger exit values.
- `scripts/check` passed its ordinary core and smoke gate: 46 Rust tests and 19 smoke executions. Full core validation also passed all 111 repository-tooling/client/architecture tests, runtime-source checks, Rust formatting, and Clippy.
- `scripts/check --full` failed in `client_server/output/test_previews::combines_old_worker_and_replacement_cell_under_one_budget` (direct mode: expected worker checkpoint file was not created). It completed 274 passing transcript executions; 14 executions were canceled, and installation checks were not reached. Final-head isolated direct and sandbox executions both passed, as did both executions with the ordinarily installed pre-correction wheel whose production tree matches main `614971d4`. The ordinarily installed baseline also passed its entire owning preview suite. The custom-worker fixture bypasses the changed embedded-Python paths; its full-run failure has not been independently reproduced with ordinary baseline installation. This remains a failed full gate.
- Separate source and relocatable wheel installation checks passed (two tests). The ordinarily installed final wheel also passed four public exit/replacement executions: direct and sandbox, with and without R. Ubuntu hosted CI passed for `7c93edbd`. [macOS CI failed](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/36788683305/job/110136607034) at `closed_input_cancels_discovery_with_blocked_stdout` with `discovery survived MCP closure`; [main `614971d4` failed the same case and assertion](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/36779719367/job/110107043352). Its fixture and startup implementation are unchanged by this PR.
- A separate full snapshot-update run timed out at `client_server/server/test_startup::cancelled_cell_is_not_replayed_after_discovery` with its five-second response timeout. That case passed in isolation. No unrelated snapshot drift was retained.
- Ruff, Yamark, rustfmt, Air, and full diff review passed; `scripts/format` is unchanged. Current-head code and security reviews completed with no findings and a fresh thumbs-up for `7c93edbd`.

title: Stabilize output checkpoints and compact stress evidence
description:
Large synthetic outputs make transcript diffs difficult to review, and cancellation tests need to observe the response-write boundary deterministically.

This changes test evidence and synchronization only; Console behavior is unchanged. Response cancellation uses an explicit write checkpoint, and pipe-tail fixtures establish a known retained prefix before filling the pipe. Stress tests check the complete response before recording exact repetition strings and counts, preserving every byte and every stress iteration.

The SSH failure snapshot shrinks from about 1.22 MB to 5 KB. Its deletion accounts for nearly all of this PR's 1.24 MB patch. This is the preparation layer for bounded response rendering and streaming collection.

Incremental diff: 10 files, +225/−370; no production changes.

title: Test R segfault recovery with a native memory fault
description:
Replace the R segfault transcript's signal trigger with a C fixture called through `.C()`. The fixture performs a volatile read at address `1` so the fault originates in runtime code and reaches R's default segfault handler.

The transcript captures the handler diagnostic, native-call traceback, crash menu, abort, and worker replacement in direct and sandboxed modes. It also checks that the replacement loses the old session state.

This changes test fixtures and transcript coverage only. The public interface and runtime implementation are unchanged.

title: Test ordered relay retirement
description:
## Why

PR #106 established an ordered relay retirement contract, but the public server-relay suite did not directly cover shutdown ordering around a blocked host resolver or late operation results after the retirement marker.

## User-facing changes

- None. This PR adds regression coverage only.

## Internal changes

- Drive blocked resolver cancellation and late R preparation through the public MCP surface with a scripted relay and fake `ir` resolver.
- Use FIFO checkpoints to establish shutdown, preparation, and retirement order without sleeps or Rust-only test hooks.
- Verify that late preparation results are consumed without retaining their R candidate, reporting failure diagnostics, blocking restart, or dropping drained output.

title: Add idle Python thread transcript
description:
## Summary

Python threads launched by `send()` already continue after the launching cell returns. Add public boundary test coverage for execution between cells and collection of background output by empty `send()` polls.

## User-facing changes

- Records that a Python thread remains alive while the runtime reports `[idle]`, then finishes and leaves its state available to the next Python cell.
- Checks that an empty `send()` poll returns `hello from background thread` after the launching cell has completed.
- Makes no runtime behavior changes.

## Internal changes

- Uses a release file and worker-private start and completion files to prove the thread runs between cells without timing-dependent synchronization in the test harness. Cleanup releases the thread before closing the client when an assertion or checkpoint fails.
- Runs the case in direct and sandboxed modes and adds the corresponding MCP snapshot in the boundary test layout.

## Validation

- `scripts/test client_server/python/test_matplotlib_cache client_server/python/test_runtime::runs_python_thread_while_idle`
- `scripts/test client_server/python/test_runtime::runs_python_thread_while_idle`
- Injected failures after launch, at the start checkpoint, and at idle polling in direct and sandboxed modes.
- `scripts/check`

title: Add ragnar R and SQL integration transcripts
description:
## Summary

Add transcript coverage for creating a ragnar store from R and querying its DuckDB data from SQL. The cases exercise just-in-time R and DuckDB extension preparation and capture the current sandbox, connection, and catalog boundaries through the public MCP tools.

## User-facing changes

There are no runtime interface or behavior changes. The new transcripts document the supported `ATTACH` and `USE` workflow and the errors an agent encounters before applying it.

## Internal changes

- Add an end-to-end transcript for live ragnar, FTS, and VSS preparation, persisted index creation, read-only attachment, and SQL retrieval.
- Add a guide-style troubleshooting transcript covering sandboxed store paths, incremental extension preparation, multiple ragnar connections, R replacement-scan name collisions, the getter-only SQL connection, and attached-catalog FTS lookup.
- Normalize transient DuckDB progress output and trailing display padding in transcript snapshots.

## Validation

- `scripts/test sql::queries_a_ragnar_store_created_in_r`
- `scripts/test sql::uses_ragnar_like_the_guide_and_adapts_to_the_console`
- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `ruff format --check tests/transcripts/sql.py`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --all-targets --all-features`

The full SQL transcript suite was also attempted, but an unchanged existing case stopped during startup when cold IR resolution could not fetch `github::rstudio/reticulate` in the test environment.

title: Compact repeated test preparation and output collection
description:
Selection and attachment tests repeatedly install the same R fixture, render the same reference plots, and run an unrelated evaluator battery. Reuse immutable preparation within each case process and keep complete evaluator acceptance in its parity and standalone owners. Every scenario still gets its own worker, workspace, environment view, mutable R-home overlay and cleanup.

Public runtime behavior and the full configuration matrix are unchanged. Internal test support shares complete copied installations, exact output collection and cancellable checkpoint waits. Native macOS/Linux marker waits use filesystem/process events; the portable Windows backend uses bounded path polling with socket cancellation. The lifecycle harness shares this mechanism. SQL preparation-failure coverage waits for exact stdin output and completion before the next cell, preserving its waiting-state and withheld-input assertions. Cold Docker callback startup keeps an explicit client-sized completion/transport budget. Cold preparation and confirmed retirement use explicit phase budgets; raw delivery, cancellation, input and native registration boundaries retain their assertions. Test-only changes outside the boundary suites include `tests/mcp_client.py` and `tests/transcript_runner.py`; portable discovery checks are separate from POSIX process tests.

The original controlled before/after pair showed a **42.69-second full-suite reduction (5.3%)**:

| Measurement               |     Before |      After | Reduction |
| ------------------------- | ---------: | ---------: | --------: |
| Full wall time            |    801.54s |    758.85s |      5.3% |
| Summed execution work     | 22,977.41s | 21,659.94s |      5.7% |
| Serial schema prelude     |      9.90s |      9.27s |     0.63s |
| Passing execution records |      1,441 |      1,441 | unchanged |
| Capability skips          |         81 |         81 | unchanged |

Both runs used the same release executable (`f34493e9…`), companion, transcript-runner dependencies, warm caller download caches and unchanged **32 jobs**. Cold-preparation cases kept private fresh caches and environments. The inventories retain all **928 selectors** and matching execution/configuration records. The 15-launch serial schema matrix is unchanged; its timing difference is incidental variation.

The before run is `a4650685` with core collection/synchronization repairs backported (`6b1ddae6`, run `20261001-203503-9t77jiph`), retaining the old repeated fixture installs, reference rendering, evaluator batteries and installation copies. The after run is `91891894` (`20261001-215629-vmwsx3b4`). Later Matplotlib and Python-without-R completion fixes are present only in the candidate, so the measured difference includes those test fixes. These full figures use one complete successful run per revision and remain sensitive to machine/load variance. Aborted runs are excluded from timing calculations and their failures remain documented.

The most recent full run, on `ad060236` (`20261002-084105-7124k8cl`) passed in **846.59s**, with **24,206.51s** summed execution work, **1,439** passing execution records and **83** capability skips. This is 45.05s (5.6%) longer than the original baseline, so it does **not** reproduce the earlier whole-suite speedup. The optional external-SSH host was unreachable; exactly its two execution records account for the inventory difference, with no additional exclusions or changed configurations. The timing evidence supports reduced preparation work and the scoped speedups below; it does not establish a consistent whole-suite improvement.

Three warm one-job samples across nine selected cases, including both execution modes, reduce summed per-case medians from **165.16s to 119.37s (27.7%)**. Peer improvements range from 5.4% to 50.2%; sampled SQL timings are essentially unchanged.

Across six peer cases, R fixture installs fall **14 → 5**, independent plot renders **4 → 1**, evaluator battery cells **110 → 0**, and MCP sends **262 → 152**. Console sessions remain **24**. The representative SQLite case copies the complete installation once instead of twice, with the same two sessions and eight sends. Worker launches were not instrumented separately.

| Compacted work                      | Surviving coverage                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Evaluator batteries                 | Complete byte-for-byte parity and R-independent standalone owners, direct and sandbox; selection probes retain executable **and prefix**, module identity, bootstrap count, children, no reactivation and bridge continuity across all five venv configurations |
| Early R fixture and reference plots | All five callers; real `.onLoad`/`.onAttach`; both plot triggers; both system-default-package initialization orders; independent PNG byte checks before normalization                                                                                           |
| Copied installations                | Complete executable, companion and license layout; private HOME, extension caches, site-packages and activated environments; cold extension, restart and crash contracts retained                                                                               |
| Collector and checkpoints           | Exact deltas/errors, text-before-completion, stdin/running state, one source submission, multipart rejection; bounded reader rendezvous, early release, peer exit, generation scoping and descriptor ownership                                                  |
| Repeated Python success plumbing    | 52 exact output comparisons share the existing collector; original cells, setup/selection assertions and state transitions retained                                                                                                                             |
| Runner fixtures                     | Real cancellation, descendants, GIL, cleanup and exit status; portable discovery, selection and formatting                                                                                                                                                      |

The serial tools/list prelude retains all seven direct/eight sandbox configurations and canonical reference ordering. Complete schema stability is checked after explicit preparation in its requirements owner. Recovery counts (512/1024), allocation ceilings, concurrency and real SSH deadlines are unchanged.

Line deltas: boundary tests **−221**; support/fixtures **+200**; tooling self-tests **+469**; snapshots **−495**; authoring instructions **+9**. Total **−38 lines**. Acceptance tests and shared helpers shrink by **21 lines**; all test source grows by 448 lines because tooling tests add adversarial collector/checkpoint, cancellation, cold-budget and executable-selection proofs.

Validation passed in phases: full core at `6faa5c2f` (53 runner and 15 client tests, architecture, formatting, clippy and Rust checks); full unscoped transcripts at `91891894`; then exclusive source/wheel installation at `91891894` in 81.90s. Revision `ad060236` also passed `scripts/check`, all 53 runner, 24 workflow and 19 client/helper tests, plus two real contention groups at 32 jobs (88 and 105 passing execution records). Four new regressions cover marker cancellation, late nested/portable markers, owner exit and the actual Docker case's cold budget with a scripted client. Focused red/green checks, repeated real contention groups at 32 jobs, genuine load/attach failure injection and normal snapshot regeneration passed. The 47-row coverage ledger records each consolidation's invariant, owner, configurations, operations and evidence.

The exact stdin-completion regression passed in a scripted replay of its actual public case, including delayed consumption, fragmented text and one input submission. At `a27f438f`, the affected real case passed from a clean tree in **18.86s** (direct **8.76s**, sandbox **9.78s**). The same source passed all **38** SQL execution records at 32 jobs in **53.47s**, all **19** client/helper tests in **18.07s**, formatting, and `scripts/check` in **26.61s**. Snapshots and timeouts are unchanged. The full suite was not repeated for this two-file repair; the whole-suite measurements above belong to their stated revisions. Hosted Linux validation of this head remains pending.

An unchanged runtime race remains unresolved: a concurrent control-only interrupt can return `worker evaluation is already being polled` while the original send still owns the evaluation wait. Controlled baseline run `20261001-214748-ekamzb1t` reproduced it in `python/test_without_r::automatic_resolution_failure_and_cancel_keep_accepted_state`. The raw regression and exact assertions remain; a production ownership fix is outside this PR. The final passing candidate run does not resolve that failure.

Windows, a physically R-free host, Linux-specific native boundary paths, Docker and SBX were unavailable locally. Hidden-R capability discovery and actual standalone acceptance passed in both execution modes. Real R, mixed initialization orders, Python-backed SQL, native macOS sandbox and localhost SSH ran. External SSH contracts passed in the original comparison; the host was unavailable in the most recent full run. The portable marker backend ran in helper tests on macOS, which does not validate an actual Windows host. Real Docker remains unvalidated locally.
