- Collect the live Python package-preparation cell through the existing polling helper. Submit its code and stdin once, then assert the complete output across running/input-request responses. A zero observation timeout reproduces the old assertion failure; the regenerated snapshot only adds that timeout field.

The R import warning reproduces with `loadNamespace("ellmer")` alone: ellmer 0.5.0 imports `:=` from both the pinned development S7 and rlang. Document this upstream limitation in the installation notes and track it as RC-1 in `docs/TODO.md`; the warning remains visible and is not fixed by this PR.

Validated on native Windows 11 with MXC, based on latest main at `71585d0`:

| Validation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `python scripts/check --full` | Passed: 42 Rust tests; tooling/architecture checks; 405 shared functional cases; wheel and source installation |
| Native source and installed-wheel acceptance | Each: 110 passed, 1 host skip; new CMD regression passed in both |
| Copied `uv` command / source reinstall | 3 / 4 tests passed |
| GNU-tar archive regression | Passed separately; combined tooling coverage is 70 passed, 97 platform skips |
| `python tests/website.py` | 22 passed on the final tree through a diagnostic wrapper |
| `R CMD build` / `R CMD check --no-manual` | Status OK: 278 passing expectations, 4 Windows skips, 1 upstream ellmer warning |
| `python scripts/format` / `git diff --check` | Passed; all formatter reports inspected |
| Exact-pin companion release contracts | 33 passed, 0 skipped with `MCP_CONSOLE_SANDBOX_REQUIRE_MXC=1` |

The website and CMD regressions failed before their fixes. The Python regression passed after snapshot regeneration and again in the full concurrent suite without `--update`. One website render on the refreshed base stopped during pkgdown before assertions without a diagnostic; a fresh diagnostic rerun passed all 22 tests.

Unavailable coverage: this profile has no 8.3 alias; four R tests require Unix shell fixtures; 97 tooling tests require Unix fixtures; shared capability filters exclude 887 whole cases and unavailable modes of another 229 executed cases. `python scripts/test --stress` reports all three allocation-scale cases unavailable because their native fixtures require macOS/Linux. These exclusions do not represent MXC skips: Console ran with `MCP_CONSOLE_TEST_REQUIRE_MXC=1`.

[Exact-revision cobox CI passed](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/cobox/actions/runs/39134405782), including its optional-MXC Windows job. Local companion validation covered the required-MXC release variant. Debug/Bazel variants were not run locally, and the optional-host CI result does not satisfy the prerequisite for hosted required-MXC validation.

title: Statically link the Windows MSVC runtime
description:
The published Windows wheel imports `VCRUNTIME140.dll` without bundling it, so Console can fail before startup unless the Visual C++ Redistributable is installed separately. Enable `+crt-static` in Cargo's Windows/MSVC target configuration for native builds, PEP 517 wheels, and source installs.

- Public changes: remove the separate redistributable prerequisite from getting started and release guidance. Preserve MSVC/Windows SDK/CMake source-build prerequisites and MXC capability rules.
- Internal changes: audit actual normal and delayed PE imports in every bundled executable/DLL/PYD and installed bundle. Reject redistributable VC runtime DLLs while allowing Windows system libraries and UCRT. Exercise the audit with compiled normal-import, delayed-import, and static PE fixtures.
- Preserve interpreter behavior across separate CRTs: dispatch interrupts through the active system-UCRT handler, retaining its module and existing publication/retirement barriers. Search beside the selected absolute Python DLL for Python's supplied dependencies, retaining normal fallback directories and component identity checks. Cover Python-only operation, both R/Python initialization orders, blocking sleeps, native SQL, and runtime-DLL provenance.

The published 0.0.5 wheel fails the new regression on Console's normal `VCRUNTIME140.dll` import. The final wheel's Console imports only `api-ms-win-core-synch-l1-2-0.dll`, `bcryptprimitives.dll`, `kernel32.dll`, `ntdll.dll`, `user32.dll`, and `userenv.dll`. The companion has no redistributable VC runtime import before or after; both executables have empty delayed-import tables. Microsoft's `dumpbin` independently agrees. Native C/C++ objects reference `LIBCMT` (`/MT`). The pinned companion, bundle digests, launcher transformation, and component identity checks remain intact. The interpreter bridge uses [Windows' system UCRT](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/windows/universal-crt-deployment?view=msvc-170).

`scripts/format.cmd` passed all four formatters. At clean head `1964d7725`, `scripts/check.cmd --full` passed with `MCP_CONSOLE_TEST_REQUIRE_MXC=1` and `PYTHON_CPU_COUNT=2` (four shared cases): tooling/core, 42 Rust tests, 109 native passes/one skip, all 398 applicable shared cases, public-tool smoke checks, installed-wheel acceptance, and four fresh source-install interoperability checks. The default 24-case run had one busy-worker response in a package-preparation test; the complete lower-concurrency rerun passed without snapshot or capability changes. The shared runner separately declared 1,561 platform/capability skips, including POSIX and Seatbelt/bubblewrap fixtures; native MXC execution actually ran.

Built the final artifact through `scripts/with-checkout.cmd uv build --wheel --out-dir dist`, audited every native member, installed it through `uv tool install --reinstall --no-cache`, and passed `python tests/windows_install.py --installed-binary PUBLIC_COMMAND` (12 executed, one profile-alias skip). The copied public launcher matches its audited environment launcher and independently has no VC runtime import. A rebuilt source archive contains the exact final Cargo configuration and runtime fixes.

The host has the redistributable installed, and no disposable Windows environment without it is available, so actual execution on such a host remains unverified. The profile-alias skip is because this profile has no 8.3 alias. Full import lists, artifact hashes, command logs, and revision-specific results are retained locally under `.dev-workflow/runtime-evidence/summary.json`.

title: Preserve Windows source types when restoring cached timestamps
description:
Windows CI on main fails before compilation when extracting the cached companion source changes the tracked `codex-rs/vendor/bubblewrap/LICENSE` symlink representation, leaving Git status dirty.

Restore only source timestamps after verifying each archived file or link target against the fresh checkout. Preserve the checkout's existing files and symlink representation, the clean-source guard, archive digest, and Cargo cache identity. GNU tar still creates the source archive on a cache miss.

Validation:
- Reproduced the old workflow failure with a public regression running the actual PowerShell step; the fixed step passes for a symlink archive, a cache miss, and reuse of a generated GNU tar archive.
- `tests/release.py PortableReleaseTests` passes on native Windows and Ubuntu WSL, covering mismatched contents, invalid paths, and real symlink preservation without changing target files. Platform-specific cases skip on the other platform.
- `scripts/preflight` and `scripts/check` pass on native Windows and Ubuntu WSL (102 native Windows cases). `scripts/format` passed every formatter on Windows.
- `git diff --check` and `scripts/review-diff origin/main` pass.

The local Windows account cannot create real symlinks; WSL exercises that representation. CI remains the comprehensive merge gate.

title: Fix Windows CI source archive drive paths
description:
Windows CI fails before tests because GNU tar interprets the drive letter in an absolute archive path such as `D:/a/_temp/sandbox-source.tar` as a remote host. This affects the source timestamp cache introduced in #584, including [the Windows job on #586](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37866379555/job/113613969647).

Pass `--force-local` to both archive creation and extraction. Add a native Windows regression that executes the actual workflow step with GNU tar against an absolute drive path containing spaces, first with no archive and then with the saved archive. It verifies restored source contents and timestamps, identical archive digests, clean Git status, and exclusion of `.git` and Cargo build outputs. Update the CI cache contract in `RELEASE.md`.

Validation:

- The new public regression failed before the fix with `/usr/bin/tar: Cannot connect to C: resolve failed`.
- With Git for Windows GNU tar prepended to PATH, `python tests/development.py` passed all applicable cases: 6 tests, 1 Unix-only skip, including both cache miss and cache hit.
- `python scripts/preflight`, `python scripts/format` (all four formatters), and `git diff --check` passed.
- `python scripts/check` passed runtime-source validation, architecture tests, and Rust formatting, then stopped at Clippy because this fresh checkout has no staged private sandbox runner. Native runtime acceptance was not reached.

Hosted CI remains the comprehensive gate. No merge is requested.

title: Fix Windows uv tool sandbox startup
description:
On Windows, `uv tool install` copies `mcp-console.exe` into the public command directory. The native executable then derives its installation prefix from that copied location and cannot find its sandbox helpers: `sandbox-setup --status` fails, and a default `serve` session fails when its first worker starts.

Windows wheels now expose an installer-generated Python entry point that resolves and launches the native executable from the installed distribution's file manifest. The native executable remains under the environment's `libexec` directory with its verified companion bundle. The launcher forwards stdio and explicitly inherited worker handles, waits through console interrupts, and preserves all 32 Windows exit-status bits. Wheel and editable builds update entry-point metadata and RECORD consistently.

The installation regression now exercises the copied public command from an isolated `uv tool install`, including setup inspection, Python state/restart, stdio and exit status. Packaging coverage checks relocation, existing entry-point preservation, RECORD hashes and prepared metadata. Native-PID and bundle-tampering fixtures select the underlying native executable.

Validation on Windows x64:

- Reproduced the setup-status and worker-startup failures with the original wheel before the fix.
- `scripts/preflight.cmd --json` and `scripts/stage-sandbox-runner.cmd` passed.
- `scripts/with-checkout.cmd python tests/windows_install.py` passed: copied-command regression (3 cases), installed-wheel acceptance (76 cases, one provisioned-sandbox skip), and source-install startup (2 cases).
- Editable-install acceptance passed (5 cases), along with the Windows workflow checkout-ownership regression.
- Focused `scripts/test.cmd` packaging, tamper-rejection and full-width exit-status checks passed.
- `scripts/format.cmd` reported all formatters successful; `git diff --check` passed.
- `scripts/check.cmd` passed with R_HOME, LC_ALL=C and the existing provisioned sandbox: 38 Rust unit tests and all 76 Windows native acceptance cases.
- Reinstalled the host tool and verified a fresh default PATH `mcp-console serve` session executes Python and shuts down with exit 0 and empty stderr. R also passed with R_HOME set. An independent Luna agent confirmed the default installed session.

macOS/Linux validation and the exhaustive shared suite were not run locally; CI remains the comprehensive merge gate.

title: Expand Windows test coverage and fix runtime portability issues
description:
Windows full validation previously omitted every shared boundary case and the portable runner/client/release checks. This makes the full Windows workflow exercise applicable shared cases alongside native acceptance, with explicit capability declarations and platform snapshots that preserve Unix references.

User-facing fixes preserve Python subprocess stdio after R compatibility calls, refresh Joblib's interpreter after live activation, recognize Windows virtualenv metadata, and retain the selected Python environment and argument identity when R supplies forward-slash paths. Windows R now retains the full interactive startup arguments and emits plain UTF-8. Invalid R startup also shuts down without an unrelated resolver retirement timeout.

Internal changes add Job-owned shared case supervision, cancellable Windows pipe readers, portable R/Python/uv fixtures, and Windows references for differing schemas and diagnostics. The parent releases the command builder's child-side resolver pipe handles immediately after spawning, allowing failure cleanup to observe EOF while preserving the retirement barrier.

The Windows development and boundary guides explain supported validation commands, deferred SQL/remote-controller features, native policy coverage, and remaining Unix fixture debt. Idle R callbacks remain a runtime parity gap; those tests now declare that requirement explicitly. Stock Windows R child-launch fixtures account for 8.3 resource paths and the launcher's ANSI argument handling.

title: Extract native worker activity and bootstrap mechanics
description:
## Problem

Native command waits, stdin shutdown observation, and Linux process re-execution lived alongside shared worker dispatch and runtime state, obscuring which parts own platform-specific activity and startup.

## Fix

Extract worker-local Unix and Windows activity modules and a native bootstrap module. Keep serialized interpreter lifecycle and cell dispatch in the coordinator, and retain shared pending-command and shutdown state in the core. Preserve each platform's existing wait, interrupt, partial-frame, idle-callback, and sideband inheritance ordering.

## Validation

- Native Windows 11 x64: the same nine existing public console/relay cases passed before and after extraction.
- Unchanged `scripts/format`: Ruff, Yamark, rustfmt, and Air passed.
- Clean-commit `scripts/check --full`: core checks, 64 checkout tests, 64 installed-wheel tests, and both source-install tests passed.
- Sol MAX and Astra XHIGH read-only reviews inspected the complete diff and affected callers/tests at the clean final commit; both returned no findings. Root separately verified the native result record, which their sandboxes could not read.
- Hosted [CI run 37243521289](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37243521289): Windows full native validation passed; Ubuntu failed 69/915 transcript cases and macOS failed 69/943. Unix core checks passed.
- The exact [base CI run](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37239702308) has the same platform outcomes and failure totals: all 69 macOS failures and 67 Ubuntu failures recur in both runs. The two additional Ubuntu startup-delivery/probe failures remain separately unresolved. Unix CI blocks merge readiness pending prerequisite repairs.

title: Fix Linux startup race and Windows CI fixtures
description:
Standalone requirements preparation could return `[worker starting]` when `timeout_ms=0` expired during initial discovery, causing the Linux preparation regression to fail intermittently. Wait for connection-owned discovery for standalone calls and add a FIFO-gated public regression that reproduces the premature response.

Fix the Windows CI fixtures by keeping configuration round trips within supported native policy, retaining managed-proxy edit coverage on supported hosts, and joining stopping AnyIO pool threads before asserting the original thread inventory. The thread check keeps a five-second total budget and still fails for leaked resources.

Validation:

- Linux (Ubuntu 26.04 WSL, Python 3.13): `scripts/preflight`, `scripts/stage-sandbox-runner`, `scripts/format`, and `scripts/check` passed. The new FIFO-gated regression failed before the fix; its snapshot was generated with `scripts/test --update` and rerun without update as part of the complete startup and custom-worker requirements suites. The synchronous client suite and R configuration-workflow tests also passed.
- Windows (Python 3.13, R 4.6.1): staging, formatting, Rust core checks, the full R testthat suite, and all applicable synchronous client cases passed. `scripts/check` ran 102 native tests: 101 passed and the plotting case failed because the initial Python lacked `packaging`; that case passed after preparing an isolated environment with the required packages. A 100-connection cleanup probe also passed. The full Windows gate was not rerun after preparing that environment.
- Windows `R CMD build r` and `R CMD check --no-manual`: passed with `Status: OK`, including vignettes and the full installed-package test suite.

Full CI remains the comprehensive gate; no merge or release is included.

title: Cache pinned Windows sandbox builds in CI
description:
Windows rebuilt the pinned sandbox in every fresh CI workspace: run [37827327371](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37827327371) spent 13m59s staging it. The existing Windows cache omitted both the sandbox Cargo workspace and its complete staged bundle, and a later test failure skipped cache saving.

This PR keeps one CI-only pinned checkout at `.sandbox-runner-source` for initial staging and all wheel/source-installation hooks. It restores and saves:

- Complete `wheel-data/data` (three Windows executables, LICENSE and NOTICE) and `target/sandbox-runner-build.json`.
- The pinned checkout's actual `codex-rs/target`.
- The existing source timestamp tar convention, excluding Git metadata and Cargo outputs.
- Cargo downloads in the existing Unix-style separate cache, saved early; the Console build/dependency cache keeps its final save.

Completed outputs have no fallback restoration. Their exact key includes the source pin, pinned sandbox Rust toolchain, Windows target/architecture, runner OS/image family, UTC week, recipe version, staging/ownership inputs and `build.rs`. Build intermediates also include Cargo dependency inputs and the timestamp archive digest, preventing archive eviction from leaving a permanent mismatch with restored build mtimes. Compatible intermediate fallbacks run normal Cargo freshness checks. Staging is skipped only for exact output and intermediate hits; the existing `build.rs` pin/target/digest checks are forced before saving or using restored files.

All sandbox caches and downloads are saved after successful staging/validation and before provisioning or unrelated tests, with ordinary success conditions. Provisioning, `scripts/check.cmd --full`, wheel and source-install acceptance remain in place. Local/source staging always invokes Cargo. Linux/macOS, permissions and cache isolation are unchanged; no account, credential, ACL or provisioning state is cached.

Validation on native Windows x64 (Python 3.13.16, R 4.6.1, `LC_ALL=C`):

- `scripts/preflight.cmd --json`
- Public regression red/green in `tests/development.py`; key inputs, exact restoration, source sharing and successful save ordering checked.
- `scripts/test.cmd WindowsCargo`: fresh-checkout tar restoration reuses Cargo; ten invalid/incomplete staging cases rejected through public Cargo builds.
- `scripts/format.cmd`: ruff, yamark, rustfmt and air passed.
- actionlint 1.7.12 and Windows PowerShell AST syntax checks passed; shellcheck unavailable locally.
- `scripts/check.cmd --full` on the clean pre-rebase commit: all core gates and all 101 native Windows tests passed; shared transcripts finished 289/300 passing with 11 failures, so the command failed before installation. These affect unchanged configuration/R validation, joblib, setup/requirements and DuckDB traceback snapshots. Two configuration-discovery failures also occurred in the original hosted run; those two and both DuckDB snapshot failures reproduce with the CI source override unset. No unrelated snapshots were updated.
- `scripts/with-checkout.cmd python tests/windows_install.py` separately passed: wheel build, isolated tool install and three sandbox smoke tests, installed-wheel 101-case native acceptance, source reinstall and two startup-order cases. All three pinned sandbox executable timestamps/sizes stayed unchanged across wheel/source builds; wheel staging reused Cargo in 1.62s.
- Rebased onto current main (`cb5dd00a`, Windows startup fix) after the complete runs; `scripts/test.cmd WindowsCargo WindowsConsole.test_startup_without_processor_architecture` passed all three cases, and `scripts/with-checkout.cmd python tests/development.py` passed all four applicable cases (one platform skip). The caching implementation and fixtures are unchanged by the rebase.
- Local diff review completed before opening for review; four files, 107 added/8 deleted implementation/tooling lines, no runtime changes or snapshots.

| Measurement | Time |
| --- | --- |
| Previous hosted Windows staging, run 37827327371 | 13m59s |
| Local cold pinned sandbox target build/staging | 7m40s |
| Local fresh-checkout archive restoration (source, target and complete outputs) | 43.1s |
| Local normal warm staging after restoration; no sandbox crates compiled | 6.0s |
| Local restoration plus warm staging | 49.1s |

Local measurements used existing Cargo downloads and the installed pinned Rust 1.95.0 toolchain. Restoration used local uncompressed tar archives; Actions network/download/decompression and Cargo-download restoration overhead have not been measured. The sandbox target archive was 3.51 GB uncompressed. No claim is made about total workflow duration or hosted warm-cache performance.

title: Fix Windows and Linux acceptance regressions on main
description:
Recent main CI failed because acceptance fixtures and snapshots had fallen behind the current runtime, sandbox, and startup-status contracts. This repairs Windows cache-path coverage and Linux acceptance coverage without changing production behavior.

- Grant the provisioned Windows sandbox account read access to the test-owned virtual environment and cache probe, including private temporary-directory ACLs.
- Give Linux resolver fixtures scoped writable cache locations and declared home directories. Initialize socket-client normalization state, verify protected host metadata before accepting Linux's masked-directory errors, and observe completion before asserting policy outcomes.
- Use silent R loader warmup and consume the rejected early cell's diagnostic before retrying. Continue asserting that its code and bundled requirements are discarded and generation retirement remains confirmed.
- Regenerate configuration, stream/progress, dependency-phase, startup-closure, traceback, and tool-description transcripts through the public runner. Capture separate direct/sandbox transcripts where explicit sandbox grants change the policy description; preserve exact canonical-handshake comparison and complete diagnostics.

These are internal acceptance-test and snapshot changes only. There are no public API or production runtime changes. The branch includes main at `395913a3`; the review-requested retry-admission snapshot is regenerated and its thread is resolved.

Windows `scripts/check` passed all 89 native acceptance tests; the two cache-path cases also passed with private ACLs and short-path temporary storage. WSL Ubuntu `scripts/check` passed, along with the original 27 focused cases, all 11 subsequently exposed Linux regressions, and the writable-root lifecycle case. `scripts/preflight` and unchanged `scripts/format` passed on both platforms. Cold Console R-cache preparation initially exceeded smoke-test wait budgets; the final ordinary gate passed after trusted dependency preparation. The review-requested snapshot passed a hosted public red/update/green run. Further work is limited to Windows and Linux. Exhaustive and packaged-installation coverage remains with CI; hosted Windows diagnosis is still running.

title: Complete Windows setup help and acceptance snapshots
description:
The full Windows gate fails on latest main because three newly added tool-description acceptance cases have no Windows snapshots. Generate their declared win32 references through the public runner, preserving Windows's R/Python-only capability set and missing-runtime diagnostics.

Also carry the previously requested sandbox-setup explanation onto main. Its earlier PR #531 merged into fix/windows-native-runner-upgrade after that parent had already been merged, so the help/output change has not reached main. Short/long help and successful setup list local accounts, their group, network rules, and protected directories; status JSON and provisioning remain unchanged.

Validation:
- Reproduced all three missing-snapshot failures on the latest-main branch; generated references using scripts/test.cmd --update, then reran the owning suite without update successfully.
- scripts/format.cmd ran unchanged; all four tools passed.
- scripts/check.cmd --full passed with configured R_HOME, LC_ALL=C, and explicitly provisioned Windows state: 38 Rust tests, all 88 checkout native cases, all 211 applicable shared cases, copied-command acceptance, all 88 installed-wheel native cases, source reinstall, and both startup smoke cases. Provisioned-account tests passed in checkout and installed-wheel runs.

This branch starts at origin/main 09f8c921, fetched before branch creation. Platform-inapplicable Unix/SQL cases retain their declared skips.

title: Fix Windows R discovery through batch launchers
description:
Windows hosts using rig's `R.bat` launcher were treated as Python-only even when R was installed. Discover `R.exe`, `R.bat`, and `R.cmd` in PATH order and invoke the selected launcher to capture the R installation. Preserve explicit `R_HOME` precedence, broken-selection errors, and the captured installation across worker restarts.

Add public Windows regressions for both batch extensions, an earlier batch launcher taking precedence over a later executable, restart after the launcher changes, and broken-launcher diagnostics. Align R test capability detection and discovery helpers, and update the Windows guide.

Validation on Windows x64:

- `scripts/preflight.cmd` and `scripts/stage-sandbox-runner.cmd` passed.
- `scripts/test.cmd WindowsConsole.test_discovers_r_from_batch_launcher WindowsConsole.test_reports_broken_r_batch_launcher WindowsConsole.test_python_without_r WindowsConsole.test_r_without_python` passed; new regression cases failed before the fix.
- `scripts/test.cmd WindowsConsole.test_r_persistence_and_restart` passed using this host's actual rig launcher with `R_HOME` unset.
- `scripts/test.cmd client_server/server/test_r_selection::rejects_invalid_local_r_home` passed.
- `scripts/test.cmd client_server/r/test_runtime::launches_r_children_from_interpreter_identity` passed with `R_HOME` unset; its Unix sandbox execution was unavailable on Windows.
- `scripts/format.cmd` passed all four formatters.
- `scripts/check.cmd` passed all core checks and 77 native cases; one explicitly provisioned elevated-sandbox case was skipped. The gate used `R_HOME=C:/Program Files/R/R-4.6.1` and `LC_ALL=C`.
- `git diff --check` passed. Cross-platform and exhaustive `--full` validation remain for CI.

title: Refresh Windows snapshots after local-host-only removal
description:
Windows boundary snapshots left behind by #497 still referenced removed execution targets, so the shared Windows suite failed snapshot comparison. Refresh the Windows CLI/configuration, tool-presentation, and bounded-output snapshots through the supported runner. Configuration override errors now match the generic snapshot, so remove that case's redundant Windows snapshot and platform marker.

Validation on native Windows x64 with Python 3.13.16, R 4.6.1, LC_ALL=C, and the explicitly provisioned network-restricted sandbox:

- `scripts/preflight.cmd` and `scripts/stage-sandbox-runner.cmd` passed.
- Reproduced the canonical handshake and configuration snapshot failures before refreshing them; focused comparisons passed afterward.
- `scripts/test --full --update` passed: 189 applicable shared cases, with supported snapshot pruning.
- `scripts/format` passed all four formatters; `git diff --check` passed.
- `scripts/check --full` passed on the final working tree before commit: tooling/source/architecture checks, Clippy, 38 Rust tests, all 76 native tests with no skips, and all 189 applicable shared cases. The installed wheel passed all 76 native tests; the source install passed both interpreter startup-order checks.

Windows SQL and Unix-specific fixtures retain their declared capability exclusions. No additional Windows runtime or packaging defect surfaced. Production code is unchanged.

title: Fix managed Python selection and CI transcript stability
description:
Recent Windows and Linux CI failures exposed unsupported Python 3.9 being selected from sparse managed inventories, changing interpreter catalogues, and nondeterministic test fixtures.

Managed Python selection now excludes CPython versions below 3.10 before ranking candidates or applying constraints. Public regression coverage exercises sparse and unsupported inventories, and the configuration guide documents the supported-version filter.

Internally, prefer the shared direct handshake when Windows has no platform-specific reference, with a public transcript-runner regression. Pin CI to uv 0.12.24 and install Python 3.12 in both Windows inventories to preserve the existing traceback/debugger baseline. Stabilize startup/rollback fixtures and canonical handshake references. Keep the declaration round-trip case on explicit R resolution so optional Arrow probes cannot add tzdb, and open the Linux interrupt checkpoint as a raw FIFO so warning delivery cannot change the transcript.

Merge the latest main documentation reorganization and preserve the PR's documentation additions in their current owning guides.

title: Fix remaining Windows CI acceptance failures
description:
Provisioned Windows CI workers cannot launch reliably from GitHub-hosted Console and runtime paths outside the native backend's standard read roots. Prepare inherited read/execute ACLs for the selected Console bundle, R/Python installations, R libraries, and uv cache using the sandbox accounts verified by public setup status, before enabling acceptance tests.

Add a public regression that relocates a complete Console installation into a private directory and exercises provisioned input and interruption. Its `--require-configured` preparation mode preserves explicit local provisioning. Repair the shared Windows checks by retaining native CRLF output in the idle Python thread snapshot and regenerating the stale interrupt traceback. Merge per-case timing logs in the supervisor to prevent concurrent Windows CRT appends from overwriting records.

Follows the discovery fixture repair in [PR #514](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/514). Its subsequent [Windows CI failure](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37453039773/job/112233889738) was reproduced locally with the private-installation regression before applying the read-access fix.

Validation completed before rebasing this follow-up onto main at `fff301d9`:

- All 19 Windows workflow tests and both focused public timing tests passed.
- Full core checks, 86 native checkout tests, and 207 shared transcript executions passed.
- Complete Windows installation acceptance passed: 3 copied-command checks, all 86 installed-wheel tests including both provisioned sandbox cases, and 2 source-install checks.
- `python scripts/check` passed as the final gate.
- `python scripts/format` passed all four formatters on the new base; `git diff --check` passed.

The combined PR head is being validated with `python scripts/check --full`, Python 3.13.16, R 4.6.1, and the existing configured sandbox. Unsupported platform/capability cases are skipped as declared by the suites.

The Linux traceback mismatches from the failing run are already repaired in [PR #515](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/515).

title: Fix Windows CI native discovery fixture
description:
Windows CI on main fails during native test discovery because the temporary checkout used by the workflow regression omits `support.installation`, now imported by the Windows acceptance modules. Copy that module into the fixture so `scripts/test --list` and `--locate` can discover cases and installed-binary execution still skips builds.

Reproduced the existing `WindowsWorkflow.test_native_discovery_and_installed_binary_skip_builds` failure before the fix, matching [the Windows job on main](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37401986085/job/112071282639).

Validation:

- All 13 Windows workflow regressions passed with Python 3.13.
- `scripts/preflight.cmd` and `scripts/stage-sandbox-runner.cmd` passed.
- `scripts/format.cmd` passed all four formatters; `git diff --cached --check` passed.
- `python scripts/check-core --full` passed with Python 3.13, `LC_ALL=C`, and an explicit `R_HOME`.
- `python scripts/check` passed with the same environment: 77 native acceptance tests passed, and the opt-in provisioned elevated sandbox test was skipped because no state directory was configured.

Full shared boundary and installation profiles were not run locally; CI runs the comprehensive gate.

title: Fix Windows validation with uv-installed Python and CRLF documents
description:
Formatting CRLF Markdown and Quarto documents on Windows could replace the newline before a Python closing fence with a lone carriage return. Configure Ruff to emit LF and add a public formatter regression for both document types. Windows CI installs Ruff and yamark so this regression executes there.

Two native acceptance fixtures also rejected uv-installed interpreters when run from a uv-created Python environment. Prefer system Python while allowing already-installed managed interpreters, retaining disabled interpreter downloads. The Windows validation guide now configures R_HOME and the C locale explicitly and explains why an R batch launcher can pass preflight while native R discovery treats R as absent.

These changes affect development formatting, acceptance fixtures, CI dependencies, and developer guidance. Application runtime behavior and published interfaces are unchanged.

The full Windows gate passed on clean commit da93ef42 with Python 3.13.16 and R 4.6.1: 38 Rust tests, 64 native acceptance cases from the checkout, the same 64 against an installed wheel, both source-install startup checks, and repository tooling/architecture/source checks. The new formatter regression failed before the LF policy and passed afterward; both previously failing native fixture cases also passed after repair. Preflight, companion staging, scripts/format.cmd, and diff checks were run. Unix-only suites and elevated-account provisioning were not exercised locally.

title: Fix native Windows JSONL framing test expectations
description:
## Problem

The JSONL framing refactor merged in #472 left three Windows acceptance tests failing. R reports the idle-interrupt acknowledgement through `console_diagnostic`. In the inherited-writer fixtures, the test-owned descendant also retains the outer stdout handle, so the test reader cannot observe EOF after the relay exits.

## Fix

Match R's diagnostic event and terminate/wait for the fixture-owned descendant after proving that relay retirement completed while that descendant was still alive. Preserve the split UTF-8, retained-command, refill, and terminal-event assertions. This changes only the three existing cases in `tests/windows_relay.py`.

## Validation

- Reproduced all three original failure signatures natively, then passed the three repaired cases.
- Clean commit `386735679fb0a07c577691f74d9a720efeba176e`: `python scripts/check --full` passed, including core/tooling checks, 64 checkout tests, 64 installed-wheel tests, and two source-install startup cases.
- Native host: Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200 x64, CPython 3.13.16, R 4.6.1, Rust 1.99.0 MSVC, `LC_ALL=C`. A task-local standalone Python was used so the managed-runtime fixtures could discover a system interpreter; an initial temporary uv virtualenv failed those two discovery cases.
- `scripts/format` ran unchanged. Ruff, Yamark, and rustfmt passed; Air was unavailable locally. Unrelated formatter output was restored before committing.
- Sequential exact-head Sol 6.1 MAX and Astra XHIGH reviews passed with no findings. The ordinary hosted reviewer completed this head and gave a thumbs-up.


- Windows hosted CI passed its full core, native-test, and installation phases ([run 37235359514](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37235359514/job/111533251950)).
- Overall CI remains blocked: Ubuntu failed one of 898 transcripts and macOS one of 925, both in the existing runtime-free configured-language presentation fixture. That separate timing-sensitive fixture repair is owned by [#475](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/475). Coordinated integration must pass all gates before merge.

title: Support native Windows development workflows
description:
Native Windows contributors can run the development commands through `.cmd` launchers or `python scripts/<command>`. Preflight inventories supported capabilities, check/test select native acceptance, and `check --full` validates wheel and source installation in a temporary virtualenv. Optional R probe failures remain visible without failing a Python-only Windows preflight; required probes still fail the command.

Shared workflow helpers and the packaging backend live under `scripts/`, with isolated builds using `backend-path`. The workflow and backend share checkout ownership, including nested builds. Windows Jobs retire descendants before releasing ownership, console cancellation wakes waits, and validation records tolerate transient reader locks. Source archives, Docker recipes, CI cache references, and test fixtures use the relocated helpers. Windows CI runs the same development entry points.

Validation:
- Windows `scripts/check.cmd` passed on clean commit `1db767a3`, including Rust checks and all 37 native cases. `scripts/preflight.cmd --json` passed at `c4ded66b`.
- `python tests/windows_workflow.py -v`: all 12 public command regressions passed. New optional-R cases failed before the fix and cover stale `R_HOME`, failed version/home probes, retained diagnostics, and fatal required-probe failures.
- Windows `scripts/check.cmd --full` passed at `fda3982e` after moving the helpers: core checks, 37 native cases, 37 installed-wheel cases, and two source-install cases. Subsequent changes are covered by the focused regressions and final ordinary gate.
- `scripts/with-checkout.cmd uv build --sdist --out-dir .dev-workflow/scripts-layout-dist` passed with the relocated backend and helpers included.
- WSL Ubuntu: all 24 workflow cases passed after fixing the review's interpreter-alias issue. The public fixture now launches check-core through a distinct `python3` symlink and compares executable identity; default, quick, and full profiles all failed before the fix and pass afterward. Earlier staging (3), development (4), focused release (3), transcript entry-point (5), and source/archive installation (1) coverage passed. A launcher case passed on an isolated rerun after initial 10-second timeouts under concurrent build load. The Unix preflight case also passed after the optional-R fix.
- `scripts/format`: Ruff, Yamark, and rustfmt succeeded. Air is not installed on this host. Unrelated formatter-only changes were reverted. macOS and full Unix runtime/provider coverage were not run locally.

title: Run warmup dependency preparation with host permissions
description:
`warmup` and the background warmup started by `configure-client` now prepare dependencies with host permissions while preserving the configured resolver environment and cache locations. This lets trusted installation downloads and builds populate the caches when resolver sandbox restrictions would otherwise prevent setup. Runtime checks and later sessions retain their configured sandbox policies.

Internally, a private launch hint selects trusted preparation and is removed from resolver and worker child environments. Older pinned releases can ignore the hint and retain their existing preparation policy. CLI help and the trust guides explain this installation boundary; public regressions cover preparation permissions, cache assignments, reuse with resolver networking disabled, and worker write restrictions.

Local macOS validation passed: `scripts/check`, focused warmup and CLI help suites, resolver/cache cases, and 23 website checks. Linux and Windows execution were not tested.

title: Follow system color preferences across documentation
description:
On page load, the guides and R package reference now follow the browser's light or dark preference automatically. Saved manual theme choices take precedence.

Enable Quarto's preference detection and pkgdown's automatic theme support, including its Light/Dark/Auto control. Add rendered-page regressions and document the behavior. Console runtime code is unchanged.

title: Prepare Windows cache-fixture working directory before sandbox logon
description:
On a fresh hosted Windows runner, the first cache-path acceptance case can fail with `CreateProcessWithLogonW failed: 267` before worker readiness. The fixture grants the sandbox account access to its virtual environment and cache probe, but creates the session's working directory outside that grant. The native runner applies read ACLs in the background, so that directory can still be inaccessible at first logon.

Keep the cache fixture's session directory beneath its explicitly prepared read root. The Windows test harness now accepts a parent directory for its temporary workspace. This removes reliance on background read-ACL traversal for these fixture assets while retaining the cache assertions and native retirement checks.

This is a Windows acceptance-fixture change only, following the merge of #544. There are no public API or production runtime changes, and no additional macOS work.

Native `scripts/check` passed all 89 acceptance tests, and unchanged `scripts/format` passed all formatters. The two cache-path cases also passed three times each locally under Python 3.13 with private temporary-directory ACLs and short paths. The [hosted reproduction](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37664675991) supplies the failing first-launch evidence; follow-up CI will verify the fresh hosted launch.

title: Fix Windows full CI prerequisites and path fixtures
description:
Windows full validation fails after enabling the shared acceptance cases: plotting fixtures cannot find `ir`, the hosted checkout and uv Python installations can occupy different drives, and abbreviated Windows temporary paths remain in Quarto snapshots.

Use uv to install `packaging` and `matplotlib` into the selected acceptance interpreter, and install `ir`, `ruff`, and `yamark` as isolated tools with their executable directory added to the CI PATH. Keep the relative-path fixture on the Python installation drive and create its parent on cold runners. Normalize both original and resolved workspace spellings in the affected recording cases, and close the R requirements fixture through its MCP client context before temporary-directory cleanup.

These are Windows CI and test-fixture changes; the public Console runtime is unchanged. The Windows development guide records the full suite's `ir` prerequisite.

title: Prepare the worker before wheel evaluation checks
description:
Wheel smoke tests time out on a cold runner because MCP initialization no longer prepares the built-in runtime.

Start the worker explicitly under the existing startup timeout before evaluating R. Keep the ordinary evaluation timeout unchanged, and cover both timeout boundaries through the release script's CLI tests. This changes release validation only; runtime behavior is unchanged.

title: Reduce transcript test noise and runtime
description:
## Summary

Reduce transcript-suite noise and avoid unrelated cold dependency resolution in Matplotlib cases. In local before-and-after runs, the complete transcript suite fell from about 83 seconds to about 48 seconds without removing coverage or loosening synchronization.

## User-facing changes

- Name a running transcript case after five seconds instead of three, keeping more normal startup work on the compact progress line.
- Keep MCP, relay, worker, runtime, and transcript snapshot behavior unchanged.

## Internal changes

- Shorten only the copied runner fixture threshold so the runner regressions retain their existing coverage without waiting five seconds.
- Preserve the ambient IR cache while Matplotlib tests continue to isolate XDG and Matplotlib state, avoiding repeated cold R dependency resolution.

## Testing

- `scripts/check`

title: Bound synchronous request cancellation before recovery
description:
A synchronous Python caller could recover from KeyboardInterrupt before the MCP SDK finished cancelling the previous request. Wait for confirmed request retirement and reject new calls while cancellation settles. An interrupted response wait publishes cancellation before reopening admission; ordinary response waits still allow concurrent control calls.

Each request owns its host response future and native SDK task. Submission and cancellation are posted without waiting for the SDK loop, including when it is busy validating a result. Interrupting before task creation prevents the queued request from being sent. Task completion confirms retirement even when cancellation prevents its coroutine from starting; the SDK retains protocol, session, and transport ownership.

Cleanup has a five-second limit, and a second interrupt also ends the wait. Incomplete cleanup invalidates the connection and posts another native cancellation to escape shielded SDK cleanup. The abort follows the initial cancellation's task step, so a previously busy loop cannot merge both interruptions. Close confirms request retirement before shutting down the transport and portal; if that request still cannot stop within five seconds, close raises and retains ownership. After actual SDK teardown, a finally block records a disconnected state even if teardown raises. Successful closure permits a fresh session. Admitted cells continue running until explicitly interrupted or the connection closes.

Public regressions cover cancellation ordering, concurrent admission at interruption and during cleanup, permanently held SDK cleanup, a busy SDK loop followed by shielded cleanup, interrupts during queued submission, teardown errors, peer/thread retirement, and recovery/reconnection. The new failure cases failed against the earlier implementation. The full synchronous client suite, scripts/check, and all formatters pass locally; fresh hosted CI, current-head review, and the final release rehearsal remain required. No R repository or release-workflow changes are included.

title: Fix startup completion ownership and SDK R fixture isolation
description:
Interrupting the first cell during worker startup could publish its completion while retaining startup ownership. An immediate follow-up cell could then fail with `worker startup interrupted`. Release startup ownership before both early completion paths so the follow-up cell can start normally. This is the public behavior change and applies across platforms.

The other changes are internal: use the shared R test environment to isolate the bare SDK fixture from personal startup profiles, declare its R requirement, and record the inherited-procfs error portability finding in `docs/TODO.md`.

## Validation

On Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 with CI-pinned uv 0.12.24:

- `scripts/check` passed after updating to current `main` (`ccbb6ac9`).
- `scripts/test --jobs 6 client_server/lifecycle/test_startup_interrupt client_server/integrations/test_python::callable_tools_follow_connected_server_fields`: all 8 executions passed on the updated base.
- `scripts/format` reported every formatter successful; unrelated formatting changes were excluded. `git diff --check` passed.

Baseline audit at `071101d9`, followed by validation with these fixes:

- `scripts/test --full --jobs 11` completed 1,741 baseline executions: 1,739 passed; the two failures led to these fixes. The related lifecycle, Python startup/setup, and SDK integration suites subsequently passed all 207 executions.
- `python tests/install.py` passed source, editable, sdist, wheel relocation, and Python 3.11/3.14 client checks. The affected startup cases also passed all 15 executions with R physically absent in an Ubuntu 26.04 container.
- `scripts/check-core --full`, all three `scripts/test --stress --jobs 3` cases, R package build/check, `python tests/website.py`, sandbox installation checks, and the original 87 R-free executions passed during the audit.

The separately exercised inherited-procfs transcript still fails: `network_setns` records EACCES (13) rather than the expected EINVAL (22), while all policy and supervisor-isolation assertions pass. Opening the namespace handle is denied before `setns()` runs on this host. This reproduced in host and container execution sharing Linux 6.8; the complete errors and assertions remain unchanged. Native ARM64 and the older Linux ABI floor were not tested.

title: Restore startup regression coverage and fix restart checkpoints
description:
Restore the regression that retries interrupted Python selection while adding `py-yaml12`, then checks that the package is available and selection runs once on retry. The shared direct/sandbox test and its generated snapshot retain the original coverage.

The final Ubuntu check for #422 timed out waiting for restart contention. Its native checkpoint kept only one in-flight mutex wait, allowing an overlapping wait to be missed and the slot to be cleared by another returning thread. Track each wait until it returns, preserving the existing cancellation, replacement-input, and late-return assertions without changing timeouts.

These are test-only changes; Console runtime behavior and the public API are unchanged. The exact hosted timeout did not reproduce in focused local runs.

title: Fix cache lifetime and stdout capture races in CI tests
description:
Fix two test-fixture races exposed by CI after #356. These changes affect test infrastructure only; there are no public API or runtime changes.

- Give `ir` the canonical cache root in the localhost SSH fixture. Its shared resolution records previously retained temporary cache symlinks, which another fixture could remove between a resolver lookup and R startup. That left R unable to find `DBI` or `jsonlite`. Keep the aliases used by worker path assertions and uv.
- Hold the stdout fixture's completion message until the server records the full payload. Stdout and sideband completion travel independently, so finishing a pipe write did not guarantee that the response contained its tail. Use filesystem events and a FIFO checkpoint, assert every output byte, and remove the unused partial-tail assertion. Existing snapshot expectations stay unchanged.

A deterministic cache-lifetime reproduction fails with the temporary path and succeeds with the canonical root. `scripts/check` passed on macOS at `e7e2292e`, including core checks, applicable transcripts, and source/wheel installation checks. After the stdout fix, `scripts/format` and the complete `client_server/output/test_streams` suite passed locally in direct and sandbox modes at the tree committed as `24c6481a`.

title: Fix Linux startup restart checkpoint in CI
description:
Fix the Ubuntu CI failure in `restart_replaces_first_use_cell_and_stdin` observed on #354. The native fixture treated any futex wait with expected value `2` as worker-mutex contention. A timed thread-pool condition-variable wait can have the same value, so the fixture could select an unrelated wait and time out at `old evaluation released the worker lock`.

Only untimed waits now enter mutex-contention tracking. Timed waits retain their separate role in confirming that the old evaluation returned to the pool. This changes only the test fixture; production behavior, public interfaces, transcript snapshots, ordering assertions, and deadlines are unchanged.

The focused transcript passes in both macOS execution modes. A controlled Linux reproduction that inserts a competing timed futex wait fails before the fix and passes afterward, using the existing 0.0.4 container and preinstalled R libraries. Formatting and core checks pass. Full local `scripts/check` is still running through the transcript suite; installation checks have not run yet.

title: Clarify test transcripts and embedded programs
description:
Some snapshots repeated full handshakes, and embedded fixture programs were indented inconsistently.

- Add canonical handshakes for workspace profiles, SSH targets, and the R/SQL interface so their transcripts use `!same-as` while still comparing the complete exchange.
- Give each synthetic SSH resolver callback its own transcript and assert exactly one failure message.
- Write the SSH cells as readable multiline R and Python. Use ordinary workspace and environment values, retaining special characters in the executable prefix that passes through the remote shell.
- Fix indentation in embedded fixture programs across the tests and use the shared `code()` helper in the test harness. Keep `textwrap.dedent()` inside sandboxed programs that cannot import test support.

These are internal changes to tests, fixtures, snapshots, and test documentation. Public API and runtime behavior are unchanged.

title: Keep warmup I/O drivers out of the server runtime
description:
Restrict the server runtime to timers so enabling Tokio process support for warmup does not also add I/O and signal drivers to every server. This restores the server’s descriptor budget and startup, response delivery, and EOF coordination. The warmup client retains its separate runtime for asynchronous subprocess I/O, with the same CLI output and timeout behavior.

The timeout regression now captures the live worker’s host process identity before checking retirement. A FIFO synchronizes that observation with startup, preserving the assertion across Linux PID namespaces and PID reuse.

title: Accept SBX v0.42.1 and newer without an upper bound
description:
Console rejects every standalone SBX version except v0.42.1, and test discovery silently skips newer installations. Require v0.42.1 or newer without an upper bound so installed upgrades can run against the existing provider contract.

The adapter compares semantic versions, while test discovery checks provider availability and leaves version enforcement to the adapter. Add public regression coverage for the minimum and later patch, minor, and major versions, retain rejection below the minimum, and document the supported range. Refresh snapshots for SBX v0.45.1 diagnostics and current Console Python tracebacks.

Local validation passed on macOS 26.7 arm64 with SBX v0.45.1: `scripts/check`, all 10 provider/configuration cases, all 47 transcript-runner tests, and all 13 real-SBX runtime, lifecycle, and policy cases, including network policy and inner-Docker cleanup.

title: Restore R SQL connection after Python selects DuckDB
description:
## Summary

After Python selected managed DuckDB with `console_sql_connection(None)`, R's `sql_connection()` could still return the previously selected DBI connection until a SQL cell ran. Disconnecting that old connection then made DBI calls fail.

R's `sql_connection()` now consumes the pending managed selection before returning. A later SQL cell uses DuckDB without repeating the provider transition, and the managed catalog is reused.

## User-facing changes

- R can use the managed connection immediately after Python restores it, including after the previous user-owned connection is disconnected.
- The next SQL cell continues on managed DuckDB when R observed the restore request first.
- The runtime documentation describes when R or SQL observes the Python selection.

## Internal changes

- Pass the Python restore request through the existing native bridge and consume it under the GIL, without starting Python for R-only calls.
- Add a public transcript case for separate R and Python calls, a Python callback into R, and the absence of a repeated provider transition, in direct and sandboxed modes.

title: Synchronize the SQL interrupt test with DuckDB execution
description:
The Ubuntu job in [CI run 35231155281](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/35231155281/job/105235293847) failed because the SQL interrupt test still reported a running query after its 30-second wait. Its `COPY` marker preceded the long query, leaving a window for SIGINT to arrive before DuckDB resets its interrupt flag at query startup. A controlled reproduction that delivered SIGINT at execute entry reproduced the timeout.

Wait inside a running aggregate query's DuckDB progress callback instead. A native checkpoint forwards SIGINT to the active DuckDB handler and confirms delivery before releasing the callback. Keep the existing interruption and retained-catalog assertions, and regenerate the shared direct/sandbox snapshot. A negative control that withheld SIGINT from DuckDB still failed with the original assertion.

This changes only test fixtures and their snapshot; there are no public API or runtime changes.

The focused SQL test passes in direct and sandbox modes, and all core checks pass. The full `scripts/check` run stopped after 494 completed transcript cases when the unchanged `client_server/output/test_recovery::recovered_image_omissions_keep_bounded_state` case reached its deadline while waiting for a ping. That case passed in isolation in 1 minute 31 seconds with the same assertions and deadline. The aggregate run remains failed, and installation checks were not reached.

title: Prefer remote PATH for SSH launches
description:
SSH targets now use `mcp-console` from the remote `PATH`, falling back to `uvx mcp-console` only when it is absent. Exact paths and configured argv prefixes run without executable preflight checks; command failures propagate without selecting another executable.

External SSH coverage automatically probes the optional test host and accepts another destination through `MCP_CONSOLE_TEST_SSH_HOST`. Reachable hosts receive a private installation of the current working-tree source for the policy test. Unavailable hosts skip that case, while localhost SSH coverage continues in CI and when the external host is unavailable.

Source transfer, installation, and build caching are confined to test support; the production change is the default SSH command selection. The source cache handles file/directory changes and serializes builds. Each run owns a separate temporary installation, so overlapping tests keep their selected revision until cleanup.

Validation:

- `scripts/check` passed in an isolated checkout, including the full applicable transcript suite with real-host SSH coverage and source-installation checks.
- Runner regressions reproduced both cached-path conflicts and replacement of an active run's executable before the fixes, then passed afterward.
- Command-selection and worker-launch cases on macOS and Linux, including direct and sandboxed execution.
- Real-host policy enforcement using the current source and default command discovery.
- Unavailable-host run: external coverage skipped and localhost command cases passed.

title: Separate recorded events from MCP transcript goldens
description:
## Summary

Separate recorded session events from the public MCP transcript golden so each artifact is readable at its own boundary. This follow-up also limits format-specific artifact filenames to the PNG format MCP Console produces.

## User-facing changes

- Keep built-in PNG artifacts named `.png`.
- Store custom-worker images with other MIME types under a neutral `.bin` suffix while preserving their original MIME type and MCP content.
- Clarify that recording decodes valid base64 into artifact bytes without rewriting the MCP image.

## Internal changes

- Add a narrow companion-stream result to the transcript harness.
- Move normalized journal events into `records_tool_calls_and_images.events.yaml` as a YAML sequence followed by the produced session file list.
- Remove the duplicated JSONL block scalar and repeated binary payload from the MCP transcript golden. The public case still checks event semantics, the final newline, file permissions, and byte-identical PNG persistence.

title: Update native sandbox runner to 0.162.1
description:
Update the pinned native sandbox runner to `rust-v0.162.1` at `d77a1b391e88532b955e139192e1041ce1dc9b9c` so Console uses the reapplied runner and its Windows MXC support.

Windows launches now follow the runner's `auto` selection: compatible hosts and policies use MXC; otherwise the runner selects the elevated backend. Existing Console sandbox accounts keep automatic selection on elevated. The setup command and explicit native backend choices remain available.

Console accepts Windows managed TCP proxies when `allow_local_binding: true` is explicit. UDP, Unix sockets, and explicit resolver sandbox policies remain unsupported. The runner rejects proxy launches when MXC is unavailable; Console does not retry with weaker permissions.

Internally, the native-policy fixtures use `windows_backend`, the elevated setup case selects its backend explicitly, and the removed-Landlock snapshot records the new schema error. Windows CI requires a successful public MXC proxy launch before provisioning legacy accounts, then runs the remaining native acceptance suite, including proxy configuration round-tripping and unsupported permissions. The sandbox guides describe the new selection rules and proxy limitation.

title: Update native sandbox runner to 0.160.1
description:
Update the bundled native runner to `85d407d8a4544ed0916aff3c7a273461e739f215`, the current head of `mcp-console/sandbox-runner/rust-v0.160.1`, and align Console with its launch contract.

Native policies are now unversioned: remove `version` from complete policy payloads. Standalone Linux Landlock requests report that the backend was removed. Windows configurations use `unelevated` in place of `restricted-token`. The workspace profile also inherits native `.aws` write protection.

Internally, stage the renamed `mcp-console-sandbox` Cargo package and remove protocol-version metadata while retaining artifact identity and integrity checks. Update examples, docs, fixtures, and generated macOS/Linux snapshots. Refresh the dependency-conflict diagnostic snapshot with uv 0.12.23.

On the final head, `scripts/check` and focused Linux sandbox/resolver cases passed. Staging/integrity regressions, focused macOS cases, and source/wheel installation checks also passed. The full Linux transcript update passed before the final main merge. The full macOS run exhausted disk space; Windows runtime validation remains for CI.

title: Fix sans-R SQL transcript cache isolation
description:
## Summary

The sans-R SQL transcript now owns its uv cache and checks that a failed resolver reports a Python executable from that cache. This removes an assumption that uv always uses `HOME/.cache/uv`; the Ubuntu CI runner supplied a different cache location, so its path normalization assertion failed.

This changes test isolation and diagnostics only. Public behavior and runtime code are unchanged.

## Validation

- Reproduced the failure with an external `UV_CACHE_DIR` before the fix.
- `UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/pr409-uv-cache scripts/test client_server/sql/test_without_r::failed_and_live_extension_changes_preserve_worker_and_selected_connection` passed after the fix in direct and native sandbox modes.
- `scripts/test client_server/sql/test_without_r` passed.
- `scripts/check` passed.

title: Fix CI regressions in sans-R requirement and extension tests
description:
Fix CI failures in the sans-R requirement and extension tests against the current `main`.

- Regenerate Python error snapshots with the current restart guidance.
- Exercise rejected mixed Python/DuckDB changes in the Python state-preservation tests. Idle DuckDB-only additions are now supported, so they no longer belong in the rejected-request cases.
- Catch network denial during socket creation as well as connection in the extension-cache test. Linux seccomp rejects socket creation with `EPERM`; the probe still requires `EACCES` or `EPERM` and rejects successful connections. Include the worker response in assertion failures.

These changes address the stale snapshot failure on [main](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/36336573665), the outdated live-addition assertion in [PR #406 CI](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/36338288182), and the Linux network probe failure in [PR #405 CI](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/36336940112).

This is a test-only correction. `scripts/review-diff origin/main` reports zero production additions or deletions.

The complete sans-R Python and SQL suites passed locally in direct and native-sandbox modes. The extension-cache regression also passed in both modes in a Linux container using an installed build. A bare-host Linux run was blocked before worker startup by a native sandbox namespace permission error.

`scripts/format`, `git diff --check`, and the standard `scripts/check` gate passed.

title: Normalize Python patch version in sans-R SQL transcript
description:
## Summary

The macOS and Ubuntu CI jobs for #402 failed because the sans-R SQL preparation transcript captured the local reticulate default Python patch version (`3.12.14`), while both runners used `3.12.13`.

Use the existing Python resolution-error normalization in that public MCP case and regenerate its snapshot. The case still checks the failed resolver, its requested packages, and preservation of the current worker, Python object, and SQL catalog. Only the variable patch number is normalized. This is a test-only change; SQL behavior and the public interface are unchanged.

## Validation

- `scripts/test client_server/sql/test_without_r` passed in applicable direct and native-sandbox modes.
- `scripts/check` passed the ordinary core and smoke transcript gate.
- `scripts/format` passed.

title: Fix sandbox acceptance startup and environment assumptions
description:
Full local acceptance runs could fail during fixture setup: the R supervision cases exhausted a ten-second I/O deadline before R evaluated the fixture, and Quarto prewarm loaded a personal `.Rprofile` that required packages absent from its isolated library.

- Use the existing case supervisor deadline for R/processx startup. Keep complete readiness reads, process identity and cleanup assertions, and the ten-second retirement checks.
- Disable personal R profiles in fixture environments, retain Quarto prewarm diagnostics, and include exit codes when rendering fails.
- Document why Ubuntu AppArmor can permit `/usr/bin/bwrap` while denying the relocated bundled helper, and describe the disposable container settings used for installation checks.

This changes test support and developer documentation only. Production behavior, capability requirements, snapshots, and the empty-`PATH` bundle checks are unchanged.

The full macOS `scripts/check` passed, along with 32 concurrent focused processx retirement runs and ten supervision suite runs. Ubuntu x86_64 passed core checks, all 424 applicable transcript cases, and both source/wheel installation tests; installation checks ran in the documented namespace-capable container. A load diagnostic reproduced the original macOS timeout in 5 of 64 runs, before R reached the fixture code.

Follow-up to #287.

title: Treat reticulate declarations as explicit dependency requests
description:
Evaluated `reticulate::py_require()` calls authorize managed Python preparation under `explicit`, including declarations from R package `.onLoad()` hooks. This allows declarations before Python initializes and compatible additions to an initialized interpreter while retaining package extras, version constraints, accepted requirements, and live objects.

Register the dependency-resolution finder only under `implicit`. Under `explicit` and `fixed`, missing imports produce native Python errors without distribution inference or a preparation request. Existing Python environments also use native import errors. Display, plotting, and reticulate interoperability hooks remain independent of dependency-resolution policy.

Internally, carry declaration authorization and the captured automatic-resolution capability through the existing host/worker preparation lifecycle. Retain host admission, fixed-policy restrictions, interpreter compatibility checks, and restart rules. Update public API regressions, generated snapshots, and documentation, using small dependencies and a tiny fixture R package.

title: Fix Matplotlib show calls through reticulate
description:
R calls to `plt$show()` failed with `ValueError: call stack is not deep enough` after #561 because reticulate's native bridge supplies no Python caller frame. Calls with or without figures now follow the ordinary `show()` behavior: publish open figures immediately and close them.

Caller detection uses the current frame's `f_back`, treating `None` as an ordinary call while retaining the `plt.pause()` special case. A public regression checks empty calls, PNG bytes, output ordering, figure closure, and repeated calls in direct and sandboxed sessions. The runtime documentation clarifies that these display rules also apply through reticulate.

title: Initialize reticulate bridge on direct py access
description:
Direct R access through `reticulate::py$...` or Console's `py$...` shortcut returned `NULL` until another reticulate call initialized the bridge, even when Python was already running. Return reticulate's delayed main-module proxy before attachment so the first attribute access reaches the running interpreter and preserves its objects, including after restart.

Package loading and plain reads of the proxy stay lazy, including the active-binding reads performed by `library(reticulate)` conflict checks. During selection and attachment callbacks, retain the previous `NULL` behavior until reticulate publishes its configuration to prevent recursive initialization. Initialization errors, retry behavior, and reads from `afterInitialized` hooks remain supported.

Add shared MCP and native Windows regressions for all three getter paths, normal package loading, R-only sessions with an unavailable Python selection, hooks that read `py` or clear themselves, native selection callbacks, failed initialization retries, retained object identity, and restart. Document the attribute-access contract.

Validation on Windows x64 with R 4.6.1:

- Confirmed default package-loading and hook regressions failed before the review fixes, then passed after them.
- `scripts/preflight.cmd` and `scripts/stage-sandbox-runner.cmd`
- `scripts/test.cmd WindowsConsole.test_direct_py_access_attaches_on_demand WindowsConsole.test_loading_reticulate_does_not_start_python WindowsConsole.test_py_reads_in_initialization_hooks_do_not_reenter`
- `scripts/test.cmd --update --jobs 2 client_server/python/test_bridge`; regenerated formatted snapshot inputs through scoped `--update` runs.
- `scripts/test.cmd --jobs 2 client_server/python/test_bridge client_server/python/test_setup::partial_attachment_requires_restart client_server/python/test_setup::r_first_runs_selection_callback_once client_server/python/test_runtime::evaluates_cells_in_persistent_reticulate_state`: eight cases passed without snapshot updates.
- `scripts/format.cmd`: all four formatters passed; unrelated line-ending rewrites were excluded.
- `scripts/check.cmd`: runtime source and architecture validation, Rust formatting, Clippy, Rust tests, and 80 native Windows acceptance tests passed.

The shared Seatbelt/bubblewrap execution modes are unavailable on Windows. One native acceptance case was skipped because no elevated network-restricted sandbox was provisioned. Linux/macOS coverage remains for CI.

title: Fix R resource paths and Python optional import overhead
description:
R initialization assumed its share, include, and documentation directories were beneath `R_HOME`, which breaks split installations. Capture the selected launcher's configured resource paths before either interpreter starts so R cells and their subprocesses use the correct directories. Retain those paths outside the mutable process environment and restore them before late R initialization, so earlier Python code cannot redirect the selected installation.

Python optional-import ownership checks match canonical selected module origins against the corresponding wheel `RECORD` entries without inspecting unrelated payload files. This preserves packages' `ImportError` fallbacks through symlinked installation paths while avoiding filesystem inspection of package payloads.

Internal coverage checks split R layouts after Python changes the environment, framework Python subprocess identity, symlinked package and helper origins, and package payload inspection. The DuckDB resolver failure case compares Console's complete diagnostic against native Rscript stderr. Ragnar denial cases compare complete errors with native Rscript under the same sandbox and managed R library, retaining the denial and store-creation assertions. These snapshots record verified comparisons so unpinned package releases can change diagnostic formatting without losing coverage of Console's output. The runtime documentation describes the resource and metadata contracts.

The Linux Ragnar comparison awaits CI confirmation with the current package environment.

title: Synchronize retirement failure injection before restart
description:
Make the sandbox restart regression independent of worker scheduling during shutdown. The [failing Linux test](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/36192238305/job/108259828201) required its fixture to receive shutdown and publish a malformed message within the one-second grace period; missing that window produced a successful restart instead of the expected retirement error.

Publish the malformed worker message after the client receives cell completion, then hold its parsing with the existing native read gate until retirement joins the reader. The test confirms that the bytes are captured before requesting restart, so failure injection no longer depends on worker scheduling during shutdown. It retains the exact error assertions and existing transcript snapshot.

Only the public MCP test and its worker fixture change. Runtime behavior, shutdown deadlines, and CI configuration are unchanged.

Validated with the full `scripts/check` gate (1,059 transcript executions plus source and wheel installation checks), 40 focused macOS executions, and nine installed-build Linux executions. The original scheduling failure was reproduced by parking the fixture worker after completion.

title: Fix resolver interrupt fixture race
description:
Follow up the [macOS CI failure in #335](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/35138967599/job/104938380511). `control_only_interrupt_targets_blocked_controlled_restart_resolver` timed out waiting for `resolver-interrupted`.

The fake R resolver relied on a Python SIGINT callback while waiting on a FIFO. If SIGINT arrives inside CPython's native read call before the blocking syscall, the callback can remain pending until the read returns. Block SIGINT before publishing readiness and consume it with `sigwait()` in the fixture's interrupt mode. Preserve the interruption acknowledgment, exit gate, and exit status 130 across all three tests using this mode.

This changes only the shared test fixture. Public runtime behavior, assertions, timeouts, and snapshots are unchanged.

Validation:

- A temporary native interposer forced the signal-before-read interleaving through the existing public test: the original fixture failed at the same checkpoint as CI, and the updated fixture passed in direct and sandboxed modes.
- All 29 cases in the affected interrupt, restart, and replacement suites passed.
- `scripts/check` passed its core checks, then stopped when the unchanged `recovered_image_omissions_keep_bounded_state` test exhausted its case deadline while waiting for a ping. PR #335 documented the same local timeout. Another worktree's full check was running concurrently; its contribution is unconfirmed. The isolated rerun passed in 6m 42s with the existing deadline and assertions.
- All 63 server-relay and relay-worker cases passed. Source and wheel installation checks passed via `python3 tests/install.py`.
- `scripts/format` and `git diff --check` passed.

title: Make Python preparation cancellation deterministic
description:
## Summary

Make live Python preparation return a deterministic lifecycle error when a concurrent restart invalidates its worker generation. Previously, the result exposed whichever resolver-cancellation or sideband-shutdown event won the race, including a scheduling-dependent broken pipe.

## User-facing changes

- A live Python preparation invalidated by restart now returns `Python preparation cancelled by restart`.
- Sideband failures from the active generation retain their transport diagnostics.

## Internal changes

- Classify unsuccessful live preparation against the worker generation after the worker dialogue returns.
- Preserve successful checkpoints and current-generation preparation behavior.
- Tighten the public transcript regression and document the lifecycle contract.

title: Preserve resolver interruption causes and independent failures
description:
Preserve interruption as the cause when dependency preparation exits unsuccessfully, retaining the complete diagnostic and leaving independent failures with their own cause.

Unix observes suspension before delivering SIGINT, and nonblocking exit probes leave its stop notification intact. Windows checks the leader's terminal status after Job retirement before attributing its failure to interruption.

Public regressions reproduce signal/exit races and overlapping stop observation. Internal CI fixtures collect failed startup cells before retrying discovery and use the installed Python for offline R-only DuckDB preparation.

title: Normalize Python versions in requirements snapshots
description:
CI and local uv installations can select different Python patch releases. Requirements snapshots now scrub those resolved patch versions to `.XX`, including the interrupted replacement error that failed on both CI platforms.

The recording-boundary test uses the existing uv fixture to supply a fixed version inventory for its rejected constraints. It still records the complete error, checks that failed replacement creates no environment boundary, and uses real resolution for successful preparation and reset.

This changes tests and snapshots only. Runtime output and the public API are unchanged.

title: Fix CI cache setup and interrupt test races
description:
Fix failures in the macOS and Linux CI checks for requirement preparation and interruption.
