- Give R integration tests temporary R and ir caches so pak can resolve packages during `R CMD check`. Check preparation responses directly, and use a fresh ir cache so cached environments cannot hide resolution failures.
- Align the startup test's exact resolver-input assertion and CI prewarming with the explicitly declared R bridge dependencies. Advance the weekly R cache key while retaining compatible cache fallbacks.
- Give the automatic R resolver interrupt sole ownership of the evaluation response. Hold the SQL DB-API test inside the existing native signal checkpoint before interrupting it, so the traceback cannot race with readiness-file creation.

The interrupt tests retain the complete errors, resolver-retirement checks, and subsequent-cell state checks. This changes CI setup and tests only; runtime behavior and the public API are unchanged.

title: Synchronize resolver interrupt and prompt preview tests
description:
Fix two test synchronization races exposed by #371.

The resolver permission-error tests now wait for the server to supervise the exact resolver PID before sending an interrupt. A child-side startup marker could appear before that registration, allowing the interrupt to be acknowledged as queued between resolver phases instead of returning a live signal-delivery error.

The prompt preview test now gates input consumption and waits for the server to process completion before asserting the answer. Its snapshot explicitly records the intermediate waiting state, while retaining the exact prompt, output-budget, and final-answer checks.

Changes are limited to tests, fixtures, and one generated snapshot. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

title: Fix replacement lifecycle test synchronization
description:
Fix the two lifecycle test races exposed by [CI for #359](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/35928274954).

- The startup-failure fixture wrote its checkpoint into sandbox-owned temporary storage, which could disappear before the test observed it. Store the marker beside the test-owned startup control, grant sandbox access to that directory, and assert that the marker survives retirement.
- The restart fixture assumed worker stdin closure meant the server had finished recording the cell. Those events can race, splitting output across retained and unretained previews. A macOS/Linux fixture signals when the server closes the cell log; both affected restart tests wait for that signal and stdin EOF before emitting their shutdown output.

There are no user-facing or production changes. Existing output assertions, deadlines, and transcript snapshots remain unchanged. The diff contains 116 additions and 10 deletions in tests and fixtures; production additions plus deletions: **0**.

The marker-survival regression failed before the fix. All 19 replacement and restart cases pass in direct and sandbox execution. `scripts/format` passed, and `scripts/check` passed on macOS using the existing uv cache: core checks, 589 transcript cases (54 capability skips), and source/wheel installation checks. The full check took 11 minutes 17 seconds. The Linux interposer branch also passed a syntax check; hosted Linux execution remains for CI.

title: Delay console operations until response writes settle
description:
## Summary

A client can finish reading an MCP response before Tokio observes that the stdout write has completed. During that interval, a later `send` or `session` call could reach the worker while the server still owned the previous response. Output recovery or a worker-generation change could then race with delivery, and several waiting calls could resume in scheduler order instead of transport receipt order.

This change retains response ownership until the write settles and gives only the affected console calls bounded FIFO admission. The transport continues reading cancellation notifications and EOF directly. Once the delivery gate has cleared and no earlier waiter remains, an interrupt or restart can still run alongside a long evaluation.

## User-facing changes

- `send` and `session` calls received while an earlier response is still being delivered wait for that response and retain their receipt order.
- Cancellation before admission prevents the call from reaching the worker. If execution has already begun, queued successors remain behind that call until its handler stops.
- Closing MCP input still stops the server and worker while stdout is backpressured.
- If a client leaves stdout blocked and exceeds 64 response-gated console calls, the server closes the connection and worker session instead of retaining an unbounded handler backlog. Concurrent `send` calls are already unsupported.
- MCP tool schemas and descriptions, worker and relay wire formats, response content, and transcript goldens are unchanged.

## Internal changes

- Track a delivery claim before transport dispatch, its write future, and a completed queued operation waiting for its response write.
- Assign FIFO admission nodes only while a delivery gate or an existing gated cohort is active. Live-node accounting bounds retained state, including canceled or completed predecessors.
- Resolve queued admission and cancellation under the same request-ID token. A stale drop cannot remove a reused ID, and canceling a newer queued call does not release an older visible response.
- Hold an operation guard through handler completion so cancellation cannot release a successor while the canceled operation still runs.
- Keep request bodies out of transport-owned read-ahead while allowing cancellation and EOF to remain responsive.
- Preserve ready final responses after input EOF, abandon blocked stdout writes during shutdown, and avoid waiting for Tokio's abandoned blocking stdout task after service and worker cleanup finish.
- Extend the deterministic Zod signal checkpoint and public macOS CLI regressions for backpressure, FIFO admission, cancellation, bounded backlog, post-gate interruption, and EOF-triggered shutdown.

title: Preserve user PNG devices after managed slot reuse
description:
Closing a managed R plot and reopening an explicit PNG with the same device number and filename template previously let cell cleanup close the user device. Explicit devices now remain open and uncaptured, so later cells can draw on them and close them explicitly.

Managed devices receive registration IDs and filenames that remain unique throughout the worker's lifetime. Cleanup consults the existing native managed-device registry, whose close callback retires registrations. Public regressions cover distinct and reused filenames, opening a new managed device while the user PNG stays open, later drawing and closure, and subsequent managed plotting. The runtime and architecture docs describe the ownership rule. The completed GR-1 entry and its empty section are removed from `docs/TODO.md`, which now directs contributors to delete resolved entries.

Local macOS validation passed: 36 focused R graphics executions, `scripts/format`, and `scripts/check`. Linux and Windows coverage remains for CI.

title: fix: use startup declarations in recording exports
description:
Use each session's captured startup dependency declaration in recording exports. Selecting an existing Python interpreter in an R session now emits `python-packages: []` instead of inventing managed defaults; recorded additions still extend the header.

Pass the declaration from runtime configuration to the recorder and include it as `startup_requirements` in the journal. Preserve unknown metadata until discovery completes and retain early call ordering. Existing R defaults now follow the declaration's normalized order.

title: Retire read-only worker temporary directories
description:
Direct sessions can fail restart or shutdown when native startup or a cell creates read-only directories in private worker temporary storage. Restore owner access after worker retirement so cleanup succeeds while preserving external library permissions and contents.

Traverse through pinned directory descriptors and relative names, supporting deep trees and a temporary parent with search access only. Readable directories restore permissions through their descriptors without requiring `fchmodat2` or procfs. Unreadable directories require the platform's no-follow chmod support. Missing children and symlink open refusals allow root removal to continue; retirement requires removing the owned root or confirming that it is absent. Genuine cleanup failures still block replacement.

Public regressions cover restart and shutdown, external-library preservation during controlled races, deep trees, search-only parents, unavailable no-follow chmod, and storage failures that must block replacement.

Validated on macOS arm64 with the worker-retirement suite, `scripts/format`, and `scripts/check`. Older Linux failure modes are exercised through native fault injection; Linux and Windows were not exercised locally.

title: Preserve project R library order during activation
description:
Native R profiles and renv projects can move or hide Console's managed library. Preserve their libraries and lookup order during requirement changes, and clear inherited managed-library state for bare workers.

Track the Console-owned library at worker launch and during preparation before R initializes. Replace only its entry at its current position; when the candidate already exists as a project or ambient entry, preserve that entry without claiming ownership. Document the ownership marker and add public regressions for native profiles, real renv lookup and automatic preparation, successive requirement changes, preparation before R initialization, and bare startup/restart.

Validated on macOS arm64 with the focused R preparation, loading, project-library, sandbox-library and bare-runtime cases, `scripts/format`, and `scripts/check`. Linux and Windows were not exercised locally.

title: Extract native R bootstrap and event APIs
description:
## Problem

The embedded R runtime mixes Unix event handling and Windows startup APIs with the shared REPL and callback implementation. Native startup parameters, callback types, and event symbols are spread through the common owner.

## Fix

Move Unix bootstrap and event activity into a local Unix module, and Windows bootstrap and its interrupt callback into a local Windows module. Retain the existing activity interface and common ownership of parsing, source buffering, REPL execution, callbacks, graphics scopes, environment preparation, and interrupt acknowledgment. Preserve startup ordering, process-lifetime argument/path storage, package deferral, and the C jump boundaries. Document these invariants and the Windows absence of idle R event servicing.

## Validation

- Existing public native baseline before and after extraction: 34/34 passed, including both language initialization orders, late R, input/interrupt recovery, plots, startup paths, and R home precedence.
- Unchanged `scripts/format`: Ruff, Yamark, rustfmt, and Air passed.
- Ordered clean-head local reviews: gpt-6.1-sol MAX and gpt-6-astra XHIGH both returned no findings.
- Clean-head native `scripts/check`: passed core checks and all 65 Windows acceptance tests.
- Native installation validation: 65/65 wheel tests and both initialization-order tests after source installation passed.
- Remaining full-check tooling suites passed: formatting 2/2; development 4 tests with one platform skip.
- `scripts/check --full` remains blocked by an inherited Windows workflow fixture failure: the temporary discovery checkout omits the `support.relay_commands` dependency added by PR476 (and latest main also needs the `support.relay_lifecycle` helper added by PR480). The same existing test failed before this refactor. A separate prerequisite repair is being coordinated.
- CI at the original refactor base (`5c4322b9`) also fails Ubuntu (67/916 transcript cases) and macOS (70/944). See [the baseline CI run](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37246745479).

Validation ran natively on Windows 11 Home x64 with R 4.6.1 and Python 3.13.16. Unix compilation, idle callbacks, and transcript behavior require hosted Linux/macOS validation. This draft remains blocked on the separate CI prerequisites and hosted checks.

title: Fix CI fixtures for eager startup and preparation
description:
Update acceptance fixtures and snapshots to match eager startup: startup diagnostics are returned through MCP, idle/startup output is retained in the session log, and the extra native preflight is gone. Update preparation protocol and inspection metadata fixtures, including Windows language selection.

Keep the full diagnostics and exact byte assertions. Use canonical temporary paths, pass `TMPDIR` to wrapped workers, and release launcher diagnostics only after the server observes the UTF-8 prefix. These changes affect tests and snapshots only; runtime behavior and the public API are unchanged.

Validation:

- `scripts/format` and `UV_PYTHON=3.13 scripts/check` passed on macOS.
- Focused regressions passed on macOS, including native diagnostics with a different temporary root.
- Four Linux SSH/protocol cases passed; the Linux SSH snapshot was regenerated on Linux.
- `UV_PYTHON=3.13 scripts/test --full --jobs 6` passed at `94487ec8`: 1,511 executions, with 83 capability skips.

Native Windows and full Linux validation remain CI coverage. An additional local Linux R-preparation check exceeded its cold package-bootstrap time budget.

title: Show ordinary R package installation output in sandbox transcript
description:
The sandboxed R installation regression hid the output from `install.packages()`. This follow-up calls it normally and records the installer output in the public transcript, normalizing only the temporary library path.

The fixture uses a standard tar archive and includes a help page so fixture-generated warnings do not obscure the transcript. Runtime and user-facing behavior are unchanged.

title: Preserve base R errors when package resolution fails
description:
Missing, unresolvable R packages now preserve base R's error classes, messages, calls, and package fields after automatic resolution fails. This lets `packageNotFoundError` handlers work normally and keeps errors attributed to the user's call. Explicit requirements, interrupts, and activation failures retain their existing failure behavior.

Internally, failed host resolution defers to the original base operation. Package preparation runs before the original `library()` or namespace-restart body in the same call frame, preserving native error call chains and lazy arguments. The original `loadNamespace()` body remains intact for packages that inspect it.

Public regressions compare condition details and complete printed errors against live `Rscript --vanilla` references, including `Calls:` output and condition checks after restart. Unhandled reference errors exit naturally; only Rscript's process-exit footer is excluded. Snapshots identify successful exact comparisons, with a documented exception to literal error snapshots so R version and platform wording do not become fixed expectations.

title: Keep one MCP initialization lifecycle during Python startup
description:
When startup outlasts automatic MCP discovery, the Python SDK can switch to `initialize` on a connection that already selected the discovery lifecycle. A later `tools/list` then fails because the response lacks the metadata expected by that lifecycle.

Use the explicit `initialize` mode for Python clients so local and remote startup keep one lifecycle. Add a public regression that gates startup on the handshake itself and exercises direct and sandboxed sessions, and document the behavior. Dependency requirements are unchanged.

The SSH bootstrap acceptance fixture also compares resolved library and cache paths and always exercises a cache symlink. This fixes its failure under CI's shared cache configuration while preserving the remote-library containment assertion.

macOS and Linux CI pass, including the transcript suites and source and wheel installation checks.

title: Use CPU PyTorch wheels for the sandbox autograd test
description:
The [Ubuntu CI run on main](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/34400453875/job/102632451550) timed out after 300 seconds while installing `torch` for the sandbox autograd test. The fixture explicitly uses CPU tensors, but the default Linux resolution includes CUDA dependencies.

Pass `--torch-backend cpu` to the fixture's uv command on both supported platforms. This removes the unused GPU dependencies while preserving the live sandboxed/unsandboxed numerical comparison and its existing timeouts. This is an internal test setup change; application behavior and transcript snapshots are unchanged.

With CI's uv 0.12.4, Linux resolution drops from 29 packages (19 GPU dependencies) to 10. A fresh-cache installation of the Linux CPU wheels completed locally in 9.5 seconds, and the sandbox autograd test passed on macOS. The full local `scripts/check` run also passed, including the transcript suite and source/wheel installation checks.

title: Stabilize macOS transcript tests
description:
## Summary

Stabilize three macOS transcript cases that depended on completion timing, host executable architecture, or live R package-resolution latency. The tests retain their behavioral assertions while handling the exact provisional Python state, supporting arm64e host helpers, and using an isolated fixture package for automatic R resolution.

## User-facing changes

None. Server, runtime, sandbox, and resolver behavior are unchanged.

## Internal changes

- Wait through only the exact `[waiting for stdin]` state before requiring Python evaluation completion.
- Build the manager-observation interposer with arm64 and arm64e slices on Apple Silicon while preserving its FIFO checkpoint and lifecycle assertions.
- Exercise automatic R resolver admission with an isolated fixture package instead of `RcppRoll`, removing dependence on live package-resolution latency.
- Regenerate the affected R transcript snapshot for the fixture package name; logical results remain unchanged.

## Notes

The changes are limited to test synchronization and fixture construction. No production code changes.

title: Test console_tool() through ellmer
description:
## Summary

Replace the R package's synthetic `mcptools` protocol suite with one integration test of its supported public boundary: register `console_tool()` on an ellmer chat and execute an R tool call. The old nanonext-backed fixture could intermittently deadlock CI while exercising protocol and interrupt behavior outside the R wrapper's intended test boundary.

## User-facing changes

- None. The `console_tool()` API and behavior are unchanged.
- The package test now follows the documented ellmer usage with the real checkout binary.

## Internal changes

- Mock only the model's HTTP completions with httr2; ellmer drives the public chat and tool loop.
- Put the checkout `mcp-console` on `PATH`, register `console_tool()`, execute R through the model-requested `send` call, and confirm the R result is returned to the chat.
- Remove the `mcptools` dependency, synthetic MCP server, cancellation watcher, and direct protocol, schema, and interrupt cases from the R package suite.

title: Use separate FIFO gates for polled redraw phases
description:
Give the two polled-redraw phases separate FIFO gates. With a shared FIFO, the second reader could attach to the first phase’s writer and receive EOF when it closed, terminating the fixture during the next poll.

Update the output regression to release the completion gate explicitly, and document the rendezvous constraint for future fixtures. This changes test synchronization only; output assertions, deadlines, and Console behavior are unchanged.

title: Fix startup polling and R shutdown CI regressions
description:
Fix the polling and R shutdown failures reported by [Linux CI](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/38777142835/job/116567948132) after #637.

Admitted polls wait within their existing deadline for pending response delivery before claiming output. If another call delivered the terminal result, the poll rechecks the current evaluation and follows the normal idle path, preserving any submitted stdin.

The R selection and Python SQL startup fixtures provide the system utilities needed by R's normal embedded shutdown and assert clean restart output. Their shared snapshots no longer capture shell-specific missing-command diagnostics. A public regression uses native checkpoints to resume an earlier poll while a later cell's terminal response write is held; it checks idle output, retained stdin, and the next cell in direct and sandboxed execution. The architecture guide records the polling invariant.

title: Capture Python plots at plt.show()
description:
`plt.show(); plt.close()` previously lost the image because `show()` did nothing and Console captured only figures left open at cell end. `show()` now publishes open figures as PNGs immediately, then closes them. Remaining figures still capture at cell end, including after errors; closing an unshown figure suppresses capture. The selected Matplotlib backend is respected.

Matplotlib's internal `pause()` display captures frames while preserving its figure managers and active figure for the canvas event loop and subsequent updates. Interrupts during explicit display unwind the cell, while automatic cell-end capture retains best-effort handling. Public regressions cover repeated pause frames with multiple figures and cancellation during rendering, alongside the original show/close, output ordering, repeated shows, figure-number reuse, and plot-library coverage.

The failing CI also exposed stale embedded-runtime traceback references, startup diagnostics split across idle responses, and Windows forced resolver termination losing its interrupt cause during adapter error conversion. Snapshots were regenerated through `scripts/test --update`; the diagnostic helper now accumulates complete output, and forced Windows interrupts retain their cause while preserving confirmed Job retirement.

Validation:
- `scripts/preflight`, `scripts/format`, and `scripts/check` passed on Windows and Ubuntu WSL. Windows native acceptance had 82 passes and 14 provisioning-dependent skips; Linux passed source, architecture, Clippy, Rust, and smoke checks with Python 3.13 active on PATH.
- Focused `scripts/test --jobs 3` runs passed without snapshot updates: eight applicable Windows cases and Linux plot, setup, activation, startup, SQL, and resolver lifecycle cases in direct/sandbox execution where supported. The complete WindowsResolver suite passed all eight tests, including both attached failures and delayed retirement.
- `uv run --script tests/mcp_client.py` passed: all 22 tests on Linux and 12 applicable tests on Windows, with 10 POSIX skips. The final Linux startup diagnostic and input/interrupt cases also passed. PNGs are compared byte-for-byte with live `savefig()` output; full tracebacks are retained. All four formatters and `git diff --check` passed.

Current-head hosted CI remains the comprehensive merge gate; macOS validation is provided by Actions.

title: Fix macOS marker and SSH input transcript races
description:
Two transcript races failed the macOS and Ubuntu checks for #413. Subscribe to sandbox storage parents before discovering their data directories, so storage created during watch setup cannot leave the worker marker unwatched.

The SSH SQL-first case now uses the existing read checkpoint to hold the controller’s input acknowledgment across its first response. It records the valid partial `waiting for stdin` result, then polls for completion after the controller captures the consumed input. The test still checks live preparation admission, input routing, retained Python state, and the SQL catalog; its snapshot includes both actual responses.

These are fixture and snapshot changes only. Runtime behavior, input grace periods, interpreter selection, dependency semantics, and provider supervision are unchanged.

Validated both failures with controlled red/green reproductions. `scripts/test --jobs 6 client_server/output/test_streams client_server/python/test_ssh_without_r client_server/python/test_without_r::limits_live_python_additions_to_new_idle_distributions` passed 39 macOS executions; the two optional external sans-R SSH executions were skipped because no external fixture was selected. Both affected cases also passed their four direct/native executions on Linux arm64 in a disposable privileged Docker fixture using the installed compatible Linux application. `scripts/format`, `git diff --check`, and `scripts/check` passed, with the standard gate run on clean commit `fa5d4e7dbf6fcae4ac473bcd906eae010f61fb2b`. The Linux fixture was removed and its exact container identity confirmed absent. Full hosted CI will validate the new PR; no hosted pass is claimed here.

title: Keep Console internals out of Python cell tracebacks
description:
## Summary

Make Python cell errors show the user's source and exception without Console's private runtime frames. Runtime errors, import failures, interrupts, and plot capture errors now retain user, standard-library, and third-party frames while omitting Console's evaluator and service frames. Syntax errors show Python's diagnostic and any available source location without a runtime traceback.

NUL-containing Python source now reaches CPython's parser and follows the same Python error presentation path. It still reports `SyntaxError: source code string cannot contain null bytes`. The worker continues to reject NUL in R and SQL source.

## Implementation

The Python runtime records its private code objects and removes their frames when formatting exception chains. The evaluator handles parse and compile errors separately from execution errors, preserving user-created `exec()` frames and Python's source positions. Public transcripts cover runtime, syntax, import, plot, interrupt, and chained errors.

## Note

The optional Docker Sandbox fixture was unavailable locally: the installed `sbx` is v0.45.1, while this fixture requires v0.42.1 and a prepared template. Its existing snapshot still contains private Python frames and needs regeneration when that fixture is available.

title: Preserve cached Python streams in fork children
description:
Cached Python console streams still held reticulate callbacks after `os.fork()`, so writing through a saved stream or a logging handler created before the fork could call back into R. Detach the two original console stream objects in the child, routing writes, flushes, and terminal queries to their underlying streams. Bind these methods without probing stream state, so a closed stdout cannot prevent stderr detachment.

Parent output and logging retain their existing behavior. Explicit stdout and stderr redirection remains effective, including when cached console output is used at the same time. The implementation stays local to Python stream integration; it does not traverse loggers or change worker sideband or dependency-resolution handling.

Extend the existing relay-worker transcript tests with cached streams, an unregistered logger, stdout/stderr files, a closed stdout, exact output destinations, parent reuse, and bounded child cleanup. The cases check for R callbacks and unexpected sideband output and run in both direct and sandboxed execution. This does not extend support to arbitrary R execution or native-extension code in fork children.

Validation: `scripts/validate_runtime_sources.py` passed. All ten selected stream, sideband-isolation, and fork-resolution cases passed in direct and sandboxed execution on macOS.

title: Preserve base::loadNamespace body for pkgload compatibility
description:
## Summary

Automatic R package resolution replaced `base::loadNamespace()` with a wrapper that had a custom body. pkgload inspects that body to recover a private helper, so the replacement broke `devtools::load_all()`. This change keeps the original formals and body intact while moving the managed retry behavior into a private lexical environment.

## User-facing changes

- `devtools::load_all()` works in the built-in managed R worker, including access to both exported and internal functions from the loaded source package.
- Runtime resolution still applies when `library()`, `requireNamespace()`, `loadNamespace()`, `::`, or `:::` reaches a missing package, with the existing bypass behavior for explicit library paths and partial namespace loads.

## Internal changes

- Construct the managed `base::loadNamespace()` closure by changing only its lexical environment. That environment shadows the unqualified `withRestarts()` used by R's original body and handles its `retry_loadNamespace` restart after a retryable `packageNotFoundError`.
- Keep the existing `library()` adapter for failures that occur before namespace loading.
- Add a minimal source-package fixture and a public golden transcript that calls `devtools::load_all()` from the package directory with `export_all = FALSE`, then calls one exported function with `::` and one internal function with `:::`.
- Install devtools with the transcript dependencies in CI and update the runtime and requirements documentation.

## Notes

The direct regression fails against `main` with `could not find function "makeNamespace"` and passes with this implementation. Local validation completed with `scripts/format`, the focused devtools transcript, the complete R automatic-requirements suite, and `scripts/check`.

title: Configure binary R packages for CI
description:
Configure CRAN's native Windows/macOS binaries and PPM's portable Linux binaries for CI, documentation, release smoke tests, and both native floor containers. This avoids the failing macOS PPM endpoint and unnecessary Linux source builds, including on ARM64. Packages without compatible binaries retain source installation. There are no public client changes in this PR.

Set the selected R installation's repository data file and site profile consistently, preserve that mirror in setup-r, refresh the R cache identities, and include R's recommended runtime packages such as Matrix. Phase-status assertions retain the last MCP response, process status, and diagnostic stderr without changing their conditions or deadlines.

Merge PR #636 first to fix the synchronous-client cancellation race exposed by macOS CI. Then incorporate that main revision here and require passing CI, current-head review, and the matching five-wheel/native-floor rehearsal before merging this PR. Both branches include the Windows MXC changes from PR #634.

Repository and action-profile checks verified mirror selection, and the earlier hosted Linux builders installed DuckDB binaries on both architectures. Local scripts/check and all formatters passed on the updated branch. Fresh hosted validation remains required for the final release candidate.

title: Make managed R plot dimension units explicit
description:
Managed R plot dimensions now use `console.plot.width_in` and `console.plot.height_in`, making the unit visible where the options are set. For a 1600 by 1050 pixel image at 100 DPI, set them to 16 and 10.5.

The R graphics bridge reads the new option keys, and the peer tool description, plot guidance, fixtures, and generated snapshots use the same names. Public tests compare rendered plots with Rscript and verify that larger requested dimensions reach the PNG device unchanged, intercepting device creation to avoid allocating the large test images.

Local validation passed: `scripts/format`, focused graphics tests in direct and sandboxed execution, and `scripts/check` on the final commit. Hosted CI is pending for the updated head.

Addresses [OSS-81](https://linear.app/t-kalinowski/issue/OSS-81/make-managed-r-plot-dimension-units-explicit).

title: Preserve optional imports during Python package initialization
description:
## What this changes

Stop automatic package installation from interfering with a package's own optional-dependency checks while it loads.

For example, `rply` tries to import `rpython`, catches `ImportError` if it is absent, and carries on. Console previously installed `rpython` instead. That package contains Python 2 code, so the import failed with `SyntaxError` and broke an otherwise working `rply` installation.

With this change, `rply` imports and builds a lexer without installing `rpython`.

## The rule

While an installed package is initializing itself, its missing imports get ordinary Python behavior. The package can handle their absence itself. This also applies when the package is reloaded.

Automatic installation still works for imports made directly by user code, local modules and Python callbacks, and library functions called after initialization. Explicit requirements still work too.

This does **not** detect `try/except` or decide whether a dependency is truly optional. It treats initialization-time dependencies as the installed package's responsibility: required dependencies should be declared by that package.

## Implementation and limits

The import hook checks that the code requesting an import and the package being initialized belong to the same installed distribution. This avoids confusing local files with installed packages, including local files that shadow a package name. It handles native extension initialization, reticulate's import wrapper, reloads, and package paths retained after live environment changes.

A few boundaries are intentional:

- Packages without matching installation file records and deferred `LazyLoader` bodies remain eligible for automatic installation.
- An already-loaded C callback has no Python frame identifying its caller, so it inherits the visible initializer's context.
- Installation metadata must be valid; malformed metadata errors propagate.

Tool schemas, configuration, R/SQL production code, and the resolver protocol are unchanged. The PR also updates public regression tests and keeps their complete traceback expectations accurate as source lines move.

<details>
<summary>Validation and CI details</summary>

- Public regressions cover real rply, Python/native wheels, reload, later direct/library/local imports, cached Python callbacks, installed-name shadowing, retained and extended package paths after compatible activation, and R-backed NumPy/pandas imports. Supported behavior fixes were reproduced red before implementation; LazyLoader and cached-C cases cover their documented boundaries.
- The non-update owning run passed 81 cases in both direct and native-sandbox modes: 162 executions, including the unchanged mixed R/DuckDB recording selector, R-backed automatic imports, Python activation/lifecycle, SQL interruption, and the hosted restart-timeout selector.
- Snapshots were generated with `scripts/test --update`. `scripts/format` passed Ruff, Yamark, rustfmt, and Air. Full diff inspected.
- `scripts/check --full` passed on clean production head `c8f579b8`: 46 Rust tests, 823 transcript cases / 1,391 executions (572 direct, 570 native sandbox, 249 without execution modes), 83 capability skips, and both uv installation tests. The metadata-validity clarification changes only architecture prose; production and test inputs are identical to this full-gate head. Final-head owning validation at `1653ac3a` passed all 81 cases / 162 executions again from a clean worktree.
- Ordinary code review completed for `1653ac3a`; the connector's actual 👍 reaction was verified, and all 12 threads are resolved with complete pagination.
- [Final-head hosted CI](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/36798975010) completed: Ubuntu passed, including transcripts and both uv installation tests. macOS failed `closed_input_before_handshake_reports_cancelled_preparation`, `closed_input_cancels_discovery_with_blocked_stdout`, and `failed_handshake_cancels_discovery_with_input_open`, all at `discovery survived MCP closure`; installations were skipped. These unchanged fake-R discovery paths precede worker startup and cannot execute the modified finder. The blocked-stdout failure is also verified on main `614971d4`; baseline occurrence of the other two exact selectors is not established. One SSH policy case was runner-cancelled after those failures.
- A bounded production-code A/B and the R-backed resolver-call regression traced the mixed R/DuckDB mutex failure to import-wrapper attribution. The unchanged recording case passed in both modes in the focused run and clean full gate. The failing `4f8d5426` gate and A/B records are preserved.

</details>

title: Compose independent R and Python runtimes
description:
An ordinary Python cell in an R-capable session currently initializes R and attaches reticulate before Python can run. This change lets an explicitly selected or independently resolved Python interpreter start directly, with R and the reticulate bridge initialized when an operation needs them. R-only execution likewise leaves Python uninitialized.

Python-side `r` access works without a preceding R cell. Late attachment preserves the running interpreter, Python objects, selected DB-API connection and data, startup-hook counts, input services, display settings, and environment metadata. R startup packages use the captured Python identity; conflicting later selections require restart. Deferred startup-package plots belong to the initiating cell, and Console tools retain search position 2 after those packages attach. R-side selection callbacks and declarations retain their dependency on R, and Console still adopts Python initialized by an R startup package before its hooks are installed.

The implementation keeps both runtimes on the existing serialized worker thread:

- Prepare Linux loader paths and private worker-lifetime storage before either interpreter starts. Attach R to process-owned interrupt services without consuming pending requests, and reinstall Console services after R and reticulate hooks.
- Route idle preparation, reached imports, and R declarations through one Console-owned Python requirements and activation path. Remove the native-only preparation variant and reticulate-driven tool preparation, while retaining R declaration representation, history, conditions, and protected lifetimes in the adapter.
- Keep SQL connections in their owning runtimes and preserve the selected provider across attachment. Prepared Docker and Docker Sandbox discovery permits R-only targets and rejects invalid explicit Python selections; inspection remains on the execution host.
- Distinguish interpreter initialization, common setup, and bridge completion. Retry safe incomplete setup on the existing interpreter; require replacement after unsafe partial initialization. Worker readiness now precedes interpreter initialization, so fatal startup hooks follow the ordinary generation-replacement path.

Shared public exercises check actual R initialization state and in-memory continuity in direct, sandboxed, and SSH execution, including nested R-to-Python-to-R callbacks. Existing lifecycle coverage is extended for preparation, attachment, interruption, input, failure, and replacement transitions. Implemented documentation and the completion sketch are reconciled. The private SSH/Docker/SBX launch protocol advances to version 7; the host preparation protocol remains version 5. Separate runtime threads and SQL-only operation remain outside this change.

One safety blocker remains unresolved: late R startup is not safe while another thread accesses the native process environment. Console temporarily changes `R_DEFAULT_PACKAGES`, and R's own bootstrap also changes process environment variables before returning control to the embedder. The current R embedding API has no package-selection parameter or hook that removes those mutations. Until that boundary is addressed, initialize R before starting background threads that may access the native environment. The documentation records the constraint; this PR does not claim to fix it.

title: Verify Python environments and fix CI fixtures
description:
Verify the Python environment contract shared by standalone and R-backed sessions. The public peer-runtime tests now check NumPy imports as well as interpreter identity, streams, errors, and persistent state, and verify that both managed compositions declare NumPy by default. Dependency warnings remain enabled.

Add an installed package CLI fixture and exercise it through R's `Sys.which()` and `system2()`. Coverage includes an explicit virtualenv with spaces in its path, R-first and Python-first use, managed preparation, live package additions, and restart. The child command verifies its interpreter, virtualenv, and NumPy availability; live additions also preserve existing Python objects.

Internally, use `::` for exported reticulate calls and `:::` for literal private calls, while retaining dynamic binding access. Share the existing local-wheel fixture between Python suites. Clarify that Console explicitly sets `sys.executable`, lets CPython discover its installation and virtualenv without a PythonHome override, and configures the process PATH for R child commands.

Fix the invalid-image fixture failure seen on [main CI](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/36434318509): after a fatal image validation error, the fixture now expects shutdown and waits for forced retirement. A completion sentinel still makes the public test fail if the malformed image is silently omitted. Exact client output assertions remain unchanged. Regenerate the SSH incompatibility snapshot for bootstrap protocol 5, fixing [the latest main CI failure](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/36437055276); its rejection and replacement-blocking checks are preserved.

This adds regression coverage and documentation without changing runtime selection, managed dependency defaults, or preparation policy. Explicitly selected environments remain non-managed.

title: Warm Matplotlib font caches during Python resolution
description:
## Summary

Matplotlib rebuilt its installed-font index whenever a worker started with a fresh private temporary directory. On macOS, that discovery can add about ten seconds even though it does not require network access.

This change has the exact managed Python interpreter import `matplotlib.font_manager` on the host as a best-effort cache warmup. Matplotlib writes to its normal inherited user cache, and built-in workers reuse matching versioned indexes through read-only symlinks. No app-specific cache directory, cache copy, or shutdown cache lifecycle is needed.

Built-in workers also inherit the selected user `matplotlibrc` as a read-only input while keeping writable Matplotlib state private.

## User-facing changes

- Managed Python resolution attempts to warm Matplotlib's normal user cache before a worker needs it. The host import may create or update user-owned `fontlist-v*.json` files.
- On macOS, the inherited cache is a nonempty `MPLCONFIGDIR`, or `$HOME/.matplotlib` when `MPLCONFIGDIR` is unset or empty.
- Worker starts, restarts, and runtime Python additions reuse matching font indexes without copying them or granting evaluated code persistent writes.
- Built-in workers load an existing `matplotlibrc` selected from inherited `MATPLOTLIBRC`; otherwise they use inherited `MPLCONFIGDIR`, or `$HOME/.matplotlib` when `MPLCONFIGDIR` is unset or empty.
- User rc settings and persistent font indexes are read-only inside the sandbox. Worker-created configuration, styles, TeX state, lock files, and XDG cache data remain private.
- Cache warming is an optimization: a missing or failed Matplotlib import, an unwritable cache, or a missing matching index does not reject Python resolution. Matplotlib can discover fonts in the worker-private cache instead.
- Caller-selected non-managed Python skips host warming, but a built-in worker can reuse an existing matching user cache.

## Internal changes

- The existing host resolver invokes the exact managed interpreter with `-I -c 'import matplotlib.font_manager'` and ignores the probe's output and status.
- The resolver no longer selects or passes an app-owned cache directory.
- Before replacing `MPLCONFIGDIR`, a built-in worker records the inherited user Matplotlib directory and selected `matplotlibrc`.
- Workers link only regular `fontlist-v*.json` entries into their private writable `MPLCONFIGDIR`. The existing sandbox policy permits reads through those links and denies writes to their host targets.
- Runtime requirement resolution rescans the user cache without replacing worker-owned entries.
- The host import executes the selected Matplotlib package outside the worker sandbox as part of managed Python preparation.
- Public transcript coverage verifies host-side discovery, cache-write fallback, reuse by initial and replacement workers, runtime additions, read-only cache and configuration boundaries, and explicit and default configuration selection.
- Test worker fixtures continue to use `uv run`, with uv's cache placed under their private temporary directory and caching left enabled.

title: Keep native R startup tests independent of Python preparation
description:
Managed R native-startup tests also prepare reticulate's default Python packages before reaching their R profile checkpoints. Slow or failed Python preparation can therefore prevent these R lifecycle cases from reaching the behavior they exercise.

Select the test interpreter through `RETICULATE_PYTHON` for the managed R fixtures. R package preparation and the startup, replacement, and restart assertions remain intact. This changes test setup only; Console's public behavior is unchanged.

title: Default managed Python to explicit dependency resolution
description:
Managed Python defaults to `explicit` resolution so the model declares additional dependencies through `requirements.python` before importing them. Users can opt in to preparation on missing imports by setting `python.managed.resolution: implicit` in `config.yaml`. The on-demand policy is named `implicit` for both R and managed Python; `automatic` is rejected rather than retained as an alias. Generated configuration templates distinguish the R and managed Python defaults and use `explicit` in the Python example.

Generated Python tool guidance follows the captured environment selection, resolution policy, and Python requirement visibility. Existing environments and explicit sessions with hidden Python requirements use installed packages, startup-only environments reject later additions, and implicit mode advertises preparation on missing imports. Configuration exports leave generated Python parameter descriptions as `null` so later launches regenerate them; stored description strings remain verbatim overrides. Managed fallback entries include their effective resolution policy while retaining the candidate list.

Internally, managed Python has its own settings default, while R defaults to implicit resolution. The shared policy enum, R configuration classes, documentation, and dependency fixtures use the new name. Public regressions cover undeclared imports, declared requirements, rejection of the old policy name, YAML configuration, fallback selections, launch-time environment selection, hidden requirements, and stable tool presentation.

title: Fix Windows and Linux CI fixtures
description:
Restore Windows and Linux CI coverage after startup configuration and runtime discovery changes on main, and fix Windows startup and restart failures in the companion sandbox runner.

- Advance the sandbox runner pin to `42322a39` from [cobox PR #5](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/cobox/pull/5). Windows omits inherited drive-directory metadata such as `=C:` from target environment variables, while retaining ordinary variables and rejecting invalid explicit names. It retries transient sharing violations for up to five seconds after confirmed Job retirement; persistent cleanup errors still retain storage and block replacement.
- Keep portable startup retry transcripts shared. Compare complete canonical handshakes exactly before compacting fixture write-grant labels; retain differing exchanges and intentional policy variants.
- Make Linux inherited-procfs and root-metadata fixtures deterministic in disposable namespaces, with separate capability probes so root-write coverage does not require libseccomp. Declare the R console wrapper for GCC 15, handle split R documentation layouts, and keep R hidden in the Git-only cache fixture.
- Use portable Windows interpreter paths and preserve the complete early rejection diagnostic for Python 3.9. Install and select Python 3.9 in Windows CI so that case remains covered. Isolate Matplotlib font discovery and wait for joblib, dependency preparation, and SQL completion.
- Port the R integration fixtures to native Windows executable launch and copied uv, preserving the chat, output-clipping, complete raw-log, and requirements assertions. Compare artifact paths by filesystem identity. Add Windows CI R package build/check coverage and its dependencies.
- Compare Windows provisioning records and credentials without including concurrently appended sandbox runtime logs. Keep the native descendant-retirement assertions intact.
- Declare empty Python fixture baselines before prewarming, synchronize cancellation with explicit checkpoints, and inject an actual storage-removal failure. Preserve rollback, child-reaping, worker-state, and cleanup assertions.
- Keep the failed cell's response owner through discovery failure, assert startup observations before normalizing incidental phase labels, and allow default dependency preparation before bounded retry stdin and cancellation checks.
- Regenerate CLI and DuckDB traceback snapshots after the main merge, and prewarm optional Ragnar dependencies before the bounded CI case.

Main at `bf9521c3` is merged. Console's startup-retirement implementation is already on main. The additional public runtime changes come from the Windows companion cleanup and environment-inheritance fixes; the remaining changes cover acceptance fixtures, transcript normalization, development documentation, and CI preparation.

title: Use only uv-managed CPython for managed environments
description:
Managed Python preparation discovers and materializes only uv-managed CPython, so ambient uv preferences and interpreter selectors cannot substitute a system interpreter. Preparation fails when no supported managed version is available. Explicit `python:` selections continue to use existing environments with preinstalled packages.

Internally, discovery uses one managed inventory and environment preparation supplies `only-managed`. Public acceptance cases cover system-only rejection and explicit selection, while retry fixtures preinstall managed CPython before exercising lifecycle behavior. Windows CI and Linux floor images populate the Console dependency cache; isolated wheel smoke checks permit interpreter downloads. The configuration and environment documentation describe the selection contract.

title: Fix Windows resolver interrupts and cross-platform CI validation
description:
Preserve Windows resolver results when a natural exit races with interruption. Record whether native root termination actually started, then confirm Job retirement before reporting interruption. A natural exit keeps its original diagnostics, including when its exit code matches the interruption status.

Windows validation now attempts the local sandbox cases without a provisioning opt-in. Existing setup is discovered through the public readiness command, and missing provisioning reports a test failure with setup guidance. Sandbox provisioning remains an explicit host setup operation.

Internal repairs correct portable fixtures for late R runtime detection, recording path escaping, and the Windows uv executable name. Startup fixtures wait through cold dependency preparation and accept the preparation phase during gated retries; the SQL fixture observes cell completion before submitting another query. Resolver fixtures keep the immediate root exit assertion and bound descendant kernel teardown with an event wait. Public regressions cover the resolver exit race and unconfigured acceptance failing without an opt-in, and the Windows validation guide describes the new behavior.

title: Repair Windows R and Linux startup acceptance fixtures
description:
Windows acceptance fixtures still expect completion before native R initialization and retain older configuration and launcher snapshots. Host R startup settings can also contaminate the raw relay event stream, while Windows loses statements from the multiline `Rscript -e` reference. On Linux, the recording discovery fixture hides dependency tools from `PATH`, preventing startup from producing the expected image.

- Isolate raw relay fixtures from host R startup files and default packages, then assert R initialization start and completion before first cell completion in both partial-command tests.
- Regenerate the Windows configuration and R child-launcher snapshots for the `r` setting and native `--no-save` startup arguments, preserving the complete platform diagnostics.
- Send the width reference program through Rscript stdin so every statement executes on Windows and Unix. Keep the full native-output comparison and close the MCP client through its context manager.
- Keep the gated R discovery probe first on `PATH` while preserving the host dependency tools needed for startup.

User-facing behavior is unchanged. These are acceptance fixture and snapshot repairs; there are no production code or protocol changes.

title: Stabilize managed console input replay
description:
## Summary

Stabilize managed console input replay by polling through the exact documented waiting-for-stdin result when worker acknowledgement does not arrive within the input-report grace period. This fixes the scheduler-dependent transcript failure seen on macOS CI while preserving the existing snapshot.

## User-facing changes

None. Public output and snapshots are unchanged.

## Internal changes

- Use the existing bounded public polling helper for interrupted R and Python input replay.
- Accept only the exact prompt plus waiting-for-stdin intermediate result.
- Collapse scheduler-only polls into the original transcript call.

title: Synchronize Python setup before the startup import checkpoint
description:
Fix the [macOS transcript failure on main](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/38811125443/job/116684307503), where the ten-second automatic-import checkpoint wait also covered version discovery and initial Python preparation.

The startup fixture completes Python setup and pauses at a FIFO gate until its output has been collected. It then releases the missing import and retains the real `py-yaml12` resolution, paused-resolver ping, and environment-commit assertions. Only test synchronization and the shared snapshot's request order change; Console's public behavior is unchanged.

title: Fix macOS CI interrupt fixture and SQL snapshot
description:
Fix the two transcript failures in macOS CI on main.

- Register R input-handler cleanup before publishing the interrupt checkpoint, so an immediate interrupt cannot bypass cleanup. Include the actual output when the retained-state assertion fails.
- Refresh the ragnar SQL transcript's canonical handshake reference now that configured and bootstrap R/SQL handshakes are identical.

These changes affect acceptance fixtures and snapshots only. Console's public behavior is unchanged.

Local macOS validation passed the affected cases in direct and sandboxed sessions, six concurrent repetitions of the R case, all formatters, and `scripts/check`.

title: Wait for SQL connection fixture dependency preparation
description:
Cold dependency preparation can outlast the first `send` response's 60-second observation window, causing the SQL connection lifecycle fixture to assert against a running receipt instead of completed output ([main CI failure](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37869173354/job/113622998637)). Use the existing `McpClient.expect` helper to wait for the exact successful output within the case deadline, matching the neighboring SQL fixtures and preserving the existing transcript.

Validation:

- Windows: `scripts/preflight`, `scripts/stage-sandbox-runner`, `scripts/format`, and `scripts/check` (102 native acceptance tests passed); all formatter results reviewed.
- Windows shared cases: `scripts/test --jobs 4 client_server/sql/test_connections client_server/requirements/test_actions cli/test_config_discovery`.
- Windows after updating uv to 0.12.24: `scripts/test client_server/sql/test_connections::gets_selects_and_resets_the_active_native_connection`.
- Ubuntu WSL, Python 3.13 and uv 0.12.24 with `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8`: `scripts/preflight`, `scripts/check`, and `scripts/test --jobs 6 cli/test_r_configuration client_server/server/test_no_r client_server/sql/test_without_r server_relay/requirements/test_resolution client_server/sql/test_connections` (60 cases, covering the recently failing Linux suites).
- `git diff --check` and `scripts/review-diff origin/main`.

Local validation uses the ordinary gates and focused suites; the full hosted CI profiles remain the comprehensive gate.

title: Fix macOS CI fixtures and preserve startup cleanup barriers
description:
Recent changes split selected-Python inspection from dependency preparation. Startup now keeps cleanup evidence for every stage, preventing explicit restart after an earlier preparation peer failed to retire even when the later inspection peer retired successfully.

The CI fixtures now grant checkpoint writes through worker policy, fault only their intended preparation peer, and synchronize stage exit before suspension. Regenerated snapshots also match the current resolver diagnostic and fail-fast missing-Python configuration behavior.

The startup retirement barrier is the public behavior fix. The remaining changes are test fixtures, generated snapshots, and the owning architecture note.

title: Fix main CI startup races and installation fixtures
description:
Recent main CI runs failed in startup, shutdown, and diagnostic snapshots. This fixes the outstanding failures from [the latest main run](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37044076873).

Server shutdown now joins the preparation owner through child reaping and retains its original failure diagnostic. If protocol retirement fails, it kills the child before joining I/O and reaping, without starting another exit wait. Retiring a worker no longer prints a Python setup traceback for its canceled bootstrap inspection. These lifecycle changes have public regressions that failed before the fixes.

The remaining changes affect validation: synchronize the spool-overflow fixture at controller receipt, identify interpreter generations independently of namespace-local PIDs, use the MCP response deadline for startup waits, preserve current uv and Python inspection diagnostics, and normalize the specific ONNX hardware-probe warning.

Validation: `scripts/format`, `scripts/check`, and 20 focused local and SSH cleanup checks passed on macOS. The stalled preparation regression uses the unchanged 11-second server shutdown budget and confirms child reaping before server exit. Hosted CI is the comprehensive gate. External SSH, Docker, and SBX providers are not configured locally.

title: Recover from denied macOS process-group signals
description:
## Summary

Automatic worker replacement could stop before launching the replacement when macOS rejected `killpg(SIGKILL)` with `EPERM` during a child-exit race. Fall back to signalling the live members of that exact process group individually, then reap the group leader normally.

## User-facing changes

- Worker crash and protocol-failure recovery now continues through this intermittent macOS process-group race.
- The MCP tool surface and lifecycle response text are unchanged.

## Internal changes

- Recheck each enumerated PID's process-group membership before signalling it, and signal the group leader last.
- Exercise the denied group-signal path through the public server transcript and verify that the old group exits and the replacement remains usable.
- Include the complete worker-replacement response in future assertion failures.

title: Fix macOS R documentation CI locale
description:
macOS documentation transcripts failed because the fixture passed bare `UTF-8` to `LC_ALL`. R accepts that name for `LC_CTYPE`, but startup warned that the collate, time, messages, and monetary categories could not use it. Those warnings entered the first tool result and broke the complete-output comparisons.

Use `en_US.UTF-8` for the macOS fixture. The change is confined to test support, with no public API or runtime changes. The existing documentation assertions and snapshots remain unchanged.

Both failing cases reproduced locally before the change. The focused cases, applicable R documentation suite, formatting, and `scripts/check` pass after the change.

title: Fix macOS render and storage-retirement CI fixtures
description:
Fix the two macOS transcript failures on main. Complete Matplotlib imports and first-figure setup before the render interrupt checkpoint, and make the storage-retirement fixture deny writes to its temporary parent so cleanup still fails after Console restores permissions inside owned worker storage.

Changes are limited to test fixtures and the regenerated Matplotlib transcript. Public APIs and runtime behavior are unchanged; the existing interrupt, replacement, and shutdown assertions remain in place.

Local macOS validation passed `scripts/check` and seven focused public cases.

title: Fix macOS dependency failure transcripts
description:
Recent macOS main runs failed because their snapshots depended on uv's logging configuration and DuckDB's response to a missing extension download.

Set the recovery fixture's `RUST_LOG` to `error` and inject a deterministic extension-preparation failure in the SQL transaction fixtures. Keep the assertions that failed preparation preserves the worker and skips the submitted cell, and that successful preparation and restart work afterward. The snapshots retain the complete preparation error and exit status.

These changes affect test fixtures and snapshots. Console's public behavior is unchanged.

title: Fix remaining macOS CI failures
description:
Fix remaining CI failures in DuckDB preparation and startup cleanup.

R and Python preparation now reuse extensions built into the selected DuckDB library, using metadata also available in older releases. This avoids unnecessary downloads, including the Python `json` request that failed with HTTP 502 in macOS CI. Public regressions deny resolver downloads while adding built-in extensions and verify that existing connection and worker state survives. An additional regression pins DuckDB 0.9.2 and verifies that extension installation reaches that provider rather than failing on its metadata schema.

Connection closure now retains an independent preparation-close failure even when it also cancels Python inspection. The regression waits for inspection admission before closing MCP, preserving the failure exit status and complete cleanup diagnostic.

Internal fixtures wait for buffered stdin consumption, initialize R before FIFO interrupt checkpoints, and fail only the first startup worker so replacement cannot overwrite cleanup evidence. Generic and Windows traceback snapshots retain complete errors with current source lines.

title: Fix macOS cache permissions and resolver interrupt tests
description:
macOS transcript CI fails because the font-cache test assumes an XDG path and the resolver grants writes to that path even though Matplotlib uses `$HOME/.matplotlib`. Host-cache resolvers now grant writes to Matplotlib's macOS default, with a public regression for cache writability. The shared-font-cache test selects a temporary `MPLCONFIGDIR` explicitly.

The Python resolver fixture blocks `SIGINT` before announcing readiness and receives it with `sigwait()`, avoiding Python callbacks deferred across blocking FIFO I/O. This preserves the interrupt receipt and retirement checkpoints used by the live-preparation and replacement tests.

title: Fix resolver cache fixtures in macOS CI
description:
macOS CI fails when recording and checkpoint fixtures inherit the default Console cache policy: their temporary files fall outside the resolver write grants. The native writable-root fixture also captures cache redirects that are independent of the permissions it exercises.

Select `cache=host` for these fixtures and place their temporary recording roots in explicit resolver cache grants. Keep the existing exact output, checkpoint, lifecycle, and native-policy assertions. Default Console cache behavior remains covered by the dedicated cache-location acceptance tests.

These are internal acceptance-fixture changes. There are no user-facing runtime or CI workflow changes.

Local validation passed on the pushed head: `scripts/test --full --jobs 6` completed 1,615 executions, both source installation checks passed, and `scripts/check` passed. The full run covers all 86 distinct failing selectors collected from recent macOS CI runs. Formatting passed. Hosted macOS CI is running.

title: Fix macOS CI failures after resolver changes
description:
Recent macOS CI failures come from child-exit observation races and acceptance fixtures that still assume the previous resolver and cache layout.

When a child exits during macOS `NOTE_EXIT` registration, the observer now waits for its terminal status before the owner reaps it. This preserves Python inspection and dependency preparation results instead of appending an `ESRCH` cleanup error. A gated public preparation regression holds status confirmation until registration has observed the exit, checks that reaping waits, and verifies that the same owner can prepare another operation.

Acceptance fixtures capture resolver policies separately from worker policies and select host caches when checking exact native-policy passthrough. Regenerated snapshots retain the current `cache` and `resolver` configuration fields, tool descriptions, submitted program, and complete diagnostics. The CI workflow and its selected coverage are unchanged.

The public resolver I/O and affected CLI suites pass locally. Full local validation and hosted macOS CI are running on the current head.

title: Fix sandbox startup and extension preparation in CI
description:
Restore Linux sandbox startup for root write grants with narrower restrictions by advancing the runner to [the companion fix](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/cobox/pull/51). Missing metadata directly under an unwritable, foreign-owned filesystem root no longer requires a synthetic mountpoint. Existing metadata and nested foreign directories retain their protection. The complete-policy documentation links to the same runner revision.

Keep DuckDB extension preparation independent of unrelated installations in the shared cache. R and Python discover built-ins through a private empty extension directory, then install requested extensions into the captured cache. This avoids reading metadata held by another installer while preserving built-in preparation without downloads and the worker's selected connection. Preparation supports older DuckDB versions and cache paths containing apostrophes.

Keep the sandbox fixtures outside automatic temporary-directory write grants, and retain the original grant directory until its worker retires. Gate redraw segments until the preceding MCP response is collected so output cannot race the empty-poll assertion. Reuse exact canonical handshakes for existing Python interpreters across sandbox policies, and align the three Windows initialization aliases with the current Python selection. Add public coverage for inaccessible extension metadata and regenerate the affected traceback line references. Capture process status and server stderr when a startup checkpoint fails. These fixture and snapshot changes affect acceptance coverage only.

title: Fix resolver startup synchronization in the cancellation test
description:
The Linux CI cancellation case can exhaust its relay checkpoint deadline while launching its first sandboxed resolver. Add resolver readiness and release gates so cold preparation uses the client's preparation budget before the original short relay receipt wait begins. Cap that startup wait at the remaining case deadline with the client's existing shutdown and reap reserve, report a premature MCP result directly, and release the resolver during failed-test cleanup.

This is an internal test change: the client support code shares its deadline calculation with fixture waits, a public runner regression verifies stalled-checkpoint cleanup, and the authoring guide documents that budget. Public Console behavior, cancellation assertions, production code, and transcript snapshots are unchanged.

Validation:

- Reproduced the original relay checkpoint failure with a gated resolver before adding synchronization.
- Reproduced the review finding with a stalled checkpoint: the uncapped wait was interrupted at the runner's 16-second case deadline. The regression now reports its own assertion and reaps an unresponsive server before that deadline.
- `uv run --script tests/mcp_client.py` passed all 23 tests.
- `scripts/test --jobs 6 server_relay/interrupts/test_interrupts` passed in direct and sandbox modes.
- `scripts/check` passed, including Clippy, Rust tests, release build, and smoke transcripts.
- `scripts/format` reported all formatters OK; `git diff --check` passed.

An exploratory full run on the original main revision was interrupted after reproducing the inherited-procfs errno mismatch already recorded as SP-5 in `docs/TODO.md`; a complete full-suite pass is not claimed.

title: Fix remaining macOS acceptance regressions
description:
Recent macOS main CI failures include an R stdin test that assumes the bundled prompt has reached the server before later polls, an automatic R resolver fixture that relies on deferred Python SIGINT handling during blocking FIFO I/O, and a stale writable-root transcript.

Wait for the public prompt notice before checking silent polls, and collect the complete partial-input result. Block SIGINT before publishing resolver readiness, receive it with `sigwait()`, and require a checkpoint confirming signal receipt. Preserve assertions that interruption reaps the resolver and keeps the live R worker and its state.

Regenerate the stdin transcript and the macOS writable-root tool description and runtime observation budgets through the public acceptance runner.

These changes affect acceptance fixtures and snapshots only. There are no public API or production runtime changes.

Local macOS validation passed `scripts/preflight`, unchanged `scripts/format`, a focused `scripts/test --jobs 6` run covering 44 cases and 79 executions, and `scripts/check` on the clean committed branch. The new interrupt receipt assertion failed before the fixture change. Full cross-platform acceptance and installation coverage remains with CI.

title: Fix resolver startup reads and Linux validation workflows
description:
Large resolver opening frames exceeded the existing acceptance deadline on Linux because each byte required a native read. Buffer input before reading Open and transfer that same reader to the input thread, preserving any prefetched frames. A public Open/Close regression keeps stdin open to verify the handoff. Resolver protocol and error messages remain unchanged.

The remaining changes affect validation: resolve installed command symlinks before locating companion files, declare Rscript for the sandbox examples, and use logical CPUs minus one for default transcript concurrency (minimum one; Windows retains its cap of six). Public runner regressions cover these changes. The formatter also updated five existing embedded-program expressions.

## Validation

Linux transcript runs used Python 3.13 and `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1`.

- `scripts/check-core --full`, `scripts/check`, and `scripts/format` passed, including 48 Rust tests. The full runner suite passed separately: 58 tests, with seven Windows-only skips.
- `scripts/test --full --jobs 6`: 1,535 executions across 899 applicable cases passed. The CLI, lifecycle, output, activation, and setup follow-up at `--jobs 11` passed 142 executions.
- `R CMD build` and `R CMD check --no-manual` passed; the check against the final native binary reported Status OK.
- `python3 tests/install.py` passed both source/wheel installation tests in Debian, including relocation and Python 3.11/3.14 SDK smoke checks.
- Installed R-free acceptance passed 90 cases using `tests/without_r.py --execution direct` as an unprivileged user and `--execution sandbox` in disposable Debian.
- Three procfs/root-write-carveout cases unavailable under the Ubuntu host's namespace policy passed in privileged disposable Debian. Host security policy was unchanged.

macOS and Windows were not tested locally.

title: Fix Linux sandbox launch, interrupt routing, and validation failures
description:
Linux validation exposed failures in sandbox launch, prepared-runtime interrupts, font-cache warmup, preparation replies, and concurrent dependency preparation. This PR fixes those issues and the acceptance fixtures behind the latest main-branch Linux CI failures.

Public changes:

- Ignore non-UTF-8 host variables when application policy disables environment inheritance, preserving the trusted helper environment.
- Deliver worker interrupts after prepared Docker/SBX discovery has completed.
- Warm Matplotlib fonts in the persistent cache even when the host configuration directory is read-only.
- Drain preparation failure and control receipts before canceling output, so clients receive the failure reply.
- Grant trusted resolvers complete cache metadata access, including Git checkouts, avoiding races caused by workspace metadata masks in shared caches. Invalid cache paths are rejected before directory creation.

Internal changes map namespace PIDs to host PIDs, check Linux read-only filesystem errors, retain the system sandbox helper in isolated tool paths, grant resolver recording storage explicitly, and avoid rebuilding unrelated R dependencies in serialization/cache tests. Docker fixtures now use runtime-ready notifications, daemon events, and explicit checkpoints, and assert startup diagnostics through MCP. The signal handler also compiles without a GCC unused-result warning.

Validation:

- `scripts/preflight`, `scripts/check-core --full`, and the ordinary final gate `scripts/check` passed, including all 48 Rust tests and the tooling checks.
- `scripts/test --full --jobs 12` passed all 964 applicable case families and 1,597 executions without snapshot updates. This run included local provider-fixture edits awaiting SBX verification; those edits do not affect the executed default cases.
- All 30 Docker server cases passed without snapshot updates, including builds, cancellation, cleanup, and restart.
- Preparation failure replies and resolver interrupt permission failures each passed 36 parallel repetitions; prepared-runtime interrupts passed 48 concurrent repetitions.
- R package build/check passed with Status: OK.
- Both installation tests passed in a privileged Debian container, covering source builds, wheel/sdist installation, bundle relocation, empty-PATH launch, and Python API extras.
- `scripts/format` completed with all formatters passing.

The [Linux CI job](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37361074677/job/111936108295) passed on `12debdaf`, including core checks, Python packaging smoke, R package check, the full transcript suite, and both source-installation tests. The subsequent test-only synchronization commit passed local full validation and starts a new CI run.

SBX login expired during real VM validation. The remaining VM checks and shared prepared-image fixture/snapshot corrections await renewed login. Those additional fixture edits are local; all 12 prepared-Python Docker cases passed with them. Native macOS/Windows are outside this effort; external SSH and the nested procfs fixture are unavailable on this host. Ubuntu AppArmor denies the relocated bundled sandbox helper, so that installation path was validated in Debian.

title: Apply late Python requirements without restarting
description:
## Summary

`session(action = "prepare")` previously required a worker restart for every new explicit Python requirement after startup, even though managed reticulate workers can already activate additive environments through `py_require()`. This change routes late Python-only preparation through that existing live activation path, so a caller can recover from a missing package without losing the current session.

## User-facing changes

- A Python-only `prepare` on an idle server-managed worker now returns `[prepared]` and makes the package available in that worker. Before Python initializes, it materializes the updated manifest without initializing Python; afterward, it activates a compatible same-`libpython` environment while preserving R, Python, and SQL state.
- Failed resolution preserves the live worker, reticulate manifest, and server checkpoint. A later restart reuses the last successfully prepared checkpoint.
- Preparation during an evaluation fails promptly. A call containing a new R requirement still returns `[restart required]` and applies none of that call's additions.
- Caller-selected Python environments and workers already awaiting replacement continue to return `[restart required]` for new additions. Custom workers continue to reject managed requirements with a tool error.

## Internal changes

- Add a structured `prepare_python` worker operation with distinct success and failure frames instead of evaluating generated R source.
- Reuse reticulate's additive `py_require()` activation, the existing host resolver dialogue, and the existing candidate/checkpoint validation.
- Reserve the worker while preparation is active, reject concurrent sends or prepares without blocking, and preserve lifecycle cancellation semantics, including restart cancellation during live resolution.

title: Wait for R bootstrap before replacing an unused worker
description:
Linux CI could report successful requirement preparation and then reject the first R cell with `startup may have executed; explicit restart required`. An unused prewarmed worker could enter native R startup after replacement was selected, so retiring it left the generation unable to start its replacement.

Changed requirements now wait for bootstrap to finish when R is available before selecting replacement of an unused worker. Startup input remains available, and preparation tells the caller to supply it before changing requirements. Unchanged declarations remain no-ops even while startup is waiting for input. Python-only sessions retain replacement of an unused blocked bootstrap.

Internally, this uses the existing environment-preparation admission path and removes the obsolete startup wait after resolution and its unused wrapper. The no-op check precedes bootstrap admission, and changed candidates are recalculated after admission to account for bootstrap callbacks. The requirements and architecture guides describe the boundary.
