The public regression covers startup input before native R initialization in direct and sandbox modes. Its isolated Python fixture now lives in shared test support, so the runner can discover the requirements suite without importing a sibling test suite.

The missing-command runner regression, 22 selected public transcript cases (42 execution records), and the ordinary `scripts/check` gate passed locally with Python 3.13. `scripts/format` reported all formatters successful.

title: Preserve interpreter identity for R and Python subprocesses
description:
R and Python cells expose interpreter identity that can launch subprocesses while preserving script and user arguments. R reports the selected installation's `file.path(R.home("bin"), "R")` launcher through `commandArgs()[1]` and remains interactive. The worker supplies the selected R installation paths and preserves the caller's `R_ARCH`, so the launcher applies its configured default architecture. Python starts with interactive `sys.argv == [""]` and `sys.orig_argv == [sys.executable]`, while retaining its selected executable and environment identity.

Internally, the change is confined to interpreter bootstrap arguments and R installation environment variables. Python argument setup runs once before site hooks; later user changes survive additional cells and R attachment.

Public subprocess regressions cover R launcher defaults, exact child arguments and environment, Python executable and prefix identity, site-hook observations, command/module/script/stdin entry points, spaces and multibyte text, and R-backed and sans-R sessions. A short public transcript shows the R.home launcher comparison and `interactive()`, then Python executable/argv comparisons and an actual script launch.

Validation: fresh release builds; public red/green regressions; snapshot generation followed by normal verification; 56 passed owning executions across 28 cases in direct and sandbox modes, also confirmed on the clean final head by the expanded run. Ruff, Yamark, rustfmt, and Air passed through unchanged `scripts/format`.

The final-head `scripts/check --full` core checks passed. The transcript phase recorded 1,020 passes before an SSH preparation exit-observation assertion failed. Cancellation caused a font-test temporary-directory cleanup failure and cancelled 13 other executions. Both the SSH and font cases passed a focused, non-update rerun on the same clean head; the expanded gate remains failed, and installation checks were not reached.

An earlier expanded run encountered two sans-R SQL startup timeouts, independently reproduced with the base runtime sources. Hosted CI at the initial head encountered DuckDB replacement-failure diagnostic snapshot drift owned by #433. These unrelated results are kept separate from the passing interpreter coverage.

title: Wait for custom worker readiness before idle-input checkpoint
description:
## Summary

The macOS transcript job timed out waiting for Zod's idle-input checkpoint. The case began that 15-second wait while its sandbox worker was still starting. Send a normal request first so the checkpoint measures the idle-input sequence after the worker responds.

## User-facing changes

None. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

## Internal changes

The public custom-worker transcript checks worker readiness before requesting idle input. Its generated snapshot records the readiness request.

title: Record Linux sandbox helper source and linkage provenance
description:
Linux package staging could accept helper-source overrides or skip the helper build while recording the pinned checkout as its provenance. This change makes source and native-dependency metadata describe the helper bytes shipped in the package.

- Reject inherited helper-source and build-skip options before building, including during incremental staging.
- Generate Bubblewrap source, copyright, and build-location notices from the current pin. Inspect the stripped helper's ELF dependencies to record actual libcap linkage; require a builder-supplied notice when libcap is statically redistributed.
- Bind the new metadata and notices through the existing artifact record, preserving the helper's post-strip digest. Release validation rejects missing, stale, or inconsistent required metadata and notices.
- Add command-line regressions using fixtures for clean and incremental staging across all four supported targets.

The bundle layout, linking strategy, and macOS packaging behavior are unchanged. Linux source builds now require `readelf`; builds that statically redistribute libcap must provide `MCP_CONSOLE_LIBCAP_NOTICE`.

The complete macOS workflow passed at the independent checkpoint, and final release and installation checks passed. Linux core and provenance checks passed. A real Linux wheel matched all seven staged artifact digests; its helper remained byte-identical to the baseline and dynamically depended on `libcap.so.2`, with no libcap library bundled.

Linux end-to-end validation remains incomplete: host-side Quarto preparation failed without diagnostic output, and installed-wheel smoke reproduced the baseline helper's loopback permission failure. These are recorded separately from the package-verification changes.

title: Restore Linux host compatibility with native sandbox supervision
description:
The supervision integration required fresh procfs, pidfds, and a host subreaper even where the selected native backend could enforce the requested policy without them. This advances the runner from `d488fc969` to `7aacbcf1b` with the [coordinated changes](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/codex/compare/d488fc969da435f93ea5937c7f284fa91a8c2575...7aacbcf1bca0f173f036617a5ee8ae71e18fb8cc), starting from current main `f35a304d`.

Public behavior changes are supported inherited-procfs execution, optional pidfds, explicit Landlock selection for standalone callers, and native host-helper precedence without requiring an unused bundle. Default execution keeps bubblewrap and the requested policy. Backend or policy failures remain explicit; no automatic backend switch or unsandboxed fallback is introduced.

| Host condition                                              | Before                                                | After                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Fresh procfs unavailable, native inherited procfs supported | Launch rejected                                       | Same namespace backend and policy, with visible permitted host metadata                 |
| pidfds unavailable or denied                                | Launch or retirement fails                            | Native control channel and direct-child waits                                           |
| Host subreaper or process-tree discovery unavailable        | Required for supervision                              | Native namespace lifetime; no child-list or namespace-PID discovery                     |
| Native child completion evidence missing                    | Missing child lists could resemble successful cleanup | Explicit failure; private storage retained                                              |
| Namespace init stopped without pidfds                       | Startup already unsupported                           | Explicit retirement-deadline failure; private storage retained                          |
| Explicit Landlock                                           | Rejected                                              | Direct execution with native policy checks; no process isolation or supervised lifetime |
| Suitable host helper, damaged unused bundle                 | Launch rejected                                       | Host helper runs; selected bundled helper still requires an exact digest                |

Internally, the private control endpoint stays in native namespace init and is closed in the target on exec. Kernel namespace retirement plus the known native child wait establish completion. Packaging builds and strips the bundled helper first, embeds its digest in the runner, and uses native verification of the same open descriptor that is executed. Linux fixture mechanics and capability probes are separate from shared behavioral assertions. Documentation replaces the guessed kernel minimum with measured capabilities and a tested baseline.

Disposable same-user fixtures passed all eight combinations of fresh/inherited procfs, allowed/denied sentinel reads, and restricted/enabled networking, first against the original native backend and then the supervised Console executable. Host process visibility is recorded separately from denied environment, root, cwd, fd, memory, signal, ptrace, process-memory, and network-namespace access. Supervisor configuration and control access remained denied; allowed reads and connections followed policy. Restricted Landlock filesystem policies require truncate enforcement (ABI 3 or later); incompatible lifecycle and proxy options fail explicitly. The [compatibility and security report](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/blob/fix/linux-host-compatibility/docs/LINUX_COMPATIBILITY.md) records the interfaces exercised and remaining boundaries.

Local macOS `scripts/check`, Linux core checks and applicable public transcripts, and source/wheel installations on both platforms passed. All 439 retained Linux snapshots matched their previous behavior. Runner validation passed 223 Linux/native tests, 68 macOS contracts, and scoped Clippy on both platforms. Relocated Linux bundle checks passed eight cases with one macOS-only skip.

The [runner CI run](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/codex/actions/runs/34431093727) passed on macOS. Linux passed 77 runner contracts and 207 native tests, then stopped before Bazel test compilation when its pinned Ubuntu zlib package download returned HTTP 404; later Linux release-artifact and lint steps were skipped. Downstream Linux source/wheel checks and local scoped Clippy passed separately.

title: Cover sandbox status under inherited SIGCHLD ignore
description:
## Summary

Add a public macOS CLI transcript for launching `mcp-console sandbox` through an `exec` boundary with `SIGCHLD` ignored. The case verifies that the command still returns the sandboxed child's status without extra output.

This records existing behavior before broader sandbox-lifetime changes. Local Darwin probes showed that `exec` clears the no-child-wait state associated with explicitly ignoring `SIGCHLD`, so MCP Console does not need to reset the signal disposition at startup.

## User-facing changes

- No runtime behavior or CLI changes.
- Public acceptance coverage now protects sandbox exit-status preservation when the launching process ignored `SIGCHLD`.

## Internal changes

- Add an executable CLI transcript suite and its generated YAML 1.2 golden.
- Enter the built binary through the suite interpreter and a real `exec`, with one argument list shared by execution and recording.
- Leave process-wide signal handling unchanged.

## Validation

- `scripts/format`
- `scripts/test cli/sandbox_supervision`
- `scripts/check`
- Repeated the new case 100 times against both `origin/main` and the branch; both revisions preserved status 23.
- Exercised sandbox, server, relay, worker-crash, replacement, and shutdown paths under inherited `SIGCHLD` ignore; no reaping difference was observed.

title: Allow joblib process backend in the sandbox
description:
## Summary

Joblib's default `loky` backend queries `SC_SEM_NSEMS_MAX` before it creates worker processes. On macOS, libc reads `kern.sysv.semmns` for that query, which the Console sandbox previously denied with `PermissionError`.

This change allows that single read-only sysctl and adds a public managed-Python transcript for `Parallel(n_jobs=2)`. It also replaces a timing-sensitive transcript-runner assertion exposed by CI with explicit worker-admission checkpoints. The test repair does not change runner behavior.

## User-facing changes

- Joblib process parallelism can initialize in the default macOS sandbox, including scikit-learn operations that delegate work to joblib.
- The sandbox's filesystem and network boundaries are unchanged.

## Internal changes

- Add `kern.sysv.semmns` to the named sysctl-read allowlist.
- Cover the behavior through the public `send` tool with a generated transcript golden.
- Gate the queued-case progress regression at worker admission so it does not assume that an accepted case finishes within the fixture's 100 ms reporting threshold.

title: Rename startup_only resolution to fixed
description:
Rename the R and managed Python resolution policy from `startup_only` to `fixed` to describe a requirement declaration that stays fixed for the connection. YAML configuration and the R configuration classes accept `fixed`; the old spelling is rejected without a compatibility alias. The policy prepares startup requirements and rejects later requirement changes.

Internally, the shared policy variant and generated guidance identifiers use the new name. Configuration templates, diagnostics, documentation, examples, and discovery fixtures follow it. Public CLI and R regressions cover acceptance of `fixed` and rejection of `startup_only`, while runtime coverage checks startup preparation and rejection of later changes.

The local `explicit_runtime_requests_and_deliberate_additions` snapshot differs by three Python traceback caret lines on both this branch and unmodified `main` at `0bc2fdb1`.

title: Preserve queued send responses when MCP input closes
description:
Closing MCP stdin while startup is finishing can exit successfully without returning a queued `send` response. Wait for the transport to drain queued input before considering response delivery settled, so these calls retain their correlated responses within the existing shutdown deadline.

The transport now records when its input is exhausted. Shared EOF coverage and a deterministic startup checkpoint exercise requests that have been read but have not entered response admission. The architecture notes document this boundary; preparation and worker retirement keep their existing ownership and confirmation requirements.

title: Fix the requirements client fixture for eager startup
description:
The Python client requirements test supplied an empty R library even though the built-in worker now prepares DuckDB extensions during startup. On hosts without the required packages in a caller library, startup preparation fails and the test's `prepared` assertion fails. Both macOS and Ubuntu failed at that assertion in [the CI run](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/36812647691).

Prepare a minimal real library containing DBI, duckdb, and jsonlite with `ir`, then reuse it through the existing deterministic resolver fixture. Isolate the caller's R libraries so they cannot mask missing fixture dependencies, and include the inspected startup state in assertion failures. This changes test setup only; production behavior, public interfaces, and expected snapshots are unchanged.

The isolated test reproduced the CI assertion before the fix. The fixed test passed in direct and sandboxed execution with both synchronous and asynchronous clients, and the full Python client and eager-startup suites passed all 49 executions. `scripts/check` also passed its core checks and smoke transcript profile.

title: Forward native sandbox configuration without local validation
description:
Project sandbox settings previously rejected values accepted by the native runner and expanded defaults locally. Forward native policy fields and values as JSON so the runner owns their validation and defaults.

Project YAML now accepts `filesystem.kind: unrestricted` and `external-sandbox`, along with native filesystem entries, proxy fields, and other runner options. Omitted or null proxies and default lifecycle options are omitted from the native payload. A supplied proxy object must include the fields required by the pinned runner; the configuration guide includes an updated example and migration note. Tool descriptions report the selected filesystem and network access for both native kind representations.

Internally, Console retains launch-relative literal paths, settings captured across worker generations, and its protocol and lifetime requirements. The restricted application policy still adds host read access and the default macOS extension. Managed worker launches preserve their selected R/Python environment and dynamic-resolution setting when project policy overrides variables or disables inheritance. Application launches also preserve the sandbox runtime marker; the explicit complete-policy interface leaves target environment values under caller control.

Public regressions inspect the runner payload, compare native errors through both `serve` and `sandbox`, exercise retained worker environments across restart, and verify macOS process visibility with inheritance disabled. Verified with `scripts/check` on macOS and focused sandbox configuration, environment, and tool-description checks on Linux.

title: Bound relay output draining during worker retirement
description:
A descendant that keeps writing after the direct worker exits can keep the relay's retirement drains running indefinitely. Give stdout, stderr, and worker-sideband reads one shared 100 ms retirement allowance, then publish the normal stream closures and direct-worker outcome. Complete sideband frames already assembled are still forwarded; additional descendant output may be discarded.

Internally, wake all readers before joining them, make unstarted raw streams nonblocking, and drop unstarted sideband input without accumulating discarded frames. Process-tree cleanup stays with the sandbox launcher. Update the protocol documentation and add a deterministic CLI regression for continuously refilled stdout, stderr, and sideband.

title: Resolve IR through PATH and host uv
description:
## Summary

MCP Console could exit before MCP initialization when an unrelated `ir` executable happened to sit beside the server binary. This change resolves host tools through their documented installation paths instead of treating executable adjacency as package ownership.

## User-facing changes

- Use `ir` from `PATH` when available.
- If `ir` is absent, run `uvx --from r-lib-ir ir`. A PATH `ir` that cannot start, fails, or reports an unsupported version still fails directly.
- Require host uv for the built-in managed environment instead of allowing reticulate to bootstrap its own copy.
- Stop installing `r-lib-ir` as a wheel dependency.

## Internal changes

- Select the R resolver by PATH entry presence before launch, so a missing interpreter or loader is not mistaken for an absent `ir` command.
- Preserve an explicit startup `RETICULATE_UV`; otherwise configure managed-Python resolvers with `RETICULATE_UV=uv`.
- Verify release wheels contain no sibling `ir` and start successfully with `ir` removed from `PATH`.
- Add public CLI coverage for PATH precedence, broken PATH executables, uvx fallback, and managed-Python host-uv selection.
- Keep server-relay transcript releases consumable when the fixture opens its FIFO reader after the release, and add a causal restart regression for that ordering.

title: Queue same-call stdin before evaluation
description:
## Summary

Correct the same-call input transport contract on macOS. When a `send` contains one code cell and nonempty `stdin`, the server now queues the stdin bytes before the evaluation command. The transport order is guaranteed; which read consumes the bytes remains runtime-dependent.

This PR also makes parallel transcript progress visible and changes nearby tests and goldens to assert public behavior instead of request numbering, ambient package availability, scheduler timing, or incidental output ownership.

## User-facing changes

- Queue exact, nonempty same-call stdin before the submitted cell command. An already waiting idle read may consume those bytes first, and empty stdin sends no relay command.
- Document the guaranteed transport order and runtime-dependent consumption timing without changing the `send` or `session` schemas.

## Developer-facing changes

- Print complete submitted and started selector lines while transcript cases run, followed by the existing final result line. This output belongs only to the test runner and never enters the MCP or relay protocols.

## Internal changes

- Reserve the evaluation and register its worker operation before forwarding either command, then attach the stdin writer, flush pending input, and enqueue the cell. If stdin forwarding fails, fail the operation and use the existing worker retirement and replacement path without enqueuing the cell.
- Add direct relay-order and forwarding-failure coverage alongside public R `readline()`, Python `input()` and debugger, direct fd-0, empty-input, and idle-callback regressions.
- Make input-lifecycle tests deterministic by polling only through the exact provisional `[stdin needed]` result, asserting callback release instead of incidental prelude ownership, and publishing detached-child PID data before its readiness marker.
- Omit request IDs from rendered goldens while retaining live uniqueness and request-response correlation checks.
- Replace locked `.libPaths()` mutation, reticulate manifest and `py_module_available()` checks, ambient package-absence assumptions, and independent-pipe output timing with scripted relay results, owned fixtures, live imported-module behavior, and causal checkpoints.
- Give Zod echo commands explicit payloads and prune stale generated goldens during complete update runs.

title: Make procfs namespace isolation probes deterministic
description:
Resolve SP-5 from `docs/TODO.md`: the inherited-procfs regression combined opening a namespace file with entering it, so the recorded error depended on which stage the host rejected. Separate namespace-link access from entry through a validated namespace handle, retaining exact errors for each operation.

Run the disposable driver in its own user and network namespaces and prove that namespace entry works before sandbox launch. Transfer the handle through a socket on stdin after launch, preserving ordinary descriptor cleanup. Drop the disposable host's capabilities and assert that they are empty so the driver baseline cannot conceal a ptrace bypass. Declare the fixture's network capability in shared test support. Keep the fresh/inherited procfs, filesystem, network, host-state, and supervisor-isolation assertions. Update the Linux validation guide and remove the completed TODO.

This changes Linux acceptance fixtures and their transcripts. Public Console behavior and production internals are unchanged.

Validation: reproduced the existing failure and confirmed that the new public namespace-link and host-capability assertions failed before their implementations. Regenerated both snapshots through `scripts/test --update`, then reran `scripts/test cli/sandbox/test_procfs` without updating. `scripts/format` completed successfully. `scripts/check` passed with the documented Python 3.13 development environment selected through PATH and `UV_PYTHON=3.13`; the initial system-Python 3.12 run failed native inspection fixtures and was cancelled. Broader native-platform coverage remains with CI.

Closes #603.

title: Fix CI dependency diagnostics and R completion assertions
description:
CI transcript checks fail when dependency-specific error formatting changes or a cell returns a continuation response before completion. Keep the assertions tied to the failed operation and completed cell output.

Reuse the existing DuckDB diagnostic normalizer for extension failures, retaining explicit checks for the resolver exit status and HTTP 404. Record ragnar's denied filename and platform denial after checking the actual diagnostic and absence of a workspace file; preserve successful store creation under the worker temp directory.

Use the existing completion helper to collect automatic R package errors and wait for Python input cells before checking results or submitting new code. Submit nonblocking calls with `timeout_ms=0` to exercise continuation responses while retaining exact completion assertions, package retention, and restart checks.

Only tests and generated snapshots change. Public Console runtime behavior is unchanged.

title: Ignore custom YAML tags in configuration
description:
Treat custom YAML tags in configuration files as annotations: recursively load their values rather than rejecting the tags. This includes tagged top-level mappings, keys, scalars, sequences, and nested mappings.

Tagged configuration still uses normal YAML scalar resolution and application validation. Invalid standard scalar tags, non-mapping documents, unknown fields, and invalid underlying types remain errors. CLI overrides continue to layer onto the decoded values in command-line order. Internally, conversion unwraps tagged nodes before checking the top-level mapping; there are no runtime or tool-schema changes.

Document the behavior and cover it through public CLI/MCP launches, including validation diagnostics for both `serve` and `sandbox`.

Completed local validation on `67b54604464aa8ef7b95a877d583cac43e61533c`, with `RUST_LOG` unset:

- The acceptance regression failed before implementation.
- Both configuration suites passed all 17 cases without snapshot updates.
- `scripts/format` passed Ruff, Yamark, rustfmt, and Air. An unrelated snapshot rewrap was restored.
- `scripts/check --full` passed staging and all full core checks, including 46 Rust tests. The transcript phase passed 506 executions before an external SSH setup case expected `[done]` but received a running response. The same case failed in isolation; the full gate did not complete.
- The smoke profile passed all 19 executions.
- Source and wheel installation checks passed separately: `scripts/with-checkout python3 tests/install.py` (2 tests).

Ubuntu CI currently fails on two R-loader snapshot references (`.bare.direct.yaml` versus `.direct.yaml`), also present in main's CI at `d8a2beaff3f02db23f3c0b47571a1c1ddca8cb7d`. The external SSH test, R-loader tests, and snapshot machinery are unchanged by this PR. Their fixes are outside its YAML-tag scope. Docker and Docker Sandbox fixtures were unavailable locally.

title: Preserve collected output during MCP input shutdown
description:
## Summary

The Ubuntu detached-stdin case exposed a response-delivery race: closing MCP input could close the transport before an accepted `send` response reached stdout. This could discard an active poll's collected output and stopped-worker notice, or the response to a request accepted just before EOF.

## User-facing changes

- While stdout remains writable, the server delivers responses to `send` requests accepted before MCP input EOF, including a request whose handler has not started. An active poll includes collected text and images with its completed-cell result or stopped-worker notice.
- Shutdown remains bounded if the client stops reading stdout. The server abandons a blocked write after the delivery deadline.

## Internal changes

- Track every accepted request from reservation through admission or cancellation. Retire the worker, then let accepted responses settle before closing the transport.
- Add a regression for a request held between acceptance and admission, plus direct and sandbox transcripts for shutdown during an active cell, after completion, and immediately after the first `send` request. The detached-stdin transcript continues to require its exact stopped-worker response.

title: Fix response admission ordering and integration synchronization
description:
## Summary

Recent macOS failures combined response-write ordering, queued cancellation, worker startup, and detached-stdin readiness with pipe capacity, short negative assertions, and shared temporary markers. This change moves deterministic synchronization into the Python transcript generator and Zod fixture, and fixes the transport lifecycle bug that those fixtures exposed.

## User-facing changes

- Keep every completed `send` call registered until its correlated response is fully written, including validation failures that never acquire a worker delivery receipt. Later calls remain queued until that write settles.
- Prevent an exactly identified canceled queued call from reaching the worker or producing an extra response. The next live call proceeds after the earlier response settles.
- Preserve bounded shutdown when a detached descendant retains worker stdin.
- Make no CLI, tool-schema, or supported-platform changes.

## Internal changes

- Replace Rust CLI timing scenarios with Python transcript coverage and a test-owned socket gate. Structured Zod events identify the request, event kind, worker admission, interrupt delivery, detached-descendant readiness, and cleanup.
- Remove the production test-control module and all test-only environment handling from shipped Rust. The production diff is limited to the response-delivery state machine and focused unit coverage.
- Replace raw-descriptor polling, fixed causal sleeps, recursive marker discovery, assumed pipe capacities, ambiguous interrupt bytes, and 4 MiB input barriers in the affected and adjacent tests.
- Align replacement-startup assertions with the documented ordering boundary between independent stdout and sideband pipes.
- Delay transcript-runner status output until 60 seconds, with less frequent updates for longer-running cases, so normal 10–30 second runtime tests emit only progress dots.

title: Allow Console send calls during client setup
description:
`configure-client` now allows Console's `send` tool without individual approval prompts in both supported clients. This applies to global and project setup, including custom server names and `--no-auto-load`. Dry runs show the approval settings. Sandbox permissions and project trust remain unchanged; managed restrictions and Claude Code `ask` or `deny` rules still apply.

Internally, configuration plans validate every affected file before writing, including Claude Code's separate `settings.json`. TOML updates preserve other tool settings and comments; JSON updates preserve existing permission rules and avoid duplicate entries. Public regressions cover these changes, and the onboarding guide, CLI reference, and help describe the new default.

title: Wrap CLI help to the terminal width
description:
CLI help currently leaves long option descriptions unwrapped. Enable Clap's `wrap_help` feature so help follows the terminal width.

Capture help snapshots at 80 columns with all standard streams detached from the caller's terminal, assert that output fits that width, and regenerate the macOS and Windows snapshots. Document the capture policy.

The macOS local gate and CLI help checks on macOS and Windows passed. Checks with 80- and 120-column pseudo-terminals confirmed that help follows the terminal width.

title: Expand ~ in local Python executable paths
description:
Console now accepts a local Python executable path in your home directory:

```yaml
python: ~/.venv/bin/python
```

Previously, Console treated `~` as a literal directory inside the project, so this configuration failed. A leading `~` now expands using the controller's absolute `HOME`, including in a quoted CLI override such as `-c 'python=~/.venv/bin/python'`. Missing, empty, or relative `HOME` is an error when expansion is requested; `~user` and environment-variable references are not expanded. Relative paths retain their launch-directory interpretation, and execution-target paths retain their target interpretation.

Internally, local path resolution changes in `src/settings.rs`. Public regression coverage exercises YAML selection, CLI precedence, a home directory containing spaces, and invalid `HOME` values. The runtime case runs in direct and native sandbox modes. The compact configuration guide documents the behavior within the Python selection section.

Recorded local macOS validation at `1b9cf5e6` passed all five focused executions and the ordinary `scripts/check` gate, including 50 Rust tests and 19 smoke executions, with no skips. Runtime code, tests, and snapshots are unchanged from that validated revision. Ruff, Yamark, rustfmt, Air, and `git diff --check` passed for the documentation adjustment at `872aac3a`. The full transcript and installation profiles were not run locally.

title: Fix startup restart fixture checkpoint ownership
description:
Fix the startup restart transcript timeout observed in #429's Ubuntu CI.

The native fixture could pause the restart thread after it acquired and released the worker mutex, leaving its own replacement response blocked. Track the thread that acquired the contended mutex and reserve the return checkpoint for the previous owner. Add FIFO gates that force the restart to unlock first, reproducing the failure before the fix.

These are internal test changes. Runtime behavior and transcript snapshots are unchanged. The existing assertions still verify cancellation, replacement input, a single replacement result, and the old evaluation's eventual return without additional output.

The forced regression failed before the fix. The startup suite passed in direct and sandboxed modes on macOS and Linux, and the ordinary macOS `scripts/check` gate passed.

title: Fix CI transcript snapshots and synchronization
description:
Fix transcript failures found in the recent CI runs for #325, #326, and `main`. The failures combined stale handshake expectations with tests that assumed asynchronous input and native stdout had already reached their final response.

- Regenerate custom-worker network descriptions and canonical R-loader and SQL-storage handshake references from the current implementation.
- Exercise startup stdin with `timeout_ms=0`, then collect the completed output through the existing helper. Preserve the interruption traceback, retry count, and exact Unicode/NUL result. The helper can check a completed result with a predicate while retaining exact string checks for its existing callers.
- Gate native DuckDB progress publication and completion with FIFOs. Verify that the server recording contains every native redraw before allowing completion, and retain the assertions for at least 100 redraws and one compact final bar. The Python-only case uses the existing R-free fixture.

These are internal test and generated-snapshot changes. The public API, runtime implementation, timeout values, and transport ordering guarantees are unchanged.

The startup regression was reproduced locally before the fix. Focused macOS transcripts passed in direct and sandboxed modes, and the ordinary `scripts/check` gate passed. Linux validation includes the R-loader cases and the changed startup, progress, tool-description, and SQL-storage cases.

title: Fix intermittent sandbox and transcript runner CI failures
description:
Fix intermittent failures in the sandbox proxy and transcript-runner CI checks.

- The [Linux proxy failure](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/36245707781) mistook a sandbox-local proxy listener for the host service. Linux network namespaces can reuse the same loopback port. Hold three host listener ports and choose one outside the workload's proxy endpoints, preserving the direct-network denial assertions. Apply the same fix to the configuration-retention cases.
- The [macOS runner failures](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/36209513691) included real SDK dependency resolution inside ten-second command deadlines. Use a strict `uv run --script` fixture with the already-prepared test interpreter. Give these command tests an empty offline cache so accidental dependency resolution fails immediately.

These are test-only changes. Public MCP and CLI behavior is unchanged; the two regenerated snapshots only update the embedded probe source.

title: Streamline transcript test progress output
description:
## Summary

Replace per-case submitted, started, and success lines with compact progress dots. This keeps normal transcript runs readable while still showing that the suite is moving and identifying slow or hung cases.

## User-facing changes

- Emit one flushed dot for every passing transcript case.
- Name a case after it has run for three seconds, report it every 30 seconds through three minutes and every minute thereafter, and name it when it finishes or fails.
- Preserve named snapshot update records and complete failure diffs.

## Internal changes

- Start timing when a worker begins a case so queued cases are not reported as slow.
- Monitor initialization and serial cases through the same path as parallel cases, including running siblings after another case fails.
- Add black-box runner regressions for fast, blocked, queued, and sibling-failure behavior using causal FIFO fixtures.

## Testing

- `scripts/check`

title: Fix CI readiness, snapshots, and resolver isolation
description:
Fix CI failures caused by observing Windows input before it is ready, polling-dependent cancellation IDs, and real Python setup overlapping a synthetic resolver test.

Native acceptance tests observe stdin readiness and output through public `send` results within the session deadline. A socket gate delays the R prompt until the test releases it, and a loop-ready marker precedes interruption. Cancellation snapshots retain matching labels on targeted requests and notifications while preserving raw CLI input used by SSH framing tests.

The managed-uv inventory test configures mocked resolution before startup, enables only R execution, and rejects unintended real uv resolution. It closes the client before deleting temporary resources while retaining assertions for the selected version, managed cache paths, and PATH bypass.

These are test infrastructure and documentation changes, with no user-facing runtime changes.

Local `scripts/check` passed at `608c4533`. All 12 Python version cases passed in both direct and sandboxed modes. The new fixture assertion failed on the previous setup and passed after isolation.

title: Fix startup polling and Python inspection CI failures
description:
Startup polls can encounter an accepted cell whose initial response has reached the client while its transport write is still pending. Wait for delivery within the original call deadline before claiming output, so the poll can return the cell result. Deadline expiry reports pending delivery and leaves the output available to a later poll. Ordinary polls and stdin retain their immediate behavior.

Internally, add delivery notifications and public regressions that hold a complete response write across preparation and evaluation, including deadline expiry and retained output. Preserve the exact output assertions. Update the Python inspection fixture to distinguish isolated host inspection from permitted eager worker imports, and wait for worker startup before checking the host-import marker. The public API is unchanged.

Local validation passed on macOS: `scripts/format`, 52 focused startup, output recovery, and shutdown executions with Python 3.13, and `UV_PYTHON=3.13 scripts/check` at `16643319`. Native Linux and Windows validation remains hosted CI coverage.

title: Synchronize startup CI fixtures and runtime checks
description:
Startup-related CI tests assumed that the worker or a submitted cell had already finished. Wait for public readiness and collect complete evaluation output before parsing requirement manifests, inspecting remote bootstrap records, or checking R resource and architecture results. Remote stdin checks also wait for the worker's evaluation receipt before asserting the exact input value.

The stdin fixture waits for custom-worker configuration before input launches the worker, then publishes its startup checkpoint at a test-owned path with an explicit sandbox write grant. The unread-input restart test launches its custom worker before queuing input, so it consistently checks retirement of an existing worker.

The startup restart race holds the cancelled initializer at its own completion socket while verifying the replacement cell and stdin. This replaces native mutex interception that could select an unrelated condition-variable wait and block the response.

The R selection fixture exposes its launcher shell and retains native provider tools while keeping resolver discovery isolated. The SSH preparation test holds its resolver behind a checkpoint past the actual connection deadline, then verifies ping, interrupt delivery, and descendant retirement.

Check the full R resolution error against the selected `ir` executable before normalizing version-dependent `pak::pkg_deps()` arguments in its snapshot. IR remains unpinned and CI installs its latest release. Refresh the sans-R SQL interruption snapshot to match the current embedded Python wrapper line while retaining the full diagnostic.

These changes affect tests and fixtures only. Public runtime behavior is unchanged.

title: Fix CI fixture package lookup and SBX pipe errors
description:
The automatic-import transcript test queried PyPI for synthetic distributions despite generating local wheels. A first-priority local index now supplies those distributions. A controlled fallback returns HTTP 503 for fixture names, and the test asserts that it receives no such requests while preserving the failed-import, retained-state, and declaration checks.

The fake SBX peer now uses ordinary SIGPIPE termination when a rejected frame closes its output pipe, preventing a Python traceback from changing the controller diagnostic snapshot. A deterministic closed-reader case preserves rejection before MCP readiness and requires owned resource removal. The real SBX forwarding path is unchanged.

This PR changes three test files and one generated snapshot, with zero production additions or deletions. Console runtime selection, dependency resolution, and provider lifecycle behavior are unchanged.

Both regressions failed deterministically before the fixes. On the clean commit, `scripts/check --full` passed core checks, 1,206 transcript executions, and both source-installation checks. The transcript run reported 79 capability skips; real Docker/SBX and external R-free SSH fixtures were unconfigured. The four selected Linux suites passed 97 executions on aarch64 using the unchanged compatible installed build, with three skips: the unprivileged-filesystem case under root and two real SBX cases. The owned Linux test container was removed and its absence confirmed. Hosted macOS and Ubuntu amd64 checks will validate the new PR head.

title: Declare R prerequisite for sandbox preparation tests
description:
Declare the R prerequisite for the sandbox configuration-retention cases. Both cases restart with live Python requirements to prepare `py-yaml12`, which sessions without R cannot do on `main`.

The shared R capability follows runtime selection: an explicit `R_HOME` or an `R` entry on `PATH`, including non-executable files and broken symlinks. Invalid selections remain eligible so the runtime reports their errors. A public transcript-runner regression covers selection and skip reporting for these environments.

Clarify repository guidance to prioritize source readability: short fixture strings may use newline escapes, lists joined with newlines, or separate writes; longer programs should use readable multiline literals.

These changes affect test capability declarations, regression coverage, and contributor guidance. Existing sandbox assertions, snapshots, and public runtime behavior are unchanged.

title: Make uv source installs work without manual staging
description:
Make `uv tool install --reinstall .` install a complete sandboxed console from a clean macOS or Linux checkout. The build fetches the pinned companion source under this checkout's `target` directory, so it does not depend on another working checkout or a manual staging step.

A small Python packaging backend prepares the companion before Maturin builds the application, and holds a checkout-local lock until the wheel is complete. `build.rs` verifies and consumes the prepared bundle. Direct Cargo and Maturin builds still require explicit staging.

Local source installations invoke the runner's Cargo build each time and reuse its normal build intermediates. Build reuse follows Cargo's tracked inputs; changing external build tools through PATH can require a clean build. The installed bundle keeps separate, stripped companions and license notices, with streaming integrity verification and no embedded runner payload.

CI exercises source installation while preserving the cache behavior merged in #263. Installation checks cover compiler-flag changes between reinstalls, source archives, and relocated bundles. The R integration check refreshes its native bundle after installation tests reuse the shared target directory. Core Python checkers are executable uv scripts with declared Python versions and dependencies.

title: Reduce CI runtime
description:
## Summary

Recent CI runs spent most of their time in transcript tests and repeated environment setup. This change separates independent validation paths, reuses bounded caches, and removes incidental CPU work so warm runs can finish closer to the ten-minute target.

- Run transcript validation in parallel with core checks and wheel smoke testing, and use six transcript workers on the three-core hosted runner.
- Persist bounded IR/renv, uv, and Rust caches, cancel obsolete runs, avoid duplicate Quarto setup, and keep cache writers on `main`.
- Prefer available public macOS binaries for R dependencies, install uv tooling before R setup, and report the direct prewarmed package versions in the CI log.
- Replace incidental CPU-heavy transcript payloads and repeated package installation with deterministic filesystem and sleep gates, and initialize runtimes before time-sensitive resolver checkpoints.
- Include the repository formatter's sentence wrapping for the release guide and one existing transcript golden.

## User-facing changes

The release guide is rewrapped sentence by sentence; its wording and procedures are unchanged. Runtime behavior and the public MCP interface are unchanged.

## Internal changes

The automatic R-resolution transcripts provision minimal fixture packages across isolated libraries. They still exercise multi-library discovery, in-evaluation activation, state preservation, and stale-candidate restart behavior without depending on ambient packages, remote download and build latency, or CI-only installation. Interrupt and graphics tests still exercise the same public behavior without busy loops, a trillion-row DuckDB query, or a full system font inventory. The UTF-8 console test now splits one multibyte character with a four-byte native input buffer instead of relying on thousands of single-byte reads and a short timing grace.

Resolver timeout, interrupt, and restart tests initialize their runtimes before entering short causal checkpoints so oversubscription does not make unrelated first-cell startup fail those gates. Yamark also normalized one existing transcript golden.

Host R dependencies now prefer available binaries even when a newer source release exists. The gettext setup remains because IR independently resolves newest package versions and can still encounter a source-only release before its binary is published.

## Testing

- `scripts/check`
- `scripts/test --jobs 6 client_server/python_auto_requirements`
- `scripts/test --jobs 6 client_server/r_auto_requirements`
- `scripts/test client_server/sql::interrupts_running_sql_query`
- `actionlint .github/workflows/ci.yaml .github/workflows/r-package.yaml`

title: Prepare built-in convenience defaults on a best-effort basis
description:
An installation failure for a built-in starter package can prevent unrelated evaluation, such as a tidyverse failure blocking Python arithmetic. Console now reports and skips failed built-in convenience defaults, prepares the remaining defaults, and starts with the available capabilities. Runtime infrastructure and packages explicitly configured or requested remain required. Failed explicit preparation still preserves live state and withholds accompanying code. Default DuckDB extensions follow the same rule.

Internally, preparation carries default provenance and delivers skipped-default diagnostics before completing. The combined preparation fast path is retained; individual retries follow confirmed cleanup and do not recover interruption or cancellation. Accepted declarations omit skipped defaults. Plain restart reuses the accepted declaration; reset retries the captured startup defaults, including under fixed resolution. No public configuration fields or APIs are added.

title: Make automatic Python resolver interruption tests deterministic
description:
Linux CI could capture `phase: dependency preparation` in the first zero-timeout response of the automatic Python resolver interruption test, while its snapshot expected no phase. This caused the sole transcript failure in [the latest completed main CI run](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/38058768546/job/114232555027).

Gate the automatic import until that response is collected, then poll after resolver readiness and assert the preparation phase. Both R-enabled and no-R cases use the shared fixture and retain their resolver-reaping and worker-state assertions. Changes are limited to the test fixture and two regenerated snapshots; there are no public API or runtime changes.

Validation on Linux:

- Reproduced the phase mismatch in both cases before adding the gate.
- `scripts/test --jobs 6 client_server/requirements/test_python_automatic_lifecycle` passed in direct and sandboxed modes.
- `scripts/format` reported all formatters successful.
- `uv run --no-project --python 3.13 scripts/check` passed.

The ordinary gate used the development/CI interpreter. The initial run with system Python 3.12 was interrupted because its global `sitecustomize.py` shadowed the native inspection fixtures. The full transcript profile and macOS/Windows validation remain for CI.

title: Wait for complete browser and startup acceptance output
description:
Recent Windows browser acceptance failed after reading an intermediate input wait before all bundled step inputs had produced prompts. Linux SQL startup acceptance also let startup errors race the first SQL cell, making its idle-output separator depend on scheduling.

Wait for the complete, exact browser prompt sequence before submitting another cell. Collect the startup failure for the missing selected Python executable and its idle receipt before submitting SQL, then assert the exact SQL refusal. Update the shared transcript while preserving the complete diagnostics.

These are internal acceptance fixture and snapshot changes. There are no public API or runtime changes.

Local macOS validation passed `scripts/preflight`, unchanged `scripts/format`, both affected cases in direct and sandboxed execution, and `scripts/check`. Windows and Linux verification remains with CI.

title: Explain Windows sandbox setup resources
description:
The Windows sandbox setup command currently lists only options in help and prints only a state-directory confirmation after success. Show the resources it provisions or reuses: the two local accounts, their security group, account-scoped network restrictions, and protected setup, credential, and helper directories.

Use the same explanation in short/long help and after successful setup. Describe UAC approval, reuse of current setup, and the default state directory. Keep `--status` JSON and failed-setup diagnostics unchanged. Native provisioning and the pinned companion contract stay with the companion.

Validation:
- Public regression tests failed before implementation and passed afterward, including a repeated setup against already provisioned state without changing saved records or credentials.
- `scripts/preflight.cmd`, focused `scripts/test.cmd`, and unchanged `scripts/format.cmd` passed.
- `scripts/check.cmd` passed with R_HOME and explicit provisioned state: all 88 native tests passed, including both provisioned-account tests. Source checks, architecture checks, Rust formatting, Clippy, and Rust tests also passed.

Stacked on #530 to keep the CLI explanation separate from the Windows build repair. Initial account provisioning is not exercised by acceptance tests; they reuse the user's explicitly provisioned setup.

title: Fix preparation failure CI tests for background startup
description:
Two sans-R preparation failure tests wait for the server to exit while MCP input remains open, causing 60-second CI timeouts. Initial preparation now runs in the background, so failure is retained as a `send` tool error until the connection closes.

Update both public cases to initialize MCP, check the exact preparation error on a SQL call and a later requirements inspection, verify a ping succeeds, then close the connection and check the exact shutdown diagnostic and exit status. The resolver-close case still confirms that the resolver received `Close` and preserves its cleanup failure. Regenerate the two snapshots and correct documentation that still says preparation blocks MCP readiness. Production code is unchanged.

Validation: both original cases reproduced the CI timeout before editing. The normal focused run passed seven executions, covering both revised cases in direct and sandboxed modes, the existing discovery-failure case, and the DuckDB replacement-failure case in both modes. `scripts/format` passed Ruff, Yamark, rustfmt, and Air. The ordinary `scripts/check` passed core checks and smoke transcripts on the clean commit. Transcript runs reused an existing release executable whose production sources and Cargo inputs match `main`.

title: Route sandboxed workers through a relay
description:
## Summary

Route each macOS worker generation through a small relay that runs beside the worker inside the sandbox. The server crosses the sandbox boundary only through the relay's standard input, output, and error descriptors, using one ordered private JSONL stream for commands and events.

This removes inherited worker-sideband descriptors from the sandbox boundary. It also establishes a transport boundary that can later move from local standard streams to a remote channel without changing the worker protocol.

## User-facing changes

There are no intended changes to the `send`, `session`, or custom-worker contracts. The worker still receives the same fd 0/1/2 and sideband interfaces, and raw worker output retains its existing MCP projection.

Restart, interrupt, shutdown, process-group cleanup, and automatic replacement retain their existing semantics. An interrupt still reports success after the operating system accepts `SIGINT`; it does not wait for user code to handle the signal.

## Internal changes

- Add a per-generation worker relay as the direct sandbox child and process-group leader. The relay creates the private worker sideband, launches the worker, forwards stdin and structured messages, captures binary stdout and stderr chunks, delivers signals, and supervises retirement.
- Use a flat, ordered JSONL protocol over relay stdin and stdout. Stdin and structured messages remain readable JSON, while only arbitrary raw output bytes use base64.
- Retain the two required handshakes: a unit terminal-commit command prevents later worker activity from overtaking server state retention, and correlated interrupt results report whether signal delivery succeeded.
- Dispatch typed relay events directly into the server's activity state machine. This removes the reconstructed virtual sideband, its duplicate serialization, and its publisher and forwarder threads.
- Stop and drain worker transports before publishing relay-owned failures. Raw output accepted before a protocol, semantic, or infrastructure failure remains ordered before that failure.
- Preserve the one-second worker deadline while allowing a bounded relay-retirement period only after timely shutdown acceptance. Outer process-group cleanup remains the final sandbox fail-safe.
- Keep logical session state, output projection, requirement resolution, and host resolvers outside the sandbox. The relay owns only worker-local transport and process lifecycle.
- Document the private boundary and add transport, output, relay-death, shutdown, and synchronization regressions around the existing worker behavior.

## Notes

The relay protocol is private and currently implemented for the macOS worker sandbox path.

title: Add runtime warmup and start it during client setup
description:
Add `mcp-console warmup` to start a configured server, evaluate checks in enabled R, Python, and SQL runtimes, prepare their caches, and report errors before the first client session.

`configure-client` now starts one detached warmup after registration, using the first selected client's executable, version, and launch arguments. Setup prints a PID and persistent log path and returns without waiting. `--no-warmup` skips it; `--dry-run` previews without launching.

Internally, warmup uses the MCP interface and existing startup and cache owners. The change enables MCP client and subprocess support and adds public CLI coverage, snapshots, and documentation for the command and background launch.

title: Expand home-relative configuration paths
description:
Expand a leading `~` consistently in public configuration paths. For example, `sandbox.filesystem.deny: ["~/.ssh"]` now protects the launching user's `.ssh` directory; previously it referred to a literal `~` directory beneath the launch directory.

Apply the same expansion to R and Python selectors and Python candidate lists, worker and resolver filesystem paths, supported Unix-socket paths, configuration filenames, `--writable-root`, and `MCP_CONSOLE_HOME`. Use the launch environment's absolute `HOME`, with Windows user-profile discovery when `HOME` is absent or empty. Materialized configuration retains expanded home paths while preserving ordinary relative paths and symlink spellings.

Internally, share home discovery and path expansion in native configuration capture, including filenames supplied by the R adapter. Update the configuration guides and R reference documentation. Environment-variable references remain literal, and Windows R startup behavior is unchanged.

title: Configure tool descriptions and parameter visibility
description:
Tool description evaluations need to vary the complete text and exposed parameters without changing the server. Add captured `tool` configuration to replace the `send` description, MCP initialization instructions, and individual parameter descriptions, including nested `requirements` fields. Replacement strings are used verbatim; omitted overrides retain generated text.

Parameters can be hidden with `enabled: false`. In particular, omitting `timeout_ms` makes calls use the existing 60,000 ms wait default, and generated polling guidance follows that choice:

```yaml
languages: [python]
tool:
  description: Run Python code in a persistent session.
  parameters:
    python:
      description: Execute one complete Python cell.
    timeout_ms:
      enabled: false
```

Hidden fields are removed from discovery and rejected before same-call effects. Python clients now leave omitted timeouts to the server, so sync/async calls and the Responses, Agents, Anthropic, and chatlas adapters can use the configured signature.

R callers can supply these settings through `ConsoleConfig(tool = ToolConfig(...))`, using exported `ToolParameterConfig()` objects for parameter settings and nested mappings. Unknown or unavailable parameter names and nested settings under scalar fields fail both `serve` and ordinary `sandbox` launches before a worker or target process starts.

Internally, typed launch settings apply overrides after language-specific presentation and validate hidden arguments recursively. Shared configuration discovery and MCP presentation use the same language-filtered parameter schema. Parameter types, constraints, runtime defaults, and worker execution behavior retain their existing contracts. Configuration stays fixed across worker restarts.

title: Configure startup package defaults and Python version
description:
Managed sessions currently use fixed optional startup package declarations. Allow users to replace them through `r.packages` and `python.managed.packages`, and choose a managed Python version through `python.managed.version` before startup.

Supplied lists replace bundled optional defaults; omitted lists preserve them, and empty lists prepare no optional packages. Managed options also apply to the selected managed fallback candidate. Reset restores the captured configured packages and version constraints, while plain restart retains accepted requirements and later additions. Recording metadata and front matter use the same startup baseline.

Internally, retain a typed baseline in the existing environment state and pass it through existing preparation and replacement paths. Without R, check DuckDB availability in the prepared managed candidate before choosing implicit extension defaults, allowing empty lists and false package markers. Runtime infrastructure, automatic resolution, interpreter selection, native startup, lifecycle ordering, and resolver permissions retain their existing behavior. This excludes resolution and trust policies and broader runtime refactoring.

Local macOS validation: confirmed a failing public regression before implementation; validated 64 focused public cases across the new configuration/requirements cases and existing native-startup, interpreter-selection, requirements, startup/replacement, and no-R cases. `scripts/preflight`, `scripts/format`, and `scripts/check` passed. The final focused rerun passed after regenerating the affected diagnostic and new snapshots. Native Linux and Windows coverage remains for CI. Keep this PR draft pending CI and review.

Diff size from `main`, with tests, docs, and snapshots counted separately:

| Category       | Added | Deleted | Changed |
| -------------- | ----: | ------: | ------: |
| Implementation |   194 |      92 |     286 |
| Tests          |   446 |       0 |     446 |
| Docs           |    76 |       8 |      84 |
| Snapshots      |  1382 |       5 |    1387 |

Snapshots retain complete responses and canonical handshake references; the only existing snapshot change updates invalid-selection diagnostics for the managed options syntax and config path.

title: Support Python and SQL over SSH without R
description:
## Summary

Enable SSH execution hosts without R to use the existing native Python/SQL session and the complete managed dependency workflow. Runtime discovery and preparation run on the execution host; the controller retains declarations, admission, activation decisions, output, and recordings.

## User-facing changes

- Discover remote R independently of controller runtimes. Genuine absence selects native Python; invalid explicit R selections and broken discovered installations retain their R errors. R-present SSH behavior remains supported.
- Use remote uv to prepare the managed NumPy, pandas, and DuckDB defaults. Missing uv or failed resolution reports an error. The Console `python` setting selects an existing remote interpreter, with relative paths resolved against `target.workspace`; explicitly selected environments remain non-managed and can use preinstalled packages or custom DB-API connections.
- Support SQL-first startup, persistent Python objects and SQL catalogs, standalone and same-call live Python/extension additions, reached missing-import resolution, exact requirement replacement/reset, empty declarations, and restart. Automatic imports resume the original cell without replay. Accepted environments also survive plain restart and crash replacement.
- Preserve native input, plotting, interruption, connection switching, child-interpreter selection, and controller-side recordings. Remote tool descriptions expose Python/SQL capabilities and omit R cells and requirements.

## Internal changes and ownership

- Extend the existing discovery, preparation exchange, and worker-environment handoff with optional native configuration. Interpreter inspection, complete-manifest resolution, interpreter constraints, and Python-backed DuckDB extension preparation run through the execution-host preparation owner using the existing resolver functions.
- Reuse the native evaluator, candidate preparation, activation operation and receipt, and requirement controller. Inspect candidates and prepare retained extensions against their DuckDB build before activation; commit the manifest, managed environment, and native launch configuration together.
- Capture remote resolver choices and the absolute-startup-HOME extension cache for the session. Workload environment changes do not redirect trusted preparation. Controller interpreter selections, HOME, loader variables, temporary directories, and cache settings are not forwarded.
- Keep shared caches and accepted environments separate from disposable worker storage. Existing remote lifecycle owners retire direct-launch private storage; the native runner owns sandbox storage.

## Compatibility and failure semantics

SSH launch and preparation negotiate protocol version 4 and the existing matching-build check. R-present payloads omit unused native fields; Docker and Docker Sandbox retain launch version 3. Unsupported peers and native combinations are rejected before worker startup.

Preparation failure or interruption before retirement preserves the current worker, objects, SQL catalog, and committed declaration. Following input and code wait for successful preparation or replacement. Successful activation remains accepted after a later import or cell failure; activation failures retain their diagnostics and restart-required behavior. Generation checks, bounded shutdown, cancellation receipts, and confirmed remote retirement remain authoritative. SSH process exit alone cannot authorize replacement.

The preparation connection's 30-second setup deadline ends at the compatible handshake. Discovery and managed environment preparation can continue beyond that allowance; cancellation and retirement retain separate bounds.

`mcp-console resolve` is the intended trust boundary for dependency preparation; SSH uses the same implementation through `ssh-prepare`. Callers trust its results and cleanup receipts. The current implementation does not enforce a secure boundary against malicious package code or worker-modifiable resolver inputs and runs with full execution-host permissions. The repository documentation records this limitation. Enforcing the boundary, including resolver sandboxing, is deferred to follow-up PRs within the preparation command.

Public acceptance uses real OpenSSH and an installed compatible build, including a physically R-free Linux execution host in direct and native-sandbox modes. It uses interpreter/cache paths unavailable on the controller and poisons controller interpreter/resolver commands. Coverage includes offline extension loading with worker networking denied, plotting, automatic imports, requirement actions, failed/interrupted resolution and inspection, committed-state reads during preparation, restart, crash replacement, connection loss, recordings, and retirement.

Validation: `scripts/check` passed on clean revision `fb6623bc`. Focused SSH protocol/control, R-present and sans-R SSH, and local preparation regressions passed **67 execution records** on the review changes. The new delayed-discovery regression failed before the fix and passes afterward. Broader local sans-R, SSH, requirements, SQL, lifecycle, and acceptance coverage passed **393 execution records** on `0b91eb0e`, including **17 sans-R SSH executions**. The physically R-free external host modes passed in that acceptance run; their temporary host is now retired and those two modes were skipped during review validation. The SQL cache-isolation regression passed in both execution modes on `e9d212f6`. `scripts/format --strict` and the complete diff whitespace check passed.

Production diff: **388 additions + 121 deletions = 509 lines**, measured with `scripts/review-diff origin/main` after staging all intended files. The existing shared runtime and dependency implementation keeps this below the requested production-line ceiling.

title: Preserve the latest output during streaming collection
description:
After the old collector reaches its byte or event limit, it drops later output, including the final diagnostic. This replaces that overflow latch with streaming collection that preserves the beginning and actual latest tail. Complete results retain the existing 8 KiB text budget.

Text overflow no longer prevents later fitting images from being admitted, and rejected images no longer suppress later text. Raw files still retain original bytes. Incremental UTF-8 decoding and terminal projection preserve partial characters and redraw behavior across polls and stream changes. Cell completion flushes incomplete characters into the response that owns those bytes. Closing one raw stream leaves the other stream’s incomplete characters available for later bytes to complete.

Internally, a bounded tape replaces the old event queue and renderer adapter. It seals source receipts at output cuts, handles image admission independently, and coalesces image omission tokens during recovery. Adjacent text is coalesced before collection scans so tiny alternating output and diagnostic events do not build a growing list of text parts. The old collector-loss notices disappear because collection now preserves the latest preview directly.

Public regressions cover huge lines, allocation bounds for tiny-event floods, image overflow, prompts, replacement output, UTF-8 completion and stream closure, and 1,024 cancelled responses containing rejected images. Existing raw-file, protocol, lifecycle, resolver, and SDK cases follow the new collection behavior. The raw-preview fixture supplies its own temporary directory so it also runs when the host does not set `TMPDIR`.

Incremental diff: 55 files, +1,722/−1,322; runtime files +466/−991, tests +521/−85, snapshots +685/−203, documentation +50/−43.

title: Prepare managed dependencies on SSH targets
description:
SSH sessions currently require a preinstalled analysis environment. This follow-up to #299 runs Console's existing R, Python, and DuckDB dependency preparation on the selected execution host.

The target configuration stays the same. Remote capability discovery precedes the MCP schema, defaults remain lazy, and explicit requirements, automatic package requests, Python-version callbacks, and restart preparation retain the existing session transactions. A selected remote Python interpreter disables managed Python additions while preserving managed R and DuckDB. Bare runtimes remain available when no bootstrap is found.

A separate trusted SSH preparation owner captures the execution host's resolver settings and runs typed operations outside the worker sandbox. The local server retains requirements, candidate environments, activation receipts, and worker generations. Resolved paths are validated remotely and carried through the versioned launch bootstrap. Native policy validation stays on the execution host, including malformed workload environment values. Oversized requests are rejected before remote admission. Large results and installer errors travel in bounded chunks followed by an explicit cleanup receipt, so confirmed installation failures preserve the session. Interrupts accepted between resolver stages stay with that preparation operation. Interrupts and cancellation reach the remote resolver process group; uncertain completion blocks further preparation and replacement. Worker network policy, local recording, and the nonexecuting remote Quarto export remain intact.

The remote host still needs compatible Console, R, a resolver bootstrap such as uv, and the required system build dependencies. Undetected network partitions retain the existing cleanup limitations. The documentation and real OpenSSH regressions cover these boundaries, including controller runtime traps, failed preparation and activation, concurrent control, output backpressure, and setup deadlines.

`scripts/check` passed on macOS, including the capability-applicable transcript suite and source/wheel installation checks. The capability-applicable transcript suite passed on Linux with six concurrent cases. A macOS controller also exercised managed R, Python, DuckDB, and restart reuse on a separate Linux target in both direct and sandboxed modes. The Linux transcript run skipped two nested procfs cases, and the optional external target policy fixture was not enabled. Full Linux repository checks run in CI.

title: Retain SQL results for bounded retrieval in R and Python
description:
SQL previews now retain their result so callers can retrieve the data in R or Python without rerunning the query. `.console$sql_last_result(n = 100)` and `_console.sql_last_result(n=100)` return successive rows, including all columns and full values. Omitting `n` retrieves all remaining rows into memory. R returns a data frame; Python returns a dictionary with native `rows` and ordered `columns`. Types and precision follow the driver.

Console keeps only the latest SQL result and manages cleanup on exhaustion, a new SQL cell, a connection change, or a retrieval error or interrupt. Data already returned remains usable. Connections and transactions keep their existing ownership.

Internally, managed R DuckDB uses Arrow batches for bounded fetching, then DuckDB's own R conversions. This temporary workaround is isolated for removal once supported DuckDB R versions include [streaming data-frame results](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb-r/pull/2587). Selected DBI connections already fetch data frames directly.

title: Simplify the public configuration format
description:
Make `config.yaml` a small human interface to the pinned sandbox runner. The previous format exposed native switches whose combinations could be contradictory or ineffective.

The public format uses grouped filesystem paths, scalar network choices or a managed-proxy mapping, mode-specific SOCKS settings, and one Unix-socket selector. Worker and resolver permissions use the same schema independently. Top-level environment values also reach dependency preparation; resolver overrides and Console-owned adjustments retain their precedence. Settings are captured once for preparation and worker restarts.

This deliberately removes public profiles, native-shaped fields, camelCase aliases, and raw options. Invalid settings fail with a configuration path, including incompatible limited-mode SOCKS settings, host-with-port rules, and malformed scoped IP literals. The configuration, sandbox, and resolver guides include short examples, defaults, native mappings, migration guidance, and platform limitations. Generated [YAML transcripts](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/tree/feat/simple-configuration/tests/snapshots/cli/test_public_configuration) pair user configuration with complete native policies; layered cases include a third document showing CLI overrides.

Internally, one normalization path validates the final file/CLI document, chooses variants, supplies process defaults, and compiles native settings. Explicit scalar networking clears the resolver's default proxy; explicit domain and resolver-filesystem mappings replace generated defaults. The worker retains its host-read/private-write baseline without workspace writes or metadata read grants beneath explicit denials. Default resolver cache grants preserve native metadata protections at each cache root; nested Git dependency builds use ordinary cache grants. Missing resolver cache homes produce an actionable error before preparation. The generic merge algorithm, complete-native-policy transport, runner fork, and dependency pin are unchanged.

Native macOS fixtures exercise limited-mode GET, rejected POST and CONNECT, destination deny precedence, filesystem protections, separate local/socket exceptions, and actual uv Git builds with both cache selections. A causal UDP fixture records this pin sending replies back to the destination; explicit `tcp_udp` requests are rejected. Windows managed proxies and explicit sandboxed resolver preparation, and nonempty Linux Unix-socket path allowlists, are rejected rather than weakened. Remaining native filesystem, socket, and local-binding limitations are documented.

Local macOS validation passes the focused configuration, filesystem, cache, and proxy suites, plus `scripts/check`. Windows acceptance shares the public policy fixtures; native Linux/Windows execution has not been rerun locally. Windows diagnostic transcript regeneration remains pending.

title: Guide language selection and include SQLite by default
description:
The `send` description now gives concrete language-selection criteria before execution instructions: DuckDB SQL for structured data inspection and queries, R for vectorized operations, statistics, and plots, and Python when its libraries simplify the task. It also describes direct file access, built-in JSON support, read-only SQLite attachment, extension preparation, and bounded SQL previews. This makes those capabilities easier for agents to discover during investigations.

SQLite is now a default DuckDB extension in managed local and SSH sessions, with or without R. Requirements inspection and reset include `sqlite`; exact declaration replacements can still remove it. The tool guidance uses the startup declaration to distinguish built-in defaults from custom workers that require explicit preparation, reflects the available languages and preparation support, and recommends switching only when multiple languages are enabled.

Internally, sessions without R prepare SQLite through the existing execution-host resolver before MCP readiness and require an absolute `HOME` for the shared extension cache. Local and SSH startup failures wait for the preparation close result and report any cleanup failure alongside the original error. Documentation and public transcripts cover default SQLite queries with automatic extension installation disabled, declaration changes, custom-worker guidance, and local and SSH execution. Custom-worker transcripts share a dedicated handshake snapshot. Python bridge fixtures now supply reticulate's default NumPy dependency, eliminating a CI failure caused by warnings that depended on uv cache contents.

title: Run built-in sessions on SSH targets
description:
Run the built-in console on one configured SSH host while keeping the MCP session, output handling, and recordings local. This lets users reuse an existing OpenSSH alias and a provisioned remote R/Python/SQL environment.

The local project configuration accepts `target.transport.kind: ssh`, `target.transport.host`, a required existing absolute `target.workspace`, and an optional `target.command` argv prefix that defaults to `uvx mcp-console`. Permission policy remains independent of placement, including with `serve --no-sandbox`, which now parses project YAML to select the target. Standalone `sandbox` commands remain local. Session metadata and source-only Quarto exports identify remote execution separately from local recording.
