Internally, a bounded bootstrap carries the captured policy and launch parameters over SSH. A compatibility check precedes worker startup, and a remote helper owns the ordinary public sandbox launcher while the existing runner retains enforcement and descendant cleanup. Relay messages remain unchanged inside the transport envelope. Replacement requires confirmed remote retirement; a broken transport cannot trigger cell replay or an overlapping replacement.

SSH uses preinstalled runtimes without controller interpreter discovery, managed defaults, or resolver callbacks. Remote dependency preparation, reconnect/resume, and network-partition leases are deferred. Cleanup after a partition can be delayed until SSH detects the broken connection.

title: Record MCP console session transcripts
description:
## Summary

Persist each `serve` run under `.mcp-console/sessions/<UTC-start>-<pid>/`. The append-only JSONL journal makes MCP tool calls, results, timing, and image artifacts inspectable and reconstructable without changing MCP responses.

## User-facing changes

- Record ordinary `send` and `session` calls as schema-versioned `session_started`, `tool_call`, `artifact_created`, and `tool_result` events.
- Save image bytes as relative artifacts as soon as the worker emits them, including before a later poll.
- Fail startup when the run record cannot be created, and reject later tool calls after a recording failure to avoid extending a partial journal.
- Document that submitted code, stdin, and returned output are stored without redaction. The generated Quarto projection and complete output spools remain future work.

## Internal changes

- Override the MCP tool-call boundary to retain request IDs, normalized parameters, results, and errors.
- Carry artifact references through worker evaluation output while preserving inline MCP image blocks and restart generation checks.
- Isolate test server working directories and add deterministic Zod coverage for live flushes, image persistence across polling, tool errors, and terminal recording failures.
- Include a normalized literal `events.jsonl` and binary image in the golden set so the produced session layout is directly reviewable.

title: Add explicit session restart
description:
## Summary

Expose explicit worker restart through the MCP `session` tool so clients can replace a runtime without relying on crash recovery. Restart retains prepared Python requirements, discards worker-owned runtime state and unread stdin, and returns after the replacement reports ready.

## User-facing changes

- Accept `session({"action":"restart"})` and return `[restarted]` after the new worker is ready.
- Close worker stdin and send the sideband shutdown message before escalating to process-group termination at the existing one-second deadline.
- Preserve prepared Python requirements across restart while clearing R, Python, SQL, debugger, and unread-stdin state.
- Reject requirements supplied with restart for now, and document the current restart and standard-stream boundary semantics.

## Internal changes

- Add generation-aware lifecycle admission so evaluations and stdin writes accepted before restart cannot reach the replacement worker.
- Reuse the existing event-driven shutdown path and retain its forced-stop behavior for unresponsive workers.
- Add public behavior transcripts and paired MITM goldens. Explicit restart records evaluated code, sideband shutdown, worker-stdin EOF, worker-sideband EOF, and replacement evaluation. Automatic recovery records a real worker `SIGSEGV`, worker-sideband EOF, replacement startup, state loss, and successful evaluation.

title: Add Markdown and Quarto session projections
description:
## Summary

Recorded sessions now include two Yamark-formatted projections beside the authoritative JSONL event journal:

- `transcript.md` is an append-only record of submitted actions, runtime results, errors, and artifact links.
- `transcript.qmd` is an executable, source-only sequence of submitted R, Python, and SQL cells.

Running `ir render transcript.qmd` re-executes those cells using the recorded working directory, submitted requirements, and reticulate's default Python selection. The direction is for that render to reproduce the analysis represented by `transcript.md`, while accepting that exact reproduction is not yet possible for every runtime detail.

## User-facing changes

- Create private `transcript.md` and `transcript.qmd` files on the first recorded `send`.
- Emit executable `{r}`, `{python}`, and `{sql}` Quarto cells without recorded output or artifacts.
- Include MCP Console's built-in and cumulative submitted R and Python requirements in IR front matter without selecting a Python version.
- Preserve submitted source and result text inside dynamically sized fences.
- Prevent leading Quarto option comments, including indented `#|` and `--|` comments, from changing replay behavior.
- Escape YAML-disallowed control characters in front-matter values.
- Keep the JSONL journal authoritative if the derived document pair cannot be updated.
- Execute rendered source outside the MCP Console worker sandbox. Render only trusted code.

## Internal changes

- Flush each JSONL event before updating the derived documents.
- Append Markdown fragments in place and atomically replace the complete QMD from incremental source and requirement state without rereading the journal.
- Extend transcript goldens with exact `.md` and `.qmd` companions.
- Exercise a real R, Python, and SQL session with an image artifact, verify Yamark formatting, and render generated R and Python cells through IR.
- Make transcript-runner progress assertions scheduler-independent and poll through only the documented provisional runtime response in the timing-sensitive fd 0 regression.

## Limitations

The QMD records submitted declarations rather than an exact environment lockfile. Automatically inferred requirements and DuckDB extension declarations are not included. SQL cells require the document user to provide a DBI connection.

title: Add inline session control to send
description:
## Summary

Add optional inline session control to `send` so callers can interrupt or restart and then provide stdin, requirements, and one cell under one lifecycle admission boundary. This removes multi-call coordination for the common controlled-cell flow while retaining `session` for standalone prepare, interrupt, and restart operations.

## User-facing changes

- Add `send.control` with exactly `interrupt` and `restart`.
- Order inline interrupt as control, stdin enqueue, a 100-millisecond grace, requirements, then evaluation; skip the cell if the previous evaluation remains active.
- Resolve restart requirements before replacement, then route same-call stdin and the cell only to the replacement.
- Start `timeout_ms` after cell dispatch or attachment. A control-only interrupt uses the requested wait after its grace, while a rejected same-call cell is not queued or waited for.
- Preserve prior terminal markers and complete worker-stop diagnostics in controlled responses; report replacement idle only after same-call stdin is accepted.
- Document the current two-tool surface and controlled response behavior.

## Internal changes

- Reserve controlled sends across lifecycle control, generation checks, requirement preparation, and optional evaluation admission.
- Generalize evaluation response reservation so prior output, lifecycle notices, new output, and final state retain one delivery owner across cancellation or write failure.
- Use one failure projection for output-tape and direct controlled failures so worker outcomes and state-loss notices cannot be dropped.
- Preserve standalone resolver-first interruption while allowing it to reach an active evaluation during inline control.
- Add deterministic built-in, custom-worker, and server-relay regressions for ordering, fresh state, timeout, requirement failure, active interruption, response reclamation, terminal markers, and failure details.
- Make transcript-runner progress regressions causal with one bounded dual-stream fixture, and use fixture-local thresholds so scheduler load does not change their assertions.

title: Cancel managed console reads on interrupt
description:
Allows `session(action = "interrupt")` to cancel managed console reads without restarting the worker. R `readline()` and reticulate-backed Python `input()` or debugger prompts unwind through their normal runtime interrupt handling, while direct fd-0 readers remain unchanged.

## User-facing changes

- Cancels blocked managed R and Python console reads and clears the provisional input state, so completed responses do not retain a stale `[stdin needed]` banner.
- Preserves partial input for the next managed console read, including lines larger than R's console buffer and interrupts that unwind between callbacks.
- Keeps the worker available when R, Python, or DuckDB handles an interrupt normally, including repeated interrupts without losing cross-language state.

## Internal changes

- Adds the `input_cancelled` worker frame and routes it through the continuous activity reader.
- Polls R's pending-interrupt flag while managed console input waits, then checks the interrupt from a C-owned frame after Rust has unwound.
- Returns unfinished managed input to replay storage at evaluation and R input-handler boundaries.
- Expands deterministic transcripts for native R, Python bytecode and blocking calls, Python-to-R calls, managed input, R boundary callbacks, and repeated DuckDB queries.
- Documents transcript goldens as generated files and preserves whitespace-only YAML scalar values during regeneration.

## Testing

- `scripts/check`

title: Avoid reticulate proxy races during Python evaluation
description:
Prevents an interrupt near reticulate result conversion from turning a normal Python interrupt into a bridge failure and worker replacement. Python cells now use one direct-conversion dispatcher while retaining persistent `__main__` state and existing output behavior.

## User-facing changes

- Python interrupts near result conversion no longer discard the worker or its in-memory state.
- Managed and caller-selected interpreters must provide Python 3.10 or later. Older interpreters are rejected before the first Python cell runs.
- Rebinding ordinary globals such as `__import__`, `exec`, and `setattr`, or changing `builtins.__import__`, does not replace bridge dispatch.
- Python tracebacks, final-expression display, persistent globals, R plots, and Matplotlib capture retain their existing behavior.

## Internal changes

- Bridge helpers live in the reserved `_mcp_console` module in `sys.modules`; the bridge does not add or remove `__main__` bindings during dispatch.
- A reserved `_mcp_console_dispatch` builtins entry provides the stable callable used by one fixed, direct-converting `py_eval()` expression.
- R passes source and filenames as values instead of assembling Python calls with repeated `paste0()` or JSON-encoded arguments.
- Interrupted runtime initialization remains retryable without duplicating the Matplotlib load hook or logging filter.
- Cell-scoped image state remains private and is drained after normal results, Python errors, and interrupts.
- The Zod SIGINT fixture uses bounded polling instead of `signal.pause()`, avoiding a lost wakeup in the interrupt acceptance test.

## Testing

- `scripts/check`

title: Add SIGINT support for live console workers
description:
Adds `session(action = "interrupt")` so a client can request `SIGINT` without restarting the live console worker and discarding its in-memory state.

## User-facing changes

- `session` accepts `action = "interrupt"` without requirements and returns `[interrupt sent]` after signaling a live worker. It does not start the lazy worker.
- R, Python, and SQL retain their native interrupt behavior. Evaluated code can catch or delay the signal, and the worker remains available when the runtime handles it normally.
- Interrupts remain best effort. `restart` is still the bounded recovery path for code that does not return.

## Internal changes

- The server signals the registered worker PID directly and never redirects a delayed request to a replacement process.
- The worker normalizes `SIGINT` before R initializes and checks only pending interrupts at managed cell boundaries.
- Worker-owned graphics, Python checkpoint, and preparation work defer interrupt handling until their cleanup completes. R boundary callbacks remain interruptible.
- Python and SQL bridges preserve escaping interrupt conditions as normal runtime outcomes instead of treating them as infrastructure failures.
- Public transcript cases cover direct delivery, runtime recovery, R boundary callbacks, bridge propagation, and the idle-boundary race.
- R input-handler transcripts use FIFO readiness barriers instead of timer sleeps, so cell-boundary ordering is deterministic.

title: Prepare DuckDB extensions in managed sans-R sessions
description:
## Summary

Enable explicit DuckDB extension preparation for local sans-R sessions with Console-managed Python. A worker can load an extension from its cache after host preparation, including when worker network access is disabled.

## User-facing changes

- `requirements.duckdb` now supports `get`, `add`, `set`, and `reset` with the existing startup and explicit-restart workflow. A changed declaration on a running worker requires restart; an unchanged declaration remains a no-op. No extensions are added to the sans-R defaults.
- Python and extension requirements can be prepared together before the first Python or SQL cell. A restart that changes Python prepares every retained extension for the new DuckDB build, even when the names are unchanged.
- Failed or interrupted preparation keeps the current worker, Python objects, SQL catalog, and committed requirements. A missing DuckDB package produces guidance to include `duckdb` in `requirements.python`.

## Internal changes

- The hidden local `resolve` subprocess runs the accepted or candidate environment's Python in isolated mode and calls its DuckDB extension installation API with validated names. It retains the existing resolver cancellation, output, and cleanup ownership. Preparation runs with trusted host permissions and uses DuckDB's default repository and signature checks.
- With an absolute startup `HOME`, the managed worker receives the captured shared extension-cache directory for its DuckDB version and platform. Spill and stored secrets remain in disposable worker storage; retirement leaves shared extension caches intact.
- Public MCP transcripts cover downloadable `fts` preparation and `LOAD` with worker network access denied in direct and native-sandbox modes, combined preparation, a DuckDB version change, requirement actions, failed and interrupted preparation, and restart and crash replacement.

## Limits

Console does not add live extension changes or SQL-triggered installation. An absolute startup `HOME` is required for explicit extension preparation; managed Python still starts without one. Explicitly selected Python environments can use preinstalled extensions and custom connections but do not get host extension preparation. R-backed, SSH, and prepared-target behavior is unchanged. Downloads already cached may remain after a failed preparation.

## Validation

Focused public sans-R SQL, DuckDB requirement, requirement-action, restart, and `HOME`-unset startup transcripts passed in direct and native-sandbox modes. `scripts/validate_runtime_sources.py` and the standard `scripts/check` gate passed. `scripts/review-diff origin/main` reports 284 production additions and 15 deletions, or 299 changed production lines.

title: Enable SQL cells in local Python sessions without R
description:
## Summary

Local Python sessions without R now accept SQL cells through the existing SQL router and Python DB-API adapter. The worker opens a private, in-memory DuckDB connection on first use. `sql_connection()` returns the active SQL connection; `console_sql_connection(connection)` selects a user-owned DB-API connection, and `console_sql_connection(None)` restores the same managed DuckDB catalog without closing the user connection. Python data frames require explicit registration. R-present SQL keeps its existing provider behavior.

Managed sans-R Python defaults now include DuckDB. Startup and restart resolve it through the existing hidden resolver and accepted-environment transaction. `get` reports the accepted declaration, `reset` restores defaults, and `set` retains exactly the requested declaration, including an empty one. Explicit Python environments remain unmanaged and can use preinstalled DuckDB or a custom connection. Missing DuckDB produces an actionable SQL error while Python and custom connections remain usable.

The managed connection places spill and persistent-secret storage in the worker's private temporary directory. Restart and crash replacement create a fresh catalog while retaining the accepted Python environment. The sans-R MCP schema, descriptions, and recordings now expose SQL where language settings permit it; R cells, R requirements, and DuckDB extension preparation remain unavailable.

Production diff: 161 additions and 39 deletions, 200 changed lines, measured with `scripts/review-diff origin/main` after staging new files.

## Validation

- `scripts/check` passed: runtime source validation, architecture, Rust formatting, Clippy, Rust tests, and smoke transcripts.
- `scripts/test client_server/sql/test_without_r client_server/sql/test_connections::recovers_when_python_dbapi_connection_raises_base_exception client_server/sql/test_connections::interrupts_python_dbapi_provider_probe` passed in applicable direct and native-sandbox modes. The new public MCP suite uses an installed build without R and covers SQL-first startup, shared state, provider switching, bounded previews, errors, interruption, restart, failed preparation, requirement actions, and storage cleanup.
- `scripts/test --jobs 4 client_server/sql/test_catalog client_server/sql/test_connections client_server/requirements/test_actions client_server/requirements/test_python client_server/python/test_lifecycle` passed for existing SQL, requirements, Python, and lifecycle behavior.
- `scripts/test client_server/python/test_without_r` passed.
- `scripts/format` passed.

title: Give sandboxed R sessions a writable temporary library
description:
## User-facing changes

Sandboxed built-in R sessions may have an unwritable first library. Each worker now prepends a writable directory inside R's `tempdir()`, so `install.packages()` can use its default `lib` destination. The directory is recreated after restart. R's `library()` listing warns while the directory is empty.

## Internal changes

The R environment bridge keeps the temporary library ahead of managed R libraries during live preparation. Direct sessions retain their existing library order. Public transcript cases cover a local source installation, restart, and managed library transitions; the runtime docs describe the library's lifetime and installation prerequisites.

title: Prepare Python requirements in local sessions without R
description:
Local Python sessions without R can prepare explicit dependencies before first use or during an explicit restart. They reuse the existing host resolver and session-environment transaction, so failed preparation preserves the running worker and its objects.

With `python` unset, Console selects uv from startup `PATH` and uses its normal configuration, cache, and Python installations. Named Python requirements work alone or with a cell before the first worker starts, and with restart both with and without code. Requirements accumulate from the NumPy/pandas defaults; inspection, replacement, reset, Python-version constraints, and publication cutoffs use the existing requirements actions. Changed live requirements require restart. No-op additions, plain restarts, and crash replacement reuse the accepted environment. Live activation, automatic import installation, R requirements, and DuckDB requirements remain unavailable in sans-R sessions.

Set `python: .venv/bin/python` in `.agents/console/config.yaml`, or use `-c python=.venv/bin/python`, to select an existing environment and bypass uv and package preparation. Explicit configuration takes precedence over legacy `RETICULATE_PYTHON` selection. Automatic PATH-Python fallback is removed, and sans-R sessions ignore `RETICULATE_UV`.

Internally, the server resolves and inspects the complete candidate before retiring the current worker, then commits the manifest, executable, and embedding configuration together through the mutable environment owner. Existing generation, cancellation, and retirement semantics remain in use; same-call restart code and input reach only the replacement. Resolver and inspection result files retain their original descriptors for bounded reads. MCP capabilities, disabled-import guidance, and recording describe the accepted environment and preparation modes.

The hidden `resolve` subprocess is trusted and runs outside the worker sandbox with full host permissions. This PR adds no resolver isolation. Documentation spells out how a client could replace a worker-writable uv wrapper, then trigger its execution through restart preparation, or supply startup code through a configured writable wheel directory. Request values still reject local paths, URLs, editable requirements, and archives; trusted uv configuration may select local sources or source builds. Worker-side transitions, SQL, SSH, and prepared targets retain their existing behavior.

Validation passed: the ordinary `scripts/check` gate; 49 transcript-runner self-tests; 107 focused public executions covering sans-R and R-present preparation, requirements actions, inspection, startup, retirement, and capabilities; and 69 sans-R, MCP capability, and resolver CLI executions with the CI `UV_CACHE_DIR` override. A fresh installed Linux build passed 24 R-free direct/native-sandbox executions, followed by four configuration executions with the inherited cache override. The resolver CLI and its unchanged snapshot passed on macOS and installed Linux; both macOS proxy cases passed separately. Production diff against main: **395 additions + 234 deletions = 629 lines**, including moved code.

title: Make the sandbox command own parent loss and bounded retirement
description:
## Summary

Make `mcp-console sandbox` safe to use as an owned subprocess before worker generations switch to that boundary. The new mode watches the exact parent identity, turns launcher-addressed `SIGTERM` into managed retirement, and keeps launcher exit as a synchronous cleanup barrier. The server continues to use its existing embedded launch path in this PR.

## User-facing changes

- Add the hidden `--exit-with-parent <PID>` sandbox option. Parent loss and explicit `SIGTERM` retirement stop the sandbox root and detached descendants, complete manager cleanup, remove the private directory when cleanup succeeds, and reap the root before the launcher exits.
- Preserve the ordinary interactive sandbox command's existing terminal and signal-forwarding behavior.
- Use the existing one-second manager cleanup policy for both worker and standalone sandbox lifetimes.

## Internal changes

- Capture the parent's PID and start time, register a `kqueue` exit watch, and revalidate the identity after watch registration and immediately before target release.
- Configure retained R and Python environments through `std::process::Command`, and combine the duplicate managed-R worker and resolver configuration paths.
- Make server sandbox tests locate roots and managers by ancestry and executable role instead of direct parentage.
- Add deterministic public transcript coverage for both owner-loss startup windows, detached descendants, explicit retirement, ignored inherited `SIGTERM`, natural root exit, and cleanup ordering.

## Testing

- `scripts/check-core`
- 38 focused CLI, sandbox, environment, and requirement transcript cases
- `scripts/check` completed the core checks and the rest of the transcript suite until three existing multiprocessing cases hit the host-wide POSIX semaphore limit with `OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device`. The focused environment cases affected by the command-configuration refactor passed.

title: Allow R to select the DBI connection for SQL cells
description:
## Summary

Allow R code to select the DBI connection used by later SQL cells while keeping the worker-managed in-memory DuckDB connection as the default. The public API now accepts the documented `connection` named argument in `console_sql_connection(connection)`.

## User-facing changes

- Add `console_sql_connection(connection)` to select a valid, user-owned `DBIConnection`, and `console_sql_connection(NULL)` to restore managed DuckDB.
- Make `sql_connection()` return the active connection while preserving the managed DuckDB catalog for later restoration.
- Return selected-connection query results through the existing bounded SQL preview, including empty and truncated results.
- Report invalid selections without replacing the active connection, and give a direct restoration path when a selected connection has been disconnected.
- Advertise the selection and restoration API in `tools/list` and distinguish managed-DuckDB behavior from selected-connection behavior in the runtime documentation.
- Accept the documented named `connection` argument so `console_sql_connection(connection = ...)` works as advertised.

## Internal changes

- Keep the managed DuckDB connection separate from the active SQL connection and continue using managed DuckDB for preview rendering.
- Submit selected-connection cells through the DBI query interface and use `dbColumnInfo()` to decide whether a result has columns, avoiding dialect-specific SQL classification.
- Preserve the existing DuckDB Arrow path, R data-frame scanning, extension handling, and catalog behavior when managed DuckDB is active.
- Add public RSQLite transcripts for selection, invalid input, result metadata, SQL error recovery, bounded and empty previews, disconnected-connection recovery, and managed-catalog restoration.

## DBI boundary

Selected connections remain owned by user code and should be restored before they are disconnected. SQL cells use `DBI::dbSendQuery()` on a selected connection. Drivers that require the DBI statement interface for a command should run it from an R cell with `DBI::dbExecute()` or `DBI::dbSendStatement()`.

The adapter does not retry a failed cell through another DBI method because the first attempt may already have changed database state. DuckDB requirements, R environment scanning, and DuckDB-specific discovery apply only to the managed backend. The MCP, relay, and worker protocol shapes are unchanged.

## Testing

- `scripts/test client_server/sql_connection`
- `scripts/format`
- `scripts/check`

title: Expose send as the sole MCP tool
description:
## Summary

MCP Console now exposes `send` as its sole MCP tool. This simplifies the public surface while retaining the existing implicit persistent session, lifecycle ordering, and runtime machinery.

## Public changes

- Remove `session` without a compatibility alias.
- Allow requirements-only `send` calls to prepare dependencies and restart-with-requirements calls without a cell.
- Use controlled-send semantics for standalone interrupts, including the existing 100-millisecond grace and `timeout_ms = 0` observation.
- Update the registered schema, documentation, public helpers, and transcript goldens for the one-tool interface.

## Internal changes

- Reuse the existing standalone preparation projection, controlled-send, restart, response-delivery, and retained-environment machinery.
- Delete only the dead standalone asynchronous lifecycle wrappers. Worker, relay, sideband, and resolver protocols are unchanged.

title: Prepare requirements in the same send call
description:
## Summary

Allow a code-bearing `send` call to declare additive R packages, Python packages, and DuckDB extensions that must be prepared before the cell runs. This removes the need to split a package-dependent cell across `session(action = "prepare")` and `send` while preserving explicit, retained requirement declarations.

## User-facing changes

- Add `send.requirements` with the same shape, validation, limits, and trust policy as session requirements.
- Treat declared requirements as preconditions of the cell for initial, running, stopped, and restart-required sessions. Successful combined calls return normal cell output; failed preparation does not dispatch the cell.
- Apply `timeout_ms` only after the cell is dispatched, preserve preparation-before-stdin and stdin-before-evaluate ordering, and record requirements in the original `send` journal event.
- Clarify that preparation does not import, attach, or load packages or extensions. Cells are not inspected for requirements and missing-package errors are not retried.

## Internal changes

- Add one exclusive pre-evaluation operation that covers requirement deltas, host resolution, live or pre-start preparation, and evaluation reservation and launch. Ordinary sends keep their existing admission path.
- Share requirement-delta calculation and pre-start resolution with restart while keeping their different commit rules separate.
- Extend public and server-relay transcript coverage for validation, live-state preservation, idempotence, failure and output ownership, cancellation and replacement races, session recording, and the timeout boundary.

title: Use public configuration for sandbox environment input
description:
`sandbox --config-env NAME` now reads the same public YAML or JSON document as `config.yaml`, so callers can supply configuration without depending on the native runner's private schema. It replaces file discovery, retains Console's defaults, and supports `--default-config`, ordered `-c` overrides, and `--writable-root`. The selected variable is consumed, and stdin remains available to the command.

Internally, the hidden `--runner-config-env NAME` flag preserves the existing native JSON passthrough without changing the payload. This escape hatch and the native schema have no public stability guarantee. Native-policy fixtures use the hidden flag; public help, documentation, and shell, Python, and R examples use the public configuration format. Development documentation describes the escape hatch.

The change also refreshes an existing stale cache-configuration diagnostic snapshot.

title: Control dependency resolution by runtime policy.
description:
Add independent `r.resolution` and `python.managed.resolution` settings so users can require deliberate dependency changes, prepare configured defaults once, or use preinstalled R packages. Both default to `automatic`; a managed fallback candidate's policy applies only when that candidate is selected.

Capture policy with the configured startup declaration and check normalized declaration changes before preparation, worker retirement, or bundled code/input. Preserve deferred interrupt admission, reject restricted runtime and reticulate additions, and let managed Python prepare through uv when R preparation is disabled. DuckDB extension preparation follows its existing provider's policy. Requirements inspection retains its existing shape.

Add focused public regressions and document policy, capability, startup/reset, and interrupt behavior.

Local `scripts/check` and focused policy regressions pass on macOS. Linux and Windows coverage awaits CI.

title: Run local dependency preparation in a configurable native sandbox
description:
Local dependency preparation currently executes package and build code with host permissions. Run the existing preparation process in a separate native sandbox on macOS and Linux to restrict its filesystem writes and network access.

The default policy permits host reads, writes to uv, IR, reticulate, renv, pak, Matplotlib, and DuckDB caches, and downloads from common package sources through the managed proxy. Users can supply a tailored native policy through the top-level `resolver` YAML mapping, independently of worker permissions. Automatic cache grants cover defaults and direct environment overrides; custom paths selected by uv configuration files require explicit resolver configuration. The resolver guide includes expanded defaults, cache selection rules, uv cache and PyPI mirror examples, and a configurable shared DuckDB extension directory.

Internally, wrap the local preparation process and retain its protocol and retirement ownership. Centralize host cache selection and capture one DuckDB extension path for installation and managed R/Python SQL connections across worker restarts. Explicitly route DuckDB extension downloads through the managed HTTP proxy. Shared caches remain writable; SSH, Windows, and `--no-sandbox` preparation retain host execution.

title: Expose explicit sandbox configuration from launch environments
description:
Expose `mcp-console sandbox --config-env NAME -- COMMAND ARGS...` so trusted launchers can select filesystem, network, and lifecycle policy through a child-specific JSON environment value. Target environment overrides preserve inheritance by default, and conflicting configuration sources are rejected. Existing no-config behavior remains; `serve` explicitly supplies its intended policy regardless of ambient configuration values.

The frontend delegates configuration and validation to the pinned runner. Coordinated runner changes keep target settings separate from host helper, loader, proxy, and control setup; remove transport variables from helper and target environments; and prevent macOS targets from reading the supervisor's launch environment. The private descriptor transport remains available with its separate acceptance-time integrity contract.

Add public regressions for explicit policy, conflicting and malformed input, transport stripping, nested-sandbox confinement, large launches, literal arguments, stdin, and ambient `serve` configuration. The runner covers deterministic parent-environment mutation before parsing and exclusion of host setup/control resources. Document defaults and size limits, with runnable shell, Python subprocess, and R processx examples.

Local macOS `scripts/check` passed, including the complete transcript suite and source/wheel installation checks. Runner contracts passed on macOS (68) and Linux (70), and 12 selected Linux public cases passed. The runner's strict Clippy command passes locally. One existing Linux procfs case is blocked by host namespace permissions, and hosted runner Bazel validation encounters a dependency URL returning 404; both failures also occur at the previous pin.

title: Launch worker generations through the sandbox subcommand
description:
## Summary

Route each worker generation through `mcp-console sandbox --exit-with-parent` so the launcher is the sole host-side owner of sandbox startup and cleanup. This removes the server's duplicate in-process sandbox path, reduces generation ownership to an ordinary child and its standard streams, and preserves launcher exit as the cleanup barrier before replacement.

## User-facing changes

- Worker generations now use the same sandbox launcher as direct `mcp-console sandbox` commands.
- Sandbox setup failures now return a stable `worker relay exited before readiness` MCP error while the detailed setup failure remains on stderr.
- Restart rejects unexpected launcher exits and relay failures first observed during retirement instead of admitting a replacement.
- A handled owned-retirement request returns launcher status 0 only after cleanup, while natural relay exits preserve their actual status. An unrelated status 137 remains visible, including after an earlier independent failure.
- Buffered old-generation relay output is drained before a nonzero launcher error is returned.

## Internal changes

- Delete `SandboxedCommand`, `SandboxedChild`, and the embedded sandbox spawn path.
- Replace server-owned sandbox state with ordinary child I/O, event-driven exit observation, bounded retirement signaling, and explicit reaping.
- Close unrelated server descriptors before launcher exec. In parent-owned mode, transfer stdin to the sandbox root without retaining another pipe reader in the launcher, while retaining stdout until cleanup completes.
- Use relay-stdout `POLLHUP` as the stream-closure condition for joining generation I/O tasks independently of launcher exit status.
- Use launcher status 0 as the owned-retirement acknowledgment and retain relay-EOF provenance only for automatic recovery, avoiding sender-side liveness inference around `kill()`.
- Move process-group cleanup beside the relay, propagate retirement-time fatal events through the server's retirement result, and update the implemented architecture and supervision documentation.

## Testing

- `scripts/check-core`
- The complete 350-case public transcript matrix after excluding three Python multiprocessing cases that cannot allocate host POSIX semaphores: `runs_joblib_process_backend`, `runs_joblib_process_backend_after_live_resolution`, and `runs_spawn_process_after_live_resolution`
- Focused startup, parent-loss, owned-retirement, descriptor, stdin-failure, restart, replacement, relay-failure, manager-crash, old-generation output-drain, and both signal/zombie race-ordering cases

title: Layer Python requirements declared at runtime
description:
## Summary

Server-managed workers now honor additive requirements declared through `reticulate::py_require()` before or after Python initialization. This lets R package load hooks make their Python dependencies available without restarting the worker or discarding live Python state.

## User-facing changes

- Resolve package-declared requirements outside the network-denied worker and activate the resulting environment through reticulate.
- Require the candidate environment to use the exact live `libpython`; rejected candidates leave the active interpreter, manifest, and Python objects intact.
- Preserve reticulate's package attribution and public requirement history.
- Keep late explicit `session prepare` additions restart-only.
- Document that evaluated R code or package loading can trigger host resolution, including network access, host-cache writes, and package build backends.

## Internal changes

- Seed server-managed manifests in reticulate, delegate its internal uv lookup to the host resolver, and observe successful activation and manifest commit without wrapping `py_require()`.
- Add nested worker/server resolve, reply, and commit frames so the server keeps candidates pending until reticulate finishes activation.
- Carry the worker's resolver `UV_*` settings except `UV_OFFLINE`, retain them across worker generations, and track worker and resolver shutdown handles independently.
- Add public transcript coverage for package requirements before initialization, live layered activation, manifest attribution, and different-`libpython` rejection.

title: Print rendered R vignettes through Console
description:
Print installed HTML vignettes as readable text, including evaluated results that the source view omits. Preserve headings, lists, code indentation, simple tables, links, captions, and image alt text.

Conversion uses Rust's `html2text` crate through one registered native R callback. R reads the artifact selected by its metadata and passes its bytes to the converter, preserving native filenames. Output supports ordinary capture, deferred pager overrides, and later S3 print overrides. Conversion requires no rendering runtime, executes no source or JavaScript, and fetches no linked assets. Non-HTML vignettes retain a labeled source view; PDF conversion, figure pixels, and JavaScript-dependent content are unavailable.

Transcripts show ordinary `?stats::lm` and `vignette()` calls with their actual client responses, including output limits and retained-log paths. The cpp11 vignette fixture uses an unmodified, pinned CRAN archive with prebuilt HTML and needs no rendering or network access during tests.

title: Add typed R session configuration
description:
Add S7 `ConsoleConfig` so R callers can choose runtimes, startup packages, resolution modes, resolver settings, and sandbox permissions through one interface. `console_tool()` defaults to no configuration-file discovery and restrictive worker permissions. `ConfigDiscovery` opts into global/project settings, `project` selects the launch directory, and `ConsoleConfig(sandbox = FALSE)` replaces `no_sandbox` and disables worker and resolver enforcement.

Sandbox constructors use uppercase CamelCase names with a shared `Sandbox` prefix. The sandbox help page explains each permission and proxy choice, with examples for writable roots, denied paths, domain filters, and Shiny development.

Internally, configuration classes share serialization that preserves omitted fields, empty mappings, and arrays. Explicit permission objects replace inherited grants, Python selections replace the whole Python node, and native configuration layers can clear whole permission nodes with `null`. The package uses S7 load/build hooks, pins development S7, and requires R 4.2. Windows CI installs the declared R package dependencies. The worker bootstrap fixture owns its sandboxed resolver cache so concurrent cases cannot mutate its mount targets.

On macOS, the focused native cases, installed-package checks with R 4.2 and 4.6, `scripts/format`, and `scripts/check` pass. Native Linux and Windows validation remains for hosted CI.

title: Preserve R interrupts and cover managed environment regressions
description:
Preserve R interrupt conditions when managed Python inspection is cancelled. Install the handler before delivering pending interrupts, while respecting the caller's `suspendInterrupts()` context, so an interrupted probe reaches the caller's R interrupt handler.

Extend public MCP coverage for mixed R/Python interrupt-plus-requirements calls, policy validation after interrupt delivery, managed cache isolation across restarts, and conditional DuckDB defaults. Declare the preparation capabilities and retain complete transcripts for both policy sessions.

Make CI fixtures deterministic by waiting for complete background stderr in the public session log and reusing prewarmed host dependencies in the Ragnar sandbox case. Refresh the remaining tool-description snapshots.

title: Use Console-owned defaults for local resolver caches
description:
Default sandboxed local dependency preparation now stores its artifacts under `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/mcp-console/resolver/payload`, keeping them separate from ordinary host caches. This covers uv caches, managed Python installations and tools, R package caches, Matplotlib fonts, and DuckDB extensions.

Missing or empty cache settings use the Console defaults. Empty or relative `XDG_CACHE_HOME` falls back to `$HOME/.cache`. Nonempty cache overrides and explicit filesystem policies retain their selected cache layout. Cache selection for `--no-sandbox`, SSH, and Windows retains its current behavior. Managed workers reuse the resolver's warmed font cache through their private Matplotlib directories across restarts, while retaining host Matplotlib configuration.

Cache paths are passed as environment variables to the existing native resolver sandbox. Its download allowlist includes Astral's installer redirect host, and macOS preparation grants Darwin's user temporary directory for utilities that ignore `TMPDIR`. Resolver executables, configuration, and package sources remain trusted inputs.

Preparation cleanup also bounds post-kill exit observation and stderr collection, reports termination failures, and reaps only an observed exited child. Children whose retirement is unconfirmed retain a background reaping owner, and connection closure retries termination. The original error is preserved, and replacement remains blocked after unconfirmed retirement.

title: Add explicit requirements inspection and replacement to send
description:
Sessions can now inspect, replace, or reset retained requirements through `send`, while keeping the existing R/Python/SQL cell interface and additive behavior by default.

Public behavior:

- `requirements.action="get"` reads the committed server declaration during idle work, evaluation, or resolution without starting a worker or consuming output. It includes Python version constraints and `exclude_newer`; large manifests remain complete in structured content and in the Python/R wrappers.
- `add` preserves accumulation and supported live additions. `set` replaces every list and session constraint, including omitted fields; an empty set stays empty through startup, restart, and later additions. `reset` restores startup defaults and discards automatic additions.
- Changed replacements require explicit restart when a worker is live. The complete candidate is prepared before commit and retirement, so preparation failure or interruption preserves the old environment and worker. Same-call code runs only in the replacement. Unchanged declarations skip preparation while honoring an explicit restart.
- MCP metadata, Python and R clients, and documentation describe the actions and existing target limits. Recordings retain committed replacement boundaries; Quarto disables execution and explains why one manifest cannot replay incompatible historical cells.

Internally, this extends the existing requirement deltas, retained resolver results, generation checks, and restart transaction. Inspection uses a snapshot published at existing commit points. Necessary R bridge and SQL packages are prepared separately from the declaration. Empty managed Python environments run standard-library code without NumPy or pandas; this is not a package denylist, cache cleanup, or a change to automatic resolution or target preparation capabilities.

Validated with `scripts/check`, 387 focused transcript executions covering requirements, automatic resolution, restart, recording, SDK clients, SQL, and capability schemas, plus the R client integration tests (15 passing expectations). Additional focused runs cover the final recording formatting and full DuckDB failure snapshot. The full local installation gate was not run; hosted CI remains the comprehensive platform gate.

title: Clarify persistent console workflows and active states
description:
MCP Console already preserves runtime state and displays normal R, Python, and SQL results, but its tool descriptions do not make the intended iterative workflow explicit. This change guides clients toward coherent sequential cells and makes active evaluations easier to continue without changing the response model.

## User-facing changes

- Explain the REPL-style workflow: submit one coherent cell, leave the primary result last, inspect its normal display, and use that result to construct the next cell.
- Document persistent cross-runtime state, R and Python bridges, runtime inventory, debugger input, timeout polling, warnings, and partial state after errors.
- Clarify when to prepare requirements, interrupt work, or restart the worker.
- Replace `[running]` with `[running; poll with an empty send]` and `[stdin needed]` with `[waiting for stdin]`.

## Internal changes

- Preserve ordinary text and image responses, existing interpreter display methods, and boilerplate-free successful calls.
- Keep evaluation, resolver, and transport protocols unchanged; only the canonical state-banner text changes.
- Synchronize registered descriptions, schema properties, documentation, public `tools/list` coverage, and transcript snapshots.

title: Add IR-backed R requirements
description:
## Summary

Add R package requirements to `session(action = "prepare")` so MCP clients can resolve them through IR before the worker starts. This gives R requirements the same additive, retained lifecycle as managed Python requirements while the worker reads the resulting library inside its sandbox.

## User-facing changes

- Accept R requirements alongside Python requirements and commit combined preparation only after both resolvers succeed.
- Prepend IR's resolved library to inherited `R_LIBS`, retain it across worker restarts, and return `[restart required]` for additions after the runtime starts.
- Return actionable tool errors when IR is missing, resolution fails, or the returned library is invalid.
- Warn tool callers that requirement resolution may execute package installation or build code on the host and that local R packages must be trusted.

## Internal changes

- Reuse the event-driven resolver process lifecycle for IR and Python.
- Add real-IR transcript coverage using CRAN and local package references plus native IR, pak, and uv diagnostics.
- Skip only the IR-dependent suite when the executable is unavailable, and install IR in CI through its documented installer.

## Notes

This change resolves the complete accumulated R requirement set into one managed IR library. Retaining multiple independently resolved managed library paths remains outside this slice.

IR currently accepts local package references, so installing them can execute package-controlled code with the OS permissions of `mcp-console serve`. This limitation is documented in the model-visible schema and user and protocol documentation. A future restriction should use an upstream IR policy that rejects local references before pak and renv process them; rejecting local references would not sandbox other source-package build code.

title: Print R help and vignette source through Console
description:
Ordinary R documentation calls can open a host pager or viewer, leaving their contents out of Console's response. This change makes `?`, `help()`, `??`, and `help.search()` return readable, capturable text, and makes `vignette()` print its installed source. Native lookup and selection, quiet assignment, later printing, and user overrides remain available.

The built-in R worker installs a text pager, plain help formatting with visible URLs, and a vignette print method after native startup. Tool guidance and runtime documentation describe normal calls and capturing long pages to print line ranges. Vignette source must be installed as UTF-8 or ASCII; this view does not contain rendered results or figures.

title: Declare dplyr and dbplyr in optional R defaults
description:
Declare `dplyr` and `dbplyr` explicitly in the optional R startup package list so data manipulation and database translation are available and visible in retained requirements. Default preparation, reset, inspection, and Quarto exports now include both packages.

Update the default declaration contract and existing public acceptance expectations. The implementation changes two package-list entries.

Validated on macOS arm64 with the affected startup, requirements, runtime, SQL, and recording cases, `scripts/format`, and `scripts/check`. Linux and Windows were not exercised locally.

title: Clarify the ellmer console tool interface
description:
## Summary

Make executable selection explicit in the R package while keeping the initial public interface small. Users can now choose a specific executable, resolve a specific release, or follow a documented default discovery order. The tests delegate MCP server behavior to `mcptools`, exercise the checkout binary without requiring a managed-runtime prewarm, and make stale Python activation lifecycle coverage deterministic under parallel transcript execution.

## User-facing changes

- Replace `mcp_console_tool(from = ...)` with `console_tool(..., path = NULL, version = NULL)`.
- Use an explicit `path` directly, or use `version` to resolve a published `mcp-console` release through UV without consulting `PATH`.
- With neither argument supplied, use `mcp-console` from `PATH` and fall back to the latest published release through UV.
- Reject simultaneous `path` and `version` arguments and require `...` to remain empty for future expansion.
- Document the discovery order and explicit selection examples in the package help and README.

## Internal changes

- Replace the handwritten JSON-RPC test server with `mcptools::mcp_server()` and a deterministic tool fixture that covers schema adaptation and requirements serialization.
- Run checkout-binary acceptance tests against the documented bare runtime, retaining coverage for persistent R state, errors, images, and cancellation without depending on resolver tools, caches, or the network.
- Build the Rust binary before R package checks and run the R workflow when runtime sources or Cargo inputs change.
- Reuse the startup interpreter for lifecycle-only Python candidate manifests, keeping stale-activation coverage independent of shared UV cache latency while asserting the public running and restart response ownership explicitly.
- Normalize the checkpoint fixture's incidental source line in resolver-error snapshots.
- Keep the existing `processx` transport for persistent bidirectional I/O, interrupt handling, and process cleanup.

title: Add an ellmer R package wrapper
description:
## Summary

Add `mcp.console`, an R package that gives ellmer chats a persistent MCP Console workbench for R, Python, and DuckDB.

## User-facing changes

- Install the package from the repository's `r/` directory and register `mcp_console_tool()` on an ellmer chat.
- Use an existing `mcp-console` executable from `PATH`, with automatic `reticulate` resolution when it is unavailable.
- Derive tool arguments from the live server schema, including configurations that disable individual languages.
- Preserve ordered text and image content from successful and failed console calls.
- Preserve the console session after a human R interrupt while preventing a late response from being consumed by the next call.
- Document installation and use with a concise `mtcars` workbench example.

## Internal changes

- Manage the server lifetime with processx and use `reticulate::uv_run_tool()` only as the executable fallback.
- Frame JSON-RPC requests as JSONL, cancel abandoned requests, and correlate later responses by request ID.
- Wait for server output through processx's interrupt-aware poll so human R interrupts reliably send cancellation without losing the session.
- Translate the MCP schema into ellmer and OpenAI-compatible strict schemas while preserving optional fields, nested requirements, and nullable enums.
- Add deterministic fake-server coverage for PATH and fallback resolution, initialization, polling, requirements, configured languages, rich error content, interrupts, and large images.
- Add a macOS `R CMD check` workflow for the package.
- Synchronize the SQL interrupt transcript through the public interrupt response instead of a racing R input-handler marker.
- Keep transcript FIFO writer endpoints open and gate resolver completion so early releases cannot deadlock CI.

## Notes

ellmer 0.4.2 cannot combine failure metadata with a rich tool value. Failed MCP calls therefore retain their complete model-visible content, including images, instead of discarding non-text output.

title: Run R event handlers while the worker is idle
description:
## Summary

R packages such as `later` register timers and input handlers that should progress between cells. Previously, the worker serviced them only at cell boundaries. This change waits through R's own activity mechanism, without busy polling or a second event loop.

## User-facing changes

Registered R callbacks can run after a cell returns, and their state changes remain available to later cells. The next code-bearing `send` collects callback text and images and can provide requested input. Empty sends remain immediate polls in this layer and do not contact the idle worker. Live requirement preparation also drains idle output and gives ready R handlers one nonblocking turn before applying the requirements; it stops the worker if a callback requests input.

## Internal changes

- Temporarily add the sideband descriptor to R's input-handler set and wait through `R_checkActivity()`, removing it before running R code and after an R long jump.
- Queue commands received during nested Python resolution and use the next explicit operation's ordinary terminal to fence preceding idle work; no activity-specific terminal is added.
- Complete worker shutdown before cancelling a nested host resolver, so resolver cancellation cannot release a command queued on the retiring worker.

## Notes

The server does not continuously read idle sideband frames in this layer. Pipe backpressure or a managed-Python request can pause a callback until the next code-bearing `send` or live requirement preparation.

title: Return R plots as MCP image content
description:
## Summary

Adds R plot support to `send`. Plots drawn on the worker-owned default graphics device return as ordered `image/png` MCP content, so clients can render them without reading files from the worker's temporary directory. The same behavior applies when a Python cell invokes an R plot through reticulate's `r` bridge.

## User-facing changes

- Returns managed plot pages in global finalization order, including when a cell switches among multiple managed devices. Once the first page opens, later console text waits until cell end so it cannot appear ahead of an unfinished page. This direct-PNG implementation does not reconstruct text emitted between individual pages.
- Adds the persistent R options `console.plot.width`, `console.plot.height`, and `console.plot.dpi`. The defaults produce an 800 by 600 pixel image at 96 DPI.
- Keeps worker-owned graphics devices cell scoped, so a plot and every operation that modifies it belong in one cell.
- Leaves graphics devices opened explicitly by evaluated code under user control. The worker does not close them, read their files, or return them as MCP images, and the managed default remains available after they close.
- Returns R plots invoked from Python through reticulate's `r` bridge under the same sizing, ordering, ownership, and cell-scope rules.

## Internal changes

- Extends the worker sideband protocol and server response model with ordered image content while preserving adjacent text coalescing, timeout polling, restart notices, and tool errors.
- Uses a lazy direct PNG device, records finalization through the managed devices' new-page and close callbacks, and applies a cell-wide console-output barrier after plotting begins. A C forwarding boundary keeps R errors from jumping across Rust frames.
- Adds deterministic Zod coverage plus real-R and Python golden transcripts for ordered content, drawing updates, R errors, explicit-device ownership and restoration, and Python-to-R plotting. Plot tests render the same R source through the selected live `Rscript` and compare the complete PNG bytes instead of storing binary golden images.

title: Select existing Python environments with bounded fallback
description:
Allow `python` to select an interpreter executable or standard venv directory, including an `existing` mapping. A flat `first_available` list can try existing paths, the incoming `VIRTUAL_ENV`, and an optional final `managed: {}` candidate. Only absent paths advance the list; broken environments fail, and the selected interpreter remains fixed across restarts.

Explicit configuration takes precedence over `RETICULATE_PYTHON`. Recognized Conda installations, including interpreter symlink targets, are rejected while ordinary venv paths retain their spelling. An explicit managed choice requires managed preparation and cannot fall back to PATH Python when preparation is unavailable.

Interpreter inspection uses worker permissions, and Console cache isolation follows the selected candidate. The shared preparation transport retains process retirement barriers; existing managed defaults remain unchanged. Cache fixtures declare their uv prerequisite. The inspection fixture recognizes platform-specific denial errors while retaining the denied-write assertion.

The macOS selection, restart, containment, shared-environment, and cache cases passed, along with `scripts/format` and `scripts/check`. The managed-selection regression failed before the fix and passed afterward on native Windows. Linux and the full native Windows suite were not run.

title: Derive Python embedding configuration in Console
description:
## Summary

Console now derives the embedding configuration used during ordinary Python startup. Reticulate selects an executable using its existing discovery rules and R-side hints; Console inspects that executable, initializes CPython through the existing native startup path, and supplies the same embedding fields for reticulate's subsequent attachment. This establishes the configuration boundary needed for a future Python-and-SQL mode without R.

## Behavior and implementation

- Inspection uses the selected executable's own runtime and `sysconfig` to find its embedding library and base Python home. It supports Linux shared libraries and macOS frameworks, preserves the selected executable's spelling, and distinguishes virtual environments from their base installation.
- The inspector requires CPython 3.10 or later and validates the library's version/build identity, ABI marker, and required startup symbols. Missing or unusable embedding support produces an error without selecting another interpreter. Inspection assumes a trusted installation that remains stable through initialization; concurrent replacement is unsupported.
- A private result file separates configuration from child startup output. Existing resolver primitives own output collection, cancellation, and reaping, with cancellation connected to the worker's existing interrupt wakeup. Inspection observes queued SIGINT requests even when R temporarily defers their delivery. Failed or interrupted inspection removes its result file and permits retry in the same worker.
- Both Python-first and R-first startup use the inspected configuration. Cached or initialized selections are not inspected again. Reticulate retains its other interoperability metadata and environment adjustments; requirement preparation, activation, retained requirements, and public protocols stay unchanged. Ordinary sessions still require R, and this PR adds no command or session mode.

The R-independent regression now supplies only a selected executable and exercises production inspection, native initialization, shared runtime setup, and successive cells through the ordinary embedded evaluator without loading libR. Public regressions cover the configuration handoff, failure and cancellation, retained worker state, and retry. Focused cases cover copied framework virtualenvs, startup output, invalid executables, missing/unusable or mismatched libraries, version rejection, and cleanup confirmation.

Validation passed on clean commit `55a38e87`: `scripts/format`, all six focused native embedding/inspection tests, the existing startup/environment/lifecycle suites, and full `scripts/check` (core, full transcripts, and installation checks). The queued-interrupt regression failed before the fix and passed afterward. Configuration handoff, queued interruption, and cancellation/retry also passed in direct and sandboxed modes on Linux. Existing platform capability skips remain in effect; hosted CI is separate from these results.

`scripts/review-diff origin/main` reports **489 production additions plus deletions** (439 added, 50 deleted) and **1,484 total additions plus deletions**, including tests, snapshots, tooling, and documentation. Existing transcript expectations are preserved.

title: Validate live Python activation and restore state on interruption
description:
Adding a dependency to a running Python session can also change existing packages and import paths. This PR extends Console's live activation path to check compatibility before switching environments and restore Console-owned state when activation is interrupted.

User-facing changes:

- Require the running Python version and reject candidates that change a loaded distribution's version or omit it, before mutating the interpreter. Match loaded module files to their owning distributions so unimported namespace contributors can change.
- Replace old environment-owned paths, including `.pth` additions, while preserving user-added paths. Set the candidate's prefixes and executable before running site hooks.
- Restore Console-owned paths, interpreter identity, and environment variables after interrupted activation so preparation can be retried. Defer interrupts during publication and commit so an accepted environment remains retained.
- Support cancellation of candidate inspection through interrupt or restart. An interrupted initial inspection can be retried by a later Python cell without losing existing R or SQL state or the environment prepared before Python started. Live `reticulate::py_require()` inspection and site activation preserve R interrupt conditions.
- Refresh `reticulate::py_config()` with the committed environment's live import path and NumPy metadata. Use the resolver's Python-version matching rules for live `reticulate::py_require()` declarations.

Internally, a worker-side probe inspects the already-selected executable for site paths, distribution versions, and conversion metadata. Its completion notifications use a pipe so Linux sandbox network restrictions do not block them. An activation transaction wraps the shared activation helper and carries the exact pending candidate and optional R configuration and declaration through publication. Lazy preparation retains its candidate only after the R declaration commits. Public regressions cover compatibility rejection, path cleanup, cancellation, rollback, retention, and configuration agreement.

Rollback covers Console-owned state; it cannot undo arbitrary site-hook side effects. Other activation exceptions still require restart. Initial `.pth` path cleanup requires startup hooks to produce the same additions in the probe and embedded interpreter; process-dependent startup additions are unsupported.

Development command cleanup also preserves the cancellation exit status when only zombie processes remain in the phase group. The native R loader fixture uses base R so package resolution cannot block its library-loading checks.

title: Dispatch Python cells and console services directly
description:
Python cells now enter Console's existing private evaluator directly through its CPython library wrapper after the retained reticulate adapter completes startup. Console also owns main-thread Python input, output, diagnostics, plot publication, and the native interrupt acknowledgment needed for those services. Persistent globals, expression display, evaluation filenames, exception handling, plotting after exceptions, and debugger input retain the existing evaluator semantics.

Reticulate remains required for ordinary Python startup and continues to own interpreter selection, startup orchestration, the requirement manifest, environment activation, automatic-resolution callbacks, object conversion, and cross-language and event integration. R is still required and initialized eagerly; managed SQL remains R-backed. Preparation transactions and blanket interrupt deferral are unchanged. This is the direct-dispatch and console-services slice discussed in #323; it does not implement the environment-ownership or independent-startup changes from that proposal.

Python managed input now reads the shared worker buffer directly, including Unicode, embedded NUL bytes, long lines, queued input, and retained partial lines. Native callbacks release the GIL while blocking. Cell dispatch and runtime installation release the library-state mutex before executing Python. The signal handler wakes managed input, respects suspended R interrupts, and acknowledges accepted interrupts once across nested language calls. Blocking Python syscalls remain interruptible after R event waits, and managed text-stream writes return Unicode character counts. Reticulate event polling stays enabled. Binary buffers, descriptors, background threads, and fork children continue to use the underlying raw streams, including cached streams and logging handlers.

Public transcript regressions cover direct dispatch with reticulate's R dispatch functions disabled after bootstrap, direct output routing, R-first initialization, nested and suspended interrupts, GIL release during input, Unicode/NUL/long input, partial-line replay, EOF, and background-thread output. Raw-stdin interruption and empty/Unicode write-count assertions cover the stream and signal contracts. The input cases establish a managed-input checkpoint before starting their bounded completion checks, so those checks exclude Python startup. Existing environment, automatic-resolution, SQL, plotting, debugger, fork-stream, and worker-exit coverage is retained. Updated existing snapshots preserve complete output and errors: private runtime traceback line numbers move, and the output-routing regression records its new instrumentation. Text, channel ordering, and empty-write suppression remain unchanged.

Validation on macOS arm64 passed `scripts/format`, `git diff --check`, focused public boundary tests, and all core checks, including Clippy and 33 Rust tests. The focused cases cover raw and managed input, nested and suspended interrupts, stream routing and fork behavior, and SQL providers. `scripts/check` stopped in the transcript suite when the unchanged `client_server/output/test_recovery::recovered_image_omissions_keep_bounded_state` stress case exhausted its deadline after 9m46s. That case uses a custom worker and does not execute the changed runtime code. The full run reported 54 existing capability skips and did not reach installation checks. Local Linux runtime validation and hosted checks for the updated head remain unverified.

title: Report committed Python activations
description:
## Summary

Have the built-in worker report a managed Python environment as soon as reticulate commits it. A terminal cell or preparation checkpoint may never arrive if later work fails, so it cannot be the only persistence boundary for an already-live activation.

## User-facing changes

A successful live `py_require()` activation is retained for later worker generations even if the worker fails later in the same cell or a subsequent R update fails during mixed live preparation.

## Internal changes

Observe reticulate's manifest assignment after `py_reqs_activate()` succeeds and emit `python_activated` at that commit boundary. Report the current manifest when Python first initializes. Existing terminal checkpoints remain in place for operation validation and pre-initialization materialization. Custom-worker behavior is unchanged.

title: Service R events at cell boundaries
description:
## Summary

Give R's registered input handlers one nonblocking turn immediately before each R, Python, or SQL cell and a second turn after a normal language outcome while the worker remains usable. This lets ready callbacks from packages such as `later` run at cell boundaries while preserving the existing worker command loop.

## User-facing changes

Ready callbacks can produce console output, request input, and return managed default-device plots at cell boundaries. Timers that become ready while the worker is otherwise idle still wait for the next cell boundary.

Shutdown or an infrastructure failure during the initial callback turn aborts the submitted cell instead of dispatching it against a worker that is already stopping or unusable. An infrastructure failure recorded by the cell also suppresses the final callback turn.

Restart prevents a callback released by worker-stdin EOF from dispatching or completing a cell, including when the callback reads fd 0 directly and bypasses R's console bridge.

## Internal changes

The worker loads R's activity and handler entry points and invokes them through a small `R_ToplevelExec()` boundary in the existing C shim. The boundary contains handler long jumps without turning them into worker infrastructure failures. The worker checks shutdown and recorded infrastructure failures before dispatch and before the final turn, and uses one nonblocking fd-0 check after each turn to recognize stdin hangup without consuming input.

title: Add initial Python requirement preparation
description:
## Summary

Add initial dynamic Python environment resolution so an MCP client can declare PEP 508 requirements before the implicit session starts. Resolution stays outside the worker sandbox, and the worker receives the concrete interpreter selected by reticulate and uv. Closing MCP input also cancels active preparation so dependency resolution does not delay server shutdown.

## User-facing changes

- Register a narrow `session` tool with `action: "prepare"` and single-line PEP 508 strings in `requirements.python`.
- Resolve additive requirements before lazy worker startup and return `[prepared]` without importing packages or starting the worker.
- Keep exact repeated requirements idempotent and leave the existing environment unchanged when candidate resolution fails.
- Cancel an in-flight preparation when MCP input closes. Preparation does not otherwise have a per-call timeout.
- Return `restart required` for additions after the worker starts. Runtime layering and an explicit restart action remain deferred.
- Let successful explicit preparation replace an inherited `RETICULATE_PYTHON` selection so declared requirements are available.

## Internal changes

- Call `reticulate:::uv_get_or_create_env()` in the existing host-side `Rscript` process, retaining NumPy as the baseline requirement.
- Pass each requirement as one UTF-8 line on `Rscript` standard input and retain the complete manifest and resolved interpreter atomically in the server.
- Run explicit resolution in a dedicated process group registered with the existing shutdown gate, and prevent queued preparation jobs from starting after shutdown begins.
- Keep the sandbox policy unchanged: uv resolution uses host network and caches, while the worker remains offline.
- Add public coverage for successful resolution, resolver diagnostics, failed-candidate atomicity, late and concurrent preparation, option-shaped requirements, retained runtime state, and bounded shutdown during active preparation.

## Notes

This slice supports one implicit session and Python requirements only. Named sessions, R requirements, runtime activation, explicit restart, and environment provenance remain unimplemented. Package preparation can execute source-package build backends in the host resolver process; the README and worker protocol document that boundary.

title: Record Console processes and actual worker lifetimes
description:
Console processes that never receive `send` no longer leave persistent recordings. The first received send publishes retained protocol traffic, startup text, and images with their original observation timestamps. Polls, input, controls, rejected submissions, and cancelled requests all activate recording. If publication fails, omitted startup text is reported as unavailable without advertising an unpublished log.

A bounded queue captures sends in receipt order independently of handlers and response delivery. Send capture and cancellation journal writes run off the Tokio executor. Lifecycle events enter the recorder queue so their journal writes do not block worker retirement. EOF closes the capture queue, settles queued capture and completed or abandoned protocol writes, and publishes outstanding output receipts before recording finalization. Recording settlement requires filesystem operations to return; it does not abandon received calls on a timer. Protocol events reference canonical send calls/results and distinguish response assembly from local write completion. A send that exceeds the capture limit is retained as a protocol receipt before the connection closes. Recording failures remain fail-open.

Both native relays report actual worker acquisition. Each acquired worker gets a numbered session within the process recording, including explicit restarts and automatic replacement. Duplicate acquisition events and readiness before acquisition are rejected as private-protocol failures. Readiness, termination, and startup failure are recorded separately; generation fencing and confirmed-retirement barriers are preserved.

This retains the existing raw-output files, artifact paths, single-QMD layout, storage selection, identifiers, permissions, and retention limits. Interval and per-cell attribution changes, transcript presentation, per-session QMDs and dependency projections, read-only completion, and export APIs remain outside this PR.

title: Use native R startup by default
description:
Use R's own initialization inside the worker sandbox so environment files, site/user profiles, workspace restoration, `.First()`, and default packages follow R's discovery and ordering. Add `r.vanilla`, defaulting to `false`, with `mcp-console serve -c r.vanilla=true` as the native `--vanilla` escape hatch. The boolean is captured at server launch and retained across restarts. Changing `config.yaml` requires a new connection; edited startup files are read on the next worker restart.

Remove `defer_r_startup()` / `finish_r_startup()`, their default-package emulation, and the unconditional R width override. Retain `--quiet`, `--interactive`, and `--no-save`, and keep native I/O, interrupts, and runtime attachment under Console's ownership. Windows passes startup flags to R's initial argument parser and processes environment files once, with native `--vanilla` suppression. Native hooks run before Console's runtime bridges and plot device attach. Console-managed resolution is available after attachment, which retains the single Python interpreter and its managed-environment metadata. The configured Console startup source keeps its existing role after runtime setup.

Retain diagnostics through the ordinary output path and require explicit restart after R exits or initialization fails or is interrupted. Calls, polls, and unused-worker replacement cannot authorize another attempt. Preparation waits for healthy native startup before replacing an unused worker. Discovery and preparation remain profile-free, including nested ir/pak drivers. Worker permissions are unchanged; `--no-sandbox` runs native startup without worker sandbox enforcement.

Transcripts use exact canonical `!same-as` initialization references and separate files for separate connections. Embedded programs use the shared code normalizer and R/Python formatting directives. Plot coverage compares two actual PNGs byte-for-byte after native startup, retains startup-package Python ownership checks, and verifies two recorded PNG artifacts from configured Console startup without a tool call.

On macOS arm64, `scripts/preflight`, `scripts/format`, and `scripts/test --full --update --jobs 6` passed all 1,714 executions. After integrating main, 137 focused executions and `scripts/check` passed; the workspace fixture also passed both execution modes after its Windows correction. Native Windows validation passed all nine shared startup cases, eight direct runtime/startup/plot checks, and configuration and canonical-handshake checks. Windows sandbox coverage is unverified locally: both the new startup case and an existing sandbox case stopped before worker readiness with a runner pipe connection timeout. Linux was not exercised locally; comprehensive platform coverage remains with CI.

title: Support prepared Docker and SBX sessions without R
description:
