Prepared Docker images and Docker Sandbox templates previously required R. This change discovers their runtimes inside the execution target and starts the existing native Python/SQL runtime when R is absent, so Python-only images can use Console without adding R or enabling dependency preparation.

The public `python` setting now selects a preinstalled target interpreter, including paths relative to `target.workspace`. It takes precedence over legacy `RETICULATE_PYTHON`; otherwise discovery uses target PATH `python3`, then `python`. Selected-runtime failures retain their error without fallback. Virtual environments, executable spelling, prefixes, site-packages, and child interpreters survive launch projection and replacement. Optional analysis packages are not startup prerequisites. Missing DuckDB leaves Python and custom DB-API connections usable.

Docker and SBX share one discovery/configuration implementation and the local/SSH worker-environment handoff. Prepared protocol version 4 adds one bounded runtime-result frame, separate from diagnostics. Compatible version/build negotiation, validated capabilities, and confirmed probe-resource removal precede retention of one immutable descriptor beside the image/template. Probing starts no analysis worker or SQL catalog. Subsequent launches validate its paths inside the target; the controller treats those paths as metadata. SSH keeps its existing version 4 negotiation and omits the unused probe selector.

Prepared targets remain non-managed: requirements inspection reports the retained declaration; mutations are rejected before restart, code, or input changes state. Console never invokes uv/ir, installs missing imports, or prepares extensions there. The image/template extension cache remains usable with worker network access blocked. Private disposable storage holds Python spill files and secrets. Docker retains native runner and outer-container ownership; SBX retains compute enforcement and VM ownership without a native companion. Restart and crash replacement reuse the captured interpreter and image/template with fresh objects and catalogs, and replacement still requires confirmed retirement.

MCP schemas, descriptions, diagnostics, recordings, and target metadata reflect the discovered runtime and existing language restrictions. New [Docker](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/blob/feat/prepared-python/examples/docker/Dockerfile.python) and [SBX](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/blob/feat/prepared-python/examples/docker-sandbox/Dockerfile.python) examples contain Python analysis dependencies and no R or reticulate; mixed-language examples remain available. The provider docs explain selection, missing dependencies, rebuild/restart expectations, prerequisites, and isolation limits.

## Cross-target acceptance

| Target                                   | Runtime coverage                                                                                                                           | Result                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Local direct and native sandbox          | R-present and sans-R; managed and explicit Python; preparation, Python/SQL, recording, replacement, cleanup                                | Passed; 88 public MCP sans-R executions plus applicable mixed-language regressions                                |
| SSH loopback and external Linux hosts    | R-present and sans-R; existing managed/explicit selection and preparation; recording, replacement, retirement                              | Passed; 17 sans-R executions, including real external direct/native, plus R-present external/loopback regressions |
| Real Docker direct                       | R-free and R-present installed builds; target selection, Python/SQL state, missing packages, recording, retirement                         | Passed; 11 R-free direct cases plus R-present image/lifecycle/setup regressions                                   |
| Real Docker with installed native runner | R-free lifecycle through `filesystem: external-sandbox`; ordinary restricted namespace rejection also checked                              | Passed; one R-free lifecycle case with native runner and confirmed container retirement                           |
| Real SBX compute                         | R-free and R-present installed templates; no companion; Python/SQL, input, plotting, interrupts, debugger, recording, replacement, cleanup | Passed; 11 R-free cases plus R-present runtime/lifecycle regressions                                              |

`scripts/check` and `scripts/check --full` passed on clean implementation revision `6828509ce498ccaf48b52e734d45af7c64ed21d9`. The full gate passed 101 repository-tool tests, 46 Rust tests, 1,262 transcript executions (including 33 Python SDK integration executions), and both source/wheel installation tests with native bundle acceptance. The separate R adapter integration passed two cases and 19 assertions. There were 23 declared transcript capability skips; applicable installation checks passed with their Linux-only helper case skipped on macOS. Final follow-up changes are documentation only. All audit-owned containers and VMs, including the SSH host fixture, were confirmed absent.

The [acceptance audit](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/blob/feat/prepared-python/docs/PREPARED_RUNTIME_ACCEPTANCE.md) records exact commands, fixture identities, execution counts, repaired failures, and skipped selectors. Mocked protocol peers are compatibility evidence only. This macOS/Colima/SBX run does not establish Linux controller acceptance or nested restricted Docker namespace support. Optional inherited SBX network-policy and inner-Docker cases remain skipped under the existing provider capabilities. Local/SSH dependency semantics, SQL formatting, and documented resolver trust limitations are unchanged.

Production diff against `origin/main`: **703 additions + 124 deletions = 827 lines**, measured with `scripts/review-diff origin/main` after staging all intended new files. No evaluator, SQL backend, provider framework, or prerequisite PR was added.

title: Bound complete responses using the existing collector
description:
Large output, errors, and recovered responses can overwhelm a tool result. This limits each complete result to 8 KiB of UTF-8 text, including notices, prompts, and terminal state. Oversized text keeps a head and tail with omission counts and retained raw-log references; argument-decoding and resolver errors use the same renderer.

The existing collector remains in place. The preview uses the text it retains, so this layer cannot promise the actual latest tail after its 8 MiB or 4,096-event collection limit. Collector loss has a separate notice from rendered UTF-8 omissions. The next layer replaces collection while keeping this 8 KiB response budget.

Internally, typed response parts preserve image ordering, source receipts, omission accounting, and delivery recovery through final composition. Receipts are captured before the old collector closes a cell file. Empty receipts and fully omitted sources are compacted so repeated cancellation stays bounded. Fixed-width process IDs in recording directory names keep incidental path length from shifting preview cuts.

Public acceptance coverage includes recovery, raw-file accounting, malformed arguments, lifecycle composition, and Python and R clients. Stress evidence retains complete assertions and records repetitions with exact counts.

Incremental diff: 72 files, +3,298/−920; runtime files +961/−498, tests +1,168/−210, snapshots +1,063/−184, documentation +106/−28. Runtime deletions include the 358-line private unit-test module replaced by public coverage. This remains above the advisory 1,000–1,500-addition review target.

title: Cover native fork callbacks and reticulate traceback paths
description:
Fork-child output tests reject native Console callbacks as well as R callbacks, covering the shared `_mcp_console_services` module. The tests retain R-first initialization, successful child output, parent-runtime continuity checks, and the executable direct-suite entry point. Five generated transcripts record the updated callback guard.

Traceback normalization recognizes reticulate’s `rpytools/call.py`, preserving the filename, line number, and complete error while continuing to reject unknown absolute paths.

Runtime fixtures collect public running responses during cold default preparation. External SSH setup remains requirement-free so preprovisioned bare targets can use their installed packages. Exact output and Python/R continuity assertions remain in place.

Generated snapshots record current configured custom-worker descriptions, canonical handshake references, and the complete current DuckDB error and backtrace.

Changes are confined to test support and generated transcripts. Public runtime behavior is unchanged.

title: Add project YAML sandbox configuration
description:
Allow `serve` and ordinary `sandbox` launches to reuse project sandbox settings from `.mcp-console/config.yaml` or `.agents/mcp-console.yaml`. Discovery stays beneath the launch working directory, rejects ambiguity, and preserves defaults when neither file exists. Literal path write grants combine with CLI writable roots; native network and proxy settings use explicit conservative defaults. Project settings are trusted launcher input and can widen permissions. The README explains this boundary, and the live `send` description reflects the captured settings.

Load YAML 1.2 through Saphyr's node API in Rust with an immutable dependency pin. Console checks supported application fields and additive filesystem entry forms; the runner owns native policy validation. Discovered settings are probed through the public sandbox launcher with a no-op process before workload startup or server readiness. Native failures propagate with filename context. Duplicate keys currently use the last value, a documented Saphyr limitation subject to change.

Capture normalized application settings once and explicitly select their child-specific environment payload through the existing sandbox boundary. Initial workers, restarts, crash recovery, and replacements with newly prepared requirements retain the same snapshot, including when a configuration file is created after startup. Explicit complete-policy launches and `serve --no-sandbox` bypass discovery. Native policy construction stays in the sandbox layer; the runner pin and protocol are unchanged.

Public boundary tests cover discovery, parsing, bypasses, native validation, filesystem isolation, real proxy allow/deny requests, and settings retention across launches. Proxy enforcement is also exercised with `network: enabled`, matching the pinned runner's managed routing behavior.

Validated locally with `scripts/check` on macOS, including 47 Rust tests, the full applicable boundary suite, and source and wheel installation checks. Linux enforcement was not exercised locally.

title: Add an unsandboxed server mode
description:
Add `mcp-console serve --no-sandbox` to run evaluated code with server permissions. Sandboxing remains the default; direct mode skips sandbox-owned temporary directories and descendant cleanup. CLI help, MCP tool descriptions, and documentation describe the selected mode.

Internally, launch the existing relay directly, preserve replacement after relay failure, retain native psutil enumeration outside the sandbox, and store R plots in each session's temporary directory. Public regressions cover built-in and custom workers, recovery, host process visibility, and concurrent plots. Startup fixtures also use the configured `uv` to avoid shared-cache bootstrap races.

title: Expose explicit R configuration discovery and editing
description:
R clients can discover configuration once, inspect and edit it as an ordinary S7 `ConsoleConfig`, and launch the chosen settings. This supports both interactive configuration experiments and scheduled agents whose runtime, environment, and permissions need to be visible in code.

- `discover_console_config()` materializes optional global/project files with explicit, replaceable paths; missing discovery files are skipped. `read_console_config()` requires one selected JSON or YAML file and bypasses discovery.
- `materialize_console_config()` fills in native defaults and complete tool presentation. `prune_console_config()` keeps settings that differ from defaults, including meaningful empty values. Both return the same typed object, with full printing and JSON-ready `as.list()` output.
- `console_tool()` now discovers when `config` is omitted. Passing `ConsoleConfig(...)` skips files. Explicit `config = NULL` and the legacy `ConfigDiscovery()` option retain their existing behavior; `resolve_console_config()` remains an alias for full materialization. The README includes migration, comparison, serialization, and scheduled-report examples, including permission edits and the separate environment-inheritance control.
- `FirstAvailablePython`, `StartupConfig`, and read-only parameter schema metadata complete the S7 representation. Fallback chains validate ordering and cardinality at construction. Executable/version and project choices remain explicit arguments, and materialization preserves runtime selection policies rather than locking dependencies.

Internally, native capture owns parsing, layering, validation, materialization, and pruning. All S7 configurations use the same private JSON-file transport for source paths and ordered overrides, keeping large descriptions and startup code out of process arguments. Files are removed after capture. The separate resolved-list launch path is removed. The shared R vignette fixture also preserves the filename encoding required by Windows while retaining its existing cross-platform transcript.

Local verification passed R CMD check, 248 R assertions, focused CLI configuration/help cases, seven website checks, `scripts/format`, and the standard `scripts/check` gate. The installed R tests report the existing S7/rlang import warning. Hosted checks will rerun on the updated head.

title: Materialize editable Console configuration
description:
Tool-prompt evaluations need a way to inspect the generated descriptions and argument schema before editing them. This adds a materialize, edit, and launch workflow that captures configuration once and avoids repeating configuration-file discovery.

- `mcp-console config resolve` exports YAML or JSON with generated instructions, descriptions, parameter visibility, and read-only type and constraint metadata. It uses the existing selection flags and overrides without starting runtimes or preparing packages.
- R's `resolve_console_config()` returns a list that prints in full and supports ordinary `$` edits. `console_tool(config = config)` uses the edited settings and retains the executable, project directory, and sandbox choice.
- Documentation explains that server instructions arrive during MCP initialization, while tool and argument descriptions arrive through `tools/list`. It distinguishes protocol timing from client-dependent model visibility during deferred loading, including the ellmer adapter's behavior.

Internally, export shares configuration capture and presentation generation with the server. Structural schema edits are rejected. Saved descriptions remain literal when parameter visibility changes; runtime-dependent interpreter, package, environment, and cache choices remain launch policies. Python `first_available` retains every candidate, including `active_venv`, for evaluation at the next launch. Interpreter paths that cannot be represented as UTF-8 return a configuration error.

Preparation also avoids waiting on an environment lock held by an idle resolver callback before admission can report the conflict. Windows CI keeps English diagnostics without forcing R's character locale to ASCII. Help and description snapshots match the generated output; the configuration round-trip transcript is shared across platforms.

Local validation passed: the standard `scripts/check` gate, focused configuration, documentation, bootstrap, and resolver cases, 144 installed R package assertions, and all seven website checks. Public export regressions verify fallback launches after removing the selected venv and controlled errors for native non-UTF-8 executable paths on Linux. `scripts/format` completed successfully. The Windows CLI help snapshot was updated from hosted Windows output.

title: Enable live managed sans-R dependencies and automatic imports
description:
## Summary

Local managed Python sessions without R can add distributions to a running idle worker, including in the same request as DuckDB extensions. A reached missing import can infer and prepare a distribution during its Python cell. The worker keeps its interpreter, objects, PID, managed DuckDB catalog, and selected SQL connection; the cell continues from the import without replaying earlier statements. Explicitly selected Python environments remain non-managed, and SQL cells continue to suppress automatic package resolution.

Explicit additions and automatic imports share the host preparation path and native activation operation. The host resolves the complete candidate against the running interpreter, inspects it, checks library compatibility, and prepares retained DuckDB extensions before activation. The worker reports the matching activation before the server commits the manifest, managed environment, and native launch configuration. Restart and crash replacement use that accepted environment.

Validation, resolution, inspection, compatibility rejection, and cancellation leave the accepted environment unchanged. A failure after activation may have begun requires restart before further requirement changes. A successful activation remains accepted if the requested module is still missing, its initialization fails, or a later statement fails. `requirements.action="get"` and recordings expose committed declarations only.

## Validation

- `scripts/test client_server/python/test_without_r client_server/sql/test_without_r` (direct and native sandbox modes)
- `scripts/test client_server/requirements/test_python client_server/requirements/test_python_transitions client_server/requirements/test_python_automatic client_server/requirements/test_python_automatic_lifecycle`
- `scripts/test client_server/requirements/test_actions client_server/sql/test_catalog client_server/sql/test_connections client_server/recording/test_journal client_server/recording/test_markdown client_server/lifecycle/test_restart`
- `scripts/test client_server/server/test_tools::initializes_and_lists_tools`
- `scripts/check` on the committed revision

Production diff: 491 additions and 114 deletions, 605 lines total, measured with `scripts/review-diff origin/main` after staging new files.

title: Allow live Python package additions in managed sans-R sessions
description:
## Summary

Allow an idle local managed Python session without R to add new named distributions through `requirements.action: add` (the default), either standalone or before a Python or SQL cell. This lets users prepare explicit packages without replacing the interpreter or losing Python and SQL state.

## User-facing changes

- Successful additions preserve Python objects, the worker process, the managed DuckDB catalog, and the selected SQL connection. Plain restart and crash replacement use the newly accepted environment.
- Already-retained declarations are no-ops. Changing the requirement for an already-declared distribution, interpreter constraints, publication cutoffs, or a `set` or `reset` declaration still requires restart. Simultaneous effective Python-package and DuckDB-extension additions remain unavailable live. The add-only check applies to declarations; complete resolution can select different versions of existing or transitive dependencies. Live activation does not lock versions or guarantee package compatibility. Explicitly selected Python environments remain unmanaged, and automatic missing-import installation remains disabled.
- Validation, resolution, inspection, compatibility, and cancellation failures leave the accepted worker and declaration intact and withhold same-call code and input. An activation exception retains its Python traceback and requires restart before further requirement changes; arbitrary activation-script side effects are not rolled back.

## Internal changes

- Use the server's requirement delta and shared PEP 508 parser to admit add-only declarations. Resolve the complete candidate through the hidden resolver constrained to the running executable, inspect it, check native library compatibility, and prepare retained DuckDB extensions against that candidate without cloning or mutating the accepted environment.
- Carry the approved native configuration through the existing preparation path. The worker uses `activate_managed_environment`; its activation report commits the manifest and native launch configuration together before same-call code runs. Existing requirement snapshots and recordings publish the accepted addition. Both private protocol documents specify the native payload, activation receipt, and commit ordering. Activation diagnostics use the console sideband before the failure receipt, so raw-stderr scheduling cannot separate the traceback from the response.
- Keep preparation protocol v3 compatible with existing SSH peers by omitting the local-only interpreter constraint when unused and accepting requests without it.

## Notes

Local validation passed: `scripts/check` (the default gate), the complete sans-R Python and SQL transcript suites, and focused R-present activation, requirement-action, automatic-import, SQL, and lifecycle regressions. The installed-build acceptance cases passed in direct and native-sandbox modes, including deterministic traceback delivery with fd 2 separated from the sideband. The legacy v3 SSH peer and hidden-resolver CLI regressions also passed.

Production diff against `origin/main`: 564 additions and 87 deletions, 651 lines total (including moved code and review fixes).

title: Support local Python sessions without R
description:
Allow local Python sessions without installing R. When R is absent, ordinary `mcp-console serve` uses Console's existing host `uv` resolver and default NumPy/pandas manifest, with no interpreter-selection variable or special launch flag. If `uv` is absent, selection checks `python3` then `python` on `PATH`; if none is available, the error explains what to install. An available resolver that fails reports its failure without fallback. Invalid `R_HOME` and broken discovered R installations remain R errors.

The session retains its environment and executable across cells, restart, and worker replacement. Embedded Python uses the selected site-packages, prefixes, and executable, including for subprocesses and multiprocessing. Workspace imports work without `PYTHONPATH`, and startup does not add the executable directory to the import path. Native startup accepts equivalent executable paths and ignores conflicting `PYTHONHOME` and `PYTHONPLATLIBDIR` values. Existing explicit `RETICULATE_PYTHON` selection remains compatible with sandbox environment overrides and disabled inheritance. Persistent objects, output, exception recovery, input, interrupts, restart, recording, and Matplotlib plots are supported; Matplotlib must already be installed in the selected environment.

Internally, the server captures runtime availability and selection, reuses the host resolver's configuration, caches, version ranking, cancellation, and subprocess cleanup, and passes the selection through internal launch configuration. Resolution invokes no R programs and installs no packages inside the worker sandbox. Startup reuses one coordinator, the embedded Python evaluator, native inspection, and shared setup; Python-only workers construct neither reticulate nor an R DBI backend. Inspection runs in isolated mode. Startup failures preserve Python diagnostics and restore thread state before extension-library teardown. Direct relay lifetimes and the native runner retire private worker storage after failure, restart, and shutdown without deleting retained environments or shared caches. Direct cleanup failures report the remaining directory and filesystem error; a failed restart does not execute its submitted cell.

This slice supports local initial resolution and Python execution. Live requirements, automatic missing-import installation, R/SQL cells, SSH, and prepared targets are unavailable in the new mode. The MCP schema and errors describe these limits, and rejected requests preserve Python state. R-present requirements and SQL behavior remain unchanged, and direct R launches preserve native `R_HOME` path bytes. Managed Python-only Quarto recordings declare NumPy and pandas separately from live-requirement capability. Documentation describes the new mode; canonical Python-only handshake snapshots retain full comparison before `!same-as` compaction. Existing R-present snapshots and CI configuration are unchanged.

Validation at `61c588d1`: `scripts/check` passed, including core checks, **1,059 transcript executions** (54 capability skips), and source/wheel installation checks. Public MCP acceptance passed all **26 cases / 48 direct and native-sandbox executions** against an installed wheel in an R-free Ubuntu 24.04 container, with primary cases leaving `RETICULATE_PYTHON` unset. Direct cases run as an unprivileged user to exercise permission failures; native-sandbox cases use a root-owned installation in a privileged container for namespace support. The container has no host R mounts. All 48 executions also passed with macOS framework Python 3.13.

`scripts/review-diff origin/main` reports **652 production additions + 84 deletions = 736 changed lines**.

title: Add native built-in sandbox profiles
description:
Project editing now needs only this configuration in `.agents/console/config.yaml`:

```yaml
extends: ":workspace"
```

The native baseline permits edits beneath the fixed launch workspace while keeping `.git`, `.agents`, `.codex`, and `.claude` readable and protected from writes by default. The leading colon identifies a native built-in; `":read-only"` is also supported, and omission preserves existing behavior. Tool descriptions and implemented documentation describe the active permissions. Custom profiles, inheritance, initialization, and other configuration features remain proposals in the design sketch.

The runner pin advances to the published [native interface extension, `2d0ad797`](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/codex/commit/2d0ad797210de821c07d1f18e4f1ffdcf06589cb), added directly to the current `mcp-console/sandbox-runner/rust-v0.154.0` patch branch. Its additive protocol-2 `extends`, `workspace`, and `workspace_options` fields select a built-in, retain a fixed workspace, and expose the two upstream temporary-directory options. The adapter stays within the extracted runner package and reuses `PermissionProfile::read_only()`, `PermissionProfile::workspace_write_with(...)`, native policy types, and workspace-root materialization, including Git pointer handling.

Console supplies `.claude` through an ordinary native read entry and defaults both `exclude_tmpdir_env_var` and `exclude_slash_tmp` to `true`; private writable temporary storage remains available. Explicit values retain native precedence, including deliberate metadata write exceptions and unrestricted/external filesystem kinds. Omitted filesystem and network settings inherit the constructor baseline. Existing writable roots, native-field forwarding, `serve --no-sandbox`, and discovery-free `sandbox --config-env` retain their contracts. The captured workspace survives directory changes, restarts, crash recovery, and worker replacement.

Public acceptance tests failed before implementation. The runner's complete public suite passed on macOS (87 tests) and namespace-capable x86-64 Ubuntu 24.04 (96 tests), with macOS Bazel, formatting, and scoped Clippy also passing. Console's full `scripts/check`, including source and wheel installation checks, passed on macOS. All nine new profile cases passed on macOS and Linux using release runners built from the exact published pin; 32 applicable existing configuration and writable-root cases also passed on Linux.

The new enforcement cases cover both YAML forms, project edits, readable metadata, blocked mutations and directory replacement, subprocesses, enclosing writable roots, explicit exceptions and read denials, absent paths, Git worktree indirection, temporary-directory options, raw-policy compatibility, and fixed permissions across worker generations. Linux retains a native limitation: an ancestor read-denial mount can hide a narrower read grant, and a further nested denial can fail during mount setup. Equivalent raw and selected policies reproduce this behavior; macOS honors the narrower read grant. Native missing-path and host-capability limits remain documented.

title: Support flat Python package configuration
description:
Managed Python settings now accept the same flat layout as R, so ordinary configuration no longer needs an extra `managed` key:

```yaml
r:
  packages: [dplyr]
  resolution: implicit
python:
  packages: [numpy, pandas]
  resolution: explicit
```

`python.version` is supported too. The nested `python.managed` form, existing-environment selections, and `first_available` candidates remain valid. An empty `python: {}` explicitly selects managed defaults; omitted or `null` Python settings retain the existing launch-environment behavior. Guides and the starter configuration prefer the flat form.

Internally, each input layer expands the shorthand before merging, so flat and nested settings compose across files and ordered overrides. Mixed selection forms are rejected during final validation. Runtime selection and preparation are unchanged, and configuration exports retain their nested representation for existing consumers.

title: Isolate caches for local sandboxed sessions
description:
Sandboxed dependency preparation can write artifacts to caches shared with host uv, R, and DuckDB processes, which may later execute those artifacts with host permissions. This PR gives local sandboxed sessions Console-specific dependency caches and restricts default resolver persistent writes to those caches on macOS and Linux.

Users get `cache: console` by default. uv, IR libraries, reticulate tooling, renv, pak/pkgcache, DuckDB extensions, prepared Matplotlib caches, and Python user/bytecode caches use a dedicated `dependencies` directory beneath the platform-specific Console cache: `$HOME/.cache/mcp-console` on Linux, `$HOME/Library/Caches/mcp-console` on macOS, or `%LOCALAPPDATA%/mcp-console/cache` on Windows. An absolute `XDG_CACHE_HOME` selects `<XDG_CACHE_HOME>/mcp-console/dependencies`, including when `HOME` is absent. `cache: host` or `serve -c cache=host` restores host installations and cache settings while retaining resolver sandboxing on macOS/Linux. `--no-sandbox` defaults to host caches; explicit Console caching with unsandboxed or remote execution is rejected.

Internally, Console captures cache selection before launching the resolver and worker, overrides inherited cache-location variables, and retains that selection across preparation calls and worker restarts. On macOS and Linux, default resolver grants cover only the dependency directory and private temporary storage. The sibling `mcp-console/sandbox` source checkout and build artifacts used by host-side companion staging remain read-only to that sandboxed resolver. Console creates its dependency root even with explicit filesystem entries; those entries still replace the default grants. Host R and installed resolver executables remain readable. The download allowlist includes Astral's installer redirect domain.

Public session coverage checks cache redirection, host opt-out, restart retention, cold directory creation, missing `HOME` with absolute XDG configuration, companion-cache write denial, and real managed R/Python/DuckDB artifacts. Existing host-cache and recording fixtures select host caching explicitly; resolver process and font probes follow native launcher ownership and confirmed retirement.

Windows redirects cache paths but still prepares dependencies with host permissions. SSH cache behavior is unchanged; Docker/SBX use preinstalled environments. Worker XDG and Matplotlib caches retain private temporary storage, and explicitly selected Python retains preinstalled packages and DuckDB extensions. On macOS, cold reticulate uv bootstrap remains blocked by the system shell's temporary-file behavior; use uv on `PATH` or an installed `RETICULATE_UV` selection.

title: Enable live DuckDB extension additions in managed sans-R sessions
description:
## Summary

Allow an idle, running local sans-R session with managed Python to add DuckDB extensions without restarting the worker. This lets a user prepare an extension after creating Python objects or a DuckDB catalog, then load it on the existing managed connection.

## User-facing behavior

- `requirements.duckdb` additions work alone or before a same-call Python or SQL cell. An unchanged Python requirement can accompany the addition.
- The worker PID, interpreter, Python objects, managed DuckDB catalog, and selected SQL connection remain in place. Preparation installs files through the host resolver; the worker loads an extension only when user code requests `LOAD`.
- Effective Python package, interpreter-constraint, or exclusion-date changes, and changed `set` or `reset` declarations, still require explicit restart. Unsupported mixed requests fail before preparation.
- A failed or interrupted installation leaves the worker and committed declaration unchanged. Same-call code and input are withheld; already cached downloads may remain. `requirements.action="get"` continues to show the committed declaration during preparation.

## Internal changes

- Select live eligibility from the effective requirement delta and reuse the running-worker admission, reservation, and generation-checked commit path.
- Share the Python-backed extension resolver path with startup and restart preparation, using the accepted managed Python environment and captured extension-cache directory. No package resolution, interpreter inspection, Python activation, worker database operation, or permission change is added.
- Update the managed sans-R capability description and documentation. Additions use the existing requirement snapshot and ordinary call/result recordings, without a replacement boundary.

## Notes

The complete sans-R SQL suite and tool handshake passed in direct and native sandbox modes. Focused requirement-action, R-backed SQL extension, catalog, and lifecycle regressions passed. The required `scripts/check` default local gate passed; the full local profile was not run.

`scripts/review-diff origin/main` reports 69 production lines added and 53 deleted, or 122 additions plus deletions.

title: Fall back to home Console directory for recordings and config
description:
## Summary

Console keeps projects without an existing `.agents/console` directory free of session records by writing them under `~/.agents/console` instead. Launches also discover the home Console configuration when the project configuration file is absent.

## User-facing changes

- Recordings use the launch directory's `.agents/console/sessions/` only when `.agents/console` already exists there. Otherwise, they use `~/.agents/console/sessions/`.
- `serve` and ordinary `sandbox` launches read `~/.agents/console/config.yaml` when `.agents/console/config.yaml` is absent. An existing project file takes precedence, including when it is invalid. CLI overrides still apply afterward.
- `MCP_CONSOLE_HOME` selects an absolute fallback Console directory in place of `~/.agents/console`, containing `config.yaml` and `sessions/`. Project configuration and an existing project recording directory retain their independent precedence.
- Raw-log paths are relative to the launch directory for project recordings and absolute for home recordings. A home path that cannot be represented in UTF-8 disables recording with a diagnostic instead of advertising a path that cannot be used.

## Internal changes

- A shared Console home resolver serves configuration discovery and recording selection. Directory inspection errors disable recording with a diagnostic.
- Transcript cases and MCP fixtures use private `MCP_CONSOLE_HOME` directories while preserving `HOME` and the host tool environment. This keeps R, uv, and Docker state available without probing tools or reconstructing their paths. Transcript cases, wheel smoke evaluations, installed-client checks, and R integration tests use temporary workspaces and remove their recordings after shutdown. Fixtures leave project configuration absent unless a case supplies it; home-fallback cases opt in explicitly.
- Public cases cover configuration precedence, recording selection, unrepresentable home paths, and fixture isolation. Focused-runner regressions verify that unrelated cases never probe R. The background stderr fixture confirms the expected bytes have crossed the pipe before checking the idle preview. Documentation and tool descriptions reflect the selected paths.

title: Support sandboxed execution on Linux
description:
Linux now supports default sandboxed `serve` and `sandbox -- COMMAND`, with read-only host files, private writable temporary storage, restricted networking, and PID isolation. Startup fails when host namespace or procfs policy prevents isolation; `--no-sandbox` remains an explicit opt-out. Targets retain inherited ignored signal dispositions after sandbox setup.

Internally, add a Linux subreaper manager with pidfd-based cleanup and recovery, share runner setup across platforms, and package the pinned runner and bubblewrap in Linux wheels. Verify both bundled executables during build and before launch. The runner update fixes local IPC and stdin handoff. Also release startup admission before publishing replacement completion so an immediate retry can prepare requirements. Relay and worker protocols are unchanged.

Update lifecycle fixtures to resolve namespace PIDs before host signaling, consume generation-specific checkpoints before retirement, and reject broadcast-style cleanup IDs. Preserve platform-specific denial diagnostics in the transcript coverage and document Linux prerequisites and signal behavior.

Validation passed in an isolated Linux container: `scripts/check-core`, all applicable sandbox suites, the interruption suite, and rebuilt installed-wheel smoke checks including an empty `PATH`. macOS validation runs in CI.

title: Allow idle workers to prepare R requirements
description:
## Summary

Late R package requirements currently force callers to restart the worker and lose in-memory state. This change applies the complete resolved IR library to an idle built-in worker, so new packages become discoverable without replacing the R session.

## User-facing changes

- `session prepare` can add R requirements after the built-in worker has started while preserving its PID, globals, and other live state.
- The new complete managed IR library replaces the previous managed entry in `.libPaths()`, preserves other library paths, and remains available to later worker generations.
- Mixed R and Python preparation retains both configurations only after both live changes succeed.
- After a synchronized failure may have partially changed the live worker, evaluation remains available so callers can save state, while new requirement additions return `[restart required]` until an explicit restart. Transport and protocol failures still stop a worker whose usability is unknown.

## Internal changes

- Add `prepare_r`, `r_prepared`, and `r_preparation_failed` sideband messages backed by a fixed private R bridge.
- Keep live Python candidates provisional until a mixed operation succeeds. A failed mixed operation may reuse its matching provisional candidate only to keep the current worker evaluable; it is never retained across worker replacement.
- Add generation-scoped admission state for requirement changes and clear it after a successful explicit restart.
- Update the MCP descriptions, architecture and protocol documentation, and public transcript coverage for live R preparation, mixed failure behavior, state preservation, and restart retention.

title: Bootstrap Rust project
description:
## Why

Start implementation from the design sketches with the smallest executable Rust package and a shared local/CI check path. This keeps the first review narrow and makes the boundary between implemented and proposed behavior explicit.

## What changed

- Creates a single Rust binary package with package metadata and a committed lockfile.
- Adds the first public behavior: `mcp-console --version`.
- Tests that behavior through the compiled binary.
- Adds `scripts/check` and CI for formatting, Clippy with warnings denied, and tests.
- Adds a root `AGENTS.md` that records the current state, repository map, and narrow-PR guidance.
- Updates the root README with the implemented command and local check entry point.
- Updates the draft CLI document to use `--version`.

## User-facing changes

`mcp-console --version` prints the package name and version. The MCP server and language runtimes are not implemented yet.

## Internal changes

The repository now has one dependency-free Cargo package. Local development and CI invoke the same check script.

## Testing

- `scripts/check`

title: Initialize enabled runtimes eagerly after worker transport readiness
description:
The server already starts the worker while the client connects, but interpreter initialization waits for the first cell. This PR initializes enabled R and Python during connection startup so that work can finish before the first cell arrives. MCP initialization, tool discovery, and pings remain responsive.

- Startup hooks run without submitted code. Their output, plots, and input prompts are available through `send`.
- An early cell waits for initialization and runs at most once. Timeouts, polling, and response cancellation preserve it. An actual startup interrupt discards the waiting cell; other incomplete setup preserves the cell and its diagnostics.
- The first requirements `set` or `reset` can replace an unused prewarmed worker without an explicit restart. Failed preparation preserves the original worker.
- DuckDB connections and queries remain lazy. Custom workers retain their existing launch behavior. Bare R remains usable when Python or its selection adapter is unavailable.

Internally, initialization uses the existing serialized worker thread after transport readiness connects callbacks. A separate bootstrap receipt gates evaluation; the controller orders interrupt admission against cell release so a late signal still discards the waiting cell. Python services restore signal handling after R startup. Preparation reserves startup callbacks before locking the environment, and deferred sideband events retain their order in a private temporary spool capped at 16 MiB. Retirement releases the spool and confirms worker shutdown before replacement.

Local sandbox and target workers retain the controller's enabled-language selection across restarts. The private target launch protocol advances to version 10, requiring matching executables on SSH and prepared targets. Preparation protocol version 5 is unchanged.

title: Start the default worker eagerly in the background
description:
Begin preparing and launching the default built-in worker when the MCP server starts, so the first cell can reuse a worker that has already reached transport readiness. MCP initialization, tool discovery, and pings proceed independently. R, Python, and SQL retain first-use initialization. Tool presentation remains configuration-derived and stable before and after readiness; the timeout description reflects the new deadline.

Early cells occupy the existing evaluation slot. One observation deadline includes shared startup, and expiry returns the ordinary running response. Empty polling collects the accepted cell's result without resubmitting code. Cancelling an early call releases its response wait while the accepted cell and shared startup continue; connection closure owns cleanup.

The existing startup owner publishes one shared readiness result. Requirements use the existing preparation and retirement machinery, including replacement of an unused prewarmed worker after successful resolution. Once code or nonempty input reaches the worker, the existing live-change and explicit-restart rules apply. Custom workers keep lazy launch. Early tool records wait for recording metadata, and failed discovery discards them. The worker protocol is unchanged.

Default preparation and worker launch now occur even when a client submits no code. First-use interpreter startup remains part of the first evaluation. The startup and send documentation describes acceptance, cancellation, timeout exceptions, and this trade-off.

Local validation passed: focused public-API regressions, full core checks, and source/wheel installation checks. The full capability-applicable transcript profile passed all 1,388 executions before the final main merge; after integration, `scripts/check` and all 256 affected Python executions, including the 20 new optional-import executions, passed.

title: Add configurable Docker execution targets
description:
Allow a project to run its persistent R/Python/SQL console in a Linux image while keeping the MCP server and recordings on the controller. This lets the image supply Console and its analysis environment, with Console owning container creation and retirement.

The public configuration keeps transport and compute separate. Local Docker targets support an existing image with `never`, `if_missing`, or `always` pull policy, or a build from an explicit context and separate Dockerfile. Configuration also accepts a container workspace, command argv prefix, explicit bind mounts, and an optional user. Omitted targets and explicit local host targets retain the existing launch path; SSH configuration and its command default are preserved.

- Resolve one immutable image before readiness and use it for every probe and worker generation. Restart creates a fresh container: bind-mounted files persist, while the writable container layer is discarded.
- Probe compatibility, shared R, Python, workspace, and native policy inside the image. Use preinstalled packages and disable dynamic preparation, including worker callbacks and reticulate managed environments.
- Preserve native sandbox defaults and target-side validation. Explicit `external-sandbox` delegates filesystem and network enforcement to Docker; `--no-sandbox` skips the inner runner while retaining owned container retirement.
- Keep journals, output spools, and image bytes at controller paths. Record image and generation container identities, and make Docker Quarto projections non-executing by default. Declared mounts can expose recordings to the worker.

Internally, a local ownership helper tracks each container from creation, observes controller and attachment loss independently of blocked output, and requires confirmed removal before replacement. Image setup is cancellable and separate from generation lifetime. SSH and Docker share the versioned target bootstrap and target-side launcher; the relay-worker protocol is unchanged.

The change also fixes two issues exposed by container validation: R errors and interrupts now unwind within a live C frame while preserving protection-stack roots, and macOS child launch enumerates open descriptors instead of scanning the full descriptor limit. Public acceptance cases cover Docker setup, mounts, mixed runtime behavior, cancellation, transport loss, and retirement, alongside the existing local and SSH regressions.

`docs/DOCKER.md` and `examples/docker/Dockerfile` provide the complete schema, build instructions, prerequisites, and lifecycle limits. The tested ordinary daemon rejected nested bubblewrap namespaces; that failure remains explicit, with no added privileges or fallback. External mode uses ordinary bridge networking and supplies no native metadata protection. Cleanup cannot be guaranteed after daemon, host, or ownership-helper failure. Private registry authentication, remote TLS daemons, and BuildKit cancellation remain unverified. SSH plus Docker, managed container package preparation, file synchronization, and reusable containers are deferred.

title: Support reciprocal `ir` and `uv` resolver bootstrap
description:
## Summary

MCP Console can now establish dynamic environment resolution from either `ir` or `uv` instead of requiring both host commands. This keeps release-wheel startup working when the host provides one resolver entry point while preserving a broken selected executable as a clear startup error.

If neither command nor ambient reticulate can provide a resolver, the server now starts a bare runtime instead of failing MCP initialization.

## User-facing changes

- Prefer `ir` on `PATH`; otherwise run `uv tool run --from r-lib-ir ir`.
- When `ir` is the only command, resolve the managed R library first and use its exact `Rscript` and reticulate installation to obtain `uv` for managed Python.
- Try ambient reticulate when neither command is on `PATH`.
- In bare mode, retain R, Python, and SQL cells, omit `requirements`, and disable automatic R and Python package resolution.
- Make the active capability clear in tool prose, documentation, and the transcript journal.

## Internal changes

- Retain the selected `ir` command, R installation, and `uv` executable for the session.
- Use an embedded R probe with controlled unavailable statuses and one machine-readable `uv` path.
- Derive Quarto managed defaults from the capability recorded in `session_started`.
- Exercise release wheels through `uv tool run` and fail if startup attempts to use `uvx`.

title: Add default DuckDB extensions and restart-time requirements
description:
## Summary

Prepare DuckDB's JSON and ICU extensions for the built-in worker so common JSON and time-zone operations work without a separate requirement request. FTS and other specialized extensions remain on demand.

This also makes `session(action = "restart")` accept the same additive R, Python, and DuckDB requirements as `prepare`, so callers can change the retained environment and replace the worker in one operation.

## User-facing changes

- Built-in server startup installs JSON and ICU into DuckDB's native version- and platform-specific cache without loading extension code outside the sandbox.
- Restart requests can add R packages, Python packages, and DuckDB extensions. Omitting requirements still restarts with the retained environment unchanged.
- Custom workers continue to skip default environment preflights. They can add R and DuckDB requirements during restart, while managed Python additions remain unavailable.

## Internal changes

- Restart resolves the complete R, DuckDB, and Python candidate before stopping the current worker. The retained environment is committed only after every required resolver succeeds, so a failed mixed request preserves the running worker and prior checkpoint.
- Public transcript coverage exercises default JSON and ICU loading, failed and successful mixed restarts, functional FTS use after replacement, and custom-worker restart preparation.
- The tool schema and protocol documentation now describe the default extension set and the expanded restart contract.

title: Add on-demand DuckDB extension preparation
description:
## Summary

Add on-demand preparation for core DuckDB extensions. Clients can include `"duckdb": ["json"]` in `session(action = "prepare")`, allowing DuckDB to download extensions with host network access while keeping extension loading and execution inside the sandbox.

This uses DuckDB's own installer instead of inspecting or intercepting submitted SQL.

## User-facing changes

- Add additive, idempotent `requirements.duckdb` entries for core extension names.
- Store prepared extensions in DuckDB's standard version- and platform-specific `~/.duckdb/extensions` cache and expose that cache read-only to workers.
- Preserve an idle worker's R, Python, and SQL state while preparing extensions, and retain prepared extensions across R updates and worker replacement.
- Allow custom workers to prepare explicit R requirements and DuckDB extensions when they implement `prepare_r` and honor the supplied R library and extension-cache environment. Managed Python preparation remains limited to server-managed workers.
- Reject repository names, URLs, paths, SQL fragments, unknown core extensions, and DuckDB additions during `restart` with explicit errors.

## Internal changes

- Run DuckDB's `INSTALL ... FROM core` through the existing cancellable host-resolver lifecycle, using the DuckDB version selected by each resolved R environment. Warm cache entries remain no-ops.
- Track the resolved R libraries that may supply DuckDB to a live worker and populate each applicable version-specific extension cache before committing retained state.
- Keep the worker's writable extension, secret, and spill paths private, disable automatic installation, and expose the host cache only as a secondary extension directory.
- Keep both nanoarrow and arrow in the SQL preview bridge: nanoarrow carries DuckDB's DBI Arrow stream, while arrow supplies the bounded record batch used for slicing and temporary DuckDB registration.

title: Support MCP_CONSOLE_CACHE_DIR for managed caches
description:
`MCP_CONSOLE_CACHE_DIR` lets users relocate Console-managed caches independently of host tool cache settings. Nonempty values must be absolute; dependencies live under `<MCP_CONSOLE_CACHE_DIR>/dependencies`. The setting takes precedence over XDG/platform defaults, is ignored with `cache: host`, and retains the current defaults when unset or empty.

The existing resolver cache selector applies the override before constructing dependency paths and write grants. Public regressions cover inherited and configured environments, startup without `HOME`, explicit resolver grants, restart, validation, and host-cache opt-out. The configuration and cache guides document the setting.

title: Add workspace profile and sandbox tempdir modes
description:
Adds a `workspace` sandbox profile and a single `tempdir` selector to `config.yaml`, shared by `serve` and the ordinary `sandbox` command.

```yaml
sandbox:
  profile: workspace
  tempdir: managed # managed | read_write | read_only
```

`workspace` reuses the native `:workspace` profile, including its metadata protections. Explicit filesystem permissions compose with it; network selection remains independent. Omitting the profile retains the existing host-read baseline. The R `SandboxPolicy()` API, materialized configuration, and documentation use the same settings.

- `managed` (default) creates private writable storage, redirects temporary environment variables, and removes the storage after retirement.
- `read_write` preserves the configured/inherited temporary environment and grants writes to host temp locations, including under the base read-only policy.
- `read_only` adds no automatic temporary write grants; explicit filesystem permissions still apply.

On Windows, `read_write` exports the granted host default as `TMPDIR`, `TEMP`, and `TMP` when all three effective child variables are unset or empty. Existing nonempty temp selections retain their values. Relative values keep their normal runtime meaning; their write grants are captured against the launch directory. Use absolute temp paths when working directories can change.

Console guarantees tempdir cleanup only with an active sandbox and `tempdir: managed`. `--no-sandbox` skips managed storage and its cache redirection. In other modes, Console adds no temporary-directory cleanup guarantees. R uses its normal embedded shutdown sequence, including best-effort session-tempdir cleanup; its usual `PATH` and filesystem-permission limits apply. Native Python DuckDB keeps its normal storage defaults and persistence outside managed mode. Hiding SQL in `languages` preserves access through Python.

Windows configuration rejects case-colliding names in the effective worker and resolver environments after layering and merging. Exact-spelling overrides remain supported; Unix names remain case-sensitive. Console-owned assignments and removals retain precedence over differently cased Windows keys. MXC enforcement is unchanged.

Internally, the native runner owns managed storage. The DBI adapter skips DuckDB non-query fetches to avoid deferred warnings from successful DDL/DML. CI fixtures use the shared MXC capability gate and wait for interruption completion.

Validation:

- Targeted public configuration, materialization, sandbox profile/tempdir, SQL startup, R selection, and real `renv` tests on macOS, rerun without snapshot updates.
- R configuration and Console tool integration tests.
- `scripts/check`, `scripts/format`, `scripts/test --full --list`, and `git diff --check` on macOS.
- Native Windows build, configuration acceptance, and a controlled public startup regression for differently cased Console-owned variables. The environment-collision and owned-marker regressions were verified to fail before their fixes.

The managed cleanup regression includes a non-writable subtree and an external symlink whose target contents and permissions must remain intact. A public sandbox probe confirmed the documented relative-temp-path behavior before and after `chdir()`.

Native Linux checks and the full functional suite were not run locally for this update. The shared Windows transcript runner could not bootstrap because uv reported an untrusted mount point in the host Python installation. Native MXC fallback/SQL storage cases and a selected complete-policy proxy check were blocked by existing legacy Console sandbox accounts. The controlled Windows startup regression passes without launching an MXC workload.

title: Add --no-global-config and --config-file
description:
Allow launchers to use project configuration alone or select one configuration file without loading automatic sources.

- Add `--no-global-config` to load project configuration and CLI overrides only.
- Add `--config-file PATH` to use a single YAML or JSON file, then apply explicit `-c` overrides. Missing files and conflicting selectors fail launch.
- Support both options before or after `serve` and ordinary `sandbox`, and document file selection and existing inline configuration options.

Internally, reuse the existing loader and settings compiler, distinguish required files from optional discovered files, and construct Console home paths from native components for consistent Windows diagnostics. Update public regressions and generated help/error snapshots.

The macOS local gate and 46 focused CLI cases passed, along with 11 targeted native Windows configuration/help cases. A broader Windows runtime case could not complete because the host R library lacks `duckdb`. Linux was not exercised locally.

title: Add yyjsonr to default R requirements
description:
Add `yyjsonr` to the default managed R requirements so JSON parsing is available in newly prepared R sessions. Document it alongside the other defaults. Explicit declaration replacement can omit it; reset restores it. Runtime infrastructure requirements remain unchanged.

Extend the public requirements and first-cell preparation cases to check the declared default, managed-library location, namespace loading, and exact package request sent to `ir`. Regenerate affected requirement, Python activation, SSH preparation, DuckDB, and mixed-language recording snapshots through their public cases. Refresh stale custom-worker presentation, managed SQL snapshot aliases, and the current Ragnar dependency error. The production change is one addition to the default package list.

The requirement-action suite and managed-R case passed in direct and sandbox modes after regeneration and without updates. Full core checks passed, and all 1,353 locally available transcript executions passed across the full run and focused continuations after snapshot refreshes. Source and wheel installation acceptance passed. `scripts/format` passed Ruff, Yamark, rustfmt, and Air. Validation unset inherited `RUST_LOG`.

`scripts/check --full` did not complete in one uninterrupted run: optional external SSH preparation encountered a cold DuckDB source build and shared R installation lock contention; subsequent runs stopped at stale snapshots, whose public cases were regenerated and rechecked. The completed local coverage excludes optional external SSH, Docker, SBX, and Linux-only capabilities. Localhost SSH remains covered; hosted Linux validation is separate.

title: Preserve worker console output channels
description:
## Summary

Preserve ordinary and diagnostic console identity from the embedded R boundary through the worker protocol and internal output tape. This keeps information available for future transcripts or UI presentation without changing the current MCP response shape.

## User-facing changes

MCP output is unchanged: ordered adjacent text still renders as the same merged text content blocks.

The custom-worker wire contract now uses `console_output` and `console_diagnostic` message kinds. The former `output` kind is no longer accepted.

## Internal changes

- map `R_WriteConsoleEx` type 0 to `console_output`, and nonzero types and `R_ShowMessage` to `console_diagnostic`
- carry console channel identity until MCP projection while keeping direct fd 1 and fd 2 capture distinct
- update Zod, protocol documentation, and public wire goldens, including reticulate stdout and stderr coverage

title: Improve mixed-language console guidance
description:
## Summary

MCP Console already provides a persistent R, Python, and DuckDB SQL workbench, but its registered tool descriptions did not communicate the full range of uses or show agents how to choose between languages and move objects between them. The generated `session` schema also hid useful field information behind references, and R code needed to spell `reticulate::py` to access Python globals.

This PR describes both quick, general-purpose computation and longer mixed-language analysis. The tool descriptions now cover arithmetic, parsing, file inspection, language selection, exact object-sharing paths, plotting, package preparation, session control, sandbox boundaries, and ordinary language errors. The human-facing README demonstrates a Python to R to SQL to Python to R analysis without intermediate files.

## Public-facing changes

- Python reads R globals through `r.name`, R reads Python globals through `py$name`, SQL scans R data frames by name, and R borrows the DuckDB catalog through `sql_connection()`.
- R exposes `py` through the attached `tools:mcp-console` environment without attaching reticulate. The binding survives clearing R global state and still permits a same-named global binding to take precedence.
- The `session` schema is inlined so clients can display its actions and requirement fields directly. Its descriptions explain initial R preparation, live Python additions, restart behavior, and host-side package installation.
- The plotting descriptions cover managed R graphics and cell-scoped Matplotlib capture.
- The `stdin` description states that MCP supplies text and the console queues its UTF-8 encoding exactly, without adding a newline.

## Implementation

The runtime change is one forwarding active binding beside the existing `sql_connection()` helper. Public transcript tests cover access before and after clearing R global state, global shadowing, the generated schemas, and the registered guidance. Golden transcripts and the exact-description reference are updated with the public interface.

## Testing

- `./scripts/check`

title: Let configuration files override client defaults
description:
Let global and project configuration choose Console's sandbox profile ahead of the client's launch preference. Add repeatable `--default-config KEY=VALUE` assignments below configuration files, while ordinary `-c` overrides retain highest priority. Generated client registrations use this defaults layer for inherited permissions, so projects can select another profile without editing the client command.

Make `config init` select `sandbox.profile: workspace`, with comments explaining project writes, protected metadata, host reads, and the launch directory. Overridden profiles receive their own guidance. Keep filesystem customization examples commented, including guidance for restricting writes to selected directories.

Internally, reuse the assignment parser and merge rules for defaults and overrides, preserve file discovery and final validation, and render guidance from the validated profile selection. Update the configuration and onboarding guides, CLI help, public acceptance coverage, and generated snapshots.

title: Add config init for shared Console settings
description:
Add `mcp-console config init` so users can create and edit shared Console settings without starting from a blank file. It creates `.agents/console/config.yaml` in the current directory, including outside Git. `--global` selects Console home, and `--directory PATH` selects another existing project directory.

The starter spells out workspace writes and read-only project metadata, with examples for temporary storage, network access and localhost services, package preparation, Python environments, environment variables, and cache relocation. `##` marks explanations and `#` marks YAML to uncomment; the header links to the full configuration reference.

Ordered `-c`/`--config` assignments override the starter permissions. Other defaults remain implicit, and discovered configuration is not copied into the new file. The command reports its destination and contents; `--dry-run` previews them without writing. Existing destinations cause an error and remain untouched.

Internally, reuse normal configuration validation and YAML serialization, with a private layout for guidance and examples. Create files atomically without replacing existing paths or preparing interpreters and packages. Add public CLI coverage for creation, overrides, previews, and loading uncommented examples; publish the help and update the configuration and onboarding guides.

title: Add client sandbox profiles with explicit fallback
description:
Console currently chooses execution permissions independently of the MCP client's sandbox metadata. This adds an opt-in inherited sandbox profile with a configurable fallback, defaulting to `read_only`. One configuration can inherit client permissions where available and use the chosen default with clients that do not supply them. Missing metadata selects the fallback silently; malformed or unsupported metadata warns on server stderr and selects the same fallback. Omitting the inherited profile preserves existing behavior.

Recognized filesystem and network permissions become the selected base, with explicit local permissions applied afterward. An untranslatable filesystem entry makes the whole inherited policy unavailable, so dropping a denial cannot widen access. Inherited full access disables worker and preparation sandboxing and defaults to host caches; local restrictions are then unenforced. Proxy configuration remains local because the supported metadata does not supply it.

Internally, startup waits for the first `send` before runtime preparation. Captured permissions survive worker restarts; changed permissions or incompatible metadata after capture require reconnecting before the call can execute. Configuration export preserves profile and fallback choices, including automatic cache and network settings. Native and R configuration expose the profiles, with documentation and public regression coverage. Console continues using its pinned sandbox implementation.

title: Add full and pruned configuration output
description:
`config resolve` currently prints the complete default configuration, making small overrides hard to inspect. It now defaults to `--prune`, which prints differences from the binary's built-in defaults independently of global and project configuration. `--full` retains the complete editable configuration, including generated tool prose and parameter metadata. The flags are mutually exclusive, and an unchanged configuration prints `{}`.

Internally, materialization and serialization are separated so both modes share configuration capture and validation. Pruning removes unchanged mapping entries recursively while retaining complete changed arrays, empty values, and overrides needed to preserve conditional resolver inheritance. Tool prose is compared with generated defaults for the selected languages, permissions, and timeout visibility, preserving explicit descriptions and instructions when dropping them would change the text after reload. Both YAML and JSON exports remain editable and reloadable. The R helper explicitly requests `--full` to preserve its complete editable list. Documentation, public regression coverage, and CLI help snapshots describe the two modes.

title: Layer global and project configuration
description:
Global configuration currently serves only as a fallback, so adding a project file discards unrelated user preferences. Load global configuration, merge launch-directory project configuration, then apply CLI overrides in order. Sparse project mappings now preserve global settings while project values win conflicts.

Add `--no-config` to skip both automatic files, alongside `--no-project-config` for integrations that have not authorized project configuration. Both flags work before or after `serve` and ordinary `sandbox`. Document project configuration as trusted launcher input and global settings as overridable defaults.

Reuse the existing raw-value merge algorithm and final settings compiler. Apply exclusions before discovery, deduplicate files, reject non-regular configuration targets, retain source paths in diagnostics, and support native Windows home discovery when `HOME` is absent or empty. Preserve launch-relative paths and settings snapshots across worker restarts and resolver operations.

Local macOS checks passed. Native Windows and Linux behavior was not exercised locally.

title: Layer CLI overrides over project configuration
description:
Allow `serve` and `sandbox` to override project configuration for one launch with repeated `-c KEY=VALUE` flags. Read `.agents/console/config.yaml` from the launch directory, then apply overrides in command-line order, including flags before and after the subcommand. Dotted keys and nested inline values accept bare or quoted scalars, lists, and objects with either `:` or `=` separators.

Mappings merge recursively; lists, scalars, and explicit `null` replace earlier values. Validate the resulting configuration against the application schema after layering. The configuration file is not edited.

Internally, file loading, inline parsing, and merging now operate on a generic value tree without application field names. The existing application schema remains in `settings.rs`, and the server retains the captured settings across worker replacements. Document the merge rules and cover them through public CLI regressions.

Validation: `scripts/check` passed on macOS, including core checks, the complete applicable transcript suite, external SSH policy validation, and source and wheel installation checks. Linux-only cases and tests requiring unavailable Docker or Docker Sandbox fixtures were skipped. The initial CLI regressions were confirmed to fail before implementation.

title: Configure managed cache directories explicitly
description:
Put cache location alongside cache policy in `config.yaml`, with an explicit `directory` field shared by package preparation and workers:

```yaml
cache:
  directory: /path/to/cache
```

Custom paths use `<directory>/dependencies`, override `MCP_CONSOLE_CACHE_DIR`, and support relative paths and a leading `~`. Bare `cache: managed` and `cache: host` select the standard policies; `console` remains a compatibility alias. A directory named `host` is unambiguous as `cache: {directory: host}`. The selection persists across worker restarts, and managed caches continue to require sandboxing.

Internally, capture the directory once and reuse the existing preparation/worker cache handoff and resolver write grants. Update configuration exports, the starter template, the R adapter, and the configuration documentation to use the explicit mapping.

title: Clarify sandbox inheritance and enable it during client setup
description:
Client registration now opts into sandbox inheritance for the integration that supplies sandbox metadata. This applies to both uvx and direct executable launches; forwarded serve arguments retain precedence.

Rename the profile's scalar value, fallback mapping key, and exported R constructor to describe inheritance explicitly. Update internal selection and serialization, public acceptance fixtures, generated R reference material, and guides together.

title: Add client configuration subcommand
description:
Add `mcp-console configure-client <CLIENT>...` to register Console with supported MCP clients without editing their configuration by hand. A single invocation can configure multiple clients, defaulting to the nearest Git project or, outside Git, global settings.

The default launcher is `uvx mcp-console serve`. `--pin-version` accepts an exact PEP 440 version, `latest`, or `current`, which saves the version running setup. `--no-uvx` saves an absolute executable path. Temporary uvx runs with recorded direct sources first install that source persistently with uv (0.11.29 or newer), retaining direct URLs and resolved Git revisions. Temporary index and `--find-links` runs are rejected before installation or configuration changes because their original resolver selection cannot be recovered; install persistently with the same resolver options first. Unidentified temporary installations also fail before changes. `--scope`, `--name`, and arguments after `--` control the destination, server name, and server arguments. Console tools are configured for automatic visibility by default, with `--no-auto-load` to retain client discovery. `--dry-run` previews configuration and any installation command for review or manual application. Recorded source queries are redacted from installation reports and captured uv output.

Internally, add TOML editing through `toml_edit`, JSON merging, launch planning, source discovery through `uv pip freeze`, and version validation through `pep440_rs`. Invalid version suffixes and server names are rejected according to each client's rules before changes, and all selected files are parsed before installation or writes. Existing files are edited in place to retain ownership, ACLs/DACLs, symlinks, and file identity; these writes are not atomic. New files use atomic creation. Unrelated settings, TOML key comments, and comments around replaced values are preserved; comments inside replaced managed arrays are discarded. Completed changes are reported if a later write fails. Add public CLI acceptance cases, valid local wheel fixtures exercising real offline uv installation and source preservation, portable help snapshots, and onboarding and reference documentation.

title: Preserve startup output and report setup failures
description:
Startup can produce output and fail before the first tool call. This PR retains that output in the session recording and exposes setup diagnostics through `send`, while keeping MCP initialization, tool discovery, and pings available.

- Startup and idle text are retained in `outputs/session.log`; images produced outside a cell are retained as session artifacts. On Unix, preparation, provider, and launcher diagnostics enter the bounded session output.
- Native sandbox validation runs during the owned worker launch. Requirements inspection reports an unconsumed prelaunch failure with its diagnostics, then permits declaration inspection. The standalone `sandbox` command retains preflight validation.
- Early calls and results remain recorded if discovery fails. When startup output has already created the recording, buffered calls and results retain their timestamps and precede the discovery event. A session-log creation failure reports recording disablement on server stderr even without a tool call. Quarto files from failed discovery retain source with evaluation disabled and an unknown environment.
- Python attachment reuses an interpreter initialized during R startup and preserves its virtualenv prefixes. Conversion paths and NumPy metadata describe the running interpreter after environment and startup hooks, without importing optional packages for inspection. Unavailable or unusable optional NumPy metadata is treated as absent. Optional `rpython` probes no longer trigger Python 2 toolchain installation.

Internally, recordings can begin before discovery supplies runtime metadata. The recording owner retains a session timestamp from before early calls. Pending calls are replayed before worker configuration becomes available to early control calls. Requirements inspection uses the same lock order as evaluation admission and idle polls. Diagnostic producers own their UTF-8 decoders and retain other producers' pending terminal updates on EOF. Diagnostic ingestion and recording failure notices preserve incomplete UTF-8 characters on worker stdout and stderr. Output summaries use platform path operations, and cell logs remain separate from session output when recording fails.

Journal schema version 2 represents unknown discovery metadata and images without a call owner. Python conversion metadata uses preparation protocol version 6 and Docker/SBX launch protocol version 11; older peers are rejected during negotiation. SSH launch remains at version 10.

title: Allow additional writable paths in sandbox launches
description:
Add a temporary, repeatable `--writable-root PATH` option to `serve` and `sandbox` so launchers can grant writable output and cache locations ahead of the configuration front end. Console resolves paths against the launch working directory and checks UTF-8 without inspecting, creating, or removing them. The option augments default permissions and conflicts with `serve --no-sandbox` and `sandbox --config-env`.

Internally, retain a path list across worker restarts and replacements, then forward it to the sandbox frontend. `src/sandbox/runner.rs` appends explicit write entries through the existing configuration transport and pinned runner. The next configuration front end can supply the same list through `sandbox::resolve_writable_roots` and the launch functions. Linux payloads omit the macOS Seatbelt extension field.

Filesystem handling remains with the runner. macOS supports individual file grants and lets the workload create missing roots. On Linux, a missing directory needs to exist before a new sandbox launch, such as a worker restart, to receive its grant.
