The pinned Linux runner currently fails on existing file roots while preparing directory metadata protections. Console does not substitute a parent-directory grant or change backends.

Acceptance tests cover file operations, subprocess writes, neighboring and symlink-target denials, relative and missing paths, invalid UTF-8, option conflicts, restart, replacement, and persistent user data after cleanup. The companion `.runner.yaml` transcripts capture the actual configuration sent at runner exec on macOS and Linux, including the complete macOS extension; only temporary host paths and server PIDs are normalized. Native test fixtures include arm64 and arm64e code on Apple ARM hosts so resolver helpers can load them. R interruption assertions collect completion before submitting the next cell, respecting the existing 100 ms grace and preserving retained-state checks.

Core checks, all 429 applicable macOS transcript cases, source and wheel installation checks, and 17 focused Linux sandbox cases passed. The R lifecycle and server–relay interrupt suites also passed all 27 selected cases on each platform after the completion-wait change. The existing Linux inherited-procfs fixture could not run on the test host because it requires nested namespaces.

title: Resolve R packages automatically on demand
description:
## Summary

Resolve missing plain CRAN packages at the point of use in the built-in R worker. This lets callers use the package best suited to a task without probing installation or declaring ordinary CRAN requirements first.

## User-facing changes

- Resolve missing packages from `library()`, `require()`, `requireNamespace()`, `loadNamespace()`, `::`, and `:::` in the current R process.
- Retain successfully activated environments across cells and restart while preserving live R, Python, DuckDB, and stdin state during resolution.
- Start resolution only when execution reaches a supported package-loading operation; R source is not scanned in advance.
- Keep `requirements.r` for staging packages and supplying explicit supported IR references.
- Reject non-plain automatic package names before host resolution and document that accepted installation or build code runs with server permissions.

## Internal changes

- Add distinct resolve, activate, and failure messages across the worker and relay protocols while keeping the relay as a mechanical translator.
- Resolve server-owned managed-R candidates and commit them only after the worker applies the library path and reports activation.
- Prepare retained DuckDB extensions against each candidate before activation.
- Serialize automatic callbacks with explicit environment preparation and preserve generation, interruption, shutdown, and restart ownership.
- Add deterministic public regressions for runtime behavior, lifecycle races, failure paths, protocol encoding, and tool descriptions.

title: Improve website navigation and add builder and sandbox guides
description:
Reorganize the website around learning Console, finding configuration details, and building applications. Add dedicated guides for customizing Console and using its sandbox independently.

- Separate the introductory guides from the reference, group configuration fields by topic, and preserve existing page links and section anchors. Explain configuration discovery and precedence before creation, with the generated starter at the end of the page.
- Add **Build on Console**, covering language and argument selection, tool descriptions, prepared sessions, database connections, and application integration.
- Add a standalone sandbox guide with examples for running commands, granting file and network access, and saving reusable policies. Link it from the homepage and navigation.
- Refine the homepage and introductory prose, clarify recorded output retrieval, remove migration language, and update guidance for cache selection and retained SQL results.

Website support changes embed the generated starter from its acceptance snapshot, add a right sidebar to CLI help, and update navigation assertions and documentation workflow triggers. Console runtime behavior is unchanged.

The full Quarto site rendered successfully, formatting completed, and `git diff --check` passed. Automated tests were not run.

title: Refresh website onboarding and shared platform setup
description:
Refresh the homepage and onboarding around persistent R, Python, and SQL sessions. Use `uvx` for first setup, describe global registration as the default, and show `--directory .` for project registration.

Consolidate platform setup, remove the Windows experimental label while retaining MXC requirements, and simplify guide navigation. Keep permission examples and project-configuration trust boundaries in their owning guides.

This changes documentation and rendered-site checks. The registration behavior comes from #660, the base of this PR; retarget this PR to `main` after #660 merges.

Validated locally on macOS with all 21 rendered-website checks, `scripts/format`, `git diff --check`, and `scripts/check`.

title: Clarify website onboarding and project permissions
description:
Clarify Console's interactive workbench and simplify navigation and setup. Use `uvx` throughout onboarding, make global registration explicit for compatibility with older installed releases, and move detailed launch options into the reference guides.

Lead onboarding with global registration, an analysis, and `config init` for project writes. Label global workspace policies and project write grants explicitly, and explain relative launch paths and replacement of saved server arguments. Describe automatic project configuration loading, its ability to override inherited permissions, and why Git does not establish trust.

Windows follows the shared setup guides without an experimental label. Surface the MXC host requirements and preserve existing page links and fragments.

This PR contains documentation and website checks. It is based on #659 for registration scope, directory selection, and the project-entry warning. Git-aware permission policies and a project-trust mechanism remain future work.

Validated locally on macOS with 21 website checks, `scripts/format`, and `scripts/check`.

title: Show tool defaults and recommend long polling
description:
The `send` description now shows `timeout_ms=60000` and `requirements.action="add"`, so defaults remain visible when clients omit schema metadata from agent context. It recommends `timeout_ms=300000` while waiting, explains that long polls return early on completion or input requests, and discourages repeated one-second polls.

Internally, timeout prose is shared across presentation profiles, with public schema assertions and regenerated macOS/Windows snapshots. Tool arguments, defaults, and execution behavior are unchanged.

Local `scripts/check` and focused macOS/Windows presentation checks passed.

title: Retain cell text beyond inline output limits
description:
Retain emitted cell text before the inline output budget can omit it, so models and auditors can inspect, search, or copy the output with ordinary file tools. This establishes the retention layer for protecting model context from oversized runtime output. The existing 8 MiB pending-text budget remains unchanged; this PR does not add a smaller limit on rendered responses.

User-facing changes:

- Each recorded evaluation writes console text and direct stdout and stderr to a private `.mcp-console/sessions/<run>/outputs/call-NNNNNN.log`. The file is readable while the cell runs, and reading it does not consume pending `send()` output.
- Truncation notices link to the file only when it retained omitted text, and state exactly how many omitted bytes it contains. Startup omissions remain separate from cell omissions.
- The Markdown transcript links to output files when text was omitted inline or from the file. File creation or write failures report the loss of retention while evaluation and otherwise writable recording continue.

Internally, the server attaches each file at worker-operation admission, writes text before pending-output admission, and closes it at the completion or restart cut. Typed `cell_output` journal events associate each file with its initiating call and record retention and omission counts. Bytes absent from the file may still have been delivered inline. Worker and relay protocols, image handling, and the source-only Quarto projection remain unchanged.

Each file retains at most 1 GiB, with no aggregate session quota or automatic cleanup. This covers emitted cell text: images omitted by the inline budget, preceding startup or idle output, and values omitted by language printers or SQL previews are outside the file. Raw stdout and stderr bytes may be invalid UTF-8, and their concatenation does not preserve stream labels.

A next step can use these files to enforce a much smaller budget on the complete rendered response, with a head-and-tail preview and explicit omission metadata. Full capture beyond the file cap, image retention independent of response limits, and a bounded inspection interface need separate policies.

title: Document read-only DuckDB attachments
description:
## Summary

DuckDB opens attached database files in writable mode by default. In MCP Console's worker sandbox, a plain `ATTACH` therefore fails for databases outside the worker's private temporary directory.

This updates the SQL input description to show the supported form:

```sql
ATTACH 'path' AS name (READ_ONLY);
```

## User-facing changes

- Tell SQL callers to use `READ_ONLY` when attaching an existing DuckDB database outside the private temporary directory.
- Explain that the sandbox blocks DuckDB's default writable mode for those paths, so callers can query the database directly from SQL.

## Internal changes

- Mirror the schema description in `docs/TOOL_DESCRIPTIONS.md`.
- Extend the real `tools/list` acceptance assertion and regenerate its golden transcript.
- Add a causal input barrier to the gated-cohort CLI test so it deterministically proves the server received the queued calls before releasing the blocked response.
- Leave runtime behavior unchanged.

title: Align console defaults to 200 columns
description:
## Summary

MCP Console currently formats moderately wide results inconsistently because its worker communicates over pipes rather than a PTY: R starts at 80 columns, Python formatters use their own defaults, and SQL uses a fixed 160-column preview. This change gives each supported interface a 200-column display default.

## User-facing changes

- Start each R worker generation with `options(width = 200L)`.
- Expose a 200-column terminal width to Python and initialize NumPy `linewidth` and pandas `display.width` to 200 without preventing later user overrides.
- Lay out SQL previews within 200 columns while retaining the 160-character cell cap and 12 KiB preview cap.

## Internal changes

- Install Python display defaults through reticulate load and initialization hooks so R-first Python initialization behaves consistently.
- Separate SQL preview width from cell-value truncation.
- Add public transcript coverage for R, Python-first and R-first initialization, SQL preview layout, and the existing cell limit.

Validated with `scripts/check`.

title: Reorganize website guides and add a configuration reference
description:
Reorganize the website around using Console, integrating clients, and developing Console so setup and analysis guidance are easier to find.

- Clarify that the agent runs code. Introduce the workspace profile before manual write grants and describe its permissions and equivalent filesystem configuration.
- Add a configuration reference covering accepted values, defaults, and complete nested paths such as `r.packages`.
- Move detailed runtime, requirements, tool configuration, Windows migration, and contributor material into dedicated pages while preserving existing links and anchors.
- Align the R and Python package documentation with these reading paths, including an R configuration vignette.
- Keep tables and public CLI help readable at narrow widths, with keyboard-accessible scrolling.

Internal changes update the documentation filters and website checks, and add a public regression for Python and SQLite in an environment containing only the standard library. Console runtime and client implementation behavior are unchanged.

title: Clarify implementation and compatibility review guidance
description:
Clarify contributor guidance so implementation choices and compatibility reviews have explicit criteria.

- Add guidance on readable call sites, narrow module visibility, exhaustive state handling, and keeping invariant documentation with its implementation.
- Describe how to document intentional limitations, record bug reproductions, and review compatibility across MCP, CLI/configuration, and R/Python clients.
- Extend test authoring guidance with assertions on complete structured results, shared fixtures, and explicit child-process environments.

This changes contributor documentation only. Public behavior and runtime implementation are unchanged.

title: Add an R agent tutorial and current R selector
description:
R users giving an agent an unattended task need to choose its runtime and scope its access before launch. Add “Giving an agent an R session”, a tutorial that uses a sales report as a running example. It walks through explicit configuration, sandbox permission edits, materialized and pruned inspection, and an ellmer launch, explaining the motivation before each example. The surrounding job can email the resulting summary. Link the tutorial from package navigation, the README, and configuration and launch help.

Add `current_r()` so `RConfig(executable = current_r())` selects the installation running the calling script. It uses R's architecture-aware binary directory and the platform's launcher name. Native runtime selection is unchanged. Correct the README's stale statement about default configuration discovery.

The package builds and installs the vignette, and Windows CI installs its build dependencies. Documentation builds display the workflow without starting Console or making model requests. Public launch coverage checks that the selected R installation matches the caller, and the website check verifies that readers can find the article through navigation and search.

title: Document release preparation and recovery
description:
Record the 0.0.3 release lessons: rehearse both native wheels before tagging, keep runtime startup separate from evaluation deadlines, verify the exact release commit and public installation, and distinguish unpublished-tag recovery from partial publication.

Require passing CI and the GPT connector reviewer's thumbs-up before merges, and preserve all published PyPI files. Documentation only; runtime behavior and the release workflow implementation are unchanged.

Local `scripts/check` passed core checks but stopped in `client_server/r/test_lifecycle::interrupts_running_r_evaluation` waiting for `r-interrupt-started`; that unchanged case passed when run alone.

title: Consolidate tool description expectations and expose validation scenarios
description:
Tool wording changes currently require edits to registered descriptions, phrase assertions, snapshots, and a documentation mirror. Keep the committed handshake snapshot as the wording expectation and replace the mirror with editorial guidance and links.

The registered `send` description is shorter, with preparation, control, input, display, and timeout details kept on their fields. Runtime behavior and accepted arguments are unchanged. Language filtering and invalid-input side effects become separately discoverable transcript cases, preserving schema checks and assertions that no worker or resolver starts.

title: Clarify Python integration package labels
description:
The Python reference mixes Responses and Agents under one provider heading and labels a separate SDK by its conversation object. Name each group after its integration package, with the API or SDK name beside it, so readers can connect the docs to the package they install.

Split Responses API and Agents SDK into separate reference groups and keep the three related integrations adjacent. Use the same labels in both Python integration tables and replace the generic thread SDK wording in the generated adapter description.

Runtime behavior, imports, install extras, signatures, and reference page URLs remain unchanged. A rendered-site regression checks the section membership, guide labels, and adapter description; its HTML parser is declared in the documentation requirements.

title: Add Great Docs Python reference with integration examples
description:
Add a Great Docs Python API reference at `/python/` so readers can use the package clients and framework adapters from the repository's documentation website. The Quarto guides and R pkgdown site retain their existing URLs.

The reference includes an integration overview and standalone examples for chatlas, OpenAI Responses and Agents, Anthropic, and the thread SDK. Class methods appear together on their class page, with direct links to individual members. Examples cover setup, registration, tool loops, persistent state, image results, and cleanup.

The documentation workflow installs Great Docs and adds the Python subsite to the existing GitHub Pages artifact. Changes to Python sources, configuration, and LICENSE trigger documentation builds. Static source analysis generates the Python pages without installing framework dependencies or building Console. Website checks cover navigation, search, links, member anchors, and example syntax. Python runtime behavior is unchanged; package source edits are docstrings only.

title: Add a Quarto documentation website
description:
Add a Quarto website so users can browse and search the existing documentation. The site renders the Markdown guides directly, without adding front matter, and adds a home page and getting-started page. It uses grouped navigation and light and dark themes inspired by the IR website.

A small website filter derives titles from existing headings and keeps source-file links pointing to GitHub. The documentation workflow checks rendered pages, search coverage, links, and section anchors on pull requests, then deploys changes on main through GitHub Pages. The development guide explains local preview and publishing, and one existing Linux guide link is corrected.

Console runtime behavior is unchanged.

title: Simplify Python integration examples
description:
Update Python examples to access framework adapters through `mcp_console` at the point of use. Simplify Chatlas registration on a new chat while preserving the live tool schema.

Keep short adapter names in the overview table. Changes are confined to `docs/PYTHON.md`.

title: Clarify website guides and speed up page previews
description:
Clarify the website for people setting up Console, guiding an agent's analysis, and reviewing its work.

- Tighten the homepage around interactive work, language switching, output handling, and the value of recordings.
- Expand Getting Started to cover general MCP clients and R/Python integrations, and clarify installation and workspace permissions.
- Group Sessions and languages, Packages and environments, and Recordings and reports under Using Console. Explain default environments and dynamic package preparation before configuration choices, with examples aligned to the current Python configuration.
- Keep detailed runtime contracts in the reference pages and document worker/relay overrides as internal testing hooks.

Single-page renders now skip rebuilding the R and Python reference sites and their LLM exports, so copy edits can be previewed quickly. Full renders still build the complete website. A website regression checks that rendering one page preserves the other pages and package sites.

`warmup` now skips an absent optional R runtime while continuing Python and SQL checks, including background warmup after client setup. It confirms absence from the running server's captured discovery result; broken R selections and preparation, execution, timeout, and shutdown failures still fail. Opt-in internal metadata leaves ordinary tool responses unchanged. Older pinned servers that lack this metadata retain their existing check behavior.

title: Clarify website trust guidance and onboarding
description:
Clarify the homepage's sandbox and recording guidance so users can configure permissions and check session files before sharing them. Explain when the `read_only` fallback applies, describe filesystem and proxy controls, and link to the relevant guides.

Make project registration explicit in Getting Started and replace the synthetic-data prompt with a Palmer Penguins analysis using R, SQL, and Python.

Website copy and links only; no runtime or internal changes.

title: Explain interactive data analysis in the README and homepage
description:
Introduce Console through what an agent can do with a persistent workspace: keep data and models in memory, inspect results, refine plots, and debug code. The README and homepage explain these capabilities before introducing REPL terminology.

Cover session controls, cross-language data sharing, and default dependency preparation, including cache reuse and the options to use a preconfigured Python environment or disable R package resolution. Clarify source installation prerequisites and optional R setup. Add use cases, clarify the homepage's sandbox and recording limits, and align the site description. Documentation only; no runtime or API changes.

title: Add pkgdown subsite to documentation website
description:
Render the R package's README and `console_tool()` reference with pkgdown at `/mcp-console/r/`, so users can reach the package docs from the repository website. Add links between the Quarto site and pkgdown, and point package source links to the `r/` directory.

Build the subsite in Quarto's post-render step and deploy both sites in the existing Pages artifact. Update the Documentation workflow's dependencies and path triggers, and extend website checks to cover pkgdown pages, links, search, and sitemap URLs. Document local setup and pkgdown's published search-result URLs.

title: Link detailed CI cache guidance to release contract
description:
Keep the CI cache overview in `AGENTS.md` and link its detailed policy to the existing `RELEASE.md` contract. Preserve the full command list and all practical setup, build, installation, checkout ownership, formatter, and validation guidance verbatim.

Documentation-only: one file (+1/-9), with no runtime, tooling, CI, or test changes.

Verified exact retention of the base text outside the CI-cache block, all three local Markdown links and anchors, the full diff, and `git diff --check`. Ran the unchanged `scripts/format`: Ruff, Yamark, rustfmt, and Air all reported success, with no unrelated formatter diff remaining.

title: Document GitHub installation with uv
description:
The README quickstart installs the current source directly from GitHub with one `uv tool install` command, so readers no longer need to clone a checkout first. It keeps the source build prerequisites and the explanation that installation builds the private sandbox runner, and removes the fixed Python 3.12 claim because uv selects the tool interpreter.

This changes documentation only; the installer and runtime are unchanged.

Verified a fresh macOS GitHub install using empty uv and sandbox build caches. It fetched and built the pinned companion, passed all eight applicable sandbox installation checks, and launched offline with `uvx`. `scripts/check` also passed.

title: Organize and consolidate Console documentation
description:
Console's guides repeated public behavior across user, architecture, protocol, and platform pages. Reorganize them into task-oriented guides and public references, with separate developer and historical-evidence reading paths. Add API, CLI, and open-work indexes; simplify the entry pages, client introductions, development guide, and release procedure while retaining trust warnings and publication gates.

The website keeps published package-reference links local, including from nested pages, and preserves query strings and section anchors. Add a rendered-site regression for those links. Runtime behavior, tool definitions, package implementations, and generated reference sources are unchanged.

The seven website tests, handoff integrity and static checks, all formatters, and the ordinary macOS repository check passed. Native Linux and Windows validation remains with CI.

title: Improve Console summaries for deferred tool discovery
description:
Publish a task-oriented summary in MCP initialization instructions and at the start of `send` so clients can discover Console for debugging, simulations, data exploration and analysis, database queries, calculations, and plots. Explain how persistent state helps inspect results, test hypotheses, and compare approaches.

Build summaries and field guidance from the exposed language interfaces, whether selected by configuration or the environment filter. Keep the summary on one line within 250 characters and ordinary tool descriptions within the default 2,048-character client cap. Use shared direct-handshake snapshots across supported platforms.

Document client discovery and truncation behavior beside the description builder, and extend public coverage for filtered languages and initialization instructions. Shared protocol and eager-startup snapshots include the published instructions. Repair the Windows source-cache fixture to exercise timestamp restoration against a complete, clean checkout. Schema constraints and execution behavior are unchanged.

title: Document environment variables
description:
Add an environment-variable reference so users can distinguish server, worker, and dependency-preparation settings and understand selection and override rules.

The page covers runtime selection, cache paths, R startup, temporary storage, networking, and internal variables, with examples and implementation references. Link it from the documentation index and the shared-environment configuration section. This is a documentation-only change.

title: Clarify the workspace overview and setup guides
description:
The README now introduces the persistent, shared R, Python, and DuckDB workspace before getting into operational limits, so newcomers can understand the workflow and try it quickly. It includes MCP client setup examples, R installation guidance, an agent-driven Palmer Penguins analysis across all three languages, and a path from recorded code to reproducible Quarto reports with `ir`.

The Python guide opens with a table of supported interfaces, followed by installation and integration examples. The documentation index links directly to setup, analysis prompts, architecture, and runtime details.

Only three documentation files change. There are no runtime, SDK, dependency, or test changes relative to the PR base. The README describes automatic QMD dependency tracking as the intended contract; omissions in that tracking are an implementation bug to address separately.

title: Document revised session configuration design
description:
Supersedes #156 with a design sketch for expanded configuration at `.agents/console/config.yaml`. A profile describes a session's permissions, execution target, language environments, and resources, while shared storage settings apply to the project.

The proposal keeps Console-managed files under `.agents/console/`, with timestamp/PID session directories, one journal per server lifetime, and numbered worker-generation projections and artifacts. Sandboxed workers receive a write denial for the managed directory; current and previous records remain readable unless the user restricts reads. Version-control choices remain with the user.

Console loads ordinary YAML and forwards policy to the sandbox, which owns validation and enforcement. There is no additional Console approval or file-capture workflow. Automatic dependency resolution preserves the existing host resolver behavior. The sketch also covers services, package sources, protected preparation caches, runtime scratch, retention, and implementation slices.

Clarifies that design sketches are exploratory and need not be mutually consistent or held to production specification standards. The proposal does not change runtime behavior or the public API. Also updates the proxy handshake test fixture to use the canonical config path introduced on main, preserving its expected output and no-side-effects check.

title: Reorganize current documentation by audience
description:
## Summary

Reorganizes the implemented documentation so the repository overview, current architecture, built-in runtime behavior, dependency and environment behavior, and exact transport contracts each have a clear owner. This follows the runtime-source extraction in #116 and removes duplicated detail from the README and worker protocol while keeping future design under `design-sketches/` separate.

This is an internal documentation reorganization. It does not change runtime behavior, MCP schemas, worker or relay messages, dependencies, test infrastructure, or transcript goldens.

## User-facing documentation

- Replaces the oversized README with a concise under-construction overview, representative mixed-language workflow, current limitations, security note, verified development commands, and documentation links.
- Adds an audience-oriented documentation index and dedicated guides for the implemented architecture, built-in R, Python, and DuckDB runtime, and requirements and environment management.
- Narrows the worker and relay documents to their transport and custom-worker contracts.
- Documents console behavior that affects callers: input and interrupt routing, resolver deadlines, SQL previews, output truncation, worker restart and replacement notices, image persistence, and response ownership.
- Documents dependency and environment boundaries including live-preparation admission, idempotent repeats, startup preflights, R selection, and inherited Matplotlib configuration and backend selection.
- Describes `docs/TOOL_DESCRIPTIONS.md` as a human-readable mirror; the actual `tools/list` result and registered descriptions in `src/server.rs` remain authoritative.

## Internal changes

- Preserves four local lifecycle and transport invariants in focused source comments covering completion grace, readiness admission, same-call stdin ordering, and cancellable sideband retirement.
- Contains no executable source or test changes.
- Reduces the combined committed size of `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and the current documents under `docs/` from 187,855 to 113,602 bytes.

title: Render website CLI help from acceptance transcripts
description:
The command-line reference asks readers to run an installed Console binary to see the full option list. Add a CLI help page that presents the tested printouts alongside the usage guides.

Readers get one panel per recorded `--help` command, grouped into macOS/Linux and Windows tabs and styled after [IR's CLI reference](https://r-lib.github.io/ir/reference.html). The page is linked from the sidebar, documentation index, and command-line reference.

A Quarto filter reads the existing YAML acceptance transcripts directly, so the documentation job needs no Console executable or Rust build. Snapshot changes trigger documentation builds, and the website acceptance test verifies the displayed text and command order against both transcripts. Console's CLI behavior is unchanged.

Validated locally with `python tests/website.py` (10 tests), `quarto render docs`, `scripts/test cli/interface/test_help`, `scripts/format`, `scripts/check`, and workflow lint. Also checked the rendered panels and Windows tab in the browser.

title: Compact Console tool descriptions around ordinary cell use
description:
Console's advertised definition repeats preparation, polling, and interoperability guidance across the tool and nested fields. This pass puts complete cells, automatic display, inspecting output, and reusing persistent objects first, and gives other instructions a primary home.

The public changes are shorter tool and schema descriptions, concrete package-loading and bridge instructions, captured writable locations, and argument order: `r`, `python`, `sql`, `timeout_ms`, `control`, `stdin`, `requirements`, omitting hidden fields. Ordinary `library()` and `import` usage prepares missing packages in managed sessions. SQLite attachment syntax stays directly usable without a general availability disclaimer.

Internally, the existing named sections and captured profiles compose the descriptions. Discovery remains immediate and stable across background startup success or failure, with no new probes or startup dependencies. Schema values, constraints, execution, resolution, lifecycle, sandbox enforcement, and the installed client SDK are unchanged. Test fixtures normalize temporary writable roots after assertions and use separate direct/sandbox records where captured policies differ; exact canonical handshake comparisons remain intact. The R restart/background/subprocess recipe moves into the runtime guide, while longer resolver, driver, deadline, grace, cache, and recording explanations remain in their owning guides.

The comparison uses the canonical sandboxed tool object, `result.tools[0]`, from main at `b12f2593f69b0e29cf724a1fe03e7c71222dbafb`. Complete definitions use `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))`. Schema totals sum each description separately, including nested requirements, with no added separators. Tokens use **tiktoken 0.14.0 / o200k_base** on both versions. Characters equal UTF-8 bytes here because both definitions contain ASCII text.

| Scope               | UTF-8 bytes before → after | Reduction | Tokens before → after | Reduction |
| ------------------- | -------------------------: | --------: | --------------------: | --------: |
| top-level           |              3,328 → 1,392 |     58.2% |             629 → 279 |     55.6% |
| schema descriptions |             12,625 → 6,387 |     49.4% |         2,566 → 1,290 |     49.7% |
| complete tool       |             17,239 → 8,934 |     48.2% |         3,524 → 1,852 |     47.4% |

Removing every description key recursively, including inside arrays, leaves identical tool names, schema structure, constraints, defaults, enums, and other metadata in all **25 existing canonical profiles**, including Windows. Object-key order changes only presentation. Two new writable-root profiles preserve their corresponding default/custom schemas.

Substantial instructions retained:

- Exact bridge and connection helpers, ownership restrictions beside those helpers, hidden-provider requirements, SQL file/database access, and read-only attachment syntax.
- Automatic display, default-device R plots finalized per cell, persistent plot dimensions, pyplot capture and closure after errors, and custom/bare/selected-environment restrictions.
- Declaration action and omission semantics, accepted package syntax, payload restrictions, restart requirements, preparation before code/input, and interrupt's partial effects surviving failed deferred preparation.
- One cell at a time, the control-only interrupt exception, empty polling without resubmission, exact queued stdin/newlines/unread input, cooperative interruption, restart state loss, wait budgets without cancellation, and policy-derived filesystem/network access.

Local validation used `scripts/preflight` and `scripts/format` (ruff, yamark, rustfmt, and air). Ordinary `scripts/check` passed on committed head `49902631` on macOS. Public regressions for argument order and captured writable locations failed before the producer changes and passed afterward. Canonical and affected snapshots were generated through `scripts/test --update`; the final rerun verified them without update. A semantic audit of 34 affected execution records found unchanged execution inputs and outputs after excluding handshake presentation. Existing `uv run --script tests/transcript_runner.py` and `uv run --script tests/mcp_client.py` also passed.

The final focused macOS run covered configured languages, custom/bare/managed environments, hidden providers, writable/network policies, and stability during blocked discovery, discovery failure, and successful background startup. <details>
<summary>Before: rendered tool and all schema descriptions</summary>

**send**

Persistent R, Python, and SQL workbench for exact computation, file and data inspection, transformation, visualization, statistics, simulation, and modeling. State persists across calls.

For databases and structured files, consider DuckDB SQL first for schema inspection, filtering, joins, aggregation, and nested JSON extraction. Use R for vectorized data and string operations, statistics, and plots. Use Python when its libraries or format-specific parsing simplify the task. Switch languages when useful, reusing persistent state.

DuckDB can query CSV, Parquet, JSON, and JSONL directly; JSON support is built in. Built-in managed defaults include SQLite when dependency preparation is available; sessions without DuckDB preparation require preinstalled extensions. For SQLite, use an available sqlite extension and attach the database read-only with `ATTACH 'path' AS name (TYPE sqlite, READ_ONLY)`. When preparation is supported, prepare additional extensions with `requirements={"action":"add","duckdb":["fts"]}`. SQL results include bounded table previews that abbreviate long text cells; return focused queries and summaries for inspection.

Language fields describe the configured interface, not installed runtimes. With both runtimes and their bridge available, Python reads R globals through `r.name` and R reads Python globals through `py$name`. R-owned managed DuckDB SQL can query R data frames by name; without R, Python-owned DuckDB requires explicit frame registration with `sql_connection().register(name, frame)`. R accesses its SQL connection through `sql_connection()`; R or Python can select a user-owned connection with `console_sql_connection(connection)`. Managed dependency preparation requires resolver support on the execution host; bare runtimes require preinstalled packages, and explicitly selected Python uses its preinstalled Python packages.

Send one complete `r`, `python`, or `sql` cell per call. Code-bearing calls must be sequential; a control-only interrupt may overlap a pending `send`. Inspect intermediate results before submitting dependent cells. Cells are not transactional; changes made before an error may remain.

Omit code to poll, supply stdin, control the session, or prepare requirements when available. If a response ends in `[running; poll with an empty send]`, call `send` again without code or stdin; do not resubmit the cell. Send `stdin` alone to answer an active prompt or debugger. Field descriptions specify preparation, control, and timeout ordering.

Each result has at most 8 KiB of UTF-8 text, including notices; oversized output keeps its beginning and latest tail. Images have separate limits. Retained raw-log paths are relative to the server's launch directory for project recordings and absolute for home recordings. Full retained text requires filesystem access there through existing tools; Console provides no read/search interface.

Evaluated code can read host files, cannot directly access the network, and can write in the worker's private temporary directory and to paths explicitly allowed by the launcher. Dependency resolution, when available, uses a separate native resolver sandbox on macOS and Linux with configurable host reads, cache writes, and proxy destinations. Installation or build code may run there; use only trusted dependencies.

**r**

One complete R cell evaluated in persistent global state. Prefer Console for R execution,
including tests and package checks. When a fresh session is needed and existing in-memory
state can be discarded, send `control: "restart"` and `r` together; the code runs in the new
worker. For background execution, use `timeout_ms: 0`, then poll with an empty `send`.
Avoid `callr` merely to obtain fresh state or nonblocking execution. Use a subprocess when
the task requires separate process isolation, preserving the current session while running
independently, or ordinary R behavior without Console's runtime hooks.

The cell's final visible expression autoprints through R's normal console display; R also
autoprints earlier visible top-level expressions. Leave the primary result last and print
only when additional output is needed.
When dynamic resolution is available, the built-in worker resolves missing plain CRAN
package names on demand through `library()`, `require()`, `requireNamespace()`,
`loadNamespace()`, `::`, or `:::`. Use packages directly; do not probe package availability
or call `install.packages()`. Resolution makes a package available but attaches it only
through the original `library()` or `require()` call. In a bare runtime, packages must
already be installed and these operations keep their ordinary R behavior. R source is not
scanned in advance. When both runtimes and their bridge are available, read Python globals
through `py$name`. With R-owned managed DuckDB active, R data frames are directly queryable
by name from later SQL cells. `sql_connection()` returns the R-owned SQL connection for DBI or dplyr use. Select a user-owned DBI connection for later SQL
cells with `console_sql_connection(connection)` and restore managed DuckDB with
`console_sql_connection(NULL)`. Do not disconnect the managed DuckDB connection, and restore a
selected connection before disconnecting it. Default-device plots return as PNG images. Keep
all drawing operations for one plot in the same cell. Set persistent dimensions with
`options(console.plot.width_in = ..., console.plot.height_in = ..., console.plot.dpi = ...)`;
width and height are in inches. Omit this field for polling or stdin-only calls.

**python**

One complete Python cell evaluated in persistent `__main__` state. Its final visible expression
autoprints through Python's normal display hook. Leave the primary result last and print only
when additional output is needed. When dynamic resolution is available and an import is
missing, the built-in managed worker resolves a PyPI distribution on demand, using a curated mapping for well-known
import/distribution differences and otherwise assuming the distribution matches the top-level
module. Python source is not scanned; resolution starts only when execution reaches the import.
Use `requirements.python` when the distribution differs from the inferred name, exact registry
metadata is needed, or the package should be prepared before the cell. A user-selected Python
environment or bare runtime disables both automatic resolution and managed requirements;
import packages already installed there directly. When both runtimes and their bridge are
available, read R globals and call R functions through `r.name`. Select a user-owned DB-API
connection for later SQL cells with `console_sql_connection(connection)` and restore managed DuckDB with
`console_sql_connection(None)`. With R-owned DuckDB, bind Python data frames to an R name
before querying them. Without R, `sql_connection()` returns the Python-owned connection;
register frames explicitly with `sql_connection().register(name, frame)`. At cell end,
including after a Python error, every open `matplotlib.pyplot` figure returns once as a PNG
image and is closed.
`show()` is optional. R plots called through `r` follow the R plot rules. Omit this field for
polling or stdin-only calls.

**sql**

One complete SQL cell evaluated through the active connection. The managed DuckDB backend is
used by default when its adapter and packages are available and keeps a persistent catalog.
A result with columns returns a bounded preview. With R-owned managed DuckDB, an unqualified
relation name can query a data frame in R global state, and a DuckDB table or view with the
same name takes precedence. A user-selected R connection receives cells through `DBI::dbSendQuery()`; a Python DB-API connection executes
them through its connection or cursor protocol. The selected driver supplies its own SQL
dialect and type mappings. Use DBI from an R cell for commands that require the statement
interface. Without R, managed DuckDB uses Python and requires explicit frame registration
through `sql_connection().register(name, frame)`; it does not scan Python globals.
Managed DuckDB conveniences and extension requirements apply only to the managed
backend. With the sandbox enabled, use `ATTACH 'path' AS name (READ_ONLY)` for existing DuckDB
databases outside the sandbox's writable paths; the sandbox blocks DuckDB's
default writable mode for those paths. Use `SHOW TABLES`, `DESCRIBE`, `SUMMARIZE`, and `EXPLAIN`
for DuckDB discovery. DuckDB CLI dot commands are not supported. Omit this field for polling
or stdin-only calls.

**control**

Applies lifecycle control alone or before compatible same-call fields. `interrupt` requests
SIGINT from the active host resolver or live worker and preserves in-memory state. After
successful delivery, stdin is queued and `send` waits 100 milliseconds before observing the
earlier evaluation or attempting an optional following cell; the cell is not run if the
interrupted evaluation remains active. When `requirements` is available, restart resolves
same-call requirements before replacement. It then discards R, Python, DuckDB, debugger,
and unread-stdin state and sends same-call stdin and code only to the replacement.

**requirements**

Inspect or manage retained R packages, Python packages, and DuckDB extensions.
action=get returns a read-only snapshot, including Python constraints and separate runtime
infrastructure. It cannot accompany code, stdin, control, or payload fields. The complete
manifest is in structuredContent.requirements even when it exceeds the text preview limit.
action=add is the default; action=set replaces the whole declaration without injecting defaults;
action=reset restores startup defaults. Changed replacements require control="restart" with a
live worker. Empty set means no optional requirements; bare {} is invalid.
Requirements alone perform standalone preparation. With one cell, they are preconditions of
that cell. With `control = "restart"`, they are part of the restart transaction, with or
without a cell. Only add can accompany interrupt, and only when a cell follows; Python-only
sessions reject requirements with interrupt before signaling or queuing input.
Preparation does not import, attach, or load dependencies. On a code-bearing call without
control, preparation completes before same-call nonempty stdin is queued. Standalone
preparation cannot queue nonempty stdin. With restart, failure leaves the current worker
unchanged and sends neither stdin nor code. With add, interrupt, and a following cell, signal
delivery and stdin enqueue happen before requirements are validated or prepared and are not
rolled back if that later work fails. Ordinary CRAN packages used by the built-in R worker need
not be declared here; use `requirements.r` to stage packages ahead of evaluation or provide
explicit `ir` references. In the built-in managed Python environment, missing imports normally
resolve at runtime. Use `requirements.python` to stage a distribution before the cell, provide
a version, extra, or marker, or correct automatic inference. Python source is not pre-scanned,
and SQL does not trigger package discovery. A cell is not run if explicit preparation fails or
further changes require restart. Resolution uses the execution host's resolver policy and may download
packages or extensions or execute installation or build code. Use only trusted requirements.

**requirements.action**

get inspects the committed declaration without starting a worker or consuming output.
add (default) accumulates requirements. set replaces all lists and Python constraints;
omitted fields are empty, including when only action is supplied. reset restores startup
defaults. get and reset reject payload fields. Changed set/reset with a live worker require
control="restart"; the complete candidate resolves before the old worker is retired.
add accepts up to 64 entries per language per call; set accepts the complete accumulated manifest.

**requirements.python_version**

Python version constraints, preserved by get and replaced as a whole by set. Add appends
constraints; changing constraints with a live worker requires control="restart".

**requirements.exclude_newer**

Python package publication cutoff accepted by uv, for example "2026-01-01". set clears an
omitted or null cutoff; add preserves an omitted cutoff and cannot replace an existing one.

**requirements.duckdb**

DuckDB extension names for the managed DuckDB backend, for standalone preparation,
preparation before a cell, or a restart transaction, for example `fts`, `spatial`, or `excel`.
JSON and ICU are included in built-in defaults. Names must start with a lowercase ASCII
letter and contain only lowercase ASCII letters, digits, and underscores. The host resolver
uses DuckDB's own `INSTALL`, with DuckDB's default extension repository and
native cache. Preparation does not load extension code; `LOAD` and automatic loading happen
later inside the worker.

**requirements.r**

Single-line `ir` package references for standalone preparation, preparation before a
cell, or a restart transaction, for example `data.table`, `sf`, or `yaml12`. Use this field
to stage packages ahead of evaluation or supply an explicit supported remote `ir` reference.
Automatic R discovery accepts only plain package names. An idle worker that implements R
preparation can add requirements without losing live state. Local package sources are
rejected by the managed resolution contract.

**requirements.python**

Named PEP 508 registry requirements for standalone preparation, preparation before a
cell, or a restart transaction, for example `polars>=1`, `scikit-learn`, or
`matplotlib; python_version >= '3.10'`. Use explicit requirements when automatic import
inference needs a different distribution, a version, an extra, or an environment marker, or
when the distribution should be prepared before the cell. Automatic imports infer bare
distribution names only. Paths, file URLs, editable requirements, direct references, local
archives, and local projects are rejected. Preparation does not import the package. An idle
server-managed worker may activate compatible additions without losing state. A nonempty
user-selected `RETICULATE_PYTHON` disables automatic resolution and managed Python
requirements.

**stdin**

Input for an active read, prompt, or debugger. When responding to active input, omit R, Python,
and SQL code and send stdin on its own. Its UTF-8 encoding is queued exactly; no newline is added.
Line-oriented input therefore normally needs a trailing `\n`. On a code-bearing call without
control, available requirements are prepared before nonempty stdin is queued. Standalone
preparation cannot queue nonempty stdin. After `interrupt`, nonempty stdin is queued before the
100-millisecond grace and may be consumed while the earlier operation unwinds. After `restart`,
same-call stdin is sent only to the replacement. When sent with a cell, nonempty text is queued
before the code is run; an already waiting interactive read may consume it before the new cell
begins. Empty text queues nothing. If output ends in `[waiting for stdin]`, send the requested
input here. Unread text can satisfy later reads and is discarded by restart.

**timeout_ms**

Omit for normal calls and polls. This limits how long the tool waits; it returns immediately
when execution completes. Reaching the timeout does not cancel execution. Use `0` to start
background work, then poll with an empty `send`.

Defaults to 60,000 milliseconds. One deadline starts at call entry and includes initial
background startup, evaluation observation, and one automatic worker replacement attempt. It does not cancel resolution
or startup. Inline control, interrupt grace, restart, and explicit requirement preparation happen
before dispatch and may make the complete call take longer. This value does not limit standalone
preparation. Automatic R and Python import
resolution are part of the running evaluation and count toward this wait. On expiry, the call
returns available output and a state marker, such as
`[running; poll with an empty send]` or `[worker starting]`. If evaluation remains active, poll
with an empty `send` call; do not resubmit the cell.

</details>

<details>
<summary>After: rendered tool and all schema descriptions</summary>

**send**

Persistent R, Python, and SQL workbench for calculations, data analysis, and plots. Send one complete `r`, `python`, or `sql` cell per call. Inspect its output and reuse persistent objects. Results display automatically; supported plots return as images.

For databases and structured files, consider DuckDB SQL first for inspection, joins, and aggregation. Use R for vectorized data and string operations, statistics, and plots. Use Python when its libraries or format-specific parsing simplify the task. Switch languages when useful.

DuckDB can query CSV, Parquet, JSON, and JSONL directly, including nested JSON.

Run one cell at a time. Wait for its `send` to return before another call with code. You can interrupt a pending call with `send(control="interrupt")`. An error can leave earlier changes in place. If work is still running, poll with an empty `send` until it finishes; do not resubmit the cell.

Text results, including notices, have an 8 KiB limit, retaining the beginning and latest tail; images have separate limits. Response notices report state and omitted-output locations.

Evaluated code can read host files and cannot directly access the network. Writable locations: private `TMPDIR`; subject to more specific read/deny rules. Package preparation may execute installation or build code with separate filesystem and network permissions; use only trusted dependencies.

**r**

Evaluate one complete R cell in persistent global state. Visible top-level expressions autoprint; leave the primary result last. Never disconnect the managed connection; restore it before disconnecting a selection. Default-device plots return as PNGs and finalize at cell end, including after errors; draw each plot in one cell. Explicit devices are not captured. Set persistent dimensions in inches and DPI with `options(console.plot.width_in = ..., console.plot.height_in = ..., console.plot.dpi = ...)`.

**python**

Evaluate one complete Python cell in persistent `__main__` state. The final visible expression autoprints; leave the primary result last. Import packages normally; managed sessions prepare missing PyPI distributions on first import. Use `requirements.python` when import and distribution names differ or to prepare before execution. Access R globals and call functions through `r.name`. Select a user-owned DB-API connection for SQL cells with `console_sql_connection(connection)`; restore managed DuckDB with `console_sql_connection(None)`. For R-owned DuckDB, bind Python frames to an R name through `r` before querying. For Python-owned DuckDB, `sql_connection()` returns the connection; register frames with `sql_connection().register(name, frame)` (globals are not scanned). At cell end, even after errors, open `matplotlib.pyplot` figures return once as PNGs and close; `show()` is optional. Closing a figure suppresses capture. **sql**

Evaluate one complete SQL cell through the active connection. Managed DuckDB keeps a persistent catalog. With R-owned managed DuckDB, query R data frames by name; DuckDB tables/views take precedence. Use DBI from an R cell for commands requiring the statement interface. With a sandbox, attach existing DuckDB databases outside writable paths using `ATTACH 'path' AS name (READ_ONLY)`. Use `SHOW TABLES`, `DESCRIBE`, `SUMMARIZE`, or `EXPLAIN`; CLI dot commands are not supported.

**timeout_ms**

Wait for output for up to this many milliseconds (default 60,000). `0` returns without
waiting for completion. Expiry returns available output while work continues. This is a wait
budget, not cancellation or a whole-call deadline: preparation and control can exceed it;
standalone preparation has no timeout.

**control**

Apply control before same-call stdin/code. `interrupt` requests a cooperative interrupt and cancellation of dependency preparation, preserving live state. A following cell runs only if prior work stops. `restart` discards live interpreter, database, debugger, and unread-input state; same-call stdin/code go only to the replacement.

**stdin**

Send stdin alone to answer an active read, prompt, or debugger. UTF-8 text is queued exactly; no newline is added, so line input normally needs a trailing `\n`. Empty text queues nothing. With a cell, input queues before code; an already waiting read may consume it first, including while interrupted work unwinds. Unread input can satisfy later reads; restart discards it.

**requirements**

Inspect declarations or prepare dependencies on the execution host without importing, attaching, or loading them. Requires host preparation support; bare runtimes use installed packages. Alone, performs standalone preparation. With a cell, preparation precedes code; without control it also precedes bundled stdin. Failure or a required restart withholds the cell. Compatible additions preserve live state on an idle worker; other changes need restart. With restart, candidate resolution precedes replacement; resolution failure preserves the current worker and sends no stdin/code. Standalone preparation rejects nonempty stdin. Only add can accompany interrupt, with a following cell; providers without this preparation support reject the combination before signaling or input. Otherwise interrupt and stdin precede deferred validation/preparation and are not rolled back on failure.

**requirements.action**

get reads the retained declaration, not an installed-package inventory, without starting a
worker or consuming output; use it alone, without code, stdin, control, or payload fields.
The complete declaration is in structuredContent.requirements.
add (default) accumulates up to 64 entries per language per call; bare {} is invalid.
set replaces the whole declaration without defaults; omitted lists/constraints are empty,
even with only action supplied. reset restores startup defaults and rejects payload fields.
Changed set/reset with a live worker require control="restart"; unchanged declarations are
no-ops. set accepts the complete accumulated manifest without add's per-list limit.

**requirements.python_version**

Python version numbers or ==, !=, <, <=, >, >= constraints (e.g. >=3.11).
add appends; changes with a live worker require control="restart".

**requirements.exclude_newer**

Package publication cutoff accepted by uv, e.g. "2026-01-01".
set clears an omitted/null cutoff; add preserves omission and cannot replace an existing one.

**requirements.duckdb**

Managed DuckDB extension names, e.g. fts or spatial: lowercase ASCII letter first, then
lowercase letters, digits, or underscores (at most 64 characters).
Use DuckDB's LOAD or automatic loading after preparation.

**requirements.r**

Single-line ir package references, e.g. data.table or sf, including supported remote
references; local sources and NUL/line breaks are rejected. Automatic R loads accept plain
package names only; use this field for explicit references or preparation before use.

**requirements.python**

Named PEP 508 registry requirements with versions, extras, or markers, e.g. polars>=1 or
requests[socks]. Paths, URLs, editable requirements, direct references, and local sources
are rejected. Bare or explicitly selected Python environments and custom workers disable
managed Python requirements.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reproduce counts and metadata comparison</summary>

Save this as `/tmp/mcp-console-description-counts.py` and run the command at its top from the PR checkout. It compares all baseline canonical profiles with `HEAD`.

```python
# Run with:
# uv run --no-project --with PyYAML==6.0.3 --with tiktoken==0.14.0 python /tmp/mcp-console-description-counts.py
import json
import subprocess

import tiktoken
import yaml

BASE = "b12f2593f69b0e29cf724a1fe03e7c71222dbafb"
DIRECTORY = "tests/snapshots/client_server/server/test_tools/"
CANONICAL = DIRECTORY + "initializes_and_lists_tools.yaml"
ENCODING = tiktoken.get_encoding("o200k_base")


def tool(ref, path):
    source = subprocess.check_output(["git", "show", f"{ref}:{path}"], text=True)
    return list(yaml.safe_load_all(source))[2]["result"]["tools"][0]


def descriptions(value):
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        for key, item in value.items():
            if key == "description":
                yield item
            else:
                yield from descriptions(item)
    elif isinstance(value, list):
        for item in value:
            yield from descriptions(item)


def strip(value):
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {key: strip(item) for key, item in value.items() if key != "description"}
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [strip(item) for item in value]
    return value


def sizes(value):
    serialized = json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
    groups = {
        "top-level": [value["description"]],
        "schema descriptions": list(descriptions(value["inputSchema"])),
        "complete tool": [serialized],
    }
    return {
        name: {
            "chars": sum(len(text) for text in texts),
            "utf8_bytes": sum(len(text.encode("utf-8")) for text in texts),
            "o200k_base_tokens": sum(len(ENCODING.encode(text)) for text in texts),
        }
        for name, texts in groups.items()
    }


files = subprocess.check_output(
    ["git", "ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", BASE, "--", DIRECTORY], text=True
).splitlines()
profiles = [path for path in files if path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1].startswith("initializes_and_lists_tools")]
for path in profiles:
    assert strip(tool(BASE, path)) == strip(tool("HEAD", path)), path
print(f"Identical metadata in all {len(profiles)} canonical profiles.")
print(json.dumps({"before": sizes(tool(BASE, CANONICAL)), "after": sizes(tool("HEAD", CANONICAL))}, indent=2))
```

</details>

title: Compact repository documentation around current contracts
description:
Condense repository documentation so readers can find current contracts without repeated implementation details and file inventories. The PR changes 27 Markdown paths: 23 rewrites, two additions, and two deletions. Across those paths, documentation shrinks from 700,694 to 202,072 bytes (71.2% smaller).

## Reader-facing changes

- Focus the README on installation, use, recordings, and safety, with links to the relevant contracts.
- Add a shared glossary and a recording/rendering guide covering file ownership, retained output, privacy, and Quarto exports.
- Consolidate runtime, requirements, configuration, provider, and sandbox guidance. Clarify background worker startup versus lazy interpreter initialization, timeout versus cancellation, preparation versus activation, and confirmed retirement.
- Retain exact framing and ordering rules in the private protocol references, along with the dependency trust boundary, unredacted recordings, shared-path exposure, and cleanup limits.

## Contributor guidance and scope

- Make AGENTS a short working guide and set the implementation change target to fewer than 500 added/deleted lines, with mechanical moves, tests, snapshots, and docs exempt.
- Keep practical build, validation, checkout ownership, and release instructions in their owning guides; replace exhaustive inventories with focused source entry points.
- Remove the historical runner-integration and prepared-runtime audit documents, retaining current contracts in the live guides.

All changes are documentation. Runtime code, registered MCP tools, tests, snapshots, workflows, and design sketches are unchanged.

Local validation passed on the documentation edits committed as `eacd6c7e`: all four formatters in `scripts/format`, `git diff --check`, and the ordinary `scripts/check` gate (core checks, release build, and smoke transcripts). Formatting preserves prose and example semantics apart from the requested 200-to-500 change budget.

title: Clarify timeout and fresh R session guidance
description:
The `send.timeout_ms` description now recommends omitting the timeout for normal calls and polls, explains that the call returns immediately when execution completes, and makes clear that reaching the timeout does not cancel execution. It also describes using zero to start background work, followed by an empty `send` to poll.

The R description recommends Console for tests and package checks, with `control: "restart"` and `r` together when fresh state is needed and existing in-memory state can be discarded. It discourages `callr` merely for fresh state or nonblocking execution, while preserving subprocess use for isolation, independent execution alongside the current session, or ordinary R behavior without Console's runtime hooks.

These changes clarify the public tool descriptions to avoid repeated short polls and unnecessary subprocesses. Generated MCP handshake snapshots are updated; runtime behavior is unchanged.

title: Make console tool descriptions concise
description:
## Summary

Registered MCP tool descriptions are recurring agent context. This change makes `send` and `session` concise and action-oriented while retaining the facts needed to choose and operate them correctly. It also tells clients to reassess R, Python, and SQL for each cell, so existing state does not become the sole reason to stay in one language.

## User-facing changes

- Encourages choosing the language that best fits each cell, switching when another language becomes a better fit, and using the live bridges without favoring one ecosystem.
- Removes tutorial-style inventory and debugger examples, repeated resolver details, and general analysis coaching from `tools/list`.
- Keeps persistence, one-cell sequencing, final-expression display, polling, stdin, interruption, nontransactional errors, cross-runtime bridges, dependency handling, plotting, and sandbox trust guidance.
- Leaves `[running; poll with an empty send]` and `[waiting for stdin]` unchanged.
- Keeps detailed workflow and debugger examples in the built-in runtime documentation.

## Internal changes

- Keeps schema-property descriptions field-specific and synchronizes the human-readable documentation mirror.
- Replaces tutorial-wording assertions with contract-level `tools/list` checks and regenerates only the corresponding golden.
- Does not change runtime or protocol behavior.

title: Make fast local validation the default
description:
Local validation currently runs nearly the entire transcript suite even with `--quick`. Make fast validation the default: `scripts/check` runs focused core checks and an explicit smoke profile, and selector-free `scripts/test` runs the same smoke profile. `--quick` aliases these defaults; `--full` retains comprehensive validation. Explicit case and suite selectors retain their scope with every profile flag.

The smoke profile selects 12 existing cases with 19 declared executions covering MCP/CLI admission, real R/Python/SQL execution, persistent and mixed state, interactive input, interruption, recording with a plot, and native sandbox policy. Default core checks retain runtime-source validation, architecture contracts, Rust formatting, Clippy, and Rust tests. Repository-tooling self-tests and global orphan-snapshot auditing remain in the full profiles. No product runtime code or transcript snapshots change, and expensive fixtures retain their assertions and behavior.

CI explicitly requests full core and transcript validation and retains installation checks. Repository guidance makes the default gate the ordinary final local check, reserves exhaustive local validation for requested or relevant changes, and requires reporting the scope actually run. Workflow and runner regressions cover profile forwarding, explicit selectors, provider configuration, snapshot updates, and failure reruns.

On an Apple M4 Max running macOS, three warm `scripts/check` runs on clean commit `a2e5e3ca` took 16.4, 15.6, and 15.7 seconds: a 15.7-second median. The first run took 27.3 seconds. Every run passed all 19 executions across the 12 smoke cases. No selection reduction was needed.

Full core validation passed all 12 phases. The runner, workflow, test-client, and architecture regression suites passed. The new full inventory exactly matches the previous 694 case selectors. The full transcript and installation gates remain for CI; they were not run locally.

title: Map development tasks to focused public validation
description:
A short route table in the development workflow links common changes to owning source, public suites, and selected snapshot updates. The validation ladder identifies focused iteration, formatting, the full pre-PR gate, and commands that mutate build or package state.

Transcript failures print runnable receipts that preserve custom timeouts and snapshot-update semantics. Ordinary failures narrow to the failed case; a full update retains its full scope and nondefault concurrency so orphan cleanup and serial reruns remain available. Console runtime behavior is unchanged.

Validation on the integrated stack: `scripts/check` passed at `d460d992`, including core checks, locally applicable release transcripts, and source/wheel installations. After the review changes, `scripts/check-core` passed at clean `7323987b`; strict formatting also passed. The live `scripts/preflight --json` check passed at `a1f0d899`. Optional provider and platform cases were skipped according to their capabilities.

title: Discover and validate transcript tests before compilation
description:
Test help, discovery, location lookup, and argument validation happen before release compilation. Help and syntax-only errors use the standard library before invoking uv; list/locate and semantic selector checks may prepare the script environment. Actual transcript execution still builds and uses the release binary.

Execution-fixture errors now point to the supported direct or sandboxed composition. SBX discovery keeps its serialization lock outside mutable build output. These changes affect development commands and test diagnostics; Console runtime behavior is unchanged.

Validation on the integrated stack: `scripts/check` passed at `d460d992`, including core checks, locally applicable release transcripts, and source/wheel installations. After the review changes, `scripts/check-core` passed at clean `7323987b`; strict formatting also passed. The live `scripts/preflight --json` check passed at `a1f0d899`. Optional provider and platform cases were skipped according to their capabilities.

title: Own checkout validation and retain phase records
description:
Validation commands and source packaging share a checkout lock outside `target`, preventing installation checks from hiding build output while another command uses it. Sequential nested commands reuse their live owner and wait for their children; conflicts report the lock path and advisory owner metadata. Full checks and transcript runs share a configurable host concurrency budget, with absolute cache paths required.

Validation records retain the admitted revision and worktree state, phase timings, exit status, failing selectors, and complete logs. The initial record precedes Git metadata collection, so cancellation during metadata collection is finalized. Once work and retirement finish, the completed status stays fixed through final recording and process exit. Phases write directly to files and save their result before replaying failure diagnostics. `scripts/with-checkout` gives direct commands ownership and bounded cancellation while inheriting their standard streams. Direct staging and packaging hooks retain caller-owned cancellation. Abrupt owner death requires manual cleanup of surviving commands. Docker build examples copy the required helper before staging, artifact cache identities exclude it, and generated validation records are excluded from Docker build contexts. Console runtime behavior is unchanged.

Validation on the integrated stack: `scripts/check` passed at `d460d992`, including core checks, locally applicable release transcripts, and source/wheel installations. After the review changes, `scripts/check-core` passed at clean `7323987b`; strict formatting also passed. The live `scripts/preflight --json` check passed at `a1f0d899`. Optional provider and platform cases were skipped according to their capabilities. Both Docker pre-staging COPY contexts passed the staging import/CLI check; full container image builds were not run locally.

title: Consolidate project files under .agents/console/
description:
Consolidates project configuration and generated files under `.agents/console/` so Console uses one project directory.

`serve` and ordinary `sandbox` launches now discover only `.agents/console/config.yaml`; `.mcp-console/config.yaml` and `.agents/mcp-console.yaml` are ignored. New session transcripts, journals, output logs, and image artifacts are written under `.agents/console/sessions/`, with reported output paths updated to match. The ignore rule covers generated sessions while leaving config trackable.

Internally, removes the two-location selection and ambiguity handling. Updates documentation and public acceptance coverage for the new paths, ignored legacy configuration, lazy recording creation, and private file permissions.

The macOS retirement tests also wait for the runner to observe detached children before triggering cleanup, matching its supported guarantee. They reuse the existing observation fixture and preserve the immediate cleanup assertions.

title: Consolidate session and sandbox documentation
description:
The README, development instructions, runtime guide, and requirements guide repeated subtle lifecycle and `send` rules. Consolidate those descriptions so a behavior change has one detailed reference to update.

Add a `send` operation table covering validation timing, preparation, interruption, restart, stdin ownership, failure effects, and evaluation waits. Keep component contracts in the architecture guide and detailed sandbox sequencing in the supervision guide; shorten the README and `AGENTS.md` to their intended roles.

Clarify that successful process retirement does not prove temporary-directory deletion, and that the Quarto source projection can include rejected calls and failed evaluations without reconstructing session control. Runtime behavior, registered tool descriptions, and snapshots are unchanged.

title: Prune redundant transcript matrices and explain retained fixtures
description:
Several client/server transcripts repeat language-schema assertions and SQL-provider sessions already covered elsewhere. Consolidate those assertions in the existing public MCP cases and explain the fixtures in the retained transcripts.

- Remove eight redundant boundary-test functions and their ten snapshots. With SQL, R, and both execution modes available, this removes 36 explicit Console launches per platform run. No wall-clock speedup is claimed.
- Retain all seven nonempty language combinations for both builtin and custom interfaces. Shared assertions check guidance and schema through actual MCP responses in `test_presentation::builtin_configured_language_matrix` and `test_languages::configures_captured_tool_surface`.
- Add source-owned `scenario` and `fixture` descriptions to the seven custom configuration sessions and four real SQL-provider sessions, regenerated with the native harness.
- Make the Python-backed offline-extension fixture pass `--offline` to real uv after dependency warmup. Managed preparation intentionally removes `UV_OFFLINE`, so cache freshness previously determined whether its denied-network session could start. The case retains managed Python, real DuckDB, blocked resolver downloads, uncached builtin extensions, and Python state assertions; its snapshot now includes the canonical initialization exchange and fixture context.
- Collect completed early requirements changes and initial SQL cells before asserting their results. Bound the gated startup cell marker by the client's preparation deadline and cleanup reserve; releasing the IR fixture allows materialization to begin.
- Document public-interface coverage, readable fixture context, and the existing `RUNTIME` execution-mode convention.

Console's public API and runtime behavior are unchanged. Production source, real-library sandbox workloads, lifecycle coverage, and native interrupts are unchanged. SQL ownership, provider selection, replacement, and reset remain covered by the retained language sessions and `sql/test_connections`.

Local macOS validation passed preflight, companion staging, native snapshot regeneration and comparison, all four repository formatters, and the global orphan-snapshot audit. `scripts/test --full --jobs 6` passed all 1141 functional cases on `d96105a2`. On the current merged head `74aefbfb`, the affected configuration/help, Python integration, MCP presentation, and offline-extension suites passed, as did `scripts/check`, the R configuration check (7 assertions), and `python3 tests/install.py` (source/wheel installs and Python 3.11/3.14 smoke coverage). Full tooling checks, architecture, Clippy, and all 53 Rust tests passed. Cross-platform CI and current-head reviewer approval remain merge gates.

title: Exercise Windows startup with Codex's filtered MCP environment
description:
The Windows startup regression previously inherited the whole caller environment except `PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE`, and explicitly selected the test runner's Python. That could hide failures in the minimal environment used by MCP clients.

Build the launch environment from Codex's 23-variable Windows core allowlist, matching the local Codex source at [ca466061](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ca466061d64f0b44f416135c7fd06aa7af850bbc/codex-rs/protocol/src/shell_environment.rs#L170-L201). Codex [clears inheritance](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ca466061d64f0b44f416135c7fd06aa7af850bbc/codex-rs/utils/pty/src/child_command.rs#L94-L102) and [builds its MCP environment](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ca466061d64f0b44f416135c7fd06aa7af850bbc/codex-rs/rmcp-client/src/utils.rs#L16-L58) from that list, certificate settings, and explicit overrides; this fixture covers the core list without those optional overrides.

The regression now omits ambient R/Python selections and other unrelated variables, discovers the configured fixture R through retained `PATH`, and exercises managed Python. It preserves all three cases (client filtering, Console configuration filtering, and an empty architecture value) and checks initialization/discovery, R/Python/SQL, requirements inspection, and restart. This PR changes tests only.

Validation passed on Windows x64 with configured R and `LC_ALL=C`:

- `scripts/preflight.cmd` and `scripts/stage-sandbox-runner.cmd`
- `scripts/test.cmd WindowsConsole.test_startup_without_processor_architecture` (all three subcases)
- `scripts/format.cmd` unchanged (all four formatters succeeded)
