- `scripts/check.cmd` (source/architecture checks, Rust formatting, Clippy, 42 Rust tests, and 102 native Windows tests; no skips)
- Direct comparison of all 23 fixture names with the referenced Codex source, and `git diff --check`

The full shared-boundary/installation profile and non-Windows platforms were not run locally; CI remains the comprehensive merge gate.

title: Fix Windows startup without PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE
description:
Windows MCP clients can omit `PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE`, causing R DuckDB extension preparation to terminate with `0xc0000005` and block requirements inspection and R/Python/SQL execution. Restore missing or empty values to `AMD64` at process entry on Windows x64, including preparation and worker processes, while retaining nonempty supplied values.

Add public regression coverage for inherited omission, configured environment filtering, and an empty value. Each scenario exercises preparation, requirements inspection, all three languages, and restart. Document the Windows environment default.

Validation:

- The new regression reproduced the reported access violation before the fix and passed afterward: `scripts/test.cmd WindowsConsole.test_startup_without_processor_architecture`.
- `scripts/preflight.cmd`, `scripts/format.cmd` (all formatters), and `scripts/check.cmd` passed; the gate ran 42 Rust tests and 95 native Windows cases.
- The seven configured-R sandbox cases initially skipped by the gate passed separately with `R_HOME=C:/Program Files/R/R-4.6.1` and `LC_ALL=C`, covering all 102 native cases across the two runs.
- Sandboxed startup using the captured Codex resolver environment passed R, managed Python, SQL, requirements inspection, and restart.

Validation was Windows-only; the full shared-boundary/installation profile and hosted CI were not run locally.

title: Enable SQL cells on Windows
description:
Windows currently rejects configured SQL cells and hides SQL from the built-in tool interface. Enable the existing R DBI and Python DB-API providers on Windows, including SQL-first sessions, native connection selection through captured startup, and managed DuckDB's shared `icu`, `json`, and `sqlite` defaults.

Add native coverage for R-owned and Python-owned SQL with and without sandboxing, connection persistence, interruption, startup, and restart. Port shared SQL fixtures where the behavior is portable, declare R requirements for R-backed SQL cases and the remaining POSIX fixture requirements, regenerate tool transcripts, and update the owning contracts. Latest main (`948823a7`) is merged into the branch, including its simplified `_console.sql_connection()` and `.console$sql_connection()` helpers.

Windows remains experimental. R-owned native DuckDB queries interrupt successfully; long native Python-owned DuckDB queries may require restart. The native regression covers recovery through restart.

Validation:

- `scripts/preflight.cmd`, `scripts/stage-sandbox-runner.cmd`, and `scripts/format.cmd` passed. The public Windows SQL regression failed before implementation and passes after it.
- Focused native SQL tests passed, including R, Python without R, SQL startup, both sandboxed providers, cooperative callbacks, R native interruption, and busy Python query restart.
- Windows-applicable shared SQL catalog, connections, configuration, defaults, startup, and without-R cases passed, together with server languages, descriptions, without-R, presentation, and tools cases.
- Review repair: with R absent from both PATH and R_HOME, all 36 audited R-backed cases skip and 12 Python-only SQL cases pass. With R present, catalog, connection, canonical tool, and no-R cases pass. The new main connection-helper test preserves its complete error after normalizing only diagnostic bullet presentation. Native SQL and configured startup pass with the renamed helpers.
- `scripts/check.cmd` on clean PR head `6dddba3c`: runtime-source, architecture, formatting, Clippy, and Rust tests passed; **94/96 native Windows tests passed**, including every SQL and sandbox case. The gate still fails on the same two resolver-interruption tests previously reproduced on clean main (`28b9ee4a`): `WindowsResolver.test_cancellation_before_gate_release_retires_resolver_and_descendants` and `WindowsResolver.test_interrupt_confirms_descendant_retirement` report `control: null` instead of `Interrupted`.
- Linux/macOS and full installation validation were not run locally; CI remains the comprehensive merge gate.

title: Support idle R later callbacks on Windows
description:
Windows workers waited only for sideband commands and interrupts, leaving `later`'s window timers unserviced between cells. Wake the idle wait for Windows messages and dispatch R events on the interpreter thread through R's protected top-level boundary.

Pending pipe I/O is settled and the command-reader lock is released before callbacks run. Partial command frames survive these wakeups, and callbacks use the existing input and graphics scope. Portable callback acceptance cases now run on Windows, with native coverage for input, plots, interrupts, error recovery, shared R/Python state, restricted-token execution, and a command split inside a UTF-8 character.

### Validation

- Public idle-callback regression reproduced the failure before implementation and passed afterward.
- Ten applicable shared boundary cases passed, including callback input during dependency preparation; the Windows retirement snapshot was generated and verified.
- `scripts/preflight.cmd` and `scripts/stage-sandbox-runner.cmd` passed.
- `scripts/format.cmd` passed all formatters; unrelated line-ending-only changes were reverted.
- `scripts/check.cmd` passed source/architecture checks, Clippy, 38 Rust tests, and 81 native Windows acceptance tests. One explicitly provisioned elevated network-restricted sandbox case skipped.

Native validation used the installed R runtime with `R_HOME`, its native executable directory on the scoped `PATH`, and `LC_ALL=C`. macOS/Linux execution and the provisioned elevated sandbox were unavailable locally; CI remains the comprehensive gate.

title: Document WSL2 development setup for Ubuntu and Fedora
description:
Document the verified WSL2 development workflow for Ubuntu 26.04 and Fedora 44: independent Linux checkouts, native system prerequisites, a Python 3.13 development environment, serial R preparation, and Windows-to-WSL MCP stdio launch.

The Ubuntu CI run also exposed a race in `live_extension_additions_require_an_idle_worker`: stdin acknowledgement can arrive before Python finishes the current cell, so the next code submission was rejected as busy. Use the existing completion helper after ordinary input and debugger continuation before submitting dependent cells. Preserve the busy-worker, retained-input, and worker-state assertions and existing snapshots.

Validation:

- The failing SQL case passed in direct and sandboxed modes on Ubuntu 26.04 and Fedora 44.
- `scripts/format` ran unchanged before committing; Ruff, yamark, rustfmt, and Air all passed. The ordinary `scripts/check` passed on Ubuntu with the repair.
- The WSL setup previously passed preflight and the ordinary gate in both distros. A Windows MCP client executed R, Python, and SQL through the Ubuntu server and confirmed clean shutdown.

Docker, Docker Sandbox, and external SSH providers were unconfigured. The full local gate was not run; hosted CI runs on the pushed head.

title: Collect worker activity continuously
description:
## Summary

- continuously collect worker console output, images, input state, and managed-Python callbacks between tool calls
- make an empty `send` snapshot idle output immediately without sending a worker command or waiting for callbacks
- keep evaluation and preparation terminals behind owner acknowledgments so retained state commits before later background activity is published
- preserve output boundaries across completion, restart, and reader cancellation, including callbacks that run while the worker is idle

## Testing

- `scripts/check`

title: Remove legacy Windows sandbox integration
description:
Windows sandbox execution uses MXC, but startup and maintenance still carry assumptions from the account-based sandbox. Remove that compatibility layer as an intentional clean break so Console behaves as an MXC-only implementation.

User-facing changes:

- Legacy local accounts and state no longer block sandbox startup. Native MXC availability and supported-policy checks still run before workload execution.
- Remove obsolete backend/state controls, setup and migration guidance, the WFP cleanup command, and their acceptance fixtures and CI steps. Unknown configuration fields remain errors through the normal schema.
- Preserve configured Windows temporary-directory values, including when environment inheritance is disabled. Explicit host execution remains available.

Internal changes:

- Pin the MXC-only companion from https://github.com/t-kalinowski/cobox/pull/50, which removes Console account provisioning, legacy resource identities, and compatibility launch plumbing. Native setup retains trusted executor variables; an internal relay applies the exact workload environment after MXC creation, within the existing Jobs.
- Remove duplicate frontend backend selection and use the process default pipe DACL so MXC R/Python workers can open their protocol pipes.
- Keep managed proxy enforcement, the non-breakaway Job, and confirmed retirement before private-storage cleanup. Update configuration regressions and Windows capability/fault fixtures around the single MXC path.
- Report the digest-scoped Windows companion selected by the staging manifest in preflight inventory, distinguishing a missing current build from older bundles on disk.

With `sandbox.tempdir: read_write` and `inherit_environment: false`, sandboxed Python can create temporary files through both the CLI and an MCP session. The workload receives the granted `TMPDIR`, `TEMP`, and `TMP` without affecting native platform-directory discovery or having those values replaced by Windows package defaults.

title: Deduplicate failure sessions and canonical transcript snapshots
description:
The transcript suite repeats three no-R failure scenarios in the peer-runtime suite and runs six SQL semantic cases in two modes without asserting distinct policies. The peer wrappers also discard their R-enabled captures and combine independent Console sessions in one transcript.

- Keep every initialization discovery probe, compare complete equal exchanges, and remove eight duplicate canonical YAML files totaling 104,052 bytes and 2,004 lines.
- Run the peer failure helpers with R enabled only. Preserve their no-R owners and both execution modes, and record each R-enabled session separately with initialization, fixture context, and complete diagnostics.
- Run six SQL connection-selection, rendering, and error cases through `RUNTIME`: sandboxed on Unix and direct on Windows. Retain direct plus sandboxed DBI conformance and the existing policy, interruption, and lifecycle cases.

This removes twelve repeated scenario executions on fully provisioned Unix. Canonical discovery launches remain unchanged. No post-change speedup is claimed.

The change is internal to tests and snapshots; production source and public APIs are unchanged. The complete diff changes four Python test sources and eleven snapshot files, with 628 added and 2,266 deleted lines.

Local macOS validation passed the affected suites, native snapshot regeneration and verification, all formatters, `scripts/check`, and full case discovery with no orphan snapshots. The full functional run at 32 workers completed with 19 failures among 1,154 applicable cases, including temporary storage exhaustion and polling timing failures. Rerunning those 19 selectors at six workers on both the original base (`caec3e46`) and PR head (`e96934b5`) produced the same result: 17 passed, and two R documentation cases failed with identical locale startup warnings:

- `client_server/r/test_documentation::help_lookup_and_capture`
- `client_server/r/test_documentation::vignette_rendered_html`

The full local profile is therefore not a pass. Linux and Windows validation remains for hosted CI.

title: Fix cross-platform CI fixtures and generated documentation links
description:
Repair platform-dependent documentation assertions, offline dependency preparation, and resolver-readiness waits in the public acceptance fixtures, plus broken guide links in the generated R documentation site.

- **R documentation:** select a supported UTF-8 locale for Unicode help and vignette setup. Compare complete help pages after the existing trailing-space normalization, complete source bytes instead of R encoding attributes, and deferred pager bytes against native `file.show()` conversion. Select the Unicode-library vignette before switching to the C locale, preserving native filename representation and both C-locale rendering comparisons. Keep capture, return-value, deferred cleanup, and error assertions.
- **Offline SQL:** warm the real managed dependencies, then replace the fixture's PATH-visible `uv` with a wrapper that delegates to the saved executable using `--offline`. R-free preparation ignores `RETICULATE_UV`, and Console removes ambient `UV_OFFLINE`; an invocation receipt now proves the wrapper ran. Retain real DuckDB queries and no-download assertions under the denied resolver proxy policy, declare the POSIX wrapper requirement, and keep the canonical MCP handshake.
- **Custom-worker preparation:** replace the fixed 10-second resolver-readiness wait with the client's preparation deadline. Watch MCP output alongside the readiness checkpoint so an early setup failure reports its complete response. Preserve the held resolver gate, inspection before commit, and worker-startup barriers.
- **Generated website:** rewrite README guide links in the pkgdown R index from `../docs/` to `../`, where the shared rendered guides are published.

Regenerate the affected transcripts through `scripts/test --update`. The final diff against main contains fixture/support changes, generated transcripts, and the pkgdown link repair; it contains no Rust or CI workflow changes.

Validation performed:

- Earlier Windows documentation and tool-configuration suites passed without snapshot updates. After merging main, `python scripts/test client_server/r/test_documentation::vignette_rendered_html --jobs 1` passed with both the default and C caller locales, using the existing bundle whose R documentation sources are unchanged.
- After merging main, WSL focused verification passed for the offline SQL case in sandbox mode, both affected custom-worker cases in direct and sandbox modes, and the rendered-vignette and non-UTF-8-library-path cases in direct and sandbox modes. The offline-wrapper receipt assertion failed before the PATH fix and passed afterward; a controlled resolver failure confirmed that the readiness wait reports the complete early MCP error.
- `scripts/check` passed in WSL for the resolved merge using Python 3.13.16, including staging, core checks, Rust tests, the release build, and smoke transcripts.
- `scripts/format` ran unchanged on Windows and Linux; Ruff, yamark, rustfmt, and Air reported success. Generated snapshots were inspected and rerun without updates, and `git diff --check` passed. All seven website checks passed before the merge.
- The [documentation build on preceding head `53746cbe`](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/38184534681/job/114603926422) passed. CI for merge commit `7ce1b8c7` was not polled. No local macOS validation was available, and full/stress profiles were not run on the final revision.

title: Repair remaining Windows and Linux acceptance failures
description:
Recent main CI fails on Windows and Linux because acceptance fixtures assume a Unix host environment or a particular startup schedule. The changes retain the runtime, selected-environment, SQL-withholding, cache, and interruption assertions while making their prerequisites and observation boundaries explicit.

Windows fixes:

- Capture a home-directory fallback and explicit writable temporary directories when Python layout tests disable environment inheritance.
- Declare POSIX and SQL requirements for the shebang custom-worker/DuckDB cache fixture.
- Collect the initial R cell through completion when cold dependency preparation exceeds the first response deadline.

Linux fixes:

- Measure the OpenAI Agents tool call against its wall-clock wait budget; startup can consume that budget before the cell admission clock starts.
- Collect the missing-R startup receipt before submitting SQL, preserving the complete errors without a schedule-dependent idle separator.
- Hold the prepared-candidate launch checkpoint through the initial observation deadline, and allow its documented optional phase observation to be absent while the owner is contended.

Snapshots were regenerated with `scripts/test --update`. No production runtime or protocol changes.

Evidence: [current main CI](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37671258503) failed three of 215 Windows cases and two of 964 Linux cases. Local Windows coverage also reproduced cold R preparation exceeding the first response. The Linux startup-interruption baseline failed once in twelve concurrent repetitions.

Validation:

- `scripts/preflight` on native Windows and Ubuntu WSL; Windows companion staging.
- `scripts/format` unchanged on both platforms: Ruff, yamark, rustfmt, and Air passed.
- Windows focused reruns passed for R initial requirements and both Python layout cases; the custom-worker case reports its POSIX/SQL exclusions.
- Ubuntu WSL focused reruns passed in direct and sandbox modes, including six concurrent repetitions each of the startup-interruption, SDK wait, and missing-R SQL cases.
- `scripts/check` passed on Windows and Ubuntu WSL. Windows final native acceptance passed all 89 cases; all shared boundary suite selectors with `--full --jobs 6` passed all 214 applicable cases.

An exhaustive WSL diagnostic attempt encountered local R 4.5 native-fixture compilation and nested-procfs limitations and was stopped; it is not claimed as a full pass. An unchanged diagnostic-layout regression passes with uv 0.12.23, matching CI. Hosted CI remains the comprehensive merge gate.

Known separate main failures: macOS reports a stale writable-root transcript and a failure installing the DuckDB fts extension in a selected environment. This Windows/Linux PR does not claim macOS validation.

title: Prefer shared transcripts over platform-specific variants
description:
Portable features should not require a Windows runner just to refresh transcripts. Make shared transcripts the default, removing 23 unnecessary Windows YAML variants and three Windows QMD companions while retaining variants for native platform contracts.

- Make fixtures deterministic, normalize narrowly verified presentation differences, and separate SQL coverage into cases with declared capability requirements. Preserve complete errors, tracebacks, exit statuses, and exact canonical handshake comparisons.
- Keep Python lifecycle evidence focused on the Python requirements the case owns after checking the full public response, instead of recording unrelated platform-dependent provider inventories.
- Require a nonblank contract reason for every platform snapshot declaration. Document the shared-default policy in AGENTS.md, the development guide, and the boundary test guide.
- Let successful focused updates retire obsolete platform companions, including removed declarations from another host. Preserve unselected/skipped cases, other declared platforms, and unavailable declared execution modes; cover these rules through public runner regressions.

There are no production or user-facing behavior changes. Thirteen Windows YAML companions remain across eleven explicitly justified case owners, including native filesystem diagnostics, interpreter identity, retirement status, and Windows tool presentation. The branch includes the latest main changes through 4467ac46.

Local Linux sandbox coverage involving R remains incomplete because cold built-in dependency preparation did not finish; macOS coverage was unavailable. CI remains the comprehensive merge gate.

title: Provision elevated Windows sandbox acceptance in CI
description:
Windows CI currently skips provisioned elevated sandbox acceptance because it never provisions sandbox accounts or selects a state directory. Build the staged Console, prepare its sandbox state, verify readiness, and export `R_HOME` and `MCP_CONSOLE_TEST_WINDOWS_STATE_DIR` before the existing full gate. Checkout and installed-wheel acceptance then exercise the elevated input/interrupt case alongside restricted-token coverage.

The preparation command reuses an already-ready state without requesting provisioning. A failed or unconfirmed setup stops the job before exporting the environment. Public command regressions cover initial provisioning, reuse, and unconfirmed setup; the Windows guide documents the matching local validation setup.

Validation:

- Both new public preparation regressions failed before implementation and passed afterward.
- The preparation command reused this machine's existing provisioning and exported the local test environment successfully.
- `WindowsSandbox.test_provisioned_network_restricted_input_and_interrupt` passed locally with the reported state directory.
- `scripts/preflight.cmd`, companion staging, and all four formatters passed.
- Full core checks passed, including all 15 native workflow regressions.
- All 78 checkout native acceptance tests passed, including the provisioned elevated test, with no native skips.
- All 191 applicable shared executions passed; platform/capability exclusions were reported by discovery.
- `python scripts/check --full` passed with Python 3.13, `LC_ALL=C`, and the exported local environment. Installation acceptance passed for the copied `uv tool install` command, all 78 wheel native tests (including elevated acceptance), and both source-reinstall startup cases.
- CI provisioning PowerShell parsed without syntax errors; final formatting and diff checks passed.

Local integration reused existing Console provisioning. Fresh provisioning and failed readiness are exercised by the command fixtures; provisioning a fresh hosted runner remains CI validation.
The local full gate ran on the staged implementation based on `19a85667`, before commit.

title: Measure CI concurrency and collect transcript failures
description:
Make CI transcript concurrency measurable and collect failures across the suite so timing issues can be diagnosed in one run. Retain six workers by default and allow manual runs with six or twelve workers, with separate cancellation groups. Keep the full transcript, R package, wheel, and source-installation checks.

Local and CI transcript runs continue after individual failures. Once more than 15% of selected, capability-applicable cases fail, stop starting new cases and let active cases finish under their existing deadlines. Report every failed selector and its diagnostics, plus the number of cases not started. Count execution modes as one case, include initialization in the total, and preserve explicit cancellation and cleanup.

Synchronize timing-sensitive tests at the state they assert:

- Observe send admission before cancellation or competing submissions during discovery.
- Hold the first accepted result at a recording gate before closing MCP input.
- Await configuration before issuing a zero-timeout control call, and await setup before dependent requests.
- Give cold native Python inspection, requirements inspection, managed-uv preparation, and SSH resolution the existing preparation budget; allow 30 seconds for the resolver interrupt checkpoint.
- Use a FIFO receipt after advancing the fixture clock before releasing blocked requirement resolution.

Record runner details, native resource usage, and per-execution timings in job summaries and downloadable artifacts. On the same code tree and runner image, the [six-worker comparison](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37029134080) took 13m50s on Linux and 23m25s on macOS; [twelve workers](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37029119907) took 19m17s and 27m02s. Every case was attempted; the six-worker Linux and twelve-worker macOS runs reported fixture failures addressed here. Keep six as the default pending further measurements. Maximum RSS is a per-process high-water mark, not the combined peak of concurrent workers.

These changes affect CI and development commands; there are no runtime API or behavior changes.

title: Reuse runtime caches in slow transcript tests
description:
Reduce repeated runtime preparation in the transcript tests. The mixed-language Python SDK case now inherits the standard R test environment, so it can use CI's restored R and Python caches while still forcing `LC_ALL=C`.

CI also prewarms the default packages with `praise`, and with both `praise` and `zeallot`. The expanded R cache uses a new key and can restore existing caches from the same UTC week. The release guide records the prewarm behavior.

These changes affect test and CI setup only. Public Console behavior and the existing transcript expectations are unchanged.

title: Reuse weekly Cargo build caches across PRs
description:
Ordinary source edits currently create large Cargo cache snapshots that compete with the shared caches on `main`. Keep one build baseline per dependency set and UTC week so PR updates, new PRs, and merge commits can reuse it. Cargo still checks the current sources and rebuilds changed inputs.

Replace whole-workflow hashes with an explicit `CI_BUILD_CACHE_VERSION` version for changes to build inputs outside the hashed files, such as workflow build flags or native dependency setup. Unrelated workflow edits preserve the caches, while weekly resets, native-environment boundaries, and exact source matching for finished release outputs remain in place.

Add a workflow that deletes caches scoped to a closed PR's merge ref, without checking out PR code, and document the cache policy. These changes affect CI only; Console's public interfaces and runtime behavior are unchanged.

title: Reuse build outputs and dependency caches in CI
description:
Test-only pushes can restore Cargo caches and still rebuild unchanged executables. Preserve unchanged companion files, the staging manifest, and generated Rust so Cargo can reuse those builds while retaining integrity checks and removal of obsolete files.

CI now caches complete release wheels and native bundles using the source, packaging inputs, toolchain, runner image, and staged companion digests. It preserves pinned runner source timestamps, includes companion licenses and Clippy preparation in the build caches, shares the uv cache between packaging and runtime preparation, and gives the R package check a separate cached library. Completed builds are saved before tests.

Each platform still has one job running all applicable checks. R checks and transcripts use the prepared executable; source installation checks run last because they replace and hide the shared target directory. Source installations continue to invoke Cargo, and the console's runtime interfaces are unchanged.

title: Reuse build caches across PR runs when checks fail
description:
Let pull-request runs save the private sandbox runner and Cargo dependencies so subsequent runs of the same PR can reuse a new runner pin or dependency set before it reaches `main`.

Save the staged runner immediately after a successful build, and enable `rust-cache`'s `cache-on-failure` for both Cargo workspaces. Later check failures no longer discard these caches; the Cargo post-job save can also retain dependencies from partial builds.

GitHub scopes PR caches to that PR's merge ref, while allowing PRs to restore caches from `main`. Existing cache keys are preserved. This is an internal CI change with no public-facing runtime changes.

Local `actionlint` passes, and core checks passed. The full `scripts/check` run stopped on four relay-worker snapshot mismatches containing extra reticulate-resolution events. Those four cases passed when run together on both the unchanged base and the preceding workflow revision.

title: Run macOS CI on one runner
description:
## Summary

Run all macOS validation in one GitHub Actions job so each CI batch consumes one hosted macOS runner.

- Run core checks, wheel smoke testing, the R package check, and transcript tests sequentially in one `macos` job.
- Reuse checkout, Python, R, Rust, uv, and build caches across the validation path.
- Keep transcript cases parallel inside the runner with `scripts/test --jobs 6`.
- Check the R package against its ordinary dependencies before installing transcript-only Quarto and development reticulate dependencies.
- Disable the first R dependency cache because its deferred post-job save would otherwise capture the later transcript dependency state. The transcript and managed-environment caches remain enabled.
- Update workflow-shape tests to require one macOS runner and preserve the dependency order and cache boundary.

## User-facing changes

None. This changes repository CI only.

## Internal changes

Pull requests and pushes to `main` now use one macOS job instead of separate core/package and transcript jobs. Validation takes longer because those phases no longer overlap, and the ordinary R package dependencies are installed on each run to keep their state separate from transcript-only dependencies.

## Testing

Run locally on macOS arm64:

- `scripts/format`
- `scripts/check` (all 290 transcript cases passed)
- `actionlint .github/workflows/ci.yaml .github/workflows/release.yml`
- Maturin 1.14.1 release wheel build and `scripts/release.py smoke-wheel` with uv 0.12.4
- `R CMD build` and `R CMD check --no-manual` (`Status: OK`)

title: Use latest CI tool releases
description:
Remove fixed uv, Quarto, and Maturin versions from CI and release workflows so new tool releases can be picked up without manual version bumps. Keep uv's normal cache reuse for IR, Yamark, and Maturin, and retain checksum and version verification for Quarto downloads.

Keep Maturin within the supported `>=1.15,<2.0` range. CI installs it before restoring finished release outputs, includes the installed version in the cache key, and builds with that executable. The release action reads the supported range from `pyproject.toml`.

This changes CI and release tooling only; there are no changes to Console's public API or runtime behavior.

title: Reduce CI dependency setup overhead
description:
Reduce repeated CI dependency setup while keeping one job per platform, six transcript workers, and the full test profiles.

- Install Quarto 1.10.18 from checksummed portable archives. This avoids the macOS package installer, which took 53 seconds in the observed run. Quarto is downloaded each run and is not cached.
- Cache only compressed Linux `.deb` downloads, about 58 MB in the observed run. Use weekly keys without restoring older weeks; exclude installed system files, apt indexes, and Quarto. Install missing requirements without upgrading already-installed system packages or pulling recommended packages.
- Install required R dependencies for transcripts and the Windows bridge, excluding unused suggestions. Start fresh versions of these smaller caches and save transcript packages before tests. Retain suggested packages for the R package's own checks.

Remove the CI worker-count input and its DEVELOPMENT.md section. These are CI-only changes; Console behavior and test coverage are unchanged.

title: Enable incremental release builds in CI
description:
CI enables incremental compilation globally, but release build steps override it with `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`. Remove those overrides so the private runner, release wheel, and source installation builds can reuse compiler state across revisions.

Clarify that Cargo build data is restored across source and dependency changes within the same native build environment and UTC week. Exact matches of compiled and packaging inputs additionally let CI skip the release build and reuse a finished wheel and native bundle. Both paths run the current tests.

The weekly cache reset and one job per platform remain in place. These are internal CI and documentation changes; runtime interfaces are unchanged.

title: Reuse incremental Rust builds across CI runs
description:
Retain application workspace artifacts and incremental compiler state so source edits can reuse prior compilation. The cache key covers the compiler, platform, R version, build inputs, and compiled sources; a transcript-only change can reuse an exact cache entry without uploading another copy.

Include the UTC ISO week-year and week number in every application and sandbox build-cache key and restore prefix. Each Monday starts a new cache namespace, so old build artifacts cannot carry forward across weeks. Cache Cargo downloads separately so they survive the reset; the staged sandbox executable remains keyed by its source pin and staging script.

Replace the post-job Rust cache with explicit restore/save steps. Each cache is saved only after its build succeeds. Compile the application, test executables, and release wheel before saving the application cache, then run checks and smoke tests. Debug/test builds use incremental compilation; release builds retain their existing settings.

Cache sandbox intermediates separately and restore them only when the staged runner is missing. This avoids downloading the sandbox build tree on ordinary PR pushes while retaining it for a later pin change within the same week. This is an internal CI change with no public-facing runtime changes.

A local three-trial probe restored compressed build archives, refreshed checkout timestamps, and changed CLI help text. Median debug/test compilation took 2.1 seconds with incremental state versus 4.9 seconds with dependency artifacts alone. The compressed archive grew from 207 MB to 343 MB; these measurements exclude network transfer and do not establish an end-to-end CI speedup.

Workflow lint, UTC week calculation checks across Monday and year boundaries, core checks, all-target builds, and installed-wheel smoke checks passed locally. The full `scripts/check` run stopped at the expected-error assertion in `retains_automatic_r_package_after_error_and_restart`. That case passed in isolation on both the base with incremental compilation disabled and this branch with it enabled.

title: Reduce macOS CI runner concurrency
description:
## Summary

Consolidate the R package validation into the existing core-checks runner and remove the standalone R package workflow.

- install the R package dependencies after the existing core and wheel checks;
- run `R CMD build` and `R CMD check` against the debug binary already built by the wheel smoke test;
- retain the separate transcript runner, which remains the longest validation path;
- remove the duplicated checkout, R setup, Rust setup, cache restore, and binary build from `.github/workflows/r-package.yaml`.

## Effect

Source changes that previously started three simultaneous macOS jobs now start two. The core/package job should still finish before the transcript job on warm runs, so this reduces use of the constrained macOS runner pool without materially lengthening the CI critical path.

The package check now runs in every ordinary CI run rather than using a separate path-filtered workflow. That keeps the workflow simple and does not affect the expected completion time while transcripts remain longer.

## Testing

CI is the validation for this workflow-only change.

title: Install IR and Yamark with uv in CI
description:
## Summary

CI now installs IR and Yamark as uv tools. This replaces the custom IR shell installer and its path setup with the packages now published for both tools.

## User-facing changes

None. MCP Console behavior is unchanged.

## Internal changes

The macOS CI job runs `uv tool install r-lib-ir` and `uv tool install yamark` after setting up uv.

title: Update sandbox runner to rust-v0.163.0
description:
Advance the bundled sandbox runner from `rust-v0.162.1` (`46faf2a5`) to the `rust-v0.163.0` branch tip (`1d93f1236`) to include the merged runner updates. These include managed proxy environments, Windows environment-name comparison, Linux readiness, and startup with unwritable host roots through [cobox #58](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/cobox/pull/58).

The native domain matcher accepts `*` and `?` wildcards and rejects character classes such as `[0-9]`. Document this behavior, update the pinned protocol link, and cover rejection before workload execution. Public configuration keys and the MCP, R, and Python APIs retain their existing contracts.

Internal fixture changes remove incidental R preparation from Python-only cases, keep isolated Rscript launchers and their dependencies in the selected installation, and request consistent source-install help output. A controlled origin supplies the missing DuckDB extension's expected 404 while preserving comparison with the real installer's complete diagnostic. Recovery and SQL tests collect exact output from the same admitted cells after dependency preparation. Mixed-language recording prepares its real dependencies before code cells; generated literal YAML companions preserve its complete Markdown and Quarto output through formatting. Assertions, case deadlines, and real-library sandbox coverage are preserved.

Command Prompt launches can also reject inherited hidden `=ExitCode` metadata before native setup. [cobox #59](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/cobox/pull/59) contains the separate environment-capture fix; it is not included in this pin.

The shipped runner still fails sandbox launch from Windows SSH with DLL initialization error `0xc0000142`, also described in an [upstream SDK report](https://github.com/microsoft/mxc/issues/1465). A separate local experiment selecting an explicit Windows desktop allowed launch on the existing host. That SDK change is not part of the dependency shipped by this runner pin. Interactive Windows validation applies to the existing host; the upstream runner matrix on a fresh MXC-capable host remains outstanding.

The Linux resolver-checkpoint timeout and Windows EOF response loss have additional failure diagnostics, but their causes remain unknown. This PR does not claim that those diagnostics fix either intermittent failure.

title: Update sandbox runner after the MXC integration merge
description:
Advance the sandbox runner pin from `c32634c4` to `90a6c52c`, the merged head of `mcp-console/sandbox-runner/rust-v0.162.1` after [t-kalinowski/cobox#50](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/cobox/pull/50). This picks up the Windows workload environment relay and target `TEMP`/`TMP` permission fixes.

Update the Python and R MXC acceptance probes to recognize the runner's new unavailable-runtime diagnostic. Normalize the R probe's `cmd.exe` path to native Windows separators so its supported-host check executes correctly. Document the Windows fresh-host requirement and the legacy provisioning state that must be removed before using a previously provisioned host. Point the complete native policy schema link to the pinned runner revision.

title: Update sandbox runner for unrestricted and external policies
description:
Advance the sandbox runner pin from `689f48c30` to branch tip `3f060c421`, retaining the `rust-v0.154.0` release base and protocol 2. The existing `sandbox --config-env` interface now supports supervised unrestricted policies and policies that delegate enforcement to an outer sandbox.

Update the configuration and Linux compatibility docs to describe filesystem classification, network and proxy behavior, and the lifecycle limits of external enforcement. Link the expanded upstream JSON reference and document the Docker procfs setting needed for local installation checks. Console's default policy, project YAML restrictions, and runtime adapter remain unchanged.

Add public CLI coverage for the new modes, including network access, literal stdin, exit status, transport consumption, and private-storage cleanup. Update Linux classification and Landlock snapshots, and assert that the proxy handshake advertises its proxy settings.

macOS `scripts/check` passed, including source and wheel installation. The applicable Linux sandbox cases and bundle installation checks also passed. Broader Linux validation encountered two direct R callback failures that reproduce with the previous pinned bundle. Upstream run 34605557365 at the new pin passed 87 of 88 Linux executable contracts; `reference::upstream_tagged_paths_aliases_and_ignored_fields_reach_execution` failed while building a bubblewrap command with `Permission denied (os error 13)`.

title: Reuse CI caches across runner image revisions
description:
Routine GitHub-hosted image updates changed every native build cache key, even when the project's relevant build inputs were unchanged. Use `ImageOS` (`macos26` or `ubuntu24`) for the shared cache identity and keep the full `ImageVersion` in diagnostic output.

This is an internal CI change with no user-facing runtime or API changes. Preserve the existing architecture, compiler, dependency, recipe, and UTC week boundaries for build data and finished artifacts. Update the CI documentation to describe reuse across image revisions and manual invalidation for native changes Cargo does not track.

The new key format needs an initial cache population. Subsequent runs can reuse those caches across routine image revisions within the same OS version and week.

title: Update sandbox runner to rust-v0.154.0
description:
Advance the bundled sandbox runner from `rust-v0.150.1` to commit `689f48c30deeb6aaa95a193e31e5971dd6820465` on `mcp-console/sandbox-runner/rust-v0.154.0`, so source installations and wheels use the requested release base.

Keep protocol 2, Rust 1.95.0, and Console's launch API and application policy unchanged. Update the current protocol and policy documentation references to the new pin.

Normalize incidental panic line and column numbers in the Linux file-root rejection transcript so source layout changes in the updated runner do not fail CI. Preserve the panic text, source filename, exit status, and file-state assertions.

Validation includes a full macOS `scripts/check` for the runner update and focused writable-root suites on macOS and Linux for the transcript adjustment.

title: Upgrade to Rust 1.95 and update dependencies
description:
## Summary

Raise the project MSRV to Rust 1.95 and refresh compatible Cargo dependencies. This keeps the compiler and dependency graph current while preserving the existing CLI, MCP, and runtime behavior.

## User-facing changes

- Building mcp-console now requires Rust 1.95.
- No MCP tool, CLI, or runtime behavior changes.

## Internal changes

- Update base64 from 0.22 to 0.23 and refresh 33 other locked crates to their latest Rust-1.95-compatible releases.
- Simplify one relay event-loop condition for Rust 1.95 Clippy.
- Normalize the relay shutdown grace in one transcript so live deadline rounding cannot produce a one-millisecond snapshot difference.
- Keep rmcp on 2.2.0 because 3.x changes the SDK's protocol model, and keep the Ark pins because they already match the configured fork's current head.

title: Refresh dependencies and development toolchains
description:
Keep builds, CI, and client integrations on current upstream versions by refreshing the dependency requirements and pinned tools.

Source builds now require Rust 1.99. Update the direct Cargo requirements and lockfile, advance Ark to `2411df0d` and S7 to its current main revision, and refresh the Python and R integration requirements. The public client, CLI, and MCP interfaces remain unchanged.

Use Python 3.14 and uv 0.13.1 across CI, release builds, and Linux wheel validation, and update pinned GitHub Actions. Python 3.15 is deferred until DuckDB publishes compatible wheels; the development guides record that boundary. Older versions used by compatibility fixtures remain intentional.

Internally, adapt to the updated rmcp and html2text APIs. Preserve clean shutdown after discovery-only MCP exchanges and keep cancellation of unfinished initialization working when output is blocked. Refresh the DuckDB, Great Tables, pandas, and Selenium acceptance packages and their transcripts; the Selenium regression checks both IPv4 and IPv6 sandbox denials and retains the complete error chain.

title: Make multiline string literals readable in source
description:
## Summary

Record a repository-wide preference for showing multiline string content with source newlines. This makes generated documents and diagnostics easier to read where they are defined.

## Changes

- Public output is unchanged: Quarto documents, diagnostics, and tool descriptions retain the same string values.
- Convert Rust messages and document templates, plus Python fixtures and exact-output assertions, to readable multiline literals. Preserve indentation and trailing newlines; keep escapes when they represent data or clarify a short value.

title: Use the sandbox checkout's Rust toolchain
description:
Source builds now use the compiler channel from the pinned sandbox checkout, even when `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN` selects a different compiler for Console. Remove the duplicate manifest field so the sandbox source owns this configuration.

Python package builds and installations now require Python 3.11. Staging reads the toolchain file with standard-library `tomllib`, with no fallback or extra dependency. The Python interpreter used inside Console keeps its existing minimum of 3.10.

CI exports repository and commit metadata before checkout and keys runner build caches on the checked-out toolchain file. Release wheels build Console with stable Rust, matching CI, and retain explicit build targets.

Public staging and installation regressions cover independent compiler selection and wheel Python metadata while preserving artifact integrity, relocation, and native-flag rebuild coverage.

Follow-up to #276.

Local validation passed: focused staging tests, the full installation suite with `UV_PYTHON=3.11`, Actionlint, `scripts/format`, and `scripts/check` with six transcript workers.

title: Publish macOS wheels through PyPI
description:
## Summary

Prepare MCP Console 0.0.2 for distribution as binary-only PyPI wheels, so macOS users can run the existing Rust CLI through `uvx` or install it as a uv tool without building the repository.

## User-facing changes

- Adds `uvx mcp-console` and `uv tool install mcp-console` installation paths for native Apple Silicon and Intel macOS wheels.
- Declares `r-lib-ir>=0.4.0` as a package dependency. MCP Console first looks for `ir` beside its installed executable, then falls back to `PATH` for source and Cargo installations.
- Documents the R requirement, first-start dependency preparation, installation, release setup, verification, and recovery.
- Keeps the existing CLI contract: `mcp-console serve` remains the MCP stdio entry point, with the same `--help` and `--version` behavior.

The initial release does not include a source distribution, universal wheel, Linux or Windows wheel, or GitHub binary archive. PyPI release 0.0.1 remains unchanged and unyanked.

## Internal changes

- Adds Maturin binary-package metadata and keeps `Cargo.toml` as the version source for the Rust binary and Python package.
- Adds normal-CI wheel construction and installed-wheel acceptance, plus a tag-driven release workflow for both macOS architectures.
- Moves release validation and smoke-test logic into `scripts/release.py`, with public Python tests run by `scripts/check`; the GitHub Actions YAML now primarily orchestrates those commands.
- Requires a stable version tag that matches `Cargo.toml`, points to a commit on current `main`, and has successful CI from a push to `main` before publication.
- Verifies the expected wheel set, exact CLI version and help output, `uvx` and uv-tool installation, sibling `ir` resolution, sandbox execution, and an MCP R evaluation with bounded waits.
- Publishes through PyPI Trusted Publishing. Manual workflow dispatches build and inspect artifacts but cannot publish.

## One-time release setup

Before publishing `v0.0.2`, create the GitHub Actions environment `pypi` and configure the existing PyPI `mcp-console` project with the Trusted Publisher described in `RELEASE.md`. No PyPI token secret is required.

title: Support interactive stdin in R evaluations
description:
## Summary

Route stdin as a worker-owned fd-0 stream so `send` can supply input before, during, or after a top-level R evaluation. This keeps the contract simple for current console reads and future background runtime jobs. Control and output remain on the worker sideband, while paired input-request and input-received events avoid an unnecessary tool boundary when queued bytes satisfy a supported console read promptly.

## User-facing changes

- `send` accepts `r` and `stdin` together, or `stdin` alone while the worker is evaluating or idle.
- Nonempty stdin sent while idle lazily starts the worker when needed, queues the bytes, and returns `[idle]`. `timeout_ms` bounds evaluation waits, not that cold idle startup.
- Stdin is UTF-8 encoded and queued exactly, without adding a newline, validating or limiting the text, or treating the end of a payload as EOF.
- Console input requests remain provisional for up to 10 milliseconds. A successful-read receipt suppresses `[input]`; an outstanding request returns accumulated output, its prompt, and `[input]` so partial payloads can continue in later calls.
- Unread bytes remain available to idle background consumers or later reads and evaluations. `timeout_ms` can return `[running]` while code is blocked on a direct fd-0 read, which emits no request or receipt.

## Internal changes

- Keep complete R source and worker control on the JSON-lines sideband while one background FIFO writer owns worker fd 0.
- Keep evaluation result, output, and provisional-input state together so prompt output is delivered exactly once across receipts, timeouts, and completion.
- Pair each supported R console input request with a receipt after a nonempty fd-0 read; direct readers remain independent of that state.
- Close worker stdin as part of bounded shutdown.
- Extend the Zod fixture and public transcript suite to cover cold and warm idle writes, bundled and follow-up stdin, request receipts, retained prompt output, direct fd-0 reads across timeouts, partial payloads, UTF-8 buffer boundaries, unread input, and stalled-worker shutdown.
- Record worker-scoped stdin ownership, request/receipt semantics, idle startup, and the short grace-window tradeoff in the implemented protocol and design sketches.

title: Add development worker sideband protocol
description:
## Summary

Add a small server-side development worker path so MCP Console can build and test the sideband protocol before the production runtime exists. The normal server remains an echo service unless the hidden worker option is selected.

## User-facing changes

- On macOS, `mcp-console serve --worker PATH` lazily launches `PATH` inside the existing MCP Console sandbox and routes `send` calls containing exactly one `r` string to it.
- Normal `mcp-console serve` behavior is unchanged.
- `docs/WORKER_PROTOCOL.md` records the exact implemented launch, framing, messages, handshake, shutdown behavior, and current limits.

## Internal changes

- Add an inherited-pipe, newline-delimited JSON sideband and a server-side worker client.
- Serialize worker evaluations and move blocking pipe and process work off the Tokio runtime.
- Start a one-second shutdown deadline when MCP input closes or the transport is released. The graceful sideband message runs independently, so a blocked pipe cannot postpone sandbox cleanup.
- Add the executable Python Zod fixture and transcript coverage for evaluation, sandbox enforcement, stalled evaluation shutdown, and a blocked sideband writer.
- Carry output directly as JSON text; arbitrary binary output is outside the current protocol.

## Notes

Full descendant supervision remains the sandbox lifetime supervisor's responsibility. This slice force-stops the worker process group only while the direct sandbox process is still running; it does not add the broader supervisor planned separately.

title: Add a minimal MCP console server
description:
## Summary

This adds the first MCP-facing behavior to the Rust binary: a minimal stdio server that exercises the protocol lifecycle before the runtime and session layers exist.

## User-facing changes

- Run `mcp-console` or `mcp-console serve` to start the MCP server over stdio.
- Discover exactly one tool, `console`.
- Call `console` with any JSON object and receive that object back as JSON text.
- Code execution and state retention remain unimplemented.

## Internal changes

- Implement the stdio adapter with the official Rust MCP SDK and a current-thread Tokio runtime.
- Add public acceptance coverage for initialization, tool discovery, tool calls, echo output, and shutdown on EOF.
- Raise the minimum Rust version from 1.85 to 1.88 for the MCP SDK's macro dependencies.
- Update `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` to describe the implemented surface.

title: Advance native sandbox runner to latest 0.163.0 tip
description:
Advance the native runner pin on `mcp-console/sandbox-runner/rust-v0.163.0` from `3d7ac640` to `9a6111f4` to include the Windows private-storage cleanup fix from [cobox #61](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/cobox/pull/61).

On Windows, cleanup now retries transient DLL image mappings after workload retirement. Permission denials still fail immediately, and persistent mappings still report failure. Cleanup does not follow reparse points or change the attributes of surviving hard links.

The Console diff only updates `sandbox-runner.json`. Configuration and the companion protocol are unchanged.

title: Fix recent main CI acceptance failures
description:
Acceptance fixtures can lose initial SQL fetch prompts, assume an ordering between R installer streams, and omit required license files from relocated Windows wheel installations. The R cache-directory test also compares resolved paths using the input's spelling.

- Capture the local R installer's stdout and stderr separately, replay each complete stream before the cell finishes, and require a clean restart response.
- Cover relative and absolute cache inputs in R configuration tests, expecting native absolute paths without creating the cache directory.
- Collect the initial SQL fetch response together with subsequent polls so the fixtures retain input prompts regardless of which response delivers them.
- Check the exact native Python import error type and attributes under explicit dependency resolution while preserving unchanged declarations and successful explicit package additions.
- Copy flat wheel license files along with the Windows sandbox runner, and verify that a relocated installation reaches the same public sandbox startup result as the original.

These changes are limited to acceptance fixtures and generated snapshots. Public APIs and runtime behavior are unchanged.

title: Reorganize Console documentation and unify the Python API reference
description:
Give new users a guided introduction, returning users guides for specific tasks and a settings index, and application authors a dedicated place for integrations. Bring the Python API reference into the main Quarto website so it shares the site's navigation, theme, and search.

- Use **Get started**, **Guides**, **Build**, and **Reference** in the top navigation. Get started and Guides share an expanded Learn Console sidebar; Build and Reference have their own sidebars. Keep Development in the footer and align the R package site's top navigation with the main site.
- Make Get started a first-analysis walkthrough, followed by Sessions and languages, Packages and environments, Sandbox and trust, and Recordings and reports. Keep the **I want to…** table on the Guides landing page, with direct links to R and Python use. Combine installation and MCP client setup in **Install and connect**.
- Give Build a data assistant walkthrough and guides for R, Python, and direct MCP integration. Separate practical guides from exact contracts: consolidate package declarations, policies, sources, and caches in Package settings; collect send operations and requirements in the MCP reference; move recording storage details into a dedicated reference. Use one index of configuration keys and consolidate configuration export documentation.
- Reframe the homepage around native runtimes, configurable sandbox permissions, automatic package preparation, and recordings for review and reports. Keep the standalone sandbox example within the runtime section, add a complete `--config-env` example to its guide, and apply the Soft forest dark palette.
- Publish lowercase directory URLs without `.html`, such as `/builtin_runtime/`, while retaining descriptive source filenames. Update navigation, links, search, sitemaps, inventories, and downloadable documentation to those routes; preserve Python symbol fragments and inline methods.

Internally, pin Great Docs to 0.17.0 and use its static reference generator before Quarto discovers pages, replacing the separate Python HTML build. Keep inventory-based cross-references, source links, Markdown/LLM downloads, and reference styling within the main site. Retain the R pkgdown build.

Add simple uv-based preview and render scripts that forward arguments to Quarto. Preview retains the outputs Quarto needs to track changes and reloads the current clean URL; full renders remove those intermediate outputs. Extend rendered-site coverage for navigation, search, links and anchors, package references, partial renders, and live preview, and use the render script in documentation CI.

Console runtime behavior is unchanged. The executable-source change updates the documentation link in the generated configuration starter; Python client changes are docstrings.

title: Fix startup admission and Windows preparation acceptance
description:
Startup and Windows preparation acceptance now establish the runtime state their assertions require. The terminal-response regression receives its cell's running/startup response before releasing discovery, then polls for completion. This prevents default package preparation from consuming the fixture's one-shot DBI gate before the cell is admitted, while retaining the response-write gate, paused poll, idle and retained-input assertions, and existing deadlines.

Windows resolver restrictions are exercised through ordinary MCP sessions. A separate trusted-warmup case verifies host preparation before an unavailable worker sandbox rejects launch. The shared startup-failure exchange observes the rejected cell before closing input, and native fault-injection diagnostics retain captured output. The uv bootstrap fixture selects a PATH without an installed ir beside Python, so it exercises the intended bootstrap command.

Only acceptance fixtures and generated direct/sandbox transcripts change. Runtime behavior, public interfaces, permissions, and the companion pin remain unchanged.

title: Preserve resolver close-failure coverage with best-effort defaults
description:
Align the invalid DuckDB extension-cache regression with best-effort defaults. A failed implicit `sqlite` install reports its diagnostic and lets SQL run; the regression now checks that the later resolver Close failure still makes connection shutdown fail.

The acceptance test retains the Close marker, exact resolver error and sandbox exit status 47, and server exit status 1. The direct missing-HOME case continues to verify fatal startup and repeated failure responses. This changes acceptance coverage and its generated transcript; runtime behavior and public interfaces are unchanged.

title: Make client registration global by default
description:
Client registration now defaults to global scope. `--scope project` writes in the current directory, `--scope project --directory PATH` selects another existing directory, and `--scope auto` preserves the previous Git-root/global selection.

When global registration finds a same-named project entry, it reports its path and explains that it may take precedence. The check follows each client's project-file discovery rules, including user-configured root markers where supported, and excludes aliases of the global configuration file. Project files and client approvals remain intact. Unreadable or malformed project files encountered by the check fail before installation or writes.

The implementation is confined to client registration. Update the owning reference, generated CLI help, and public regressions for scope selection, directory validation, legacy registrations, ancestor discovery, and dry runs.

Validated locally on macOS with 28 CLI cases, `scripts/format`, and `scripts/check`.

title: Fix Windows configuration acceptance and path diagnostics
description:
`config init` now builds its destination from native path components, so creation messages, previews, and existing-file errors display consistent Windows paths. Public acceptance tests assert the complete path before normalizing it for shared snapshots.

Configuration acceptance checks each platform's exact managed temporary-directory description and resolver rejection order. Dedicated Windows snapshots cover the resolver error and read-only workspace fallback. These test changes preserve the existing permission behavior.

title: Specify the custom-resolver trust and activation contract
description:
## Problem

Optional custom-resolver support lacks a proposed trust and acceptance contract defining preparation authority, runtime ownership and result acceptance while preserving captured policies and permissions.

## Fix

Add an unapproved design sketch covering validated declarations, inspected runtime selections, R/Python/mixed preparation, activation and cleanup receipts, and executable/configuration/output trust. Preserve receipt-based live R/Python activation and server-owned DuckDB extension-only acceptance. Reuse existing local owners and identify decisions requiring Tomasz's approval before implementation. Public APIs, runtime behavior and sandbox permissions remain unchanged.

## Validation

Native macOS: scripts/preflight, scripts/format and scripts/check passed, including core checks, release build and smoke transcripts. Source audit confirmed the acceptance distinction; MCP Console verified all ten links. git diff --check origin/main...HEAD passed. Repair committed as 494d75ef; committed document matches the validated bytes. WORKPAD.md is current and uncommitted. Full-suite, Linux/Windows and hosted CI/review coverage were not run.

Passed local checks: `uv run --no-project --python 3.13 python scripts/check`.

title: Measure managed-graphics interrupt behavior and document recovery limits
description:
## Problem

Managed R graphics can defer interruption during native drawing and device closure. The reported large-PNG stall needed bounded measurements and recovery guidance.

## Fix

Add a resource-limited measurement harness, complete admission/control/poll output accounting, public graphics recovery regressions with a native FIFO gate, and a guide with measured timings and resource limits. Preserve worker identity across PID namespaces and declare the R capability for graphics fixtures. Synchronize startup-defaults assertions through public readiness while preserving the exact reset checks.

In three direct Mac trials, Quartz drawing settled 0.63–0.72 seconds after interrupt, and restart restored plotting. The reported large-PNG stall was not reproduced; no production graphics defect was established. This PR delivers tests, measurements and recovery documentation.

## Validation

Clean head `97ee05c87da5b1279cbd048f5d5a42782f31d86d` passed `scripts/check` on macOS and ordered local Sol 6.1 MAX then Astra 6 XHIGH review. Focused graphics recovery tests passed all four direct/sandbox executions with unchanged snapshots; hosts without R explicitly skip those cases. All formatters and diff checks passed.

The guide retains dated baseline measurements. Local validation was on macOS; Linux/Windows native graphics timing was not measured. Hosted results are tracked in the PR checks.

Passed local checks: `uv run --no-project --python 3.13 python scripts/check`.

title: feat: select an installed R executable
description:
Allow projects to select an installed R executable or launcher with `r: PATH` or `r.executable`, alongside `r.vanilla`, so workers and dependency preparation use the same installation. Expand shorthand before configuration layers merge, capture relative and home-relative paths once, and retain the selection across worker restarts and explicit startup retries. Preserve native path bytes and whitespace in the reported R home.

Internally, inspect the launcher with worker permissions and suppressed startup files, then derive matching Rscript, runtime library, and resource directories. Capture selected file contents with SHA-256 and check them and resource directory targets before worker launches and preparation operations, including operations issued to an already running resolver. Native R startup and default discovery retain their current behavior. The installation and all code it loads remain trusted preparation inputs; these checks do not prevent concurrent replacement or cover every executable dependency.

Validated on macOS arm64 with public R selection, Python selection, configuration suites, `scripts/format`, and `scripts/check`. Native Windows and Linux execution were not exercised for this revision.

title: Trim configuration discovery warnings
description:
Remove the broad safe-mode disclaimer from configuration docs and CLI help so the warning stays focused on project configuration's ability to change sandbox permissions. Native startup containment and environment inheritance remain documented in their own sections.

Internally, store project configuration help in a multiline constant and regenerate help snapshots on macOS and Windows. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

The macOS local gate, native startup containment regression, and help checks on macOS and Windows passed.

title: Add conservative DuckDB INSTALL preflight without bundling DuckDB
description:
## Problem

Future DuckDB INSTALL interception needs to distinguish supported top-level requests from INSTALL text inside comments, literals or unknown grammar. Console currently forwards complete cells to the selected DBI or DB-API provider; a semicolon alone cannot establish a safe statement boundary.

## Fix

Add a pure Rust recognizer for complete INSTALL-only cells, exported from a minimal same-package library without adding DuckDB or parser dependencies. Plans borrow unchanged source and retain exact UTF-8 byte spans, safe quoted names, original case, explicit repository aliases and Default when FROM is omitted. Mixed or unknown grammar, unsupported forms, incomplete input and resource-limit excess decline the whole cell without a partial plan. FORCE CHECKPOINT remains ordinary grammar; FORCE INSTALL is unsupported. Analysis is iterative and bounded to 1 MiB and 1,024 installs.

Add public API contracts for adversarial syntax, Unicode, nested comments, source round-trip and limits. Released R/Python binding conformance covers quoted INSTALL syntax, whole-batch parsing, later catalog errors and transaction rollback. Document the scanner choice and integration obligations. This adds a recognition API and contract documentation; SQL tool behavior, provider ownership and execution remain unchanged. Host authorization, resolver wiring and sequential execution belong to subsequent integration.

## Validation

On clean b8a3370e, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 scripts/check` passed companion staging, runtime-source and architecture validation, Rust formatting, Clippy, all 58 Rust tests (including 10 recognizer contracts), release build and 13 smoke cases across 20 executions. Debug assertions remained enabled.

`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 scripts/test --jobs 2 client_server/sql/test_install_contract client_server/requirements/test_resolver_sandbox::r_duckdb_uses_resolver_cache client_server/lifecycle/test_startup_interrupt::interrupts_first_cell_before_resolver_registration client_server/sql/test_connections::prepares_builtin_extensions_without_downloads` passed all four selected cases across six executions, without snapshot updates.

`scripts/preflight`, unchanged `scripts/format` (all four formatters) and `git diff --check` passed. Coverage is local macOS; native Linux/Windows and hosted CI for this head remain unverified.

title: Tailor tool descriptions to configured visible languages
description:
## Problem

Explicitly hidden languages still appeared in tool and exposed-field descriptions. R-only guidance mentioned Python preparation, custom-worker guidance mentioned SQL and Python, and requirements/control/timeout descriptions retained irrelevant language advice. Visibility also made it easy to mistake an exposed Python field for ownership of the managed SQL provider.

## Fix

Compose tool and field guidance from captured configured visibility, including nested requirements, control, stdin, and timeout descriptions. Keep SQL-only guidance provider-neutral, omit excluded-language examples, and qualify Python connection/frame-registration helpers by provider ownership. Preserve provider preparation keys, runtime capabilities and routing, missing-runtime diagnostics, and default/full guidance. Descriptions remain stable through runtime discovery.

Add public tools/list coverage for all seven nonempty macOS configurations with built-in/custom workers, missing runtimes, and both hidden SQL providers. Update the owning documentation and regenerate affected canonical handshakes/dependent transcripts through the prescribed workflow. Retain necessary formatting in five Python fixtures; Python ASTs and rendered R programs are identical, and the complete formatter pipeline is idempotent.

## Validation

On clean committed b3066e7e, focused validation passed 25 cases (42 executions). Ordinary scripts/check passed companion staging, source/architecture checks, Rust formatting, Clippy with warnings denied, debug Rust tests, release build, and all 13 smoke cases (20 executions). Two unchanged scripts/format runs passed every formatter and produced identical final output. All 106 changed values across 13 existing recordings are descriptions; default/full handshakes are unchanged.

Commands run:

```sh
scripts/preflight
scripts/format
scripts/test \
  client_server/server/test_descriptions \
  client_server/server/test_languages \
  client_server/server/test_tools::initializes_and_lists_tools \
  client_server/server/test_presentation \
  client_server/output/test_previews::summarizes_empty_cell_after_oversized_startup_output \
  client_server/python/test_setup::cancels_native_inspection_and_retries \
  client_server/python/test_startup::interrupts_embedded_sitecustomize \
  client_server/python/test_startup::interrupts_embedded_pth \
  client_server/python/test_startup::interrupts_embedded_startup_after_r \
  client_server/python/test_startup::interrupts_sql_first_embedded_startup \
  client_server/python/test_versions::validates_registry_only_python_requirements \
  client_server/python/test_versions::resolves_python_version_constraint_semantics \
  --jobs 1
scripts/check
```

Focused tests and the final gate used invocation-only CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2, CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0, CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0, CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0, and PYTHON_CPU_COUNT=1; debug assertions remained enabled.

Native Windows generation/checks remain pending for:

- client_server/server/test_descriptions::builtin_visible_language_descriptions — tests/snapshots/client_server/server/test_descriptions/builtin_visible_language_descriptions.win32.yaml
- client_server/server/test_descriptions::custom_visible_language_descriptions — tests/snapshots/client_server/server/test_descriptions/custom_visible_language_descriptions.win32.yaml
- client_server/server/test_descriptions::missing_runtimes_keep_configured_descriptions — tests/snapshots/client_server/server/test_descriptions/missing_runtimes_keep_configured_descriptions.win32.yaml

Windows tests and assertions remain declared; Windows SQL remains deferred. Native Linux, exhaustive checks, current-head hosted CI, and hosted approval were not verified by this macOS run.

title: Fix Windows staging after native runner upgrade
description:
Windows source installation fails after #529 because staging selects `codex-windows-sandbox`, while the pinned runner now registers Console's setup and runner binaries in `mcp-console-sandbox-windows`. Select the Console package and update the public Cargo staging fixture to reproduce that package boundary.

Repair the Windows validation failures uncovered by native testing: resolve R batch launchers before spawning them, normalize both sides of the R interpreter-identity comparison, align the setup-required assertion with the pinned native diagnostic, prepare the plotting fixture's font cache, and regenerate the stale Windows configuration snapshots. Document the public setup command and the required version-6 provisioning refresh.

Validation on native Windows x64 with Python 3.14.5, R 4.6.1, and `LC_ALL=C`:

- Reproduced the source-install and public staging regression before the fix; `scripts/with-checkout.cmd uv tool install --reinstall --force .` now succeeds.
- `scripts/preflight.cmd` and unchanged `scripts/format.cmd` passed; all four formatters succeeded.
- `scripts/check.cmd` passed: embedded sources, architecture, Rust formatting, Clippy, 38 Rust tests, and 84 native acceptance cases.
- `scripts/check.cmd --full` exercised portable tooling regressions and all 208 applicable shared cases. It found four shared fixture/snapshot failures; 204 passed. All four repaired cases passed together without `--update`. Three Windows snapshots were regenerated through `scripts/test.cmd --update` and reviewed.
- `scripts/with-checkout.cmd python tests/windows_install.py` passed: wheel build, three copied-tool-command checks, 84 installed-wheel native cases, isolated source reinstall, and both R/Python startup smoke tests.
- `scripts/review-diff.cmd origin/main` and `git diff --cached --check` passed. The implementation change is one package selection; the rest is tests, snapshots, and docs.

Two elevated sandbox cases were skipped in checkout and installed-wheel acceptance: this host's existing setup marker is version 5, while the pinned runner requires version 6. Read-only setup inspection confirmed the helpers are available but provisioning needs an approved interactive `mcp-console sandbox-setup` refresh. No account or firewall provisioning was performed. Native Linux/macOS coverage remains with CI.

title: Report elapsed evaluation time and empty-poll status
description:
## Problem

Running responses did not show an evaluation's age or whether its latest observation received worker output. Per-call deadlines cannot measure a cell across polls, and empty previews can hide received bytes or omitted images.

## Fix

Retain one monotonic admission timestamp per evaluation and add an elapsed notice beside the existing running banner. Include `no new output` when the observed interval received no worker text or images. Admission age includes startup and preparation before execution.

Track worker activity in the existing output owner and capture it with finite response cuts, before decoding, redraw compaction, or image omission. Exclude server notices and native diagnostics. Control responses without output ownership report age without claiming silence; recovered responses retain their original notice. Preserve polling instructions, control/completion behavior, generation ownership, observation deadlines, and the complete 8 KiB text budget.

Update the runtime contract, public collectors, causal regressions, and generated transcripts. Regenerate the Linux loader snapshot through its owning native test, preserving the complete loader result.

## Validation

On clean committed head 5fc8ace4, native ARM64 Linux `scripts/test --jobs 1 client_server/r/test_loader::loads_native_libraries_from_selected_r_home` passed without snapshot updates. The same selector reproduced the missing elapsed line before its snapshot was regenerated with `--update`.

macOS `scripts/check` passed staging, runtime-source and architecture checks, Rust formatting, Clippy, Rust tests, release build, and smoke transcripts. `scripts/format` and `git diff --check` passed before commit.

Focused output, control, startup, recovery, and callable-client tests passed during implementation. Native Linux coverage is limited to the loader test; the full Linux gate, Windows, exhaustive checks, and hosted CI were not run in this repair.

Publication at clean Mac head `5fc8ace4d9105aa0ff3d97e9e409c0f69c07bf8f`: an inspectable same-head ordinary `scripts/check` passed, every `scripts/format` result passed, and fresh ordered gpt-6.1-sol/MAX then gpt-6-astra/XHIGH local reviews returned no findings. Native Windows checks/snapshot updates remain a separate follow-up PR by another runner; this Mac executed no Windows tests. Native Linux and latest hosted CI are unverified. This PR makes no Ready or all-CI-green claim.

Known native Linux snapshot gap: `tests/snapshots/client_server/r/test_loader/loads_native_libraries_from_selected_r_home.yaml`, owning `client_server/r/test_loader::loads_native_libraries_from_selected_r_home`. Requires native Linux supported regeneration and strict rerun; no golden was hand-edited. This remains a separate Linux blocker to merge readiness.

title: Include shared test support in Windows discovery fixture
description:
Windows CI on main stops in native test discovery because the temporary workflow fixture omits imported shared helpers (`support.checkpoints` is the first missing module). Copy the complete support package, excluding bytecode caches, so discovery exercises the real native suites without a stale dependency list.

Reproduced the failure from [main's Windows job](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37407646079/job/112088961443) locally before the fix.

Validation:

- `python tests/windows_workflow.py`: all 15 tests passed with Python 3.13.16.
- `python scripts/preflight --json`, `python scripts/stage-sandbox-runner`, and `python scripts/format` passed; all four formatters succeeded.
- `python scripts/check --full` passed: full core checks, native acceptance (85 tests), shared boundary transcripts, copied tool command smoke checks, installed-wheel acceptance (85 tests), and source-install acceptance.
- `python scripts/test WindowsSandbox.test_provisioned_network_restricted_input_and_interrupt` passed separately against the existing configured sandbox.

Validation used base `d03f2657` with this patch. Platform/capability exclusions were skipped as reported by the suites. The full checkout and installed-wheel runs skipped the provisioned sandbox case because its state directory was not selected; the separate focused run covered that case in the checkout.

title: Simplify oversized spill notices
description:
## Problem

Oversized-output notices repeat long paths and recording instructions, consuming the same 8 KiB text budget as useful output.
