Recorded images omitted during response composition need readable artifact locations, and very long paths can exceed the notice budget. The R adapter test also expects superseded wording.

## Fix

Use one concise omission notice with compact markers at later gaps. Share retained log/artifact locations and distinguish unavailable output and retained prefixes. Locations beyond 512 UTF-8 bytes use exact session/file paths explicitly relative to the Console recording directory. Sizing and rendering use the same notice within the unchanged 8 KiB budget.

Artifact locations are internal presentation metadata; raw recording, retention, delivery, image admission and public schemas remain unchanged. Update owning docs, public tests and focused snapshots. The R adapter test verifies the concise notice, exact readable log path and complete raw output while preserving budget, head/tail and ellmer forwarding checks.

## Validation

Passed on macOS: `scripts/preflight`, unchanged `scripts/format`, and ordinary `scripts/check` on the clean committed head. `testthat::test_local()` passed 21 assertions. `R CMD build` and `R CMD check --no-manual` returned Status: OK with zero test failures, warnings or skips.

Passed: `scripts/test client_server/output/test_notices client_server/output/test_recovery::long_recording_paths_keep_image_omissions_readable client_server/output/test_recovery::composed_image_omission_names_existing_artifact`. Coverage includes normal/oversized text, UTF-8/newline accounting, readable short/long locations, image-only/mixed composition, recording failures and consumed polls. Intentional snapshots were regenerated through `scripts/test --update`.

The stale R assertion failed locally before repair. Native Linux/Windows and exhaustive local validation were not run; hosted Ubuntu CI must rerun.

Passed local checks: `uv run --no-project --python 3.13 python scripts/check`.

title: Support interpreter paths containing spaces in release fixtures
description:
## Problem

Python interpreter paths containing spaces make the raw shebangs in generated fake Console and Rscript fixtures fail with ENOENT, before public release smoke and R_HOME syntax-validation assertions run.

## Fix

Use a shell/Python fixture launcher that executes the quoted selected interpreter, preserving stdin and arguments without PATH lookup. Apply it only to the three affected executables. Add a spaced-virtualenv regression through existing public cases and verify interpreter identity. Production behavior and packaging are unchanged.

## Validation

Reproduced both failures with Python 3.13.11 and confirmed regression red/green. Focused tests passed, including interpreter identity, empty-PATH probing and R_HOME selection.

Passed:

- `scripts/with-checkout /Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.13/bin/python3.13 tests/release.py`: 34 tests.
- `scripts/with-checkout '/tmp/oss163-execution-yh6pvukn/python with spaces/bin/python' tests/release.py`: 34 tests.
- `scripts/format` and `git diff --check`.
- `scripts/check` on clean commit `32df50cb`.

Validation ran on macOS. Native Linux and Windows execution were not covered. Hosted CI and review remain controller-owned gates.

Passed local checks: `uv run --no-project --python 3.13 python scripts/check`.

title: Supervise macOS sandbox process lifetimes
description:
## Summary

Supervise the full observed lifetime of the public macOS `sandbox` command. The launcher now manages foreground signal delivery, tracks descendants across process groups and sessions, limits inherited file descriptors to an explicit allowlist, and completes teardown before removing the command's temporary directory.

## User-facing changes

- Run a terminal-owned sandbox command in a dedicated foreground process group so terminal-generated signals reach it once.
- Relay `SIGHUP`, `SIGINT`, `SIGQUIT`, and `SIGTERM` sent directly to the launcher unless the signal was already blocked or ignored.
- Terminate observed descendants after the root command exits, including `processx` children that create another session, and wait up to five seconds for them to be reaped.
- Preserve stdin, stdout, and stderr while closing other inherited file descriptors at exec.
- Treat process-observation failures as launcher errors, attempt to stop the root process group and reap the direct child, and preserve the temporary directory when cleanup cannot complete safely.
- Document the remaining boundaries: signals have no timeout, stopped and continued job-control states are not proxied, and a descendant that orphans itself before observation may escape supervision.

## Internal changes

- Combine kqueue process events with libproc snapshots and identify processes by PID and start time.
- Keep an exited root waitable through descendant teardown so its process-group ID cannot be reused before fallback termination.
- Pass worker sideband pipes through an owned descriptor allowlist and change descriptor inheritance only in the child before exec.
- Keep worker shutdown separate: workers retain bounded root process-group termination and do not run the descendant tracker.
- Split sandbox acceptance coverage into policy, supervision, and terminal-behavior suites.

## Testing

- `scripts/check`
- GitHub Actions on `macos-latest` and `ubuntu-latest`

title: Render tool descriptions for each worker profile
description:
## Summary

Static package guidance accurately described the default managed worker, but it also advertised built-in language behavior and server-managed package preparation to configurations that do not provide them. Render the tool surface once from facts known before MCP initialization: worker selection, initial Python resolution, and operating-system support. This keeps the direct package workflow while making each advertised action match the selected runtime.

## User-facing changes

- The managed built-in profile tells clients not to probe package availability and to prepare desired packages through `session` before loading them normally.
- The inherited-Python profile describes direct imports from the active environment and the `prepare`-to-`restart` transition required after that worker starts.
- Custom workers advertise worker-defined language and package behavior, plus a restart-only `session` schema without requirements.
- Platforms without a worker runtime report that code, nonempty stdin, package preparation, and restart are unavailable while retaining server-state polling.

## Internal changes

- Store one profile-rendered RMCP tool router and use it consistently for tool listing, lookup, and calls.
- Carry the initial managed-Python result into bounded description templates and schema overlays.
- Keep separate canonical `tools/list` transcripts for managed, inherited-Python, and custom-worker profiles, with public lifecycle and unsupported-platform regressions.
- Synchronize the exact-description reference and current-state documentation. Worker execution behavior is unchanged.

title: Replace native macOS sandbox backend with facade API v2
description:
## Summary

Replace mcp-console's native macOS sandbox policy and outer process-tree implementation with the pinned sandbox facade. This preserves the current macOS worker boundary while moving policy enforcement and lifetime supervision behind the API that later platform support can build on.

## User-facing changes

There are no intentional user-visible changes. The `sandbox` command and worker runtime retain host-read-only access, a private writable temporary directory, denied direct network access, native terminal behavior, and the existing exit and status semantics. Linux and Windows remain unsupported, and golden transcripts are unchanged.

## Internal changes

- Add a thin adapter that constructs complete child environments, resolves executables, owns private runtime and launch directories, and validates the required macOS capabilities.
- Use a dedicated Tokio driver to bridge asynchronous process and pipe handles into the existing ordered relay writer and independently drained event reader.
- Map root observation, conditional termination, and complete retirement onto the facade while preserving worker deadlines, output draining, and cleanup error composition.
- Keep the relay inside the sandbox and keep the R, Python, and DuckDB resolvers on the host.
- Remove the local SBPL policy, direct `sandbox-exec` launch, outer `waitid` and process-group supervision, and duplicate retirement state.
- Pin the sandbox facade to immutable revision `855e8f9ef5b4211408791252e02e38b4757218cc` and align compatible shared dependencies.

The MCP, relay, and worker protocols are unchanged. Managed proxy networking and non-macOS workers remain out of scope.

title: Bound SSH controller liveness and retirement
description:
SSH partitions can leave remote workers and dependency resolvers alive indefinitely when the connection never reports EOF. Add independent bidirectional controller leases to the worker-launch and trusted preparation channels so either owner initiates retirement within a bounded interval after losing contact.

- Add `target.lease_ms`, frozen with the target: 30,000 milliseconds by default, with an allowed range of 1,000 through 300,000. Challenges run every sixth of the lease, or five seconds by default.
- Establish a challenge/response round trip before discovery, preflight, or workload execution. A versioned outer envelope keeps control messages out of relay JSONL and preparation messages, with bounded framing and flow control.
- Service expiry and input closure independently of busy workloads, resolver completion, partial frames, and output backpressure. Cleanup remains with the existing launcher and resolver owners; an expired lease or local SSH exit cannot replace their explicit cleanup receipts.
- Preserve prompt healthy shutdown, bounded local shutdown, and the block on conflicting preparation or replacement after unconfirmed retirement. Setup deadlines and `send.timeout_ms` retain their existing meanings.

This is the first of the two SSH lifecycle changes. Detected connection closure still requests immediate retirement; #305 adds reconnect/resume as a stacked change. Direct execution retains its existing descendant-cleanup limits.

Public acceptance coverage adds real OpenSSH stalls in each direction, worker and resolver retirement, discovery, busy evaluations, input prompts, output backpressure, and malformed lease traffic. `scripts/format` and the full macOS `scripts/check` passed. Linux lease cases and real macOS-to-Linux policy checks also passed; the full Linux repository check was not run.

title: Resume SSH connections within the same live session
description:
Allow brief SSH interruptions to resume the same remote worker and trusted preparation context while the local MCP server remains alive. Recovery preserves R/Python memory, admitted operations, output, and local session state within each channel's finite lease.

This is the second SSH lifecycle change, stacked on #304. Review its diff against `feat/ssh-liveness`.

- Keep each existing launch or preparation helper under a bounded remote owner while replacing disposable SSH attachments. The launch helper remains the sandbox runner's caller. Creation happens once; ambiguous startup can only attach to the original identity or fail with uncertainty.
- Authenticate attachments and every control frame with a private capability, immutable owner/channel/generation identity, and attachment epochs. Credentials remain in memory and private startup pipes. A private Unix socket provides the attachment endpoint; sandbox process and descriptor isolation supplies the workload trust boundary.
- Sequence input, output, diagnostics, and retained results through bounded replay windows with content identities and ingestion acknowledgments. Reconnection resends only missing bytes, including partial frames and terminal results, without repeating evaluations, stdin, interrupts, or resolvers. Larger outputs stream through the window with backpressure while leases and cancellation continue.
- Keep MCP responsive during recovery and defer new work while either channel is unreconciled. Existing controls retain their generation. Explicit shutdown stops recovery, and an attachment handshake never clears missing cleanup proof or commits an environment without its original completion and activation checks.

Recovery is limited to the same live server and its adapters. Expired or missing owners and integrity failures are terminal; uncertain code and installation are never rerun automatically. At-most-once dispatch depends on the original owner retaining its state. Direct execution keeps its descendant-cleanup limits, and independent recovery after runner death remains unsupported.

The change also fixes macOS descriptor readiness and child descriptor enumeration where they delayed attachment setup or blocked transport progress, and documents both channels, replay limits, lifecycle states, authentication, and retirement receipts.

Public acceptance cases cover real OpenSSH closure and directional blackholes, loss around acceptance, images and partial frames, retained resolver results, restart and interrupt races, controller death, backpressure, stale authentication, exhausted capacity, and sandbox attachment isolation. `scripts/format`, the full macOS `scripts/check` with the independent Python startup fix in #303, Linux SSH/core and Python SDK suites, and real macOS-to-Linux recovery and policy checks passed. The full Linux repository check and the reverse cross-host direction were not run.

title: Diagnose and repair intermittent prepared-probe frame truncation
description:
## Problem

Failed prepared-target attachments could cancel forwarding midway through an outer HELLO frame. The following retirement frame was consumed as HELLO payload, replacing the original malformed-probe diagnostic with a truncation error. A causal public regression reproduces this boundary; the historical failing mode remains unknown.

## Fix

Allow failed attachments to finish finite queued output before cancelling forwarding, with a one-second bound and immediate controller-loss cancellation. Preserve output diagnostic precedence and retirement ownership. Add malformed-mode failure context, optional peer frame receipts, and a native FIFO-gated public MCP regression that verifies original diagnostics, rejection before worker launch, no evaluation, confirmed removal and exactly one create/remove. Its generated snapshot retains full startup error and stderr.

## Validation

The public regression failed before repair and passed afterward. scripts/preflight, scripts/format, git diff --check and clean-head scripts/check passed on macOS.

Clean-head command: scripts/test --jobs 1 client_server/server/test_prepared_protocol client_server/server/test_docker_sandbox_provider cli/test_docker_sandbox_provider client_server/server/test_docker_sandbox_lifecycle client_server/server/test_docker_lifecycle::attachment_loss_retires_with_backpressured_output. All 22 available cases passed; nine real-provider cases skipped.

The default-concurrency run retained the previously recorded startup-prompt timeout in prepared_bootstrap_withholds_and_runs_first_cell_once (21/22 passed). Serialized passing coverage does not resolve it. Native Linux/Windows and real Docker/SBX coverage remain unavailable locally. Workflow-driver reviews, current-head hosted CI and hosted approval remain pending.

title: Replace Windows sequencing sockets with network-independent gates
description:
## Problem

Windows input, inspection, relay, and resolver tests used loopback sockets for ordering, tying ordinary sequencing to network access. The positive loopback test also counted asynchronous runtime preparation against its 10-second networking deadline.

## Fix

Use public stdin readiness for input/interrupt sequencing and private local named pipes for trusted host inspection, relay, resolver, and inherited-writer fixtures. Preserve explicit readiness/release, pinned process identities, bounded waits, cancellation completion, EOF, and retirement assertions. Add cancellation before resolver release, include the gate module in isolated native discovery, and reuse the runtime scenario for direct, restricted-token, and opt-in provisioned elevated sessions.

Keep the explicitly network-enabled loopback exchange and complete a public Python readiness cell before starting its networking deadline. Document coverage boundaries. Changes affect tests and documentation; production IPC and sandbox permissions are unchanged.

## Validation

`scripts/preflight --json`, `scripts/format`, and clean-head `scripts/check` passed on macOS. Focused public checks passed:

```sh

```

A temporary probe executed the existing loopback test against the real macOS runtime with discovery held at a FIFO checkpoint: the original ordering timed out; the repaired ordering completed the request/reply exchange. Python syntax and native selector discovery passed. Native execution was skipped on macOS.

title: Collect completed output in the no-R stdin validation regression
description:

## Fix

title: Own and retire resolver subprocess I/O with each materialization operation
description:
## Problem

Resolver subprocess reads and writes ran in detached threads. Early errors could skip their results, and descendants retaining stdout/stderr could leave successful materialization waiting for EOF. Process-stop success alone supplied cleanup confirmation; failed cleanup could hide the original diagnostic and leave exit observation unowned. Cancellable observation must preserve terminal-status evidence and keep Linux preparation working when pidfd_open is unavailable or denied.

## Fix

Each materializer invocation owns its child, non-reaping exit observer, cancellable endpoints and stdin/stdout/stderr tasks. Success, cancellation, interruption, registration failure and process/I/O failures share one retirement path. It cancels stdin independently, performs native process cleanup, settles observation, preserves collected output plus a finite queued tail, and joins every I/O task. Primary and cleanup errors remain separate until diagnostic formatting. Cleanup confirmation covers the invocation's native process scope and settled tasks; accepted interrupts retain their resolver attribution.

Unix preserves process-group signalling and the unreaped leader until observation settles. macOS confirms terminal status with WNOWAIT after readiness. Linux uses owned SIGCHLD notifications and non-reaping waitid checks, without pidfds or timed polling. Registration precedes the initial probe, only the observer thread unblocks SIGCHLD, and notification removal settles callbacks before endpoints close. Cancellation neither signals nor reaps the child. Windows preserves suspended creation, kill-on-close Jobs, confirmed-empty-Job evidence and its retirement allowance.

Managed R/Python/DuckDB materializers and Python inspection use the invocation owner. Public outputs, exception types, resolver policy and preparation-connection ownership are preserved; runtime programs remain embedded. Public regressions cover inherited output, blocked/failed stdin, diagnostics, interruption, failed cleanup, macOS terminal confirmation and Linux pidfd denial. The existing MCP post-exit interrupt test now gates owned observation. Supporting changes provide explicit fixture cache roots, regenerate an outdated startup schema snapshot, and document retirement evidence.

## Validation

At clean head 1afb072a014b1fee3a936b92a74b944b7c5196ae, 49 focused Mac cases (69 execution records), 27 native Linux cases, ordinary Mac scripts/check and native Linux Clippy passed. All four Mac formatters passed. The new public Linux regression first reproduced a live-child observation error under actual seccomp denial, then passed with EPERM and ENOSYS and an inherited blocked SIGCHLD mask. It verifies successful output, closed inherited readers, subsequent preparation and EOF. The failed-stop case verifies live-child cancellation with unconfirmed cleanup.

```sh

scripts/test client_server/requirements/test_custom_workers cli/test_resolve cli/test_resolver_io cli/relay/test_exit_observation client_server/server/test_startup client_server/python/test_lifecycle::interrupts_live_python_resolver client_server/python/test_lifecycle::restart_cancels_live_python_preparation client_server/python/test_without_r::failed_managed_preparation_preserves_worker_and_input client_server/python/test_without_r::shutdown_cancels_sans_r_python_preparation client_server/python/test_versions::recovers_from_python_version_resolution_failure server_relay/requirements/test_resolution::restart_consumes_late_r_preparation_retirement_events server_relay/interrupts/test_interrupts::control_only_interrupt_targets_blocked_controlled_restart_resolver client_server/requirements/test_resolver_sandbox::python_duckdb_uses_resolver_cache client_server/requirements/test_resolver_sandbox::r_duckdb_uses_resolver_cache
```

title: Close relay command admission at shutdown without renewing deadlines
description:
## Problem

Windows continued parsing and forwarding commands after Shutdown and could replace the first retirement deadline with a longer allowance. Unix left stdin admission open after worker-sideband EOF and could replace the earlier deadline on later control input. Source inspection established the Windows differences; no normal-client Windows failure was reproduced.

## Fix

The shared retirement policy closes command admission and retains the first worker deadline. Both supervisors enforce admission, stop explicit-Shutdown parsing, and ignore trailing frames and bytes. Controller EOF, worker-sideband EOF, cancellation completion, child exit and fatal failure remain distinct. Failed Windows sideband forwarding initiates retirement even when stdout is blocked, preserving direct-child reaping and terminal event ordering.

Protocol documentation explains the behavior and native sideband-EOF difference: Unix waits for the worker; Windows sends cooperative shutdown. Public boundary scenarios cover trailing work, repeated allowances, EOF, interrupt correlation and blocked output. The Windows fixture uses a channel to publish its stdin-EOF checkpoint before acknowledging shutdown. No MCP operation or wire format is added.

## Validation

On macOS/aarch64, scripts/preflight, scripts/test cli/relay/test_lifecycle cli/relay/test_backpressure (16 cases), scripts/format and git diff --check passed for the repair contents. scripts/check passed on clean committed head 849ffa59447cc5ea13cac1140455d3282c0a1c76, including staging, core checks and smoke transcripts.

A gated TCP checkpoint probe reproduced the ordering failure before the repair. PYTHONPATH=tests python3 -m unittest windows_relay.WindowsRelay.test_sideband_eof_closes_admission_without_renewing_deadline -v explicitly skipped on Darwin before and after the repair. Native Windows compilation/acceptance and native Linux acceptance remain unverified. WORKPAD.md records the disposition and validation.

Passed local checks: `uv run --no-project --python 3.13 python scripts/check`.

title: Extract resolver native process operations without duplicating control policy
description:
## Problem

Resolver process code mixed native spawning, interruption, and retirement with the shared control/result state machine. Its Windows Child/Job ownership lived outside the resolver component. This is an internal ownership refactor; no functional failure is claimed.

## Fix

Select resolver-local Unix/Windows implementations at the process boundary. Move native command setup, spawning, interruption, and retirement into those modules, including Windows Child/Job ownership. Keep shared control attribution, cleanup confirmation, exit-observer events/settlement, and result collection in one place, preserving caller signatures and Windows Python-inspection consumers.

The moved bodies retain Unix process-group signals, Windows suspended creation and Job assignment before execution, Job-wide termination and zero-active-process confirmation, and existing observation/reaping order and retirement deadlines. Other edits are imports, visibility, module wiring, entry-point naming, and ownership comments. Public behavior, diagnostics, preparation policy, and resolver I/O ownership remain unchanged.

## Validation

title: Make target-owner signal wakeups nonblocking and signal-safe
description:
## Problem

Target-owner processes handle `SIGTERM`, `SIGINT`, and `SIGHUP` by writing to a pipe watched by a cancellation thread. The watcher observes readiness but never drains the pipe. Repeated delivered signals can therefore fill it and block the old handler, potentially preventing cancellation and resource cleanup. The handler also changes the interrupted thread’s `errno`, and closing the pipe while handlers remain installed creates stale-descriptor and `SIGPIPE` risks during setup failures or retirement.

## Fix

Make the write endpoint nonblocking before publishing its descriptor or installing handlers. A queued byte permanently records the shutdown request, so a full pipe (`EAGAIN`) safely coalesces further signals. Retry interrupted writes (`EINTR`) and restore the interrupted thread’s `errno` before returning. The ordinary watcher continues to perform cancellation outside the signal handler.

Keep both pipe endpoints alive for the dedicated owner process’s lifetime, starting before the first handler is installed. This protects handlers across partial setup failures, watcher exit, and retirement-frame delivery.

## Validation

A native fixture deliberately saturates the actual wakeup pipe and injects an interrupted write. The tests exercise handler installation, provider creation, blocked output, and retirement; they check handler returns, preserved `errno`, resource cleanup, a single retirement frame, and retained provider diagnostics. Output pressure starts after evaluation receipt, so the blocked-output case exercises an admitted cell. Fixture failure tests cover installation checkpoint failure, retirement input closure, and retirement release; cancellation releases every gate and confirms the owner exits before workspace removal.

These are controlled failure-mode tests with a fake provider. They establish signal publication and cleanup behavior; they do not establish a reproduced real-provider outage.

At `c65e5b0182a182cea891018cbde0b1fd6a56a50a`, `UV_PYTHON=3.13 uv run --no-project --python 3.13 python scripts/check` passed on macOS, and local review found no actionable regressions. [Ordinary hosted review](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/461#issuecomment-5970642074) completed for this commit with a fresh thumbs-up and no unresolved review threads. [CI for this commit](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37159197612) passes on macOS, Ubuntu, and Windows. Native Windows and Linux execution were verified by those hosted jobs; this local runner is macOS.

title: Fix startup transcript completion races
description:
The Ubuntu main run at `80f9da25` failed three startup transcript cases because the tests treated an accepted nonblocking send or stdin submission as proof that startup had finished. The newer main run at `9d15213d` failed three selection cases through the same shared fixture.

Use the existing causal checkpoints and bounded public output collectors:

- Look up the UTF-8 test's recording session after the relay's processed checkpoint, when output has reached the tape.
- Wait for the deferred-selection bootstrap's exact interruption output before submitting the next R cell. An unspecified expected output can stop at a still-waiting stdin snapshot.
- Submit startup stdin once and collect the cancelled response's first-cell result to completion. Apply the same correction to the nearby R startup hook test.

These are internal transcript-test changes. Public behavior, production code, snapshots, and timeouts are unchanged. The UTF-8, stream-ordering, raw-tape, call-number, cancellation, bootstrap-preservation, and exactly-once assertions remain intact.

Validated on `6da03803c838456d57fe10d7db26c671def42e16`:

- All four assumptions reproduced before editing with controlled startup/input checkpoints using the existing native interposers. The fixed cases passed two controlled repetitions in direct and sandbox modes (16 executions).
- Four focused cases passed six ordinary runs in both modes (48 executions).
- The three affected suites passed all 45 cases and 89 applicable mode executions.
- `scripts/preflight`, all `scripts/format` formatters, and ordinary `scripts/check` passed.
- `scripts/test --full --jobs 6` passed all 872 applicable cases and 1,477 executions in 17m57s: 610 direct, 607 sandbox, and 260 without a mode parameter. Zero failures and zero unstarted cases; 81 cases were excluded by existing capability requirements.

Local validation used macOS, Python 3.13, prepared CI R environments, and Quarto. The full run used the runner's supported binary override with a verified copy of the installation bundle and a canonical temporary path. An earlier full run was invalidated when its active build outputs disappeared; `/var` versus `/private/var` aliases also affected two unchanged peer-runtime assertions. The initial affected-suite attempt with default Python 3.14 hit two fixture interpreter-path errors; the successful validation used the documented Python 3.13 selection.

Both inspected main runs are complete: Windows and macOS passed, and Ubuntu failed only the cases described above. Linux/Windows validation, external SSH/Docker/SBX fixtures, wheel/source installation checks, R package checks, and the exhaustive tooling gate were not rerun locally. PR CI remains the platform merge gate.

title: Add native Windows support for local unsandboxed R and Python
description:
Windows x64 supports experimental local `mcp-console serve --no-sandbox` with preinstalled R and Python. Either runtime initializes lazily, in either order, and each can run without the other installed. Persistent state, interactive input, plots, cooperative interrupts, restart, recording, and optional reticulate interoperability follow the shared peer-runtime coordinator.

Windows uses native pipes, process handles, and interrupt events. Python inspection starts suspended in an owned Job and confirms cleanup before accepting results. Packaging omits the sandbox companion and holds a blocking checkout lock. Relay framing, failure ordering, stdin failures, final-frame draining, and R startup path ownership follow the existing transport contracts. Empty Python selections fall back to discovery; retirement confirms concurrent process exit; queued MCP input drains before normal EOF shutdown.

Idle interrupts now wake the command reader. The coordinator waits for interrupt publication before dispatching the next command, preserving partial command frames and consuming idle interrupts before another cell. Windows acceptance covers idle interrupts, same-call interrupt-plus-cell requests, both runtime initialization orders, and delivery of stdin to the following cell. The existing Unix idle-interrupt case previously did not run on Windows.

### Scope

- Local execution requires explicit `--no-sandbox`.
- Windows SQL, managed dependency resolution (including `resolve`), sandboxing, and SSH/Docker/SBX controllers are deferred.
- R idle callbacks such as `later` are unsupported. Unsandboxed retirement reaps the direct worker; cleanup of evaluated-code descendants is not guaranteed.
- Windows wheels can be built locally; the release workflow does not publish them.

### CI repairs and validation

The failures in [run 37019556299](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37019556299) were traced to a Windows test assuming stdin readiness within 50 ms, Python path checks leaking `FileNotFoundError` instead of the intended environment-mismatch diagnostic, and stale traceback line numbers. The readiness test now polls to its deadline, path checks preserve the diagnostic, and four snapshots were regenerated with `scripts/test --update`. The older-Python fixture can explicitly select Python 3.9 on Linux as well as use the macOS system interpreter.

Latest `main` (`ea5c1e73`) is merged in `93fdaadd` without conflicts.

- Windows release build, 34 Rust tests, Clippy with `-D warnings`, runtime-source validation, four architecture checks, and Rust formatting passed.
- All five focused Windows runtime cases passed against the final production code. The full Windows suite passed 35/37; two fixture launches were blocked by host Application Control error 4551. Further relay checks encountered the same host restriction; those failures remain visible.
- After merging main, all five focused Linux cases passed in both direct and sandbox modes (10 executions): idle Python interruption, rejection of Python before 3.10, startup environment mutation, and Matplotlib setup failure/interruption.
- `scripts/format` ran unchanged; Ruff, Yamark, and rustfmt passed. Air is unavailable locally. Unrelated formatting changes were restored.

Both macOS and Ubuntu jobs in [run 37026627271](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37026627271) stopped on stale traceback line numbers from the Python runtime changes. The remaining three affected snapshots were regenerated with `scripts/test --update`; all three cases then passed in both direct and sandbox modes (six executions).

`uv run --python 3.13 --no-project scripts/check` passed in the isolated WSL Linux checkout with Python 3.13.15, matching CI. An initial run using Ubuntu's system Python 3.14 could not complete because the inspection fixtures' startup hooks were not loaded under isolated Python.

The [Windows job](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/37026627271/job/110902787310) passed, including native acceptance, installed-wheel validation, and source installation. Full macOS and Ubuntu CI validation of the corrected snapshots is pending.

title: Prepare runtimes without blocking MCP initialization
description:
Prepare runtimes in the background so MCP initialization, tool discovery, and pings do not wait for interpreter discovery, dependency preparation, or execution-target setup. The configured tool schema and descriptions remain unchanged.

Public behavior:

- Every `send` awaits the same retained preparation result before runtime operations. Worker startup and language initialization remain demand-driven.
- Cancelling a waiting call discards that call without cancelling shared preparation or replaying its cell later.
- Initial preparation failures remain available as bounded tool errors, while tools remain discoverable. Start a new server session after correcting the host setup to retry discovery.
- Connection closure and failed handshakes cancel owned preparation and preserve the existing resolver/provider retirement guarantees, including when initialization output is blocked.
- Launch configuration and applicable local native-policy preflight remain synchronous. This changes the default startup path and adds no configuration flag.

Internally, one background startup owner retains the runtime or failure and delegates preparation and retirement to the existing client, resolver, and target owners. A non-consuming input observer detects connection loss during preparation. Runtime recording starts after successful discovery, and response delivery retains its existing settling allowance.

Public acceptance cases use FIFO checkpoints to verify responsive discovery, shared-result cancellation, failure retention, and exactly-once execution. Runtime-selection and startup-failure cases await discovery through `send`; schema cases compare the configured interface before and after preparation.

title: Make Python startup hooks interruptible and retain platform snapshots
description:
Connect Console's input and interrupt services before running executable `.pth` files and `sitecustomize`. Startup hooks can request input through `send`, including embedded NUL bytes, and be interrupted without discarding the interpreter. Interrupted site processing and SQL adapter installation can retry; completed site processing is retained across later setup and R attachment.

The shared Python bootstrap defers automatic site processing, restores normal flags so child interpreters can load installed packages, and installs the evaluator after startup hooks so their customizations precede Console's module defaults. Already initialized interpreters retain their site state. Adds direct and sandboxed startup transcripts for input, interruption, retry, and framework Python.

Full snapshot updates preserve companions recorded on the other supported platform while removing obsolete local companions and explicit orphan snapshots. Adds a transcript-runner regression for this behavior.

title: Fix resolver shutdown ordering and restart checkpoints
description:
## Summary

When MCP input closes during managed preparation, queue relay shutdown and resolver cancellation before closing the preparation connection. Worker and preparation retirement then proceed together under the existing deadlines. The preparation owner stops admitting controls after its close request, preventing a late cancellation from writing to an exited host.

This fixes sporadic `Broken pipe` server exits during shutdown while preserving the cancelled preparation result and cleanup confirmation. The public shutdown regression forces an early preparation closer ahead of the relay write and verifies the exact shutdown, control, and close order.

The startup/restart test fixture excludes the main MCP driver thread from worker-mutex selection. Its untimed Linux condition-variable wait can have the same expected futex value as a contended mutex and occupy the fixture's waiter slot. The fixture retains the existing cancellation, worker-unlock, and evaluator-return checkpoints.

The runtime change affects shutdown ordering; the restart change is internal to the native test fixture. Transcript expectations are unchanged. Production review volume is 24 additions and 2 deletions, including the shared shutdown refactor.

## Validation

- The strengthened public shutdown regression failed on macOS and Linux with `close, shutdown, control` before the fix and passed after it.
- `scripts/test server_relay/shutdown/test_shutdown server_relay/restart/test_restart client_server/lifecycle/test_startup` passed on macOS and Linux in direct and native sandbox modes.
- The SSH preparation control and protocol suites passed on macOS alongside those lifecycle suites.
- `scripts/check` passed on macOS at the committed revision.

title: Move local resolution into hidden resolve subcommand
description:
## Summary

Move local host resolution into a dedicated, hidden `mcp-console resolve` child. This gives local preparation the same operation and cleanup ownership as SSH preparation while the server continues to own environment declarations, candidate commits, and worker generations.

## User-facing changes

The documented CLI and MCP behavior are unchanged. `resolve` is an internal subcommand omitted from help.

## Internal changes

- Exchange JSON lines for preparation requests, requirement manifests, operation controls, resolved environment data, and cleanup receipts.
- Capture local resolver choices in the child and keep it for the session, including across worker replacements. Custom workers open it when they first need host preparation.
- Preserve the local R home path and existing interruption and restart contracts. Update the CLI and lifecycle boundary cases for the new process.

title: Reduce parallel sklearn test work and wait for completion
description:
The scikit-learn transcript could receive a valid running response and assert the final output too early, as seen in the macOS CI failure on #384. Its model training also did more work than needed to exercise parallel execution.

Keep this regression small while preserving its process and data-transfer coverage:

- Use a constant classifier and 16 rows for grid search. Retain preprocessing and an input just over joblib's 1 MiB memory-mapping threshold.
- Synchronize each candidate's two folds with a blocking FIFO handshake and verify two distinct worker process IDs. Keep synchronization files in worker-owned temporary storage.
- Reduce the forest to two depth-one trees and the permutation check to one repeat over two features. Preserve exact comparisons with serial results.
- Submit these evaluations in the background and collect their complete output through the existing polling helper, within the test client's existing response budget. Preserve explicit process-pool shutdown.

This changes only the public MCP regression and its shared direct/sandbox snapshot. There are no production runtime, sandbox-policy, or public API changes.

title: Reject incomplete and invalid R cells before evaluation
description:
Reject incomplete and invalid R cells before evaluating any expression, so a complete prefix cannot change session state. Report the parser's message and source excerpt without exposing helper calls, invoking `options(error)`, or replacing `.Traceback`. The next cell starts fresh; runtime errors still retain effects from earlier expressions.

Cache a private `suppressWarnings(str2expression(source))` helper in R's base environment and evaluate it under `R_ToplevelExec()`. It returns `NULL` on success or a diagnostic string on failure; Rust writes the diagnostic directly. Preflight muffles parser warnings without changing warning options, invoking task callbacks, adding history, or updating `.Last.value`. Accepted source stays on the existing DLL REPL. Update documentation and public regressions for rejection, warnings, callbacks, and traceback preservation, and keep the smoke profile pointed at the renamed rejection case.

title: Allow concurrent validation across worktrees
description:
## Summary

Separate worktrees currently compete for one host-wide validation slot, so an agent running a focused test can block another agent's check. Let checks and transcript tests run concurrently across worktrees while retaining checkout ownership for each worktree's mutable build state.

## User-facing changes

- `scripts/check` and `scripts/test` no longer fail with `full-check budget is busy` because another worktree is validating.
- Concurrent staging of the same pinned sandbox runner waits for the shared source build, then stages the runner into each checkout. `scripts/preflight --json` no longer reports the removed host budget.

## Internal changes

- Keep the shared sandbox source lock through fetch, Cargo freshness checks, and artifact copying. Allow that lock to wait while checkout lock conflicts still fail fast.
- Update the public command tests and development documentation for concurrent worktrees. The MCP runtime is unchanged.

title: Restore managed input coverage in startup restart test
description:
Restore managed Python input coverage in the first-use restart regression, following #386.

Use `input()` again and queue the replacement text without its newline. The test must observe the exact restart notices, `[input requested: ""]`, and `[waiting for stdin]` before supplying the newline and collecting completion. This makes the waiting state deterministic without depending on input consumption within the notification grace.

Keep the checks that the old cell and its input are discarded, the replacement runs once with the correct input, and the old task cannot leak a cancellation error into later output. Regenerate the shared direct/sandbox snapshot with the restored notice and separate completion response.

This is a test-only change; public runtime behavior is unchanged. The restored notice assertion failed against the direct-read version, and all 30 focused startup and stdin executions passed after the change. All four formatters and the ordinary `scripts/check` gate (core checks and smoke transcripts) also passed.

title: Fix shutdown cancellation and restart-test CI failures
description:
Fix recent CI failures on PRs #381 and #383.

- The [Linux cancellation failure](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/36253636523/job/108436331137) came from the MCP library's EOF drain writing an already-cancelled tool result. Console now requires a live response reservation before forwarding a tool result. Responses that were not cancelled still reach the client during shutdown.
- The [macOS restart failure](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/36252515697/job/108433128034) depended on managed `input()` consuming queued stdin within its 10 ms notification grace. The test now reads stdin directly, preserving the exact replacement-input and old-generation assertions. Runtime input behavior is unchanged.

Add public regressions that hold a result until the server observes EOF, then verify cancelled-result suppression and ordinary response delivery in direct and sandboxed modes. The cancelled case reproduced the failure before the transport change. Update the shutdown documentation and regenerate the affected snapshots.

Local validation passed: 55 focused transcript executions, all four formatters, and the ordinary `scripts/check` gate (core checks and smoke transcripts).

title: Enable evaluation in generated transcript QMDs
description:
Generated `transcript.qmd` files now include a frontmatter comment showing `ir render transcript.qmd`. SSH, Docker, and Docker Sandbox transcripts no longer set `execute.eval: false`, so rendering replays their recorded cells. Previously the render command displayed only source for those targets. Users need to prepare the original files and environment because they are not copied into the transcript.

Internally, the QMD writer builds the shared frontmatter once. Tool descriptions and documentation now describe the rendering behavior. Public SSH cases snapshot generated QMDs for direct and sandboxed targets, and transcript assertions check the header across target types.

title: Extract worker coordination and shared input handling
description:
The embedded R backend currently owns the worker message loop and dispatch for every language. Move that coordination into a shared worker module with R, Python, and SQL adapters beside one another.

The coordinator owns preparation and cell dispatch, completion, shutdown, and failure handling. A shared input module owns stdin buffering and partial-line preservation. The R adapter retains initialization, native events, graphics, and console callbacks.

This is an internal refactor. R still initializes before readiness; the public interface, dependencies, and runtime behavior are unchanged. Existing transcript cases and snapshots are retained.

Part of the replacement stack for #317.

title: Reduce allocation work in bounded response previews
description:
Keep preview results unchanged while reducing allocation work for tiny output events and image-heavy responses. Rebuilding the retained text on each append and cloning images during text sizing can otherwise copy far more data than the response contains.

Compact text after bounded batches, append small writes into the current buffer, and count projected text without constructing content blocks or copying image payloads. Collection, recovery accounting, output ordering, and the 8 KiB result policy remain unchanged.

Add public allocation regressions for a 100,000-event stream and for text budgeting beside an 8 MiB image. The tests use the measurement support introduced with collection recovery.

Merge order: [collection (#318)](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/318) → [complete-result budget (#319)](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/319) → [allocation efficiency (#320)](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/320). This stack replaces #316.

Local validation: both new allocation regressions failed before the optimization and pass afterward. The full check passed Rust checks but stopped at an existing mixed-requirements checkpoint timeout; that case passed unchanged in a focused rerun. The full check has not completed successfully on this layer. Hosted CI has not been awaited.

title: Bound complete tool results to 8 KiB of text
description:
Apply one 8 KiB UTF-8 text budget after composing output, prompts, errors, and lifecycle notices. This keeps combined restart-and-cell calls and large error details within the same limit as ordinary output while retaining the beginning, latest tail, and active input report.

Add the final rendering policy and route server validation errors through it. Images keep their independent allowance, and raw-file retention remains separate. Client methods and tool arguments are unchanged; tool descriptions and runtime, Python, and target documentation explain the complete-result limit and where retained logs can be read.

Public regressions cover combined response regions, long prompts and errors, Python synchronous and asynchronous clients, the R ellmer adapter, and SQL previews. Update the existing collection and recovery assertions to the complete-result bound.

Merge order: [collection (#318)](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/318) → [complete-result budget (#319)](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/319) → [allocation efficiency (#320)](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/320). This stack replaces #316.

Local validation: the full `scripts/check`, focused budget regressions, and the R ellmer adapter assertions passed. Optional external SSH was disabled; unavailable platform capabilities were skipped.

title: Preserve head and tail output during streaming collection
description:
Large output previously stopped admission after a pending-output limit, which could hide the final diagnostic and suppress later images. Collect a bounded beginning and latest tail while continuing to drain output, and give images their own admission limits.

This layer retains up to 16 KiB of ordinary text with separately bounded control notices. Rendering adds omission markers and raw-file references; the following layer applies one 8 KiB budget to the complete result. Tool arguments and client methods are unchanged.

Replace the output tape with incremental UTF-8 decoding, terminal redraw projection, and typed response regions. Shared receipts keep omission accounting correct across delivery recovery. Empty receipts are released, fully omitted sources share one journal summary, and rejected-image markers coalesce. Active polls replay an unclaimed response before collecting later output; restart finishes its raw file before composing recovered intervals.

Public regressions cover collection, image admission, raw retention and loss, polling, cancelled delivery, allocation bounds on recovery state, and active-response replay. Keep repeated cancellation exchanges compact in snapshots after verifying every exchange, preserving all returned output.

Merge order: [collection (#318)](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/318) → [complete-result budget (#319)](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/319) → [allocation efficiency (#320)](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/320). This stack replaces #316.

Local validation: the full `scripts/check` passed, including the public recovery regressions. Optional external SSH was disabled; unavailable platform capabilities were skipped.

title: Return bounded response previews with retained-file continuation
description:
Superseded by the three-layer stack: #318 → #319 → #320. The original branch and commits remain available. Collection and recovery correctness, the complete-result text budget, and allocation efficiency now have separate review diffs.

---

Large responses previously stopped admitting output after the pending text or event limit, which could hide the final diagnostic. `send` now returns up to 8 KiB of rendered UTF-8 text across the complete result, including notices, with a preview of the beginning and latest tail. Small responses retain their content and ordering; images use separate limits.

Raw per-cell logs still retain up to 1 GiB. Preview notices distinguish rendered omissions, retained raw bytes, and bytes not retained in those logs, and identify paths in the Console server recording workspace on the controller. When recovered output spans many cells, fully omitted intervals share one summary pointing to individual file paths and counts in the session journal. Existing tools need filesystem access there to retrieve retained text. Tool arguments and Python/R adapter methods are unchanged; Console-owned retrieval remains deferred.

Internally, streaming collection replaces the pending-output drop latch while preserving response cuts, delivery recovery, lifecycle notices, and raw-file recording. Collection compacts in bounded batches, text sizing avoids image copies, and empty file receipts are published and discarded. Fully omitted intervals release their receipts after accounting for omissions, so recovery keeps bounded source metadata. Public regressions cover large lines, tiny-event floods, progress redraws, UTF-8, prompts, image limits, polling, restart, partial writes, adapter results, repeated cancelled deliveries, and allocation work.

`scripts/check` passed on macOS, including source and wheel installation. The SSH activation case also passed locally in direct and sandboxed modes. Localhost SSH coverage ran; optional external SSH, Docker, and SBX acceptance cases were unavailable locally.

title: Simplify interpolation in shell test fixtures
description:
Replace bare placeholder substitutions in nine shell fixtures with f-strings and named `.format()` fields so the inserted values are easier to follow. Keep shell quoting at each insertion and use named fields for the long launch command.

This changes only test construction; generated shell programs and public runtime behavior are unchanged. Retain replacements in R templates, where Yamark/Air interprets interpolation braces as R blocks, and in the YAML template with literal braces. Output normalization and deliberate edits to existing scripts continue to use `.replace()`.

title: Use a bundled Codex-derived sandbox runner
description:
## Status

This draft is a handoff, not a merge-ready implementation. Development and validation have stopped at the user's request so another agent can continue from the published repository state.

The detailed handoff is committed as [`SANDBOX_HANDOFF.md`](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/blob/use-bundled-codex-sandbox-runner-validated/SANDBOX_HANDOFF.md).

## Starting revisions

- MCP Console main: `50d2f5c613f382b1381447b64505e269262ff2a9`
- Codex sandbox patch branch: `mcp-console/sandbox-api/2161ec27`
- Codex sandbox API v2 commit: `855e8f9ef5b4211408791252e02e38b4757218cc`
- Intended Codex runner branch: `mcp-console/sandbox-runner-v1-validated`

## Work preserved

The intended design is recorded in the handoff: a focused private `mcp-console-sandbox` binary, protocol-v1 JSON launch specification over a private descriptor, native command arguments and inherited environment, direct-exec topology, unchanged relay and worker data planes, private wheel bundling, no Codex crates linked into MCP Console, and host-side R/Python/DuckDB resolution.

Raw recovery fragments from the prior implementation attempt remain on the [`codex-sandbox-runner`](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/tree/codex-sandbox-runner/.validation) branch under `.validation/`. The recovered transport is malformed and is not represented as an applied implementation diff in this PR.

## Publication blocker

The connected GitHub App installation includes `t-kalinowski/mcp-console` but not `t-kalinowski/codex`. Direct writes to the Codex fork return `403 Resource not accessible by integration`, and the attempted cross-repository publisher did not have a repository secret with Codex write access. The Codex runner branch therefore has not been created.

## Remaining work

1. Add `t-kalinowski/codex` to the GitHub App installation, or provide a fine-grained token with Contents write access.
2. Create `mcp-console/sandbox-runner-v1-validated` from `855e8f9ef5b4211408791252e02e38b4757218cc`.
3. Recover or reapply the focused Codex runner implementation and commit it.
4. Record that immutable Codex commit in MCP Console and recover or reapply the provider, packaging, test, and documentation changes.
5. Replace this handoff-only diff and body with the real implementation.
6. Run the requested Codex and MCP Console checks, inspect attributable CI failures, and leave the draft open for review.

Do not merge this PR in its current handoff-only state.

title: Document progressive config.yaml design
Compact proxy-enabled initialization handshakes in snapshots
description:
The proxy-enabled handshake in `retains_project_settings_after_edits.yaml` differed from the default sandbox reference, so it remained expanded. Add a canonical reference captured from a live proxy-enabled session and regenerate the affected snapshot as `!same-as`.

Add a runner regression covering repeated proxy handshakes after earlier transcript entries, and document the new reference. Exact matching still preserves changed and incomplete handshakes. These are internal test changes; runtime behavior and the MCP interface are unchanged.

title: Add x86-64 Linux support
description:
## Summary

This draft extends the current macOS implementation to x86-64 Linux through the pinned private sandbox runner.

## Public-facing changes

- Support `sandbox`, `serve`, the worker relay, built-in R, Python, and DuckDB execution, managed requirements, plots, interactive input, worker replacement, and sandbox-lifetime cleanup on Linux.
- Build and smoke-test a native x86-64 Linux wheel containing the private runner and its modified Bubblewrap companion. A system Bubblewrap installation is not required.
- Run the complete CI check on macOS and Linux.
- Preserve Linux-native Matplotlib configuration and cache locations and native non-UTF-8 target arguments.

## Internal changes

- Share the relay transport and worker stack across macOS and Linux.
- Adapt sandbox capability checks, PID-namespace process inspection, descriptor inheritance, Linux R loader setup, and Python fork-child output handling.
- Carry native Unix target arguments through an inherited argument file while keeping Linux target executable paths in the version 1 Unicode protocol.
- Make transcript cases platform-aware while preserving inapplicable goldens.
- Pin private runner release `rust-v0.150.1` to commit `b4de42be4e329fd6df06e6755b99f37f4a7ff5c6`.
- Build and stage the exact modified Bubblewrap companion expected by that runner, verify its compiled digest, statically link the selected libcap archive, and validate package provenance and license material.

## Linux requirements and limits

Linux support requires x86-64, kernel 5.11 or newer, and a host policy that permits unprivileged user namespaces.

The standalone `sandbox` command does not forward terminal signals or transfer terminal foreground ownership on Linux. Built-in console interrupts remain supported because the relay delivers them inside the sandbox.

Windows remains unsupported.

## Review slices

1. Transcript platform applicability and snapshot preservation.
2. Linux sandbox, relay, worker, language runtime, lifecycle, and acceptance tests.
3. Linux wheel staging, CI/release integration, provenance, and license verification.
4. User, architecture, protocol, and release documentation.
5. Deterministic shutdown, restart, and PTY transcript synchronization.
6. Native target-argument transport and the final private-runner pin.

## Testing

- `scripts/format`
- Linux core checks: runtime-source validation; 18 release tests; 47 library tests; 24 CLI tests; format and protocol checks; and all 17 sandbox-adapter tests, with the ownership-sensitive executable-search case run as the non-root fixture owner.
- Complete transcript suite in an Ubuntu 24.04 container with six concurrent workers.
- Complete R transcript suite twice with six concurrent workers.
- All 64 private-runner tests against the exact staged Linux runner and companion in privileged Ubuntu.
- End-to-end Linux regression for a non-UTF-8 target argument through `mcp-console sandbox` and the real staged runner.
- x86-64 Linux wheel build and smoke test.

title: Make the sandbox processx PTY test deterministic
description:
The sandbox processx PTY acceptance test currently reads once after the first readiness notification and then kills the child. This replaces that exchange with a finite shell child that consumes one input line and returns a prefixed response. The test collects output through EOF, waits for successful child exit, and shares the existing five-second deadline across reads and completion.

Terminal echo is explicitly disabled, and the response omits a newline so PTY line-ending conversion does not affect the expected bytes. The complete output is checked before snapshot serialization. R cleanup now has a local scope so `on.exit()` runs on failure. Capability requirements and snapshot organization are unchanged.

Only the acceptance test and its generated snapshot change; there are no public-facing behavior or production-code changes.

The final case passed 20 standalone runs and 10 runs alongside its suite on each of macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64. One-character reads passed; wrong or extra output, echo alone, nonzero exit, and an unfinished child were rejected with cleanup verified.

The full macOS `scripts/check` passed on the independent checkpoint. On the final commit, core checks passed, but the full run stopped when the unchanged `cli/sandbox/test_supervision::retires_processx_descendants_across_sessions` case timed out waiting for startup output; that case passed alone. Broader Linux checks encountered separate Quarto prewarm and relocated-bundle startup failures (`RTM_NEWADDR: Operation not permitted`).

title: Reuse staged sandbox runners on exact CI cache hits
description:
The staging step in [this CI run](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/actions/runs/34520178891/job/103015441053?pr=142) took 2 minutes 51 seconds after the macOS runner image changed from `20260831.0337.3` to `20260907.0351.1`. That image change correctly missed the native build caches. The preceding run reused cached build data and completed Cargo's runner build in 1.90 seconds. The step emitted 1,326 Cargo fingerprint diagnostic lines because the workflow explicitly enabled that logging.

Skip CI runner staging when both the finished runner and its build data are exact cache hits, and remove the fingerprint diagnostic setting. If either cache misses, staging still invokes Cargo and saves missing cache entries before tests. Requiring both hits preserves the weekly build-data reset and prepares the runner workspace for source-install checks.

The idle-callback acceptance test now waits for a server acknowledgement before submitting the next cell. Its worker-local checkpoint could become visible before the server received the output, causing a spurious missing idle-output separator. A relay fixture supplies the acknowledgement without draining the output; the exact snapshot is unchanged in direct and sandboxed execution.

Changes are confined to CI, test synchronization, and documentation. Runtime behavior, local source builds, cache keys, and the runner-image boundary remain unchanged.

`scripts/check`, workflow linting, all nine cache-condition combinations, and the complete callback suite passed. Pausing the relay reproduced the callback assertion failure before the fix and passed with the acknowledgement in place.

title: Document and test Linux sandbox policy compatibility
description:
Make the adopted Linux policy/backend contract explicit, and verify policy rejection through the public sandbox command so an unrelated native setup failure cannot satisfy a regression.

The compatibility and configuration documentation now distinguish default and explicit bubblewrap execution from direct Landlock execution, identify which restrictions belong to the native backend, runner integration, or Console defaults, and explain why networking does not grant filesystem writes. The filesystem table follows the pinned policy classification, including effective carveouts and same-target precedence. Landlock options distinguish omitted/null defaults from explicit lifecycle requests. The earlier host validation record is labeled historical.

The existing configuration suite already covered filesystem/network allow and deny behavior, explicit Landlock execution, denied truncation, private-storage rejection, and configuration transport. This change extends those cases and adds missing public executable coverage for full-write rejection, incompatible Landlock options and policies, the truncate-capability requirement, and supported bubblewrap carveouts. Rejection cases assert the intended diagnostic, an absent stdout start marker, and a successful public-command control. Native fixture mechanics remain in Linux test support; validation before native setup does not require a working enforcement backend. Existing snapshot records and deadlines are preserved.

There are no production behavior changes. The runner source and pin remain unchanged. Full-write supervision remains a separate feature: the native full-filesystem builder can omit namespace setup with networking enabled, and writable inherited procfs could expose the host supervisor; the existing guard preserves the integration boundary.

Reviewed and tested from Console main `27bb7cfc4f98c70bb9909917ee861108320f2706`, with runner pin `689f48c30deeb6aaa95a193e31e5971dd6820465` (protocol 2). Validation passed:

- macOS 26.6.2 arm64: focused configuration tests and aggregate `scripts/check`, including source and wheel installation checks.
- Ubuntu 24.04.4 x86_64, kernel `6.8.0-139-generic`, Landlock ABI 4: `scripts/check-core` (including Clippy and 47 Rust tests), CLI and client-server configuration suites, and CLI writable-root tests.
- The same Linux kernel in a privileged disposable container: default and explicit bubblewrap root-write policies enforced read-only and denied carveouts, and native Landlock policy-rejection snapshots matched. The host cannot run the nested namespace fixture. Read-only outer mounts supply root metadata targets without creating host root directories. A seccomp fixture separately makes the Landlock ABI query unavailable and verifies the specific truncate-enforcement diagnostic.

title: Verify sandbox bundles and Linux wheel dependencies
description:
Verify every file in the installed sandbox bundle before launch, including bubblewrap when a suitable system helper is available. Missing or modified bundled files fail immediately; intact bundles retain native host-helper-first selection.

Audit the wheel's main executable and both private companions for architecture, loader, shared-library dependencies, and GLIBC requirements, and check the wheel's declared platform tags against its metadata. Release and local builds use the same native GNU companion build path and existing runner pin.

Document build prerequisites, companion runtime libraries, and the separate full-runtime findings, including the ARM R error/interrupt issue and the deferred musl packaging and preparation blockers.

The macOS aggregate check and installed x86-64 GNU wheel checks passed. The Linux wheel was built with Zig absent from PATH and exercised actual R/Python/SQL cells, preparation, interruption, and restart.

title: Support private transcript test modules
description:
## Summary

Allow transcript suites to keep private support modules beside their tests. Suite discovery now ignores Python files whenever any component of the relative path begins with `_`, so helpers under `client_server/_zod/` are not treated as suites.

## User-facing changes

None. MCP behavior, transcript selectors, and golden snapshots are unchanged.

## Internal changes

- Split Zod fixture control, response gating, process observation, and shared helpers into private modules under `client_server/_zod/`.
- Keep every existing `test_...` case in `zod.py` with explicit helper imports.
- Add Python runner coverage proving that an ordinary nested suite is listed and executed while a suite-like file in a private directory is neither listed nor executed.

title: Synchronize plot, output, and shutdown tests with checkpoints
description:
Synchronize the plot-session isolation test with explicit FIFO checkpoints. Each worker signals after opening its plot device and waits for release, so the test controls completion order without assuming that a stdin reply has already been consumed.

Synchronize the accepted-shutdown test by holding the relay's output read until retirement joins it. This keeps the shutdown acknowledgment free to reach the server and replaces the timed pause of the whole relay. Check that the server lets the launcher finish without a retirement signal, while preserving the output and descendant-cleanup assertions on macOS and Linux.

Gate the partial-retention test's output batches on FIFO checkpoints and wait for the server to process each batch before collecting it. This preserves the exact retention and truncation counts without assuming a stdin reply has already been consumed.

Disable the unused Chrome apt repository before R setup in Linux CI and release builds. This prevents inconsistent Chrome repository metadata from failing apt update before the build starts.

The plot assertions still check separate plot directories and the expected PNG files in both direct and sandboxed runs. This changes only tests, fixtures, generated snapshots, and workflow setup; console behavior is unchanged.

title: Support Linux in no-sandbox mode
description:
Add Linux support through `mcp-console serve --no-sandbox` and `console_tool(no_sandbox = TRUE)`, including R, Python, DuckDB, dependency resolution, interrupts, restart, graphics, and recording. Linux does not provide sandboxing; unsandboxed worker descendants may survive server shutdown.

The implementation shares the Unix relay and resolver stack, adds Linux startup-closure observation and native R library lookup, and keeps Matplotlib caches private to each worker. Descriptor sanitation supports kernels and seccomp profiles without usable `close_range(CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC)`, preserving descriptor isolation, fork/exec safety, and spawn-error reporting. Restart prevents cancelled evaluations from leaking errors into replacement sessions.

Portable tests run directly on Linux and retain applicable direct and sandboxed coverage on macOS through centralized capabilities, explicit execution fixtures, shared native/process helpers, and shared snapshots. Regression coverage includes descriptor fallback, process retirement, exact failure diagnostics, and runner selection and snapshot updates. Linux packaging omits the private macOS sandbox executable.

Compatibility:

- The descriptor fallback requires mounted procfs when `close_range` returns `ENOSYS`, `EINVAL`, or `EPERM`. Linux process-observation tests additionally require inotify and pidfds (kernel 5.3+).
- Release wheels target x86-64 and ARM64 Linux with glibc 2.39+. Source builds use the host glibc. Managed R packages may require compiler and system-library development packages; see `docs/REQUIREMENTS.md`.
- Wheel builds require Maturin 1.15+; CI pins 1.15.0.

Validation: Linux core checks and all 339 applicable transcript cases passed, including 47 Rust tests, Clippy, and runner/client/release/architecture checks. `R CMD check --no-manual` finished with Status OK and five passing tests, with no skips.

Not verified for the final head: CI completion, native macOS checks, and wheel smoke checks. Execution on an actual older Linux kernel, native ARM64 Linux and Intel macOS wheels, and a native macOS sandbox-runner cache hit remain unverified.

title: Cache the built sandbox runner in CI
description:
Cache the staged private sandbox executable, licenses, and build manifest so CI can skip rebuilding the pinned runner on an exact cache hit. The key includes the OS, architecture, sandbox source and compiler pin, and staging script.

This is a CI-only change; runtime and packaging behavior are unchanged. Keep the existing Cargo cache for builds on a miss, and save the staged artifacts before Rust cache cleanup removes them. Successful main runs populate the artifact cache for subsequent runs.

title: Replace the built-in sandbox with the private Codex runner
description:
This PR is stacked on #150 and contains only the sandbox backend migration.

## Summary

- Replace MCP Console's direct Seatbelt and descendant-manager implementation with the private `mcp-console-sandbox` executable protocol.
- Keep the relay-worker boundary, direct stdin/stdout/stderr/sideband transports, public CLI behavior, and transcript output unchanged.
- Resolve bare target names on the host, then pass the absolute executable and arguments to the runner.

## Runner pin

- Codex release: `rust-v0.150.1`
- Codex commit: `a615297bb7fe61ec8b710623edae45524c381a67`
- Protocol: version 1

The dedicated runner branch required additional focused changes during integration. Those changes complete macOS observed-descendant retirement across process groups and sessions, control-loss and manager-failure recovery, terminal foreground restoration, failed-launch state reporting, and target-directory cleanup after a target removes directory permissions. Executable contract tests cover each correction.

## Installation and policy

The wheel installs the private runner at `libexec/mcp-console-sandbox`, with its license and notice under `share/licenses/mcp-console/`. It is not installed as a public command, searched on `PATH`, downloaded, or compiled at application runtime.

MCP Console verifies the exact release, source revision, protocol version, macOS Seatbelt backend, setup state, required capabilities, and empty companion layout before sending one launch request. The fixed policy maps to a read-only host, one writable target-facing temporary directory, denied network access, preserved terminals, direct target stream descriptors, and bounded `status`, `interrupt`, `terminate`, and `wait` operations. Runner state remains separate from the target temporary directory.

The obsolete SBPL construction, `sandbox-exec` launcher, relay startup gate, hidden sandbox-manager command, and duplicate descendant-supervision modules are removed.

## Validation

- Runner: 75 executable contract and native lifecycle tests; argument-comment lint; Clippy; locked release build; Cargo manifest verification; Bazel lock, build, and contract test; workflow lint; `git diff --check`.
- MCP Console: `scripts/check-core`; all 308 transcript/golden cases at the six-job macOS CI concurrency; 17 focused protocol-boundary tests; seven real native sandbox CLI tests; release-tool tests; `git diff --check`.
- Wheel: built with Maturin 1.14.1, inspected for private artifacts and executable modes, installed through `uv` in isolation, exercised with a scrubbed `PATH`, and verified not to expose `mcp-console-sandbox` as a public command.

Existing transcript and golden files are unchanged.

The focused shared Codex sandboxing suite reported 92 passes and two failures that reproduce unchanged on pristine `rust-v0.150.1`; both are assertions about stderr emitted by denied shell redirects and are outside this runner patch.

## Platform support

This PR preserves the current macOS-only product support. It builds and exercises Apple Silicon and Intel macOS wheels. Linux and Windows remain unsupported and are not expanded by this change.

The existing macOS observation boundary remains: a descendant that exits and reparents before the native tracker can observe it is outside the recorded lifetime.

title: Allow Python to select DB-API connections for SQL cells
description:
## Summary

- expose `console_sql_connection(connection)` in Python after reticulate initializes
- accept Python DB-API connections while preserving the managed DuckDB and R DBI paths
- execute SQL through DB-API cursors and reuse the existing bounded SQL preview renderer
- add a public transcript case using the standard-library `sqlite3` driver

## Testing

- Python transcript source compiles locally
- macOS repository CI pending

This is the next SQL-focused slice of the runtime refactor. It intentionally retains embedded R and reticulate.

title: Extract shared worker process services
description:
Move shared worker process services from `worker::embedded_r` into `worker::core`: sideband state, deferred operation routing, resolver exchanges, console/input/image publication, and shutdown/failure state. This establishes a shared process layer for future R, Python, and SQL peer runtimes and a sans-R mode.

The embedded-R backend retains initialization, the R event loop and DLL REPL, interactive input, interrupts, and language dispatch, including the SQL callback resolution gate. This is an internal refactor: public behavior, protocols, diagnostics, and runtime hosting are unchanged.

title: Strengthen the sandbox CLI process boundary
description:
## Summary

- make the server choose between the public `mcp-console sandbox ... relay ...` command and a hidden direct-relay development path without importing sandbox implementation details
- keep lifecycle ownership generic in server transport code and confine sandbox manager, policy, startup-gate, and private-directory state to the sandbox command
- add structural checks and public boundary workflows covering sandbox/direct substitution, startup failure, protocol independence, and process cleanup
- update architecture, relay, supervision, test, and user documentation to match the implemented ownership model

## Validation

- Python compilation and pytest collection for the added boundary tests
- `python3 scripts/validate_sandbox_boundary.py`
- `git diff --check`
- repository macOS CI on the published PR head

title: Simplify sandbox launcher exit observation
description:
## Summary

- replace the per-generation child-exit observer thread and channel with bounded `waitid(WNOHANG | WNOWAIT)` polling
- preserve non-reaping child observation so the process owner remains the sole reaper and PID reuse cannot occur before cleanup
- keep the public `mcp-console sandbox ... relay ...` boundary and relay stdin/stdout/stderr protocol unchanged

This is a deletion-focused follow-up: 31 production lines added, 90 deleted.

Existing boundary tests already cover public sandbox CLI launch, direct relay launch, abnormal launcher exit, stop/continue, restart, and retirement cleanup.

## Validation

- `git diff-tree --check 1b1aba68332b432ceaf55c6684f651d188bc474f 8c3541d64bf8e5a21e6133332a9cc2615469f711`
- commit-sourced structural source checks
- `cc -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2` waitid contract harness
- exact committed-content, mode, manifest, and artifact checks

Rust formatting/build/tests were not run because this environment has no `rustfmt`, `cargo`, or `rustc`. The macOS sandbox integration suite was not run because the available environment is Linux.

title: Cancel startup resolvers when MCP input closes
description:
Closing the MCP client during built-in startup currently leaves host resolvers running because environment preflights finish before the transport observes input closure. Watch pipe and socket closure during startup and cancel through each resolver's existing process-group cleanup path.
