A private startup guard preserves buffered MCP input, stops the active resolver, and rejects later resolver registrations after cancellation. Connect discovery, default R preparation, uv bootstrap, DuckDB preparation, and managed Python preparation to that guard. File and device input keep their existing EOF behavior; package defaults and startup ordering are unchanged.

Public server regressions cover closure during discovery and default preparation, including a blocked resolver descendant, and successful initialization with a buffered request. Document when startup cancellation is available.

title: Strengthen the sandbox CLI process boundary
description: Superseded by #215, which was rebuilt from current `main` without the temporary publication artifacts from the interrupted attempt.

title: Supervise standalone macOS sandbox processes
description:
## Summary

Make `mcp-console sandbox -- COMMAND [ARG]...` own the lifetime of the sandbox processes it observes on macOS. The standalone launcher now tracks descendants after process-group or session changes, preserves shell terminal semantics, closes unintended inherited descriptors, and returns only after bounded cleanup.

This is the focused standalone-supervision slice extracted from #150. It does not change the MCP surface or the server, relay, and worker-generation ownership model.

## User-facing changes

- Retire descendants observed from the sandbox root, including processx children and grandchildren that call `setsid()`. Cleanup first closes the root process group while its leader remains waitable, then retires identity-tracked descendants without losing the command's exit status.
- Preserve foreground terminal behavior for direct jobs and pipelines. Ctrl-C reaches the sandbox job once, Ctrl-Z stops both the job and launcher, SIGCONT resumes them, and a shell-created pipeline retains foreground ownership so peer stages receive terminal signals.
- Close inherited file descriptors above the standard streams for standalone sandbox commands. The generic server launch path still preserves the explicit relay and worker descriptors it requires.
- Keep the private sandbox temporary directory until all observed descendants are gone. Preserve it on containment failure instead of deleting files beneath a potentially live process.

## Internal changes

- Add a kqueue and libproc descendant tracker keyed by PID and process start time. Parent relationships are rechecked before adoption, fork and reap events update the owned set, and partially initialized tracker state remains available for cleanup when setup fails.
- Add peer-aware foreground terminal ownership and blocked-signal relay logic for direct jobs, shell pipelines, stop and continue, terminal closure, and post-root cleanup.
- Add public transcript regressions for session-changing processx trees, crash supervision, the root-exit fork race, tracker-setup failure, descriptor inheritance, Ctrl-C delivery, Ctrl-Z and continue, pipeline job control, and terminal closure.

## Scope and limitations

macOS has no unprivileged atomic descendant-containment primitive. A descendant that becomes orphaned and leaves the root process group before post-spawn observation remains outside this standalone guarantee; the README documents that boundary. Once a descendant is observed, teardown retains ownership across process-group and session changes.

After the root exits, cleanup is intentionally forceful, bounded, and non-interruptible so a second terminal signal cannot abandon owned descendants. Host-side launcher crash recovery, server worker-generation ownership, startup gates, and relay lifecycle changes remain in #150.

## Testing

- `scripts/format`
- `scripts/check`
- `scripts/test --jobs 1 cli/sandbox_supervision`
- `scripts/test --jobs 1 client_server/zod`
- The focused standalone supervision suite passed ten consecutive serial runs during review and was rerun after the final cleanup.

title: Supervise standalone macOS sandbox processes
description:
## Summary

- track descendants observed from the standalone `mcp-console sandbox` root across process-group and session changes
- keep terminal-attached commands in the shell-created job process group, preserving terminal reads, pipelines, stop/continue, window changes, status requests, and terminal interrupt delivery
- isolate non-terminal launches in a dedicated process group and retire that pinned group before observed-descendant cleanup
- close unlisted inherited descriptors before exec
- add focused standalone CLI transcript coverage

## Scope

This is the first standalone slice of #150 after #150 changed to a host-side sandbox-manager design.

It deliberately excludes:

- crash-independent manager ownership and launcher-crash recovery
- server and worker-generation supervision
- manager startup gating, owner recovery, relay changes, and broader protocol/documentation updates

Those remain in #150 as sequential follow-up work. After this PR merges, merge `main` into #150; the shared process-observation, descriptor, job-control, and standalone behavior should disappear from #150's diff, while the host-side manager and server lifecycle work remain.

## Size

The total diff remains below 2,000 changed lines.

## Coverage

- processx descendants that cross process groups and sessions
- same-group children forked immediately before a non-terminal root exits
- direct interrupt relay followed by descendant retirement
- closure of unlisted inherited descriptors
- single delivery of terminal interrupts
- foreground `Ctrl-Z` / `SIGCONT` job control
- background terminal reads stopped by `SIGTTIN` and resumed with `fg`
- foreground shell pipelines whose sandboxed first stage reads from the terminal
- `SIGWINCH`, `SIGINFO`, and `Ctrl-C` delivery to a foreground pipeline

Split from #150.

title: Bound macOS sandbox cleanup after supervision failures
description:
## Summary

This PR keeps macOS sandbox failure cleanup bounded and conservative when the manager or its owner cannot establish that the sandbox root will exit.

- treat only an identity-checked direct root signal as proof that tracker completion can be awaited; cleanup of an old PID-named process group is not enough after the root changes groups
- wake the existing descendant tracker into bounded retirement when direct root termination fails, so already observed and signalable descendants are still retired
- preserve the private temporary directory whenever cleanup remains incomplete and retain the group, root, tracker, and control errors that explain the failure
- exercise manager crashes, root-exit races, owner recovery failures, startup cleanup failures, and sandbox-owned preservation attempts through public transcript tests
- verify that a custom worker relay stays gated when its manager fails before readiness and that a replacement generation starts normally

There are no MCP, relay, worker protocol, or documentation changes. The observable change is that failed root termination produces a bounded manager error and preserves the sandbox directory without abandoning already observed descendants. Internal coordination now uses a one-shot kqueue user event to wake the tracker; the test fixtures use causal process and FIFO checkpoints.

## Testing

- `scripts/test client_server/sandbox_crash::server_crash_after_relay_exit_removes_temporary_directory`
- `scripts/test cli/sandbox_crash::manager_owner_loss_stop_failure_remains_bounded`
- `scripts/test cli/sandbox_crash::manager_owner_loss_after_root_group_change_remains_bounded`
- `scripts/test --jobs 6 cli/sandbox_crash`
- `scripts/check`

title: Gate worker relay startup until supervision is ready
description:
Split from #150.

## Summary

Prevent configured relay and worker code from starting before both host-side lifetime observers are ready.

- run built-in and custom worker relays behind the existing hidden `sandbox-target` startup gate
- attach the server-owned observer and wait for the independent manager to adopt the temporary directory and report readiness before releasing the relay
- preserve the existing ownership model: the server owns normal retirement, and the manager owns cleanup after abrupt server loss

## User-facing behavior

If manager startup fails before readiness, the blocked relay root is retired without executing configured relay or worker code. A later request can start a fresh worker generation.

This changes startup ordering only. It does not change the relay protocol, terminal job control, or retirement ownership.

## Internal changes

- carry only the private startup gate across `sandbox-exec`, then close it before relay exec so no nonstandard descriptor reaches relay code
- retain the same gated root process identity when the wrapper executes the configured relay
- split sandbox command construction, spawn, and child retirement into focused modules
- document the startup ordering and remaining Darwin observation boundary

## Limitations

A server exit before manager readiness can still leave the owner-created temporary directory behind. After readiness, a later descendant that becomes orphaned before an observer resolves its fork event remains outside that observer's cleanup guarantee.

## Testing

- `scripts/check-core`
- `scripts/test --jobs 6`
- `scripts/test --jobs 6 client_server/sandbox_startup client_server/descriptors client_server/sandbox_crash client_server/sandbox_supervision cli/sandbox_crash`
- five consecutive reruns of `client_server/sandbox_startup::manager_failure_before_readiness_keeps_custom_relay_gated`

title: Separate the worker facade from the embedded-R backend
description:
## Summary

Separate the crate-facing worker API from the current embedded-R runtime implementation. `src/worker.rs` now selects the platform backend and exposes the callbacks used by the binary and language bridges, while `src/worker/embedded_r.rs` owns the R main-thread event loop, cell dispatch, console callbacks, resolver callbacks, and mixed-language runtime state.

This gives a later built-in worker backend a stable integration point without changing existing callers or runtime behavior.

## User-facing changes

None. This PR does not add a no-R mode, change runtime initialization or threading, move Python or SQL to another process, expand platform support, or change the worker and relay protocols.

## Internal changes

- move the embedded-R implementation behind the worker facade while preserving initialization order, runtime ownership, resolver callbacks, graphics, stdin, and interrupt behavior
- keep macOS backend selection and the existing unsupported-platform error in the facade
- update the repository map for the new source boundary
- publish the Zod callback marker atomically so parallel tests cannot observe a partial response
- make idle-input and DuckDB progress transcripts follow the public polling contract instead of depending on scheduler timing
- reuse the host IR cache in the managed-uv test while continuing to isolate reticulate's managed environment

title: Export SQL documentation source snapshot
description: Temporary CI-only PR used to export authoritative tool-description sources for the SQL DB-API slice. This PR will not be merged.

title: Generate SQL DB-API transcript fixture
description: Temporary CI-only PR used to run the repository transcript harness in `--update` mode and upload the generated SQL DB-API golden fixture. This PR will not be merged.

title: Allow selecting a DBI connection for SQL cells
description:
## Summary

Allow R code to select a caller-owned DBI connection for subsequent SQL cells while retaining the managed in-memory DuckDB connection as the default.

## User-facing changes

- `console_sql_connection(connection)` selects any valid `DBIConnection` for later `send(sql = ...)` calls.
- `console_sql_connection()` and `sql_connection()` return the active connection.
- `console_sql_connection(NULL)` restores the managed DuckDB connection without discarding its existing catalog.
- Query results from custom DBI backends use the existing bounded SQL preview renderer.
- The caller continues to own the custom connection and is responsible for disconnecting it.

## Compatibility and scope

- The managed DuckDB path retains its existing Arrow query path, persistent catalog, R data-frame scanning, extensions, preview format, and interrupt behavior.
- Custom connections use generic DBI query and statement execution; DuckDB-specific environment scanning and relation registration do not transfer to other backends.
- This slice does not change embedded R, reticulate, Python ownership, runtime threading, or dependency requirements for the built-in worker.

## Testing

A public transcript selects an in-memory RSQLite connection, executes DDL and DML, previews `SELECT` and `INSERT ... RETURNING` results, restores the managed DuckDB connection, and verifies that its earlier catalog remains intact.

The branch is one commit and changes only the SQL bridge and its public transcript coverage.

title: Retire observed descendants after standalone sandbox exit
description:
## Summary

Extract the next coherent slice from #150: normal root-exit supervision for the standalone macOS `mcp-console sandbox` command.

- Retire descendants observed from the sandbox root after that root exits, including descendants that moved into another process group or session.
- Identify tracked processes by PID plus process start time so PID reuse cannot redirect cleanup to an unrelated process.
- Preserve the direct command's exit status and remove its private temporary directory only after successful descendant retirement.
- Keep partial tracker state on setup or observation failure and perform bounded best-effort retirement of every identity already observed before returning the error.

## Scope boundary

This PR intentionally does **not** add:

- crash-surviving manager ownership;
- launcher signal forwarding or terminal job-control changes;
- server/relay worker-generation integration; or
- supervision for generic `SandboxedCommand::spawn()` callers.

Darwin does not provide an atomic child-subtree observer at spawn time. A descendant that becomes orphaned before the post-spawn root watch or a corresponding fork event is observed remains outside this guarantee. That limitation is recorded in the implementation and README rather than hidden behind additional manager or terminal machinery.

## Test-first verification

The first commit adds the public transcript regressions before production code. Its CI run passed core checks, Python packaging, and the R package check, then failed only in the transcript suite because current `main` allowed the detached descendants to survive.

The implementation commit makes the full macOS workflow pass, including:

- nested `processx` descendants that enter separate sessions;
- a `processx` crash supervisor and supervised child outside the root process group;
- direct-command exit-status preservation, including inherited ignored `SIGCHLD`; and
- temporary-directory removal after successful retirement.

## Size

10 files; 1,039 additions and 6 deletions. The production tracker is split into process identity, tree observation, event tracking, and bounded retirement modules to keep later manager integration from requiring another structural move.

title: Use causal synchronization in load-sensitive tests
description:
## Summary

Several macOS lifecycle and transcript tests assumed asynchronous resolver or worker work would reach a specific state within one short wait. Under host contention, the runtime correctly remained active, but the tests failed before reaching the behavior they meant to verify.

This replaces schedule-based readiness checks with causal FIFO checkpoints and bounded polling of the public console result. Runtime behavior and production timeout and cleanup bounds are unchanged.

## User-facing changes

None. This changes test fixtures and transcript collection only.

## Internal changes

- Publish resolver process-group records before signaling FIFO checkpoints, and use explicit lifetime gates instead of fixed sleeps in CLI and Zod fixtures.
- Prove the resolver descendant exists before its leader exits.
- Preserve per-response output cuts across valid running polls for ordinary R output. Keep native DuckDB redraws in one bounded response; the Zod fixture snapshots compaction across poll boundaries.
- Preserve partial output from the code-bearing call in the fd-0 ordering transcript.
- Force the Python stdin-routing transcript through its documented provisional input state, then poll the public result within a bound.
- Observe the actual outer relay `killpg` fail-safe through a FIFO, then bound restart response completion from that causal checkpoint.
- Read the Zod SIGINT-denial record directly after the causal error responses.

## Scope and validation

The original failures were reproduced under the default 16-way local load. The repaired cases passed repeated stress runs: 32 Python shutdown cases, 32 resolver-descendant cleanup cases, 16 R preparation cases, 32 partial-stdin cases, eight native DuckDB progress cases, and 32 mixed Zod permission cases. The Python stdin regression also passed 16 concurrent focused runs while forcing the provisional response.

The complete `scripts/check` passes at the default local concurrency after merging current `main`. No production source changed; generated goldens record the deterministic zero-timeout Python input call and the single bounded native-progress response.

title: Collapse progress-bar redraws
description:
Fast progress bars can emit many carriage-return redraws. Returning every frame consumes client context and can displace the result that follows. This change keeps the common DuckDB progress-bar case from placing every redraw in one client response.

## User-facing changes

- Within each delivered output segment, collapse consecutive redraws from the same console output, diagnostic, stdout, or stderr stream.
- Treat bare carriage return as whole-line replacement and backspace as removal of one Unicode scalar. Preserve CRLF as a newline and preserve other controls and escape sequences literally.
- Keep response boundaries explicit. A long-running cell may return one current progress frame in each poll.
- Apply the existing pending-output limits before compaction. A truncated segment may omit its final redraw.

## Internal changes

- Apply redraw projection while assembling a response instead of retaining terminal state across polls and worker generations.
- Preserve the existing raw-stream decoding, ordering, lifecycle, and pending-output accounting.

## Testing

- `scripts/check`

title: Split environment orchestration into focused modules
description:
## Summary

`worker_client::environment` had accumulated retained environment state, requirement merging, host resolution, preparation, and runtime activation. This splits those responsibilities into focused submodules while keeping `environment.rs` as the internal façade.

The split gives further environment work narrower ownership boundaries without changing the existing lifecycle and response contracts.

## User-facing changes

None. MCP schemas, tool descriptions, worker and relay messages, resolver inputs, runtime output, error text, documentation, and transcript goldens are unchanged.

## Internal changes

- Moves retained state, requirement calculations, host resolution, preparation, and runtime R and Python activation into separate modules.
- Keeps preparation as one lock-sensitive transaction and preserves lock acquisition, resolver-handle, generation-check, and commit ordering.
- Retains the existing `worker_client::environment` imports through narrow re-exports and limits sibling helpers to the environment subtree.

title: Fix managed Python subprocesses after live resolution
description:
## Summary

Managed Python subprocesses now use the environment activated during live package resolution. Reticulate refreshes its import paths during activation, but `sys.executable` and an already-imported multiprocessing launcher could still point to the original environment. Spawned workers could then miss packages resolved in the parent.

On macOS, psutil now enumerates the relay generation's dedicated process group. The sandbox continues to deny the host-wide `kern.proc.all` query while process-backed libraries can discover their descendants for cleanup. The runtime patches only the installed psutil distribution, leaving project-local or custom modules with the same name untouched. An ordinary failure anywhere in the runtime's optional psutil probe or setup no longer turns an otherwise successful activation into a resolution failure, and automatically resolved psutil is retried after module load.

## User-facing changes

- Process-backed Python libraries can import packages added after Python initialization, including when multiprocessing was imported before resolution.
- psutil's default process enumeration and recursive child discovery operate within the relay process group.
- Project-local `psutil` modules are not imported during runtime bootstrap and retain normal Python import behavior.
- A transient failure during the optional psutil probe does not discard an activated environment or leave a subsequent successful psutil import unconfigured; resolved packages remain retained across restart.
- Live activation continues to preserve the existing Python and R session state.

## Internal changes

- Refresh `sys.executable` and multiprocessing's cached executable after reticulate activates a managed environment.
- Match the resolved psutil module origin to the installed distribution before applying the macOS process-group adapter.
- Run the complete optional psutil adapter through one ordinary-exception boundary during bootstrap and live activation, while leaving executable and multiprocessing refresh failures fatal.
- Wrap the automatically resolved psutil loader to rerun the adapter after module execution while preserving the module's original loader metadata.
- Replace psutil's macOS platform PID enumeration with `proc_listpgrppids(os.getpgrp())` while retaining its sorted public wrapper.
- Keep the host-wide `kern.proc.all` query denied.
- Make resolver-interrupt and user-selected-Python transcript output stable across host Python versions.
- Isolate the automatic R resolution test from ambient user packages.
- Flush the Zod fixture's completion frame before releasing background sideband output.
- Add public transcript regressions for live-resolved joblib workers, cached spawn launchers, global process-table denial, process-group-scoped psutil child discovery, local-module precedence, and optional psutil probe failure with immediate process APIs and restart retention.

title: Allow evals to limit send languages
description:
## Summary

Add an internal `MCP_CONSOLE_LANGUAGES` environment setting so eval runs can expose only the languages they are intended to exercise without adding a CLI option or broader public API.

The setting accepts a comma-separated subset of `r`, `python`, and `sql`. Disabled fields are omitted from the registered `send` schema and rejected before worker dispatch.

## User-facing changes

Default behavior is unchanged when the setting is absent. This adds no CLI argument or public documentation, and leaves `session`, requirements, polling, and stdin behavior unchanged.

## Internal changes

- Build the registered tool router from the configured language subset at server startup.
- Apply the same subset when admitting code cells.
- Cover schema filtering and disabled-cell rejection through the public MCP transcript test.

title: Resolve missing Python imports on demand
description:
## Summary

The built-in managed Python environment now resolves missing imports on demand. This removes the need to predeclare the common case while keeping explicit requirements for versions, extras, markers, ambiguous namespaces, and import-to-distribution mismatches that cannot be inferred safely.

When a curated mapping selects a differently named PyPI distribution, the server reports that mapping so users can see what satisfied the import.

## User-facing changes

- Missing imports trigger managed package resolution only after Python's normal import finders fail.
- Curated mappings cover common import-to-distribution differences, with conservative same-name inference otherwise.
- Differently named inferred distributions emit a bounded server notice; same-name inference remains silent.
- Successful activations continue the original import without replaying the cell and remain available across later cells and restarts.
- Actionable errors explain when to use `requirements.python`, including exact `from package import missing` lookups, selected interpreters, standard-library gaps, background threads, and fork children.
- Public documentation and tool descriptions explain the lifecycle, trust boundary, timeouts, interruption, and recovery behavior.

## Internal changes

- Reuses reticulate's additive manifest and the existing `ResolvePython` and `PythonActivated` path; no protocol variants were added.
- Carries validated import/distribution metadata with the provisional environment and emits the notice only when that environment is committed for the active worker generation.
- Routes notices through the ordered, bounded output path so partial console text is delimited and a notice is either retained whole or omitted at the output limit.
- Keeps resolution on the configuring worker thread and prevents reentrant, fork-child, and background-thread callbacks into R.
- Adds public transcript coverage for inference, activation, mapped notices, output limits, state preservation, failure, timeout, interruption, and restart ownership.
- Replaces a timing-sensitive cancelled-response test step with an input-transport barrier.
- Installs the official CRAN macOS gettext bundle in CI because a source-built `data.table` needs `libintl.h` in R's build prefix.

title: Constrain managed Python host resolution
description:
## Summary

Managed Python dependency resolution intentionally runs outside the worker sandbox, so worker-controlled resolver settings, source references, and interpreter selectors must not configure the host process. This change makes the server own resolver configuration, limits managed Python package inputs to named registry requirements, limits version inputs to supported specifiers, and restores exact decoding for payload-free protocol messages.

## User-facing changes

- Managed Python accepts named PEP 508 requirements with extras, version specifiers, and environment markers. Paths, file URLs, editable requirements, direct references, and local archives or projects now fail before a resolver starts with an actionable error.
- Worker-originated managed Python version requests accept version numbers and supported PEP 440 comparison specifiers. Interpreter paths, executable names, and installation directories fail before a host resolver starts.
- A nonempty user-selected `RETICULATE_PYTHON` remains selected. Managed Python additions through prepare, restart, or worker-originated resolver requests fail instead of replacing it.
- Managed Python resolution uses the server's startup `UV_*` configuration with `UV_OFFLINE` removed. Changes made by evaluated code stay in the worker and cannot configure the host resolver.

## Internal changes

- Removes worker-supplied environment maps from Python environment- and version-resolution protocol requests.
- Represents managed and user-selected Python policies explicitly. Managed Python resolvers use the current retained R library, or the new R candidate when R and Python commit together before worker startup or restart.
- Uses `pep508_rs` for the named-registry policy and its PEP 440 parser for supported version constraints, validating explicit and runtime requests before resolution.
- Makes every payload-free worker, relay, and Python-preparation message reject unknown or obsolete fields while preserving its existing JSON encoding.
- Keeps validation coverage behind the public console interface and updates fixtures, transcripts, protocol documentation, tool descriptions, and repository guidance to match the implemented contract.

## Notes

The public tool shape is unchanged. R requirements retain IR-owned parsing and `IR_NO_LOCAL_SOURCES`, and custom-worker Python policy remains separate from user-selected Python policy.

title: Include post-completion output in cell responses
description:
## Summary

A worker can report that a cell completed before its stdout and stderr have reached the server's output tape. This adds a one-millisecond server-side grace period before the server records the completed response boundary.

## User-facing changes

- Cell responses now include stdout, stderr, and idle callback output that reaches the tape during the completion grace period.
- Output published after that boundary remains pending for the next response.

## Internal changes

- Adds an asynchronous completion-grace phase to the server-owned evaluation lifecycle.
- Records the output-tape checkpoint after the grace period without changing the relay or its protocol.
- Extends deterministic server-relay transcripts and updates idle-input transcripts for the new response boundary.

title: Coalesce immediately available relay output
description:
## Summary

Small fd 1 and fd 2 writes can become one flushed JSONL frame per kernel read, adding substantial relay overhead. This change collects bytes that are already available after each readiness notification, up to the existing 8 KiB cap, and emits one event for that bounded burst.

## User-facing changes

- Bursty raw standard output and standard error use fewer internal relay frames and reach responses with less transport overhead.
- There is no API or schema change. Byte content, per-stream order, UTF-8 handling, and operation-result boundaries remain unchanged.
- Standard output and standard error remain independent pipes with no cross-stream chronology guarantee. Accumulating one ready stream can make their observed interleaving coarser.

## Internal changes

- The output readers drain only immediately available bytes into each capped batch. They do not line-buffer, wait for later bytes, or use a timer.
- Retirement drainage uses the same batching path, so pending bytes still drain completely before stream-closure and process-outcome events.
- A macOS process-boundary regression performs 200,000 small writes containing newline-free text, carriage returns, valid UTF-8, split UTF-8 scalars, and invalid bytes. It reconstructs each stream exactly and bounds aggregate JSONL overhead without asserting kernel read boundaries.
- The browser-input transcript prequeues debugger commands so it does not assume they are consumed within the 10 ms input-request grace.
- The relay and worker protocol documents now describe the batching contract.

## Measurements

Across five repetitions of the 200,000-write, 470,000-byte workload, `origin/main` emitted a median 33,075 output frames and 1,716,944 JSONL bytes (3.65 times the raw payload). The changed reader emitted 7,566 frames and 889,224 JSONL bytes (1.89 times the raw payload). Median latency to `completed` fell from 103.0 ms to 96.3 ms, and complete retirement drainage fell from 105.7 ms to 99.2 ms.

The 8 KiB cap also performed better than 4 KiB on a larger concurrent variant, while 16 KiB showed no consistent gain and doubled the maximum burst size.

title: Discard superseded worker environment commits during restart
description:
## Summary

A worker can serialize a preparation result or managed-Python activation before ordered retirement while semantic dispatch is blocked by replacement resolution. Once restart committed that replacement and changed the lifecycle generation, the old event was treated as a worker failure. An intentional exit could then appear as a crash diagnostic.

This change records a typed commit disposition for the retiring generation. A restart that reuses the retained environment still commits successful pre-marker environment events. A restart that already committed a newly resolved environment validates and discards successful old-generation commits instead. Worker-reported preparation failures and protocol, resolver, and environment-commit failures remain failures. Post-marker tombstones keep their existing behavior.

## User-facing changes

- Replacement restart no longer reports a spurious worker exit for a normal old-generation preparation or managed-Python activation.
- The replacement requirements remain retained, while a superseded preparation receives its existing restart-cancellation response.

## Internal changes

- Lifecycle state now carries an explicit disposition for semantic commits from the retiring generation.
- Deterministic public regressions cover a real managed worker's `python_activated` event and an R preparation result serialized before ordered retirement.
- The flat relay protocol, parse-and-enqueue reader, operation-result ordering, and post-marker retirement behavior are unchanged.

title: Clarify worker response and preparation boundaries
description:
## Summary

Clarifies four worker-boundary review points from #106 without changing runtime behavior or protocol events.

- Renames the transient worker snapshot internals to describe an idle-response boundary.
- Documents stdin as one generation-long byte stream, including newline, payload, EOF, and retirement semantics.
- Separates server-owned Python environment resolution from worker-owned reticulate materialization and activation, and defines `python_prepared` as the explicit worker operation result.
- Renames the malformed-sideband transcript and records cross-source canonicalization as structured harness metadata while retaining its losslessness, exact-once, per-stream-order, and lifecycle-notice assertions.

## User-facing changes

The README and protocol documents now describe the existing stdin and Python preparation contracts more precisely. Runtime behavior and protocol event names are unchanged.

## Internal changes

The internal `WorkerSnapshot` and `snapshot()` names become `IdleResponseBoundary` and `idle_response_boundary()`. The Zod fixture also guarantees a nonempty raw-output tail before switching to nonblocking writes, removing a fixture race without adding delays or cross-source chronology requirements.

title: Flatten worker relay events and preserve process outcomes
description:
## Why

The merged worker relay still exposed a nested virtual sideband to the server and used result acknowledgements and raw-output checkpoints to impose ordering that independent pipes cannot guarantee. This refactor makes the outer relay boundary match the events the server consumes while preserving the worker-facing sideband protocol.

## User-facing changes

- Raw worker stdout and stderr use readable JSON strings when each chunk is valid UTF-8, with base64 byte events only for invalid chunks.
- Cross-source output order now follows serialized relay observation. Each source remains lossless and ordered, but raw output written before an operation result may be observed after it and remain pending for a later response.
- Unexpected worker exit status and signal outcomes are reported before the existing stopped and replacement notices. Intentional restart and shutdown remain quiet.

## Internal changes

- Flatten relay commands and events and keep worker-sideband translation inside the relay.
- Remove operation-result acknowledgements, relay output checkpoints, and the `Activity` wrapper.
- Route sideband, stdout, stderr, and supervision producers through one queue and one flushed JSONL serializer.
- Use an ordered worker-event dispatcher with `WorkerOperationState` for operation ownership, retained failures, and idle input.
- Drain worker streams before closure and final process-outcome events.
- Keep the relay synchronous and thread based.

title: Organize transcript tests by process boundary
description:
## Summary

Organizes transcript source and golden paths around the client-server, server-relay, and relay-worker process boundaries, with direct command transcripts under `cli`. This gives each process boundary an explicit place for golden traces and establishes server-relay capture infrastructure before the later relay-protocol refactor.

## User-facing changes

None intended. The current server-relay protocol remains unchanged, including nested worker messages, base64-encoded raw output, and `terminal_committed`.

## Internal changes

- Makes transcript discovery recursive and gives every case one boundary-qualified selector.
- Renames the existing worker-wire suite as `relay_worker/protocol` and records its directions as relay and worker.
- Adds a hidden development seam that launches a deterministic scripted relay as the server's direct sandbox child, preserving process-group and cleanup ownership.
- Records representative server-relay JSONL traces for startup, evaluation, raw streams, stdin, interrupts, graceful retirement, fatal failure, and truncated output.

title: Stabilize idle callback transcript tests
description:
## Summary

Make the idle-callback transcript tests establish their preconditions explicitly instead of depending on callback scheduling.

- Wait until the worker reports the outstanding idle input request before starting live Python preparation.
- Prepare `matplotlib`, distinct from the callback's retained `py-yaml12` requirement, so the operation cannot become an idempotent no-op.
- Pause briefly between empty-send polls while waiting for a long idle callback to publish output.

## Verification

Ran both affected transcript cases three consecutive times:

- `r_requirements::stops_live_preparation_for_idle_callback_input`
- `r::snapshots_output_while_idle_later_callback_runs`

title: Stabilize idle callback transcript polling
description:
Stacked on #101.

## Summary

- validate every immediate idle response while waiting for the callback output
- remove scheduling-dependent retry polls from the recorded transcript
- remove the polling sleep and retain the terminal response under the first poll ID

## Testing

- `r::snapshots_output_while_idle_later_callback_runs` repeated 10 times
- `scripts/check`

title: Make sideband transport cancellable
description:
## Summary

- continuously read and frame the worker-to-server sideband on a dedicated thread, queueing decoded messages in order in an unbounded in-memory channel
- cancel that reader outside the worker-owner lock; cancellation wins over simultaneous sideband readiness and discards unread pipe bytes and any partial frame
- keep the inherited anonymous-pipe protocol and server-to-worker writes unchanged, with coverage for idle sideband collection and descendants that retain a partial frame

## Testing

- `scripts/check`

title: Run transcript tests in parallel by default
description:
## Summary

- run the selected initialization reference case first, then execute the remaining transcript cases concurrently using at least two workers and otherwise the available CPU count
- report remaining cases as they finish, cap the pool by the selected case count and platform limit, and cancel queued work after a failure
- add a `--jobs` override, including `--jobs 1` for serial execution
- install the R fixture into per-case temporary libraries so concurrent Python cases do not contend

## Testing

- `scripts/check`

title: Report resolver interrupt failures
description:
Reports resolver signal failures to both the interrupt caller and the requirement-resolution caller. A successful `[interrupt sent]` result now means the resolver accepted the request; a live OS-level denial is no longer hidden.

## User-facing changes

- Errors such as `EPERM` from signaling a live resolver are returned by `session(action = "interrupt")`.
- The associated preparation call returns the same failure and the resolver process group is still cleaned up.
- A resolver that exits during the signal race remains an ordinary completed resolver rather than a false signal failure.

## Internal changes

- Resolver interrupt events carry a local one-shot result channel.
- The resolver owner distinguishes a live signal failure from an already-exited group leader.
- The macOS exit check uses non-reaping `waitid(..., WNOWAIT)` so the existing watcher remains the single authority for reaping and later resolver stages cannot consume stale exit events.
- A deterministic public fixture interposes a denied resolver `SIGINT` and verifies error propagation and cleanup.

title: Route session interrupts to active resolvers
description:
Routes `session(action = "interrupt")` to an active host requirement resolver before falling back to the live worker. This lets the same public action stop package resolution that is waiting on the network or a child process.

## User-facing changes

- An active R, Python, or DuckDB resolver receives `SIGINT` through its process group.
- The interrupt call returns after the resolver accepts the request. The resolver then reports its ordinary resolution failure, while the existing worker and its state remain available.
- If no resolver is active, the request continues to target the live worker introduced by the preceding PR.

## Internal changes

- Resolver processes share one interrupt event path and signal the currently active process group.
- Each resolver child restores the default `SIGINT` disposition and unblocks the signal before `exec`, including the DuckDB resolver.
- The resolver lifecycle remains responsible for descendant cleanup and normal cancellation.
- A public transcript case synchronizes on a live Python resolver and verifies that interruption preserves worker state.

title: Add SIGINT session interrupts
description:
## Summary

Add `session(action = "interrupt")` to send `SIGINT` to an active host resolver, or otherwise to the live worker. The call returns after sending the signal without waiting for an acknowledgment or evaluation result.

This allows clients to stop long-running requirement resolution or R, Python, and SQL work without replacing the worker when the resolver or runtime handles the signal.

## Public-facing changes

- `interrupt` accepts no requirements and does not start a worker. It returns `worker is not running` when no target exists.
- Worker signals are not associated with evaluation IDs. An idle signal is consumed at the next managed boundary, while active R, reticulate Python, and DuckDB evaluations retain native interrupt behavior.
- User code can catch or delay `SIGINT`; `restart` remains the bounded recovery path.

## Internal changes

- Route interrupts outside the sideband protocol through the active resolver lifecycle channel or direct worker PID, with no acknowledgment frame.
- Reset inherited `SIGINT` state in resolver children and the worker, then check pending R interrupts at managed evaluation boundaries.
- Keep worker-owned preparation and cleanup transitions atomic while active host resolvers remain interruptible.

title: Drain background worker activity before evaluations
description:
## Summary

Drain already-published background worker activity before sending a cell. This keeps a custom worker's pending Python resolver request from consuming `Evaluate` as though it were the resolver reply.

## User-facing changes

The next `send` now collects leading background console output, images, input requests, and Python resolution before evaluating its cell. Prequeued stdin can satisfy an input request from that activity through the ordinary evaluation lifecycle.

## Internal changes

The server attaches the evaluation's stdin writer before its nonblocking sideband readiness check, routes each observed activity through the evaluation sinks until `activity_completed`, commits the activity checkpoint, and only then sends `Evaluate`. The existing preparation drain now shares the same phase-aware activity reader.

title: Retain the sideband reader descriptor
description:
## Summary

Retain the sideband pipe descriptor alongside its buffered reader and expose it through `AsRawFd`. This lets worker code wait on the same descriptor without changing JSON-lines framing or message receipt.

## User-facing changes

None. Sideband messages are read and decoded as before.

## Internal changes

`Reader` records the descriptor before erasing the concrete pipe type behind `dyn Read`. The buffered reader remains the sole owner of the stream and the sole path for consuming messages.

title: Clarify package guidance for custom Python
description:
## Summary

The `send` description told clients to prepare other packages before importing them, even when a caller-selected Python installation already provides them. It also left clients to probe package availability in cells.

This updates the static guidance to avoid availability probes, prepare additional packages through `session`, and import packages already installed in a custom Python installation directly.

## Changes

- User-facing: clarifies package loading for custom Python installations.
- Internal: no routing, schema, worker, or lifecycle behavior changes; only the static description, exact documentation mirror, and public `tools/list` regression change.

title: Preserve complete runtime diagnostics in transcript snapshots
description:
## Summary

Transcript goldens should faithfully record what an MCP client receives. Several cases replaced complete Python, R, and DuckDB diagnostics with placeholders or shortened messages, which obscured the session being tested.

This change records the complete client-visible diagnostics in the affected snapshots and limits normalization to unstable Python versions, executable or absolute paths, and timing-dependent IR progress frames.

## User-facing changes

There is no runtime behavior change. Transcript snapshots now expose complete Python resolver errors, R errors and backtraces, and DuckDB catalog diagnostics.

## Internal changes

- Remove case-specific output rewrites and whitespace trimming from the transcript tests.
- Extend the Python resolver normalizer to cover active-interpreter manifests without changing stable diagnostic text.
- Add repository guidance requiring faithful runtime errors and tracebacks in snapshots.

title: Align worker replacement responses with lifecycle boundaries
description:
## Summary

Align worker recovery and explicit restart responses with the lifecycle boundaries they describe. The initiating `send` now owns failure recovery through one replacement attempt, while an explicit restart splits old-worker output from restart lifecycle facts without letting the restart response overtake an interrupted `send` reply.

This makes timeouts, polling, worker replacement, and response ownership consistent: callers receive facts from the operation that caused them, and replacement readiness is reported as `[idle]`.

## User-facing changes

- After an established worker fails, the same `send` retires it and makes one automatic replacement attempt within the call's remaining `timeout_ms`. It returns the failure, stopped notice, starting notice, replacement startup output, and `[idle]` together when ready. If the deadline arrives during startup, it returns `[worker starting]`, and a later poll resumes that recovery.
- An explicit restart that interrupts a waiting `send` first writes that call's old-worker output and restart-cancellation facts. The restart response then reports `[active evaluation stopped by session restart request]`, any applicable ready-worker stopped notice, `[starting new worker]`, replacement startup output, and `[idle]`.
- Restart does not report lost worker state when it interrupts a process that never reached ready, and it preserves `[done]` or `[idle]` when it reserves an already-completed response.
- Requirement preparation that overlaps worker startup fails before resolution or manifest changes with `[requirements not prepared: worker is starting]`.
- Server-owned lifecycle, state, input, and infrastructure facts use consistent bracketed rendering. Language errors remain normal worker output.

## Internal changes

- Separate session occupancy from an RAII response-draining claim, so rejected concurrent polls cannot mutate stdin or leak wait ownership.
- Represent worker retirement outcomes explicitly and keep the out-of-band stop plus owner-finalization phases behind the lifecycle boundary.
- Preserve terminal completion state until the response owner collects it, including restart handoff races.
- Record direct fd 1 and fd 2 capture as distinct output events and distinguish that fallback path from worker console text without changing the worker protocol or MCP rendering.
- Track response delivery at the stdio transport boundary so replacement cannot start until an interrupted `send` reply has actually been written. Cancellation and connection closure release undeliverable replies without coupling lifecycle behavior to journaling.

## Notes

The branch includes the latest `main` changes for lazy, optional console journals. Optional call IDs and image artifacts remain observational and do not affect worker lifecycle or response delivery.

title: Create optional console journals only on first use
description:
## Summary

`mcp-console serve` currently creates a session directory as soon as the process starts. Clients can initialize or refresh the server without calling either console tool, so those processes leave journals that contain only `session_started`.

This change creates a run record only when the first ordinary `send` or `session` call arrives. Initialization, tool listing, unknown tool calls, and clean shutdown of an unused server no longer create `.mcp-console`.

Console recording is also optional. If the run cannot be created or a later write fails, MCP Console emits one diagnostic to standard error, disables recording for that server process, and continues serving calls.

## User-facing changes

- Run directory timestamps represent first console use rather than server startup.
- Recording failures do not replace tool results, suppress images, restart the worker, or reject later console calls.
- A partial journal ends at its last successfully flushed event after recording is disabled.
- Existing run records are unchanged; the new behavior applies to future server processes.

## Internal changes

- Split pending transcript state from the active journal and materialize the active state under the recorder mutex.
- Route unknown tool names without entering the recorder, including after a journal exists.
- Carry optional artifact references through the output tape so images remain in MCP responses when persistence fails.
- Preserve requests and assembled results across recorder tasks, and recover a poisoned recorder mutex by disabling recording.
- Add public transcript coverage for unused handshakes, first use through both tools, unknown tool calls, initial record-creation failure, and later artifact persistence failure. Update the recording goldens and implemented-behavior documentation to match.

title: Clarify R preparation failure regressions
description:
## Summary

Follow up on #67 by making two R preparation failure transcripts prove the user-visible behavior they describe.

## Public-facing changes

None. This PR changes acceptance coverage only.

## Internal changes

- Isolate the managed R library before using ordinary `require(zeallot)`, so the transcript shows the failed load instead of checking a namespace in a selected library directly.
- Save the sentinel to RDS before restart, preserve the file outside the retiring worker's temporary directory, then load and verify it from the replacement worker.

## Testing

- `scripts/check`

title: Adapt managed Python integration to upstream changes
description:
## Summary

Upstream reticulate revised its Python requirement internals and late-activation semantics. Its requirement display and related operations can also select a Python version through uv. Inside MCP Console's sandbox, that direct uv call could try to initialize the caller's read-only host cache and fail.

This updates the managed-Python integration so both environment resolution and Python-version selection cross MCP Console's existing host resolver boundary. The worker keeps the caller's UV settings, while the real reticulate and uv operations run outside the sandbox with normal access to the existing host cache.

## User-facing changes

- Managed Python startup, `py_require()` preparation, and requirement printing work with the current reticulate development version.
- Python-version selection uses the configured host UV cache without disabling caching or creating a separate worker cache.
- Late Python additions remain available after restart without replacing logical `py_require()` constraints with an exact patch version.
- A version-selection failure remains a normal R outcome and leaves the worker reusable.

## Internal changes

- Use reticulate's revised requirement getter, active-version helper, and history schema.
- Carry separate physical resolver and retained logical manifests through runtime environment resolution.
- Add a typed sideband request for host-side Python-version selection. It returns only the selected version and cannot execute an arbitrary host-side uv tool command.
- Pass the workflow token to CI checks so IR can resolve the GitHub-based default R environment for every complete requirement set.
- Extend the public transcript coverage and synchronize the implemented worker-protocol documentation.

title: Populate default console environments
description:
## Summary

Populate MCP Console's built-in environments with common data-analysis and SQL runtime packages so agents can use R, Python, or DuckDB for routine tabular work without preparing core packages first.

## User-facing changes

- Resolve `tidyverse`, `github::rstudio/reticulate`, `DBI`, `duckdb`, `arrow`, and `nanoarrow` into the default R library. The GitHub reticulate build supplies the fork-aware output restoration required by the worker, while arrow and nanoarrow make row-producing SQL previews available on a clean host.
- Add pandas alongside NumPy in the managed Python baseline.
- Tell agents that the default R requirements and their dependency sets include packages such as ggplot2, dplyr, readr, and jsonlite, while making clear that R packages are not attached automatically.
- Use optional packages such as `data.table`, `sf`, `yaml12`, and Polars in requirement-preparation examples.

## Internal changes

- Resolve and retain the default R library during built-in server startup, then reuse it across worker generations and explicit restarts.
- Centralize Python baseline manifest construction and normalization around NumPy and pandas.
- Extend public transcript coverage for the default R library, GitHub reticulate provenance, pandas CSV handling, manifest ordering, tool descriptions, and a row-producing SQL query with empty ambient R libraries.
- Update lifecycle fixtures for the additional startup preflight and document its host-side resolution and cancellation boundaries.
- Prewarm the exact default R environment in CI before concurrent built-in server tests.
- Keep the local-source rejection snapshot focused on the stable IR diagnostic instead of credential- and cache-dependent progress output.

title: Order worker restart notices before replacement output
description:
## Summary

When a failed worker was replaced, the restart notice was assembled after the new worker's output or error text. That made transcripts show events in the wrong lifecycle order.

This change makes the notice an ordered captured-output boundary, so replies contain prior-session output, then the restart notice, then replacement output.

## Changes

- User-facing: restart notices now appear before standard-stream, sideband, and error text from the replacement worker. Failed replacement startup remains silent.
- Internal: replacement startup reserves the boundary before spawning the new worker, commits it after the worker reports ready, and cancels it when startup fails.
- Coverage and documentation: public Zod, built-in worker, R, and Python transcript cases now assert the new ordering, and the worker protocol documentation describes it.
- Note: this also includes the YAML formatter's normalization of one unrelated transcript scalar.

title: Record the native R worker decision and expand acceptance coverage
description:
## Summary

This PR closes out the original R worker implementation exploration. [`mcp-repl`](https://github.com/posit-dev/mcp-repl) had already established the basic pattern of an MCP server backed by persistent R. This branch explored how MCP Console should implement that pattern: how to sandbox the worker, keep control traffic separate from runtime stdio, preserve R's native top-level behavior, contain R's non-local error transfers, and route interactive input. It also compared a purpose-built Harp/`libr` worker with an Ark-backed kernel. At its first complete point, the branch combined the worker, sandbox integration, sideband protocol, MCP routing, DLL-REPL evaluation, stdin, documentation, and tests in a 21-file, 3,182-line addition.

That was too much to review as one change. The branch then became a staging ground for smaller PRs, each of which delivered a working piece of the system. As those PRs landed, `main` was merged back into this branch and the duplicate implementation was removed. The current diff contains no production-code changes. What remains is the design record for the native R decision and public acceptance coverage for behavior that is now implemented on `main`.

## How the work was split up

The first group established the test and process boundaries needed by a long-lived worker:

- [#13 — Move stable CLI checks to golden transcripts](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/13) moved stable command behavior into readable snapshots while retaining process-, timing-, and host-effect checks in Cargo tests.
- [#14 — Rename transcript documents to entries](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/14) clarified the transcript test vocabulary before more runtime cases were added.
- [#15 — Refactor sandbox launcher into reusable command builder](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/15) separated the configurable process launcher and temporary-directory lifetime from the `sandbox` command.
- [#16 — Add development worker sideband protocol](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/16) landed the server-side inherited-pipe protocol, lifecycle handling, and deterministic Zod fixture before introducing native R.

The next group landed the native runtime itself in two reviewable steps:

- [#17 — Add the built-in R worker](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/17) added persistent sandboxed R through Harp and `libr`, including visible values, ordinary R errors, silent completion, and worker replacement after infrastructure failure.
- [#18 — Run R cells through the native DLL REPL loop](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/18) moved parsing, evaluation, auto-printing, warnings, `.Last.value`, tracebacks, and task callbacks back under R's own top-level machinery.

Several follow-up PRs made the remaining behavior and review surface smaller:

- [#20 — Require format checks before commits](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/20) recorded the local formatter-review step used for the transcript snapshots.
- [#21 — Simplify golden MCP transcripts](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/21) removed repeated MCP handshake and envelope noise from the snapshots.
- [#22 — Add timeout polling to send](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/22) let a call return `[running]` while retaining the active evaluation for later polling.
- [#19 — Support interactive stdin in R evaluations](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console/pull/19) completed the input path using worker fd 0, with combined, evaluating, timed-out, and idle delivery plus request/receipt observations for supported console reads.

The final stdin design differs from the early exploration. Stdin is a worker-scoped fd-0 stream rather than a sideband `Input` message or an explicit stop/resume boundary. Unread bytes can serve later reads or evaluations, and a failed worker generation is discarded so a later evaluation can start a fresh one. The older sideband-stdin and sticky-stopped-worker variants were removed when the current `main` behavior was merged back.

`main` was reconciled back into this branch after PRs #13–#15, again after #16–#17, after #18, and finally after #19–#22. Those merges reduced the residual branch from 3,182 additions and 62 deletions to 1,088 additions and 69 deletions across 14 documentation and acceptance-test files.

## Decision recorded here

Both the native and Ark-backed R-only paths were implemented and evaluated. Ark handled the tested R behavior and also provided source-bearing errors, plots, direct subprocess output, and Data Explorer comms. At the evaluated revision, however, reusing those facilities meant making MCP Console a Jupyter client: it had to own ZeroMQ channels, connection and authentication setup, message correlation, stdin translation, completion detection, and additional sandbox allowances. The reusable lower-level console path was coupled to Ark and Amalthea services, and the prototype needed an additional browser-prompt option. Ark's value proxy also changed the expression observed by top-level task callbacks.

For the current text-R surface, MCP Console therefore uses Harp and `libr` for R discovery, loading, initialization, and bindings, while delegating evaluation to the public `R_ReplDLLinit()` and `R_ReplDLLdo1()` embedder APIs. A small C-owned frame contains R's non-local error transfer so it cannot jump across a live Rust frame. A custom `ReadConsole` callback and R's busy state keep complete cell source separate from evaluation-time stdin without inspecting prompt text or pre-parsing the cell in Rust.

This is a decision for the implemented text-R slice, not a permanent rejection of Ark or a final choice for the full R/Python/SQL runtime. The backend evaluation documents the Ark-side changes, MCP Console adapter work, and optional lower-level extraction that would make an Ark-backed route practical. Ark should be reconsidered when plots, help, interrupts, debugger support, Variables, or Data Explorer become part of the implemented surface.

## User-facing changes

There are no new tools, schema changes, or runtime capabilities in this final PR. The implementation described here already landed in the PRs above.

The README now makes two existing outcomes explicit: R parse, evaluation, and auto-print failures are ordinary console results rather than MCP tool errors, and a silent successful cell returns `[done]`.

## Internal changes

- Record the Ark-versus-native prototype results, the scope of the current decision, and the work required to revisit Ark.
- Record why the native worker uses the DLL-REPL iterator and a C-owned long-jump boundary instead of whole-cell pre-parsing, direct `Rf_eval()`, the full R main loop, or private `Rf_ReplIteration()` internals.
- Add golden transcript coverage for `browser()` suspension and resumption, rejection of a new cell during evaluation, recoverable runtime and auto-print errors, useful native tracebacks, `sys.calls()`, and `.Last.value` placement.
- Add built-binary coverage for long multibyte source lines, R discovery inside the sandbox, bounded shutdown during discovery and input, the native worker's filesystem/process/network boundary, and refusal to start an unsandboxed worker on unsupported platforms.

The broader backend decision remains open. This PR does not add Ark, interrupts, source filenames, direct subprocess-output capture, plots, help, Variables, Data Explorer, or non-macOS worker support.

title: Prevent installation from local R package sources
description:
## Summary

R package resolution runs outside the worker sandbox, where installation hooks run with server permissions. MCP Console now requires IR 0.4.0 or later and sets `IR_NO_LOCAL_SOURCES` on every R resolution. IR checks the complete resolved manifest before materialization, covering direct and transitive local sources while keeping package-reference parsing in IR and pak.

## User-facing changes

- `session(action = "prepare")` returns a tool error when its R environment would install a package from the local filesystem. IR may still reuse an already materialized library because that runs no installation code.
- Configured-repository requirements and IR's accepted package syntax continue to pass through unchanged.
- Failed preparation remains atomic and leaves the prior R and Python configuration unchanged.

## Internal changes

- Remove MCP Console's package-reference classifier and delegate the resolved-source policy to IR.
- Add a public regression package whose `configure` script writes a marker outside the sandbox, and verify that the script does not run.
- Use configured-repository packages for successful R preparation and atomicity coverage, including comma-separated syntax.
- Update the schema, protocol, architecture, and user documentation to describe the IR-owned boundary.

## Notes

Python requirement handling is unchanged. Closing its analogous local-install path completely still requires a maintained PEP 508 and direct-source boundary, which is outside this change.

title: Split resolver and worker client into submodules
description:
## Summary

Split the worker client and host resolver into responsibility-focused modules. This keeps the session lifecycle, environment, evaluation, output, platform, and resolver code easier to navigate and review without changing runtime behavior.

## User-facing changes

None. The MCP tools, worker protocol, session behavior, and platform support remain unchanged.

## Internal changes

- Keep `worker_client.rs` as the orchestration facade and move environment preparation, evaluation state, lifecycle coordination, output assembly, and platform implementations into focused modules.
- Keep `resolver.rs` as the platform-gated facade and move managed R resolution, managed Python resolution, process supervision, and non-macOS stubs into focused modules.
- Update the repository map and worker protocol source references for the new layout.

title: Capture Matplotlib plots from Python cells
description:
## Summary

Return Matplotlib figures from Python cells as PNG image content so multimodal MCP clients can inspect plots during exploratory analysis. Python plotting now follows a cell-scoped contract: every open pyplot-managed figure is rendered at cell end and then closed.

## User-facing changes

- Return every open `matplotlib.pyplot` figure once at cell end, in figure-number order, including after a Python error.
- Treat `plt.show()` as optional. Calling `savefig()` still returns the figure while it remains open; calling `close()` suppresses capture.
- Keep final Python expressions on the normal display-hook path, followed by any cell-end plot images.
- Keep Matplotlib optional, default to Agg when no backend is configured, and use worker-private writable configuration and cache directories.
- Report individual rendering failures as normal Python tracebacks while continuing to render later figures and closing all figures during cleanup.

## Internal changes

- Render figures to in-memory PNG bytes and publish them through the existing worker image sideband; the worker protocol does not change.
- Install a small no-op `show()` hook through reticulate so Agg does not emit its noninteractive-backend warning before cell-end capture.
- Add public transcript coverage for multiple figures, ordering, `show()`, `savefig()`, explicit close, final-expression display, errors, render failures, and cell-scoped cleanup.

title: Support restart with optional Python requirements
description:
## Summary

Follow up on #44 by allowing `session` restart calls to add Python requirements while replacing the implicit session worker. This makes an environment update and worker restart one atomic operation: the complete candidate environment resolves before the current worker is stopped, and a resolution failure leaves the current worker and its in-memory state unchanged.

## User-facing changes

- `session` with `action = "restart"` now accepts optional additive Python requirements.
- Omitting requirements retains the current checkpointed Python environment.
- Restart requirements are rejected for custom workers without stopping the running worker.
- The worker shutdown grace period begins after requirement resolution succeeds.

## Internal changes

- Preserve the complete checkpointed Python manifest while merging additions and serialize host resolver ownership.
- Associate admitted evaluations and stdin writes with an opaque worker identity so pre-restart work cannot reach the replacement.
- Represent restart and shutdown deadlines directly in lifecycle state variants.
- Narrow the transcript fixture's public API to tool-specific `send()` and `session()` helpers, and update public transcript coverage, snapshots, and documentation.

## Notes

The branch includes the latest `main`. `scripts/check` passes.

title: Share R and SQL relations automatically
description:
## Summary

Enable automatic relation sharing between persistent R and SQL state so a session can switch between R transformations and SQL queries without manual registration or a second DuckDB connection.

## User-facing changes

- SQL first resolves persistent catalog tables and views, then scans data frames from the persistent R global environment when no catalog relation matches.
- SQL views over scanned R data frames observe later changes to the R binding.
- R code can use `sql_connection()` to borrow the worker-owned DBI connection with established DuckDB, DBI, and dplyr interfaces. The helper remains available after `rm(list = ls())`; callers must not disconnect the returned connection.
- Lazy table and view relations observe later catalog changes until collection.
- The README and worker protocol document lookup precedence, connection ownership, and lazy transfer behavior.

## Internal changes

- Route SQL preparation through a zero-argument closure rooted in R's global environment while retaining connection and source state in the private bridge.
- Enable DuckDB-R environment scanning without changing the bounded SQL preview path.
- Keep `sql_connection()` in a worker-owned attached environment behind `.GlobalEnv`, preserving ordinary R shadowing while protecting the helper from workspace clearing.
- Add public transcript coverage for direct R data-frame queries, live SQL views, catalog precedence, bridge-state name collisions, lazy dplyr relations, and helper persistence after a workspace reset. CI now installs dplyr and dbplyr for this coverage.

title: Refine Python requirement resolution
description:
## Summary

Refine initial Python requirement preparation after reviewing the merged implementation. Resolver failures now show the selected Python and complete package candidate without exposing reticulate's helper command or temporary path, while preserving uv's actual stderr. The host resolver lifecycle is also separated from worker-side Python execution.

## User-facing changes

- Show a JSON resolver-input manifest and the full uv failure instead of the internal helper command.
- Record complete resolver failures in the golden transcripts.
- Document that package-triggered `py_require()` calls currently update only reticulate's worker-local manifest and may leave newly requested modules unavailable.

## Internal changes

- Move managed-Python host resolution and cancellation into `src/resolver.rs`.
- Let `readLines()` own its standard-input connection and use `grep(value = TRUE)` to extract reticulate's Python selection.
- Remove reticulate's uv debug-command capture.
- Describe a future explicit pathway that observes package additions without wrapping `py_require()`, reports them to the server, and resolves them before an explicit restart discards live state.

## Notes

Runtime propagation of package-triggered requirements remains deferred because the current session API has no restart action, and evaluated code must not implicitly invoke unsandboxed dependency resolution. JSON reuses the existing release dependency; the repository has no runtime YAML emitter.

## Testing

- `scripts/check`

title: Add bounded SQL result previews
description:
## Summary

Replace the unbounded SQL fetch and R data-frame output path with a bounded query-result preview. This keeps small results useful while preventing the console from fully materializing or rendering large query results.

## User-facing changes

- Display query results as deterministic pillar tables with Arrow column names and physical types.
- Fetch at most 21 rows, display at most 20 rows and 12 columns, limit cells to 160 characters, and cap each SQL preview at 12 KiB.
- Preserve SQL `NULL` and exact `BIGINT`, `DECIMAL`, list, and struct values when they fit in a cell.
- Show schemas for empty results and report omitted rows, columns, and truncated cells explicitly.
- Keep DDL and DML results silent; this change does not add statement summaries or other SQL semantics.

## Internal changes

- Use `DBI::dbSendQueryArrow()` and one streaming `DBI::dbFetchArrow()` batch, with row 21 used only to detect additional rows.
- Import nanoarrow batches through Arrow's C Data Interface, select the bounded preview, and stringify and truncate only those cells through DuckDB.
- Pin pillar output settings and disable DuckDB progress output so previews do not depend on mutable R printing options.
- Add the Arrow and table-printing dependencies to CI, public transcript regressions for the preview contract, and implemented-behavior documentation.

title: Fix SQL transcript formatting
description:
## Summary

Capture the fixed SQL query result in the golden transcripts. The prior normalizer first asserted the raw result, then replaced it with a placeholder. That hid the output from snapshots and from CI's golden-diff diagnostics.

## User-facing changes

No runtime behavior changes.

## Internal changes

- The SQL transcript retains the worker's formatted `answer` result, including its leading spaces.

title: Add SQL cells backed by DuckDB
description:
## Summary

Adds the first runnable SQL-cell path to `send`, backed by the DuckDB R package and DBI. This keeps R, Python, and SQL execution in the existing persistent worker and gives SQL cells one in-memory catalog per worker generation.

## User-facing changes

- `send` accepts exactly one of `r`, `python`, or `sql`.
- SQL catalog state persists across calls in a worker generation.
- Queries print data-frame results, while statements without result columns return `[done]`.
- DuckDB errors remain normal evaluation output, and later SQL cells can continue.

## Internal changes

- Adds a private DuckDB/DBI bridge and extracts shared R bridge machinery from the Python adapter.
- Keeps DuckDB extension, secret, and spill paths inside the worker temporary directory, with environment scanning disabled.
- Extends protocol fixtures, public transcript coverage, CI package setup, and implemented-state documentation.

## Notes

This initial slice leaves bounded result previews, affected-row summaries, and R or Python relation registration for later work.

title: Preserve Python output from fork children
description:
## Summary

Reticulate routes Python text streams through the R console callback. Fork children must not retain the worker sideband, so reticulate restores their original fd-backed streams through its registered CPython fork callback. This PR makes the resulting stdout and stderr capture part of MCP Console's tested contract while keeping the sideband parent-only.

## User-facing changes

- `print()` and `sys.stderr.write()` from children created by `os.fork()` in a Python cell now appear in `send` results or later polls.
- Native extensions that fork without running CPython's registered fork callbacks and then resume Python remain unsupported.
- Fork-child capture requires reticulate from its `main` branch or a release containing fork-aware stream restoration.

## Internal changes

- Install reticulate from `main` in CI; MCP Console does not carry a private stream-remapping workaround.
- Add a public `serve` transcript that initializes Python from R, records child output as raw stdout and stderr, and confirms the parent remains on sideband after the fork.
- Synchronize the implemented behavior in the README, worker protocol, and repository state documentation.

title: Let reticulate select the Python interpreter
description:
## Summary

Let reticulate own Python interpreter selection without requiring uv to run inside the sandbox. When `RETICULATE_PYTHON` is unset or is `managed`, `mcp-console serve` now runs `reticulate::py_config()` outside the worker sandbox, using reticulate and uv's normal global caches and network access. It passes the selected interpreter path to the sandboxed worker.

This keeps the sandbox policy unchanged while allowing a clean managed setup to resolve or provision Python before the worker becomes offline.

## User-facing changes

- The default and explicit `managed` configurations resolve Python during server startup.
- Explicit `RETICULATE_PYTHON` values, including an empty value, remain unchanged and skip the preflight.
- The worker forces `UV_OFFLINE=1` and reuses the interpreter selected during preflight.
- The selection is fixed at startup; worker-side `py_require()` calls do not revise it.
- A managed preflight failure stops `serve` before it accepts MCP requests.

## Internal changes

- Move managed-Python preflight, worker environment setup, and the reticulate evaluation bridge into `src/python.rs`.
- Keep the existing sandbox implementation and SBPL unchanged; custom workers also skip managed-Python preflight.
- Replace the combined environment transcript with one public transcript per server configuration.
- Exercise default and explicit managed selection against real uv, including Python evaluation through the selected interpreter. Ordinary server and worker tests use the same discovery path without injecting a Python configuration.

title: Add worker transcript coverage for Python output routing
description:
## Summary

Add public-path regression coverage and precise documentation for Python output routing that MCP Console already implements. `RETICULATE_REMAP_OUTPUT_STREAMS` was already set once at worker startup, so this PR does not change runtime behavior. Existing MCP transcripts only showed merged response text; they could not distinguish reticulate sideband frames from raw worker standard streams or verify continuous production stream collection.

## User-facing changes

- No runtime behavior changes.
- Clarify which Python writes use reticulate's sideband console path and which remain on captured standard output and standard error.
- Narrow the descendant behavior to distinguish fork-only inherited remapped streams, direct descriptor writes, and fresh streams created after exec.

## Internal changes

- Add a transparent worker proxy under `serve` that launches the real built-in worker inside the normal sandbox, forwards both sideband directions and standard streams, and records parsed wire events as YAML documents.
- Assert the public MCP `send` result while snapshotting the underlying route.
