- Add a pipe-pressure regression that writes 4 MiB to each standard stream and verifies they are drained while evaluation is still running.

title: Document and test Python input and debugger interaction
description:
## Summary

Python `input()` and `pdb` already use reticulate's R console bridge, but the current documentation describes their input events and debugger interaction as unimplemented. Document the existing behavior and preserve it with public transcripts.

## User-facing changes

- Document that Python `input()` and `breakpoint()`/`pdb` emit input request and receipt events and accept proactively queued or follow-up stdin.
- Clarify that reads through `sys.stdin` or fd 0 directly bypass those events.
- Clarify that silent R and Python cells send `completed` without an `output` frame and project to `[done]` when no other response text is pending.

## Internal changes

- Add Python transcripts for exposed and proactively queued input, direct `sys.stdin` reads, repeated `pdb` commands, debugger continuation, and state retained after the debugger exits.
- Leave runtime behavior unchanged.

## Testing

- `scripts/check`

title: Render interactive input requests explicitly
description:
## Summary

Interactive input currently appears as bare prompt text followed by `[input]`. That makes prompt events difficult to distinguish from runtime output and does not clearly tell clients when they need to submit `stdin`.

This change records every reported request as `[input requested: <JSON-quoted prompt>]` and uses `[stdin needed]` only while the request remains outstanding. Requests satisfied by already queued stdin remain visible, while submitted bytes stay exact and un-echoed.

## User-facing changes

- Show one explicit record for every reported `readline()` or `browser()` prompt, including requests satisfied immediately.
- JSON-quote prompts so trailing spaces, quotes, newlines, and control characters remain unambiguous.
- Replace `[input]` with `[stdin needed]` when the runtime is still waiting.
- Preserve partial and follow-up stdin behavior without repeating request records or echoing submitted commands.

## Internal changes

- Render and delimit request records at the server boundary without changing the worker sideband protocol.
- Preserve record ordering around interleaved worker output.
- Expand built-in R and deterministic Zod transcript coverage.
- Update the README, implemented-state documentation, and worker protocol.

title: Run CI on macOS only
description:
## Summary

Run CI only on macOS while the Linux sandbox and built-in worker are unsupported. This prevents Linux-only failures from blocking changes to the implemented macOS runtime.

## Changes

- Remove `ubuntu-latest` from the CI matrix.
- Keep the macOS job running the full `scripts/check` suite under the existing check name.
- Leave runtime and user-facing behavior unchanged.

title: Report automatic worker replacement and preserve failure output
description:
## Summary

A worker infrastructure or protocol failure discards its in-memory R and Python state. Previously, the replacement was silent, and sideband output already received from the failed evaluation could be lost. This change preserves that output and tells the client once a replacement has started successfully.

The restart notice is rendered as `[worker restarted: in-memory state lost]\n` on a fresh line. Initial lazy startup and failures before the worker reaches `ready` remain silent because they do not replace established session state.

## User-facing changes

- Reports successful worker replacement exactly once on the next response, without adding a blank line before the notice.
- Returns worker output available at the failure response boundary before the tool error. When an error shares the response with worker output or a restart notice, brackets distinguish the server-owned error; an error returned alone remains bare.
- Preserves nonempty stdin submitted while idle when it starts a replacement, then reports `[idle]`.
- Surfaces the R fatal-signal report and menu, as well as reticulate initialization diagnostics, before the infrastructure error.

## Internal changes

- Tracks initial, replacement-pending, and running worker states so only failures after `ready` produce a restart notice.
- Keeps accumulated worker output separate from the infrastructure error until response rendering, preserving both the output and server-notice boundaries.
- Queues the notice only after the replacement reaches `ready` and drains it once; the worker sideband protocol is unchanged.
- Adds deterministic Zod startup and release gates plus public Zod, R, and Python transcripts for replacement timing, idle stdin, silent startup retries, fatal worker exits, output preservation, and fresh post-restart state.
- Updates the README and implemented worker protocol documentation.

title: Record exact source and diagnostics in transcript fixtures
description:
## Summary

Transcript fixtures previously stripped meaningful trailing newlines and replaced natural interpreter diagnostics with shorter placeholders. This updates the fixtures to record the submitted source and the actual R and Python errors.

## User-facing changes

None. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

## Internal changes

- Add a shared `code()` helper that dedents multiline fixture programs and removes only the structural leading newline.
- Preserve ordinary trailing newlines while keeping an explicit R regression for source without a final newline.
- Record real Python tracebacks, syntax errors, and NUL errors, along with natural R error and traceback output.
- Clarify that the retained print failure fixture exercises R auto-print recovery.

title: Support Python cells through reticulate
description:
## Summary

Add Python cells to MCP Console's existing sandboxed worker so R and Python can share one persistent reticulate runtime. This provides the first Python execution slice without changing the existing timeout, polling, or stdin model.

## User-facing changes

- `send` accepts exactly one of `r` or `python`.
- Python cells retain `__main__` state, write text output through the existing console path, and send the final expression through `sys.displayhook()`.
- Python tracebacks remain normal language outcomes, and R and Python can exchange objects through reticulate's `py` and `r` bridges.
- The worker reuses an initialized reticulate Python, honors `RETICULATE_PYTHON`, or selects an existing `python3` from `PATH`. It does not install dependencies or access the network.
- Python `input()` can consume proactively queued stdin. Input-request and debugger integration remain outside this slice.

## Internal changes

- Generalize worker evaluation frames to carry a language and source, backed by a shared complete-cell type.
- Initialize a private reticulate evaluator, remap Python text streams before user R can initialize Python, and keep evaluator dependencies separate from user-owned Python globals.
- Extend the deterministic Zod worker, public transcript coverage, CI dependencies, and implemented-behavior documentation for Python cells.

title: Capture worker standard streams
description:
## Summary

Capture stdout and stderr from the sandboxed worker and inherited descendants so output that bypasses the sideband is still returned through `send`, including output emitted while the interpreter is idle.

## User-facing changes

- Attach collected standard-stream output to the next response without tying collection to an active evaluation.
- Preserve worker prompts verbatim and render `[running]`, `[input]`, and `[idle]` as server-owned newline-prefixed banners.
- Decode stream output only when assembling a response, retaining incomplete UTF-8 sequences per pipe and replacing invalid sequences.
- Keep ordering across stdout, stderr, and sideband output best effort.

## Internal changes

- Launch workers with piped stdout and stderr and drain both continuously on dedicated readers.
- Queue tagged raw-byte chunks in client-owned state so output can span requests, idle periods, and worker shutdown.
- Add deterministic Zod coverage for multi-megabyte stdout, background stderr on an idle poll, prompt projection, and response banners.
- Document that stream capture does not add descendant supervision.

title: Add timeout polling to send
description:
## Why

Let MCP clients bound how long a `send` call waits without interrupting a running evaluation.

## Public-facing changes

- `send` accepts an optional `timeout_ms`, defaulting to 60,000 ms.
- A timed-out call returns `[running]` and leaves the evaluation running.
- Calling `send` without `r`, or with `r: null`, polls the active evaluation, returning its result, `[running]`, or `[idle]`.
- New code is rejected until the active evaluation's result is collected.
- Concurrent `send` calls are outside the current supported contract.

## Internal changes

- Retain an evaluation result independently of the request that started it, allowing a later poll to collect it.
- Document timeout and polling behavior in the worker protocol and project status.
- Add public transcript coverage for the embedded R worker and the deterministic Zod fixture, including explicit null polling.
- Give Zod an explicit `echo` command so unsupported fixture commands fail fast.

title: Simplify golden MCP transcripts
description:
## Summary

Simplify MCP golden transcripts so the behavior under test is easier to scan. Repeated initialization and tool-list exchanges now live in one canonical transcript, while matching transcripts reference it with a validated `!same-as` marker. Tool calls and responses also use a flatter representation that keeps the relevant payloads visible.

## User-facing changes

- MCP server behavior and the `send` tool schema are unchanged.
- Transcript authors and reviewers see compact `send` and `result` documents, with the full initialization sequence retained in a dedicated snapshot.

## Internal changes

- Verify that each initialization prefix exactly matches the canonical transcript before replacing it with `!same-as`; differing prefixes remain in full.
- Keep invalid `send` argument coverage separate from the canonical initialization case.
- Call Ruff directly from `scripts/format`, avoiding uv's network-based formatter resolution inside restricted sandboxes.

title: Run R cells through the native DLL REPL loop
description:
## Summary

Run each R cell through R's DLL REPL iterator so R owns parsing, evaluation, auto-printing, and top-level bookkeeping. This removes the worker's whole-cell preparse and per-expression `try_catch()` path while preserving the current MCP and sideband schemas.

## User-facing changes

- Complete expressions remain applied when a later expression is incomplete or has invalid syntax.
- Native top-level behavior now updates `.Last.value`, flushes warnings, and invokes task callbacks with the submitted expression.
- Parse and evaluation failures remain normal tool output, and the worker remains reusable afterward.
- Interactive input is still outside the implemented surface; evaluation-time `ReadConsole` requests receive EOF.

## Internal changes

- Add a macOS C boundary that keeps R's non-local error transfer out of live Rust frames and detects abnormal returns without reading an unspecified function result.
- Resolve `R_ReplDLLinit()` and `R_ReplDLLdo1()` from the loaded R library and feed UTF-8 cell source through `ReadConsole`.
- Use R's busy callback to keep top-level source reads distinct from input requested by evaluated code.
- Add public transcript coverage and align the implemented-worker and architecture documentation with the native loop.

title: Add the built-in R worker
description:
## Summary

`mcp-console serve` now evaluates complete R cells through a built-in sandboxed worker instead of echoing arbitrary JSON. This is the next incremental worker slice after the server-side sideband protocol: it connects that protocol to a real R runtime while keeping interactive input, interrupts, sessions, Python, and SQL out of scope.

## User-facing changes

- `send` accepts one complete `r` string, evaluates it in persistent global R state, captures console output, and prints every visible top-level value.
- R parse and evaluation errors are returned as ordinary text results, and later evaluations can reuse the worker.
- A worker exit or strict protocol failure returns a tool error. The failed worker is discarded, and the next evaluation starts a fresh worker with no in-memory state from the previous process.
- A silent successful cell returns `[done]`.
- The built-in worker is currently available only on macOS.

## Internal changes

- Add pinned `harp` and `libr` dependencies and initialize R on the worker process's main thread.
- Launch one hidden `mcp-console worker` process through the existing sandbox boundary. It discovers `R_HOME` and loads `libR.dylib` directly, without a bootstrap exec or loader environment override.
- Extend the inherited-pipe sideband for worker-side ownership and fork cleanup while retaining the Zod development-worker override.
- Add public transcripts for persistent state, visible values, console output, language-error recovery, silent completion, compiled R package code, strict protocol failures, and worker restart.

## Notes

Interactive input, interrupts, sessions, Python, SQL, structured language errors, and structured worker crash events remain out of scope.

title: Rename transcript documents to entries
description:
## Summary

Rename `TranscriptDocument` to `TranscriptEntry` so the type describes a recorded interaction rather than its YAML representation.

## Changes

- Public test-authoring names now use `TranscriptEntry` and `entry` for individual MCP and CLI records.
- Internal YAML formatting uses `transcript_text` for the serialized stream.
- The transcript test README now defines a `Transcript` as an ordered list of entries and reserves “document” for each entry's YAML serialization.

MCP Console behavior and golden snapshots are unchanged.

title: Move stable CLI checks to golden transcripts
description:
## Summary

Move stable CLI acceptance checks into readable golden transcript suites. This makes exact command and output behavior visible in reviewable YAML while keeping fixture-, timing-, process-control-, partial-match-, and host-side-effect checks in Cargo tests.

## User-facing changes

There are no runtime behavior changes. Golden transcripts now cover:

- `mcp-console --version`
- Python argument and stdout preservation in the macOS sandbox
- Python multiprocessing semaphores
- sandbox execution without `HOME`
- R runtime queries, temporary writes, and host-write denial
- processx PTY support, including the exact `\r\n` output

## Internal changes

- Add suite-level `PLATFORMS` filtering for macOS-only transcript suites.
- Keep restricted cases visible under `scripts/test --list` while skipping execution and snapshot updates on other platforms.
- Remove only the equivalent Cargo acceptance cases and document the filtering convention.

title: Simplify MCP transcript snapshots
description:
## Summary

Make MCP golden transcripts focus on behavior by omitting repeated JSON-RPC
envelope fields. Each request and response turn now records its shared ID once
at the document root, reducing snapshot noise and making PR diffs easier to
read.

## User-facing changes

None. Runtime MCP behavior and wire messages are unchanged.

## Internal changes

- Validate `jsonrpc: "2.0"` and matching response IDs before omitting them from
  recorded transcripts.
- Keep behavior-bearing request and response fields in the golden snapshots.
- Document the compact transcript format.

title: Add repository-wide format script
description:
## Summary

Add `scripts/format` as one repository-wide formatting entry point. It attempts the Python, Markdown/YAML, Rust, and R formatters independently, so contributors can run one command without requiring every formatter.

## Developer-facing changes

- Run `uv format`, `yamark format --wrap sentence`, `cargo fmt --all`, and `air format .` from the repository root.
- Keep formatter errors visible while continuing through the remaining commands and exiting successfully.
- Document `scripts/format` in the README.

## Internal changes

- Add a public script regression test that verifies all four commands are attempted with an empty `PATH`.
- Format the existing Python transcript helper with `uv format`.
- Format transcript snapshots with Yamark and compare parsed transcript trees recursively by type and value.
- Record the script in the repository map.
- Leave CI unchanged.

## Testing

- `scripts/format` followed by an idempotence pass
- `scripts/check`

title: Use clap for command-line parsing
description:
## Summary

Replace handwritten command matching and usage strings with clap so argument parsing, help, version output, and usage diagnostics come from a maintained command-line parser.

## User-facing changes

- Add generated `--help` and `help [COMMAND]` output with concise command descriptions and examples.
- Keep the explicit `serve` subcommand requirement.
- Preserve sandbox command forwarding with or without `--`; missing commands and invalid arguments now use clap diagnostics.

## Internal changes

- Define the typed command model in `src/cli.rs`.
- Preserve sandbox command arguments as OS strings and remove duplicate parsing from the launcher.
- Run help commands with color disabled and write their stdout and stderr directly to one YAML stream, adding nonzero exit codes and omitting empty stderr.
- Generalize the transcript runner so MCP and CLI snapshots share the same readable golden-file workflow.

title: Require the serve subcommand
description:
## Summary

Require an explicit `serve` subcommand to launch the MCP stdio server. This gives server startup one public entry point and lets the root command report missing usage instead of implicitly starting a server.

## Public behavior

- `mcp-console serve` remains the MCP stdio server command.
- `mcp-console` without a subcommand now prints usage and exits with status 2.
- Registration examples now use `uvx mcp-console serve`.

## Internal changes

- Add a public CLI regression test for the missing-subcommand behavior.
- Run the server transcript through `serve` and remove the duplicate golden transcript.
- Update the current-state and design documentation to match the new command contract.

title: Add external golden transcript tests for the MCP server
description:
## Summary

Replace the inline Rust JSON-RPC acceptance test with an external suite that runs the built `mcp-console` binary. Each request/response exchange is stored as one document in a checked-in YAML 1.2 stream, with notifications recorded as input-only documents. This makes protocol behavior changes visible as readable golden diffs.

## Developer-facing changes

- Add `scripts/test` with suite- and case-level selection, listing, and targeted golden updates.
- Make transcript suites directly executable through `uv`.
- Add shared MCP stdio helpers and an initial transcript covering initialization, tool discovery, and a console call.
- Run transcript tests from `scripts/check` and install `uv` in CI.

## Internal changes

- Replace the Rust JSON-RPC acceptance harness with the transcript suite.
- Remove the unused `serde_json` development dependency.
- Leave runtime and CLI behavior unchanged.

title: Add the macOS sandbox process launcher
description:
## Summary

Add `mcp-console sandbox [--] COMMAND [ARG]...`, establishing the process boundary needed for later R, Python, and SQL workers.

On macOS, the command launches its child through `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec` with one read-only policy. Linux and Windows report that the command is unsupported.

## User-facing changes

- Preserve the child command's arguments, standard streams, and exit status.
- Allow host filesystem reads while limiting regular-file writes to a dedicated temporary directory and denying network access. Scoped device and IPC operations support the retained R and Python workflows.
- Support R runtime queries, Python multiprocessing semaphores, and PTYs created by `processx`.
- Prevent commands from opening pre-existing PTYs. POSIX semaphore access remains intentionally unscoped because this generic launcher cannot assign runtime-specific names.
- Wait for the direct command and return its status. Background descendants are unsupported: they may outlive the launcher, which attempts to remove their dedicated temporary directory on a best-effort basis when it returns. Supervision is deferred because it must address process groups, session-detached children, signal forwarding, and PID reuse together.

## Internal changes

- Add platform dispatch with a macOS implementation and an unsupported-platform stub.
- Embed the filesystem and runtime compatibility rules in one read-only Seatbelt policy.
- Create a private `mcp-console-tmp-<id>` child beneath the process temporary directory, set the child's `TMPDIR` to its canonical path, and grant writes only beneath that path.
- Keep temporary-directory cleanup best-effort so child-controlled permissions do not replace the child status.
- Run CI on Ubuntu and macOS, install `processx` for the macOS acceptance tests, and update the current-state documentation.

title: Document future Python session modes
description:
## Why

Record possible standalone Python modes without changing the current R-hosted implementation direction.

## User-facing changes

The vision now identifies Python-only and Python-with-SQL sessions as a future direction. The R-hosted architecture and the rest of the current design remain in place.

## Internal changes

None. This PR changes no implemented behavior or runtime architecture.

title: Bootstrap Rust project
description:
## Why

Start implementation from the design sketches with the smallest executable Rust package and a shared local/CI check path. This keeps the first review narrow and makes the boundary between implemented and proposed behavior explicit.

## What changed

- Creates a single Rust binary package with package metadata and a committed lockfile.
- Adds the first public behavior: `mcp-console --version`.
- Tests that behavior through the compiled binary.
- Adds `scripts/check` and CI for formatting, Clippy with warnings denied, and tests.
- Adds a root `AGENTS.md` that records the current state, repository map, and narrow-PR guidance.
- Updates the root README with the implemented command and local check entry point.
- Adjusts the design sketches to allow any available combination of R, Python, and SQL.

## User-facing changes

`mcp-console --version` prints the package name and version. The MCP server and language runtimes are not implemented yet.

## Internal changes

The repository now has one dependency-free Cargo package. Local development and CI invoke the same check script. The runtime design no longer assumes that R must be present for Python or SQL sessions.

## Testing

- `scripts/check`
